We experiment under real world, dynamic conditions, evaluate the technological aspects, strategies, process flows and key observations under the broad Edge Computing domain. Research pathways include Multi-access Edge topologies in future 6G networks, model quantization, and satellite-enhanced communication platforms. Additionally, a discussion is added supporting the advanced AI functionalities, including zero-shot learning, multi modal perception, and decentralized generative AI, thereby broadening the scope of intelligent applications across various domains. The significance and research objective of this study are threefold: (1) evaluation of LoRaWAN and satellite IoT communication strategies, (2) analysis of CV workloads on edge hardware and (3) future research directions where Edge Computing can support low-latency, energy-efficient and socially impactful IoT applications. By explicitly addressing these aspects, we aim to establish a clear link between the technological feasibility, ultimately with a practical and socioeconomic relevance.

authors.name: Panagiotis Savvidis, George A. Papakostas

papers.title: Single-Radar Bilateral 3D Near-Field Imaging for Mobile Robots
papers.summary: Mobile robots operating in homes need reliable 3D perception of nearby furniture and surrounding structures, yet recovering this information on both sides of the robot's path with a single forward-mounted millimeter-wave radar remains challenging because of near-field wavefront curvature, viewpoint-dependent target visibility, and limited elevation diversity. This paper presents a motion-assisted framework for reconstructing structures on both sides of a robot's trajectory. Our near-field model relates scene reflectivity to stepped-frequency multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) observations across frequencies and robot positions using spherical paths from transmitter (Tx) to scatterer to receiver (Rx). Bilateral Tx combining provides wideband directional weighting, while sliding-aperture back-projection coherently focuses the measurements using near-field propagation distances. Top-K power fusion combines local images with different visibility. The reconstruction provides lateral-forward support for multi-layer height extraction, followed by guarded adaptive height refinement using the original MIMO channels. Experiments in controlled, office/study, and corridor environments produce mean lateral-forward localization errors of 4.65, 5.63, and 5.98 cm, respectively, with peak-to-background ratios (PBRs) exceeding 13 dB. The framework recovers bilateral 3D scattering structure from one forward pass using a single radar, without relying on learned representations of the scene.

authors.name: Yingqi Wang, Tingwei Chen, Zhongqin Wang, Min Xu

papers.title: Feel My Focus: Gaze-Triggered Digital Twin Creation for Remote Collaboration
papers.summary: We present Feel My Focus, a gaze-triggered mixed reality (MR) demonstration that enables rapid creation and sharing of lightweight 3D digital twins during remote collaboration. Unlike systems that use gaze primarily as a referential pointer, Feel My Focus treats sustained visual attention as a generative action: a fixation on a physical object initiates single-image capture, attention-guided segmentation, and one-shot 3D reconstruction, allowing a remote partner to inspect and discuss the object in situ. The system integrates gaze-tracking glasses, modular segmentation and reconstruction services, and an MR client for runtime streaming and interaction. This design prioritizes responsiveness and experiential continuity over photometric fidelity. We report observations from a public demonstration, highlighting design trade-offs, failure modes, and user control considerations for deploying gaze-triggered generative systems in real-world collaborative settings.

authors.name: Shih-Yu Ma, Suibi Che-Chuan Weng, Ming-Yuan Pai, Tom Yeh, Ellen Yi-Luen Do

papers.title: Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots
papers.summary: 3D visual perception and scene reconstruction are critical for autonomous robots and intelligent transportation, yet real-world deployments often generate long, redundant image sequences that hinder downstream processing. This report investigates BCVS (budget-aware correspondence-driven view sampling), a pose-free view selection algorithm that offers 22+ FPS on a CPU, enabling online filtering for efficient 3D perception by mobile robots. Unlike existing approaches that rely on full structure-from-motion (SfM) pipelines or camera pose estimation, BCVS employs a purely correspondence-based scoring strategy that prioritizes view novelty while maintaining sufficient overlap for geometric stability. Given a user-specified budget, BCVS iteratively selects the most distinct frames and suppresses near-duplicates, producing compact subsets that preserve connectivity and minimize reconstruction loss. Extensive experiments on benchmark show that BCVS outperforms CPU-friendly baselines at tight budgets and remains competitive as budgets scale. Field trials with large aerial and marine robotics data further validate its practicality and scalability: BCVS reduces redundancy up to 16% while sustaining robust SfM registration and high-quality 3D reconstructions.

authors.name: Vaishnav Ramesh, Jacob Carter, Shivali J. Patel, Sanjeev J. Koppal, Md Jahidul Islam

papers.title: DPGS-SLAM: Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic Visual Sensing
papers.summary: This paper presents DPGS-SLAM (Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM) for dense mapping in environments containing dynamic objects. Dynamic observations can contaminate camera tracking and scene reconstruction in visual SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping). Although 3DGS (3D Gaussian splatting) enables efficient dense mapping, existing 3DGS-SLAM systems may exhibit instability when dynamic objects violate their underlying static-scene assumption. Excluding dynamic observations can reduce their influence on tracking and mapping, but may leave occluded static backgrounds missing or weakly constrained. Our proposed DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework that supports provisional representations of insufficiently observed static backgrounds through asynchronous diffusion-based background completion and provenance-aware Gaussian mapping. Dynamic regions are identified through optical-flow-based motion discovery and temporally consistent mask propagation by SAM2 (segment anything model 2). For selected keyframes, a fine-tuned diffusion inpainting model generates plausible background appearance in occluded regions, while Metric3D v2 predicts metric depth from the completed images to initialize provisional Gaussian primitives. Provenance labels distinguish generated primitives from observation-supported primitives, excluding generated content from camera-pose estimation and observed-map optimization. When previously occluded backgrounds become visible, eligible generated primitives are removed, and observation-supported primitives are independently initialized from real RGB observations and predicted depth. Experimental results demonstrated competitive camera tracking, with average ATE RMSE values of 1.2 cm on TUM RGB-D and 2.7 cm on BONN RGB-D. On StaDy4D, DPGS-SLAM improved average PSNR by 4.60 dB over WildGS-SLAM using only monocular RGB input.

authors.name: Yifan Luo, Takafumi Matsumaru, Vibekananda Dutta, Xin He

papers.title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
papers.summary: Background: Diagnostic I-131 whole-body planar imaging in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is count-limited by low administered activity, and quality worsens under rapid acquisition. Models trained on such data struggle because their targets lack photon statistics. Purpose: To test whether high-quality post-therapeutic (PT) I-131 scans can serve as superior training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images, using transfer learning and input-image addition. Methods: In this single-center prospective study, 111 patients were enrolled in PT training (n = 19), diagnostic follow-up (FU) training (n = 58), and FU paired test (n = 34) cohorts. Five Restormer-based models were trained: FU_DLx2 on FU labels; PT_DLx2 transfer-learned on PT data; PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ with input-image addition; PT_DLx6 as a PT-only reference. Test-time processing used two-step denormalization and Poisson re-scaling to preserve noise statistics. Quality was assessed by PSNR, SSIM, and a blinded dual-reader evaluation of all 34 test-cohort patients. Results: PT_DLx2 achieved the highest PSNR (34.4 +/- 3.6 dB) and SSIM (0.81 +/- 0.07). PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ were comparable (33.8 and 33.3 dB; SSIM 0.80). FU_DLx2 ranked below the unprocessed fast scan (30.3 vs. 32.0 dB; 0.76 vs. 0.79). Subjectively, PT_DLx2+ scored highest in image quality (4.54 +/- 0.60) and diagnostic confidence (4.54 +/- 0.60), surpassing the reference standard (4.19 +/- 0.83 and 4.31 +/- 0.81; P = 0.005 and P = 0.008). FU_DLx2 and PT_DLx6 scored lowest. Conclusion: Count-rich PT scans provide effective training priors for reconstructing extremely sparse images. Input-image addition and cross-domain transfer learning from PT data outperformed direct training on count-limited diagnostic data, supporting 2x scan acceleration with quality matching or exceeding the unaccelerated standard scan for selected PT-derived configurations.

authors.name: Boyang Pan, Hang Yang, Jianchen Pan, Cui Gan, Lanxi Zhang, Hongmin Li, Nan-Jie Gong

papers.title: SPARK: Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge to Robot Control
papers.summary: Large-scale representation learning has produced public foundation models that provide strong general-purpose visual features. However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. Training robot models from scratch is also undesirable due to the limited scale and high collection cost of robotics data, as well as the substantial computational burden of pre-training. In this paper, we propose SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control. SPARK is built on two principles: temporal abstraction, which encourages the encoder to derive compact features that preserve information essential for understanding temporal changes and action-relevant scene structure, and knowledge preservation, which aligns patch-level representations with those of the original foundation model to retain useful pretrained semantics. These objectives yield compact visual state representations that remain semantically meaningful while preserving useful prior knowledge. Experiments across multiple robotics benchmarks show that SPARK consistently improves success rates and generalization over vanilla foundation models, and further demonstrate that these gains transfer to real-world robot manipulation.

authors.name: Taekyung Kim, Jeongeun Park, Byeongho Heo, Sungjoon Choi, Sangdoo Yun, Dongyoon Han

papers.title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path
papers.summary: We present a real-time method for reconstructing fully integrated pixel radiance in rendered volumetric media under direct and ambient environmental illumination, using compact, low-cost scene features and statistics. Unlike Monte Carlo denoising pipelines for volumetric rendering, which depend on computationally expensive path-traced radiance estimates, our approach directly infers the final light-transport solution from inexpensive primary-ray and environment sample evaluations. We show that these features form a near-sufficient representation of the scene, enabling accurate reconstruction at substantially lower computational cost. Using an attention-augmented image-to-image network, we demonstrate that complete pixel radiance can be inferred directly from these auxiliary features, without requiring the original radiance signal. Operating in image space also provides a more stable computational cost as the camera zooms into or out of the volume, with substantially less dependence on volume density than approaches based on explicit multiple-scattering simulation. We demonstrate real-time performance and high reconstruction accuracy in challenging volumetric cloud scenarios.

authors.name: Ludwic Leonard, Ruediger Westermann

papers.title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
papers.summary: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. To train the Cerebellum for natural, route-faithful motion, we develop a physics-grounded data engine that improves physical tracking of motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations. Together, these designs allow task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. In simulation, our navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls. Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 further demonstrates single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon task execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects. Project website: https://robbyant-research.github.io/LHNav/.

authors.name: Xueyang Wang, Zehong Shen, Dingkun Wei, Huaijin Pi, Changpeng Wang, Xing Zhu, Hujun Bao, Yujun Shen, Xiaowei Zhou

papers.title: VLA-MOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task VLA Policy Consolidation
papers.summary: Physical intelligence requires embodied agents to ground language in observations and execute actions while retaining useful skills. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies offer a shared interface, but task-specific post-training often produces separate specialists. Consolidation is difficult: mixed-task reinforcement learning provides sparse trajectory-level credit, while offline distillation may miss student-visited observations and endpoint distillation does not supervise intermediate action-generation states. We introduce VLA Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (VLA-MOPD), a protocol for consolidating flow-matching VLA specialists. After acquiring task or suite experts, a shared student collects robot rollouts and queries the instruction-routed frozen teacher at each visited observation and intermediate ordinary differential equation (ODE) state. Detached per-flow-step transition targets supervise valid action chunks through a masked local matching loss; an optional reference-policy term supports retention on other tasks. Starting from one trajectory per LIBERO task, VLA-MOPD raises mean success-once from 75.4% to 98.9%, compared with 98.15% for endpoint action distillation. It improves mean RoboTwin 2.0 success from 73.0% to 89.3%; on a Piper robot, two consolidation rounds improve average success from 70.0% to 90.0%. In a near-matched Spatial-adaptation study, reference matching limits the Object suite decrease to 3.0 points, versus 13.2 without the reference term.

authors.name: Yongxuan Lv, Zhen Fang, Lichen Man, Hao Li, Pu Li, Hengyi Wang, Langfeng Cao, Lin Chen, Jie Huang, Xiu Su, Shan You, Fei Wang, Feng Zhao

papers.title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
papers.summary: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory. We address this gap with TrajCond, which introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition for VLA planning. Specifically, we represent TrajCond as a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory and learn it with a two-stage training framework before final continuous trajectory prediction. With the simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, we name our method AutoVLA-D (Double). Experiments on NAVSIM navtest, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP show that discrete trajectories are weaker as direct outputs but more effective as TrajCond, consistently improving final continuous trajectory prediction across closed-loop and open-loop driving benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/ShivaTeam/AutoVLA-D.

authors.name: Yuguang Yang, Zhewen Tan, Canyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Cheng Chi, Chunyang Liu, Kehua Sheng, Jinyu Yang, Baochang Zhan, Bo Zhang, Yan Wang, Xianbin Cao

papers.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
papers.summary: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

authors.name: Maolin Ye, Dongqing Zhao, Linyang Li, Shuai Xue, Yuan Liu, Yiyuan Wang, Wen Li

papers.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
papers.summary: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

authors.name: Matteo Ciferri, Tonio Weidler, Matteo Ferrante, Nicola Toschi, Elia Formisano

papers.title: Deep Algebraic Fitting for Multiple Circle Primitives Extraction from Raw Point Clouds
papers.summary: The shape of circle is one of fundamental geometric primitives of man-made engineering objects. Thus, extraction of circles from scanned point clouds is a quite important task in 3D geometry data processing. However, existing circle extraction methods either are sensitive to the quality of raw point clouds when classifying circle-boundary points, or require well-designed fitting functions when regressing circle parameters. To relieve the challenges, we propose an end-to-end Point Cloud Circle Algebraic Fitting Network (Circle-Net) based on a synergy of deep circle-boundary point feature learning and weighted algebraic fitting. First, we design a circle-boundary learning module, which considers local and global neighboring contexts of each point, to detect all potential circle-boundary points. Second, we develop a deep feature based circle parameter learning module for weighted algebraic fitting, without designing any weight metric, to avoid the influence of outliers during fitting. Unlike most of the cutting-edge circle extraction wisdoms, the proposed classification-and-fitting modules are originally co-trained with a comprehensive loss to enhance the quality of extracted circles.Comparisons on the established dataset and real-scanned point clouds exhibit clear improvements of Circle-Net over SOTAs in terms of both noise-robustness and extraction accuracy. We will release our code, model, and data for both training and evaluation on GitHub upon publication.

authors.name: Zeyong Wei, Honghua Chen, Hao Tang, Qian Xie, Mingqiang Wei, Jun Wang

papers.title: AI-Generated Images as Data Source: The Dawn of Synthetic Era
papers.summary: The advancement of visual intelligence is intrinsically tethered to the availability of large-scale data. In parallel, generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has unlocked the potential to create synthetic images that closely resemble real-world photographs. This prompts a compelling inquiry: how much visual intelligence could benefit from the advance of generative AI? This paper explores the innovative concept of harnessing these AI-generated images as new data sources, reshaping traditional modeling paradigms in visual intelligence. In contrast to real data, AI-generated data exhibit remarkable advantages, including unmatched abundance and scalability, the rapid generation of vast datasets, and the effortless simulation of edge cases. Built on the success of generative AI models, we examine the potential of their generated data in a range of applications, from training machine learning models to simulating scenarios for computational modeling, testing, and validation. We probe the technological foundations that support this groundbreaking use of generative AI, engaging in an in-depth discussion on the ethical, legal, and practical considerations that accompany this transformative paradigm shift. Through an exhaustive survey of current technologies and applications, this paper presents a comprehensive view of the synthetic era in visual intelligence. A project associated with this paper can be found at https://github.com/mwxely/AIGS .

authors.name: Zuhao Yang, Yu Wei, Fangneng Zhan, Kunhao Liu, Muyu Xu, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu

papers.title: Towards Multi-domain Face Landmark Detection with Synthetic Data from Diffusion model
papers.summary: Recently, deep learning-based facial landmark detection for in-the-wild faces has achieved significant improvement. However, there are still challenges in face landmark detection in other domains (e.g. cartoon, caricature, etc). This is due to the scarcity of extensively annotated training data. To tackle this concern, we design a two-stage training approach that effectively leverages limited datasets and the pre-trained diffusion model to obtain aligned pairs of landmarks and face in multiple domains. In the first stage, we train a landmark-conditioned face generation model on a large dataset of real faces. In the second stage, we fine-tune the above model on a small dataset of image-landmark pairs with text prompts for controlling the domain. Our new designs enable our method to generate high-quality synthetic paired datasets from multiple domains while preserving the alignment between landmarks and facial features. Finally, we fine-tuned a pre-trained face landmark detection model on the synthetic dataset to achieve multi-domain face landmark detection. Our qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing methods on multi-domain face landmark detection.

authors.name: Yuanming Li, Gwantae Kim, Jeong-gi Kwak, Bon-hwa Ku, Hanseok Ko

papers.title: ProCreate, Don't Reproduce! Propulsive Energy Diffusion for Creative Generation
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose ProCreate, a simple and easy-to-implement method to improve sample diversity and creativity of diffusion-based image generative models and to prevent training data reproduction. ProCreate operates on a set of reference images and actively propels the generated image embedding away from the reference embeddings during the generation process. We propose FSCG-8 (Few-Shot Creative Generation 8), a few-shot creative generation dataset on eight different categories -- encompassing different concepts, styles, and settings -- in which ProCreate achieves the highest sample diversity and fidelity. Furthermore, we show that ProCreate is effective at preventing replicating training data in a large-scale evaluation using training text prompts. Code and FSCG-8 are available at https://github.com/Agentic-Learning-AI-Lab/procreate-diffusion-public. The project page is available at https://procreate-diffusion.github.io.

authors.name: Jack Lu, Ryan Teehan, Mengye Ren

papers.title: Paleoinspired Vision: From Exploring Colour Vision Evolution to Inspiring Camera Design
papers.summary: The evolution of colour vision is captivating, as it reveals the adaptive strategies of extinct species while simultaneously inspiring innovations in modern imaging technology. In this study, we present a simplified model of visual transduction in the retina, introducing a novel opsin layer. We quantify evolutionary pressures by measuring machine vision recognition accuracy on colour images shaped by specific opsins. Building on this, we develop an evolutionary conservation optimisation algorithm to reconstruct the spectral sensitivity of opsins, enabling mutation-driven adaptations to more effectively spot fruits or predators. This model condenses millions of years of evolution into seconds using GPU, providing an experimental framework to test long-standing hypotheses in evolutionary biology, such as vision of early mammals, primate trichromacy from gene duplication, retention of colour blindness, blue-shift of fish rod and multiple rod opsins with bioluminescence. Beyond validating existing paleontological hypotheses, our model further enables speculative explorations of hypothetical species, such as organisms with visual systems adapted to Martian conditions. These constitute our contributions to AI for life science and neuroscience. Besides, the principles derived from these biological studies can translate into practical engineering solutions. In practice, our findings suggest a minimalist yet effective approach to task-specific camera filter design, optimising the spectral response function to meet application-driven demands. Code repository: https://github.com/luyijie-research/PaleVision.

authors.name: Yijie Lu, Zhimin Zong, Junjie Zhang, Shenghan Su, Zeyun Zhao, Ziteng Cui, Yan Pu, Jing Lu, Daisuke Kojima, Lin Gu, Ruogu Fang

papers.title: LFX: Fusion-Form-Flexible Light Field Modeling for Dense Semantic Segmentation and Salient Object Detection
papers.summary: Two distinct light field (LF) observation forms, namely sub-aperture images (S.Aperture images) and focal stack (FS), correspond to two fusion settings: the central image with S.Aperture images (CS) and the central image with FS (CF). Existing LF perception methods are typically form-specific, while a modeling design that can be separately instantiated under either setting remains underexplored. To address this gap, we present LFX, a form-flexible LF perception framework. Here, ``X'' represents the LF observation form, indicating that the one modeling design can be separately instantiated under two fusion settings (CS and CF). Specifically, we propose Field-of-Parallax Angular Subspace Modeling (FoP-ASM), which maps the feature difference between each auxiliary observation and the central image to an observation-specific angular marker. This avoids pairwise modeling among auxiliary observations and form-specific geometric assumptions. Meanwhile, a shared manifold subspace and the associated regularization losses constrain the angular residuals within a common feature space, promoting semantic consistency across auxiliary observations. Extensive evaluations across three LF datasets show that LFX achieves state-of-the-art results across distinct LF forms. Under the S.Aperture images and FS settings, respectively, LFX reduces MAE by 12.12%/20.59% on DUTLF-V2 and by 6.15%/7.69% on HFUT, while achieving the best performance on UrbanLF-real. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/FeiT-FeiTeng/LFX.

authors.name: Fei Teng, Lingxin Huang, Buyin Deng, Kai Luo, Boyuan Zheng, Zheng Fang, Hong Zheng, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Yaonan Wang, Kailun Yang

papers.title: RefRef: A Dataset and Benchmark for Reconstructing Refractive and Reflective Objects
papers.summary: Modern 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis approaches have demonstrated strong performance on scenes with opaque, non-refractive objects. However, most assume straight light paths and therefore cannot properly handle refractive and reflective materials. The lack of datasets specialized for these effects has impeded efforts to fairly and thoroughly evaluate performance and thereby make progress in this domain. Most existing datasets focus on opaque scenes, while those targeting refractive objects are often limited to thin glass with negligible ray bending, untinted single-material objects, or backgrounds treated as infinitely-distant, leaving key failure modes under strong refraction untested. To address this gap, we introduce the RefRef dataset. It contains 150 synthetic and 60 real scenes spanning varying levels of geometric complexity and diverse background types that expose the limitations of existing methods. For the purpose of benchmarking, we also provide an oracle method that, given the object geometry and refractive indices, calculates accurate light paths for neural rendering, and a simple two-stage baseline that relaxes these assumptions. We evaluate these against state-of-the-art methods and show that the task is far from solved.

authors.name: Yue Yin, Enze Tao, Weijian Deng, Dylan Campbell

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Object-Centric Learning with Distant Supervision
papers.summary: Neurosymbolic learning can use symbolic rules to provide supervision for latent concepts from weak labels, but it commonly assumes that the entities referenced by these rules are already specified. Object-centric models decompose images into slot-like representations; however, such slots are not necessarily aligned with the predicates required for symbolic reasoning. We investigate object-centric neurosymbolic learning under distant supervision, where the object-level arguments of a logic program are learned directly from images using only global task labels. We introduce DeepPbjectLog, a probabilistic neurosymbolic model that integrates a slot-based perceptual encoder with a probabilistic logic layer. The encoder predicts objectness and class probabilities for candidate object representations, while the logic layer marginalizes over latent objectness and class assignments to compute the likelihood of the observed label. This formulation provides a differentiable task-level learning signal for object-centric perception without requiring per-object labels, masks, bounding boxes, or heuristic set matching. Evaluations across diverse visual reasoning tasks demonstrate that DeepObjectLog achieves superior out-of-distribution generalization to compositional, object-count, and rule shifts compared to neural object-centric and standard neurosymbolic baselines.

authors.name: Stefano Colamonaco, David Debot, Giuseppe Marra

papers.title: IKOD: Image-Attention-Guided Key-Value Merging against Object Hallucination in the Decoding of Large Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) exhibit strong visual understanding and language generation capabilities yet remain prone to object hallucination, producing plausible descriptions unsupported by the input image. Analyzing generation dynamics across eight diverse LVLMs, we observe that cross-modal visual attention steadily decays as generation unfolds because appended text tokens continuously expand the softmax denominator; consequently, hallucinated objects consistently appear later and under lower image attention than grounded mentions. Unlike existing training-free remedies that rely on input perturbations or external models, we propose IKOD (Image-attention-guided Key-value merging against Object hallucination in Decoding), a collaborative decoder that directly compresses the competing text context within the native key-value (KV) cache. At each step, IKOD keeps visual tokens intact and merges low-attention text entries into a compact auxiliary cache, fusing the resulting image-focused distribution with the base branch to correct ungrounded predictions while preserving linguistic fluency. An adaptive variant (IKOD-A) further schedules collaboration strength online from the measured attention decay under a single universal configuration. Extensive experiments across hallucination and general multimodal benchmarks on eight diverse LVLMs demonstrate that IKOD and IKOD-A consistently mitigate object hallucination while preserving object recall and general multimodal capabilities at minimal inference cost. Code is available at https://github.com/jiabingyang01/IKOD.

authors.name: Jiabing Yang, Chenhang Cui, Yixiang Chen, Tao Yu, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

papers.title: Language-Aware Information Maximization for Transductive Few-Shot CLIP
papers.summary: Transductive few-shot learning has triggered an abundant literature focusing on vision-only models, but is still at a nascent stage within the recent context of foundational vision-language models (VLMs). Only a few recent methods addressed the problem, pointing to the potential of tranduction in VLMs and to the need for VLM-tailored methods. Building on this momentum, we leverage information-theoretic concepts and recent progress in parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), developing a highly competitive transductive few-shot CLIP method. Specifically, we introduce a novel Language-aware Information MaximizatiOn (LIMO) loss integrating three complementary terms: (i) the mutual information between the vision inputs and the textual class descriptions; (ii) a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence penalizing deviation of the network's probabilistic outputs from the text-driven zero-shot predictions; and (iii) a standard cross-entropy loss based on the labeled shots. Furthermore, we challenge the commonly followed fine-tuning practices in the context of transductive few-shot learning, and explore PEFT strategies, completely overlooked in this context. Surprisingly, we observe substantial boosts in performances, which points to the potential of adapting a subset of the model's parameters in the transductive few-shot setting. We report comprehensive evaluations, which show that LIMO outperforms the very recent transductive few-shot CLIP methods by a large margin and yields significant gains over the best-performing inductive methods. Our code is publicly available at:https://github.com/ghassenbaklouti/LIMO

authors.name: Ghassen Baklouti, Maxime Zanella, Ismail Ben Ayed

papers.title: Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Model Encoders for Image-Text Retrieval in Chest X-rays
papers.summary: Multimodal learning from paired medical images and clinical text is a central challenge in medical data-driven informatics, where effective cross-modal alignment is critical for scalable analysis and retrieval. In chest radiography, vision-language pretraining is constrained by heterogeneous radiology reports that contain abbreviations, impression-only notes, and institution-specific writing styles. Unlike general-domain settings, naively aggregating large collections of noisy reports can plateau or even degrade multimodal learning when reporting styles differ substantially. We propose a domain-adapted bidirectional large language model text encoder for chest radiograph reports, trained with masked token prediction and supervised contrastive learning on stylistically diverse but clinically equivalent report variants to produce robust, generalizable text embeddings. We then integrate this encoder into a dual-tower contrastive vision-language framework using parameter-efficient adaptation to improve image-text alignment. Across 1.6 million paired studies from public datasets and a de-identified hospital cohort, the proposed models improve bidirectional retrieval accuracy and external generalization, achieving GREEN scores of 0.308 on MIMIC-CXR and 0.618 on Open-I, while reducing the degradation observed when abbreviation-rich, impression-only hospital reports are added to training.

authors.name: Hanbin Ko, Gihun Cho, Inhyeok Baek, Donguk Kim, Joonbeom Koo, Changi Kim, Dongheon Lee, Chang Min Park

papers.title: D2D: Detector-to-Differentiable Critic for Improved Numeracy in Text-to-Image Generation
papers.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models have achieved strong performance in semantic alignment, yet they still struggle with generating the correct number of objects specified in prompts. Existing approaches typically incorporate auxiliary counting networks as external critics to enhance numeracy. However, since these critics must provide gradient guidance during generation, they are restricted to regression-based models that are inherently differentiable, thus excluding detector-based models with superior counting ability, whose count-via-enumeration nature is non-differentiable. To overcome this, we propose Detector-to-Differentiable (D2D), a novel framework that transforms non-differentiable detection models into differentiable critics, leveraging their superior counting ability to guide numeracy generation. Specifically, we design custom activation functions to convert detector logits into soft binary indicators, which are then used to optimize the noise prior at inference time with pre-trained T2I models. Our extensive experiments on SDXL-Turbo, SD-Turbo, and Pixart-DMD across four benchmarks of varying complexity (low-density, high-density, and multi-object scenarios) demonstrate consistent and substantial improvements in object counting accuracy (e.g., boosting up to 13.7% on D2D-Small, a 400-prompt, low-density benchmark), with minimal degradation in overall image quality and computational overhead. Project page: https://nobliney.github.io/d2d/.

authors.name: Nobline Yoo, Olga Russakovsky, Ye Zhu

papers.title: ALICE-LRI: A General Method for Lossless Range Image Generation for Spinning LiDAR Sensors without Calibration Metadata
papers.summary: 3D LiDAR sensors are widely used in autonomous navigation, environmental monitoring, and precision mapping. Their point clouds are often projected into 2D range images for efficient processing, but conventional projection methods can lose points because of geometric inconsistencies. We present ALICE-LRI (Automatic LiDAR Intrinsic Calibration Estimation for Lossless Range Images), a metadata-free method for lossless range-image generation from calibrated spinning multi-beam LiDAR point clouds. It requires neither factory calibration files, packet-level data, nor beam identifiers, and targets operating regimes where scanlines contain enough returns for reliable parameter estimation. The method estimates the intrinsic calibration parameters relevant to projection, including beam configuration, angular distributions, and per-beam geometric corrections. Evaluation on the complete KITTI and DurLAR datasets yielded zero lost points across all point clouds. Reconstruction deviations remain below manufacturer-reported range-performance specifications, while the method runs in real time. A compression case study also shows improved reconstruction quality and a better quality-compression trade-off for a downstream application. These results enable range-image-based LiDAR processing in applications that require high measurement fidelity and preservation of acquired geometric information.

authors.name: Samuel Soutullo, Miguel Yermo, David L. Vilari\~no, \'Oscar G. Lorenzo, Jos\'e C. Cabaleiro, Francisco F. Rivera

papers.title: Edge Assisted Multi-Camera Vehicle Tracking Framework for Real-Time and Scalable Deployment
papers.summary: Cameras are a core sensing modality in modern intelligent transportation systems (ITS), providing rich visual information on road-user activities. Multi-Camera Vehicle Tracking (MCVT) uses this data to reconstruct vehicle trajectories across camera networks, supporting applications such as traffic flow prediction and optimisation. However, most existing MCVT studies emphasise tracking accuracy while paying limited attention to real-time performance and scalability, both essential for real-world and city-scale deployment. To address this gap, we propose Edge-Assisted, Scalable and Efficient MCVT (EASE-MCVT), a distributed edge--server framework designed for real-time throughput and scalable operation. On the edge side, each camera stream is processed through object detection, single-camera tracking, geo-mapping and feature extraction, while only lightweight metadata, including vehicle locations and appearance features, is sent to the central server for cross-camera association. To improve both tracking accuracy and system efficiency, EASE-MCVT is optimised from algorithmic and system perspectives. Algorithmically, it introduces a dynamic workload scheme for tracklet-level feature extraction, a server-side re-match module to reconnect fragmented tracklets, and a self-supervised camera link model that learns spatio-temporal constraints to accelerate and stabilise cross-camera association. Systemically, it integrates production-oriented data engineering components to standardise deployment and data exchange for large-scale operation. To the best of our knowledge, EASE-MCVT is the first MCVT framework explicitly designed to address both real-time performance and scalability in a distributed edge--server setting. Experiments on the RoundaboutHD and CityFlow datasets demonstrate real-time throughput with competitive tracking accuracy, paving the way for city-wide real-time traffic management.

authors.name: Yuqiang Lin, Sam Lockyer, Shucheng Zhang, Florian Stanek, Markus Zarbock, Adrian Evans, Wenbin Li, Yinhai Wang, Nic Zhang

papers.title: Matching-Based Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation Models Are Interpretable by Design
papers.summary: Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation (FSS) models achieve strong performance in segmenting novel classes with minimal labeled examples, yet their decision-making processes remain largely opaque. Explainable AI has matured on standard computer vision tasks, but not on FSS, where an explanation would tell a practitioner which support pixels the prediction rested on and which examples to provide next. We argue that matching-based FSS models are interpretable by design: their query-support similarity scores, once normalized and processed, attribute the prediction to individual support pixels. Our approach, Affinity Explainer (AffEx), makes this intrinsic interpretability explicit by extracting attribution maps directly from matching scores at multiple feature levels, without requiring gradients or external perturbations. We extend the standard causal metrics for evaluating explanations to the FSS domain and propose additional metrics to better capture the practical utility of explanations in few-shot scenarios. Experiments on two FSS benchmarks, covering seven architectures that range from classical matching-based models to recent pipelines built on vision foundation models (DINOv2/v3, SAM, SAM2) and a prototype-based head, show that AffEx outperforms adapted standard attribution methods at nearly every evaluation point, and that the gain comes from the matching mechanism itself. On pipelines whose segmentation stage transforms the matching output, the same evaluation doubles as a diagnostic of where the decision is made, and on the prototype-based head AffEx subsumes the prototype-style read-out as a special case. Qualitatively, the attribution maps expose how each architecture resolves the support set, and we show how they guide model diagnosis. Code is available at https://github.com/pasqualedem/AffinityExplainer.

authors.name: Pasquale De Marinis, Uzay Kaymak, Rogier Brussee, Gennaro Vessio, Giovanna Castellano

papers.title: Dual-Granularity Semantic Prompting for Language Guidance Infrared Small Target Detection
papers.summary: Infrared small target detection remains challenging due to limited feature representation and severe background interference, resulting in sub-optimal performance. While recent CLIP-inspired methods attempt to leverage textual guidance for detection, they are hindered by inaccurate text descriptions and reliance on manual annotations. To overcome these limitations, we propose DGSPNet, an end-to-end language prompt-driven framework. Our approach integrates dual-granularity semantic prompts: coarse-grained textual priors (e.g., 'infrared image', 'small target') and fine-grained personalized semantic descriptions derived through visual-to-textual mapping within the image space. This design not only facilitates learning fine-grained semantic information but also can inherently leverage language prompts during inference without relying on any annotation requirements. By fully leveraging the precision and conciseness of text descriptions, we further introduce a text-guide channel attention (TGCA) mechanism and text-guide spatial attention (TGSA) mechanism that enhances the model's sensitivity to potential targets across both low- and high-level feature spaces. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves detection accuracy and achieves state-of-the-art performance on three benchmark datasets.

authors.name: Zixuan Wang, Haoran Sun, Jiaming Lu, Wenxuan Wang, Zhongling Huang, Dingwen Zhang, Xuelin Qian, Junwei Han

papers.title: FIELDS: Face reconstruction with accurate Inference of Expression using Learning with Direct Supervision
papers.summary: Monocular 3D face reconstruction estimates the parameters of a 3D morphable face model (3DMM) from a single image, providing an explicit geometric representation for facial expression analysis. Owing to the scarcity of paired 2D images and 3D facial meshes, most methods are trained in a self-supervised manner by rendering the predicted face and minimizing image-level reconstruction losses, such as photometric and landmark errors, against the input image. However, these losses enforce visual alignment but do not ensure that the predicted parameters preserve affective information. Recent methods add image-level emotion consistency loss, but it can be satisfied by exaggerating facial deformations. To address these issues, we propose FIELDS (Face reconstruction with accurate Inference of Expression using Learning with Direct Supervision), which learns affect-informative expression representations in the FLAME parameter space. Specifically, FIELDS augments 2D self-supervised reconstruction with scan-derived expression anchoring and a parameter-space emotion loss. During training, scan-fitted targets directly constrain expression-related FLAME parameters to discourage exaggerated deformations, while a jointly trained emotion head uses discrete emotion and continuous valence--arousal annotations to make the predicted parameters informative for affect analysis. Experiments show that FIELDS improves affective utility from the predicted parameters in both within- and cross-dataset settings. Notably, it also achieves lower reconstruction errors overall and across most facial regions than the comparison baselines under both rigid and similarity alignment.

authors.name: Chen Ling, Henglin Shi, Hedvig Kjellstr\"om

papers.title: UniDoc: Towards Unified Thinking in Documents
papers.summary: Answering questions over long, visually rich documents demands both cross-page structural reasoning and fine-grained visual understanding. Existing approaches sacrifice one for the other: retrieval-augmented methods fragment documents and lose inter-page structure; monolithic vision-language models preserve structure but scale poorly beyond a few pages. This impasse stems from a false premise: that the macroscopic task of evidence retrieval and the microscopic task of detailed reasoning must either be split into separate systems or be processed identically. By decoupling their perceptual resolutions rather than their architectures, a single model can achieve the structural holism of monolithic processing alongside the efficiency of targeted retrieval. UniDoc realizes this through two resolution-adaptive stages: a Fast Reading stage processes all pages at low resolution to structurally identify evidence pages, and a Focused Thinking stage re-processes only those pages at high resolution for multimodal inference. To train this pipeline, we construct 30K multi-hop reasoning instances with stage-level supervision. On MMLongBench-Doc, UniDoc yields relative accuracy gains of 55.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 16.9% on Qwen3-VL-8B, while significantly reducing token cost relative to uniform high-resolution processing. Error analysis identifies page retrieval and fine-grained visual reasoning as the remaining bottlenecks, delineating concrete targets for future work.

authors.name: Qixin Xu, Haozhe Wang, Che Liu, Fangzhen Lin, Wenhu Chen

papers.title: Spectral Complex Autoencoder Pruning: A Fidelity-Guided Criterion for Extreme Structured Channel Compression
papers.summary: We propose Spectral Complex Autoencoder Pruning (SCAP), a reconstruction-based criterion that measures functional redundancy at the level of individual output channels. For each convolutional layer, we construct a complex interaction field by pairing the full multi-channel input activation as the real part with a single output-channel activation (spatially aligned and broadcast across input channels) as the imaginary part. We transform this complex field to the frequency domain and train a low-capacity autoencoder to reconstruct normalized spectra. Channels whose spectra are reconstructed with high fidelity are interpreted as lying close to a low-dimensional manifold captured by the autoencoder and are therefore more compressible; conversely, channels with low fidelity are retained as they encode information that cannot be compactly represented by the learned manifold. This yields an importance score (optionally fused with the filter L1 norm) that supports simple threshold-based pruning and produces a structurally consistent pruned network. On VGG16 trained on CIFAR-10, at a fixed threshold of 0.6, we obtain 90.11% FLOP reduction and 96.30% parameter reduction with an absolute Top-1 accuracy drop of 1.67% from a 93.44% baseline after fine-tuning, demonstrating that spectral reconstruction fidelity of complex interaction fields is an effective proxy for channel-level redundancy under aggressive compression.

authors.name: Wei Liu, Xing Deng, Haijian Shao, Yingtao Jiang

papers.title: Kelix Technical Report
papers.summary: Autoregressive large language models (LLMs) scale well by expressing diverse tasks as sequences of discrete natural-language tokens and training with next-token prediction, which unifies comprehension and generation under self-supervision. Extending this paradigm to multimodal data requires a shared, discrete representation across modalities. However, most vision-language models (VLMs) still rely on a hybrid interface: discrete text tokens paired with continuous Vision Transformer (ViT) features. Because supervision is largely text-driven, these models are often biased toward understanding and cannot fully leverage large-scale self-supervised learning on non-text data. Recent work has explored discrete visual tokenization to enable fully autoregressive multimodal modeling, showing promising progress toward unified understanding and generation. Yet existing discrete vision tokens frequently lose information due to limited code capacity, resulting in noticeably weaker understanding than continuous-feature VLMs. We present Kelix, a fully discrete autoregressive unified model that closes the understanding gap between discrete and continuous visual representations.

authors.name: Boyang Ding, Chenglong Chu, Dunju Zang, Han Li, Jiangxia Cao, Kun Gai, Muhao Wei, Ruiming Tang, Shiyao Wang, Siyang Mao, Xinchen Luo, Yahui Liu, Zhixin Ling, Zhuoran Yang, Ziming Li, Chengru Song, Guorui Zhou, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Hao Wang, Jiaxin Deng, Jin Ouyang, Jinghao Zhang, Lejian Ren, Qianqian Wang, Qigen Hu, Tao Wang, Xingmei Wang, Yiping Yang, Zixing Zhang, Ziqi Wang

papers.title: VETime: Vision Enhanced Zero-Shot Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) requires identifying both immediate Point Anomalies and long-range Context Anomalies. However, existing foundation models face a fundamental trade-off: 1D temporal models provide fine-grained pointwise localization but lack a global contextual perspective, while 2D vision-based models capture global patterns but suffer from information bottlenecks due to a lack of temporal alignment and coarse-grained pointwise detection. To resolve this dilemma, we propose VETime, the first TSAD framework that unifies temporal and visual modalities through fine-grained visual-temporal alignment and dynamic fusion. VETime introduces a Reversible Image Conversion and a Patch-Level Temporal Alignment module to establish a shared visual-temporal timeline, preserving discriminative details while maintaining temporal sensitivity. Furthermore, we design an Anomaly Window Contrastive Learning mechanism and a Task-Adaptive Multi-Modal Fusion to adaptively integrate the complementary perceptual strengths of both modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VETime significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models in zero-shot scenarios, achieving superior localization precision with lower computational overhead than current vision-based approaches. Code available at: https://github.com/yyyangcoder/VETime .

authors.name: Yingyuan Yang, Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Xuming An, Wenjun He, Meng Wang, Chenghao Liu, Chen Zhang

papers.title: Self-Aware Object Detection via Degradation Manifolds
papers.summary: Object detectors achieve strong performance under nominal imaging conditions but can fail silently when exposed to blur, noise, compression, adverse weather, or resolution changes. In safety-critical settings, it is therefore insufficient to produce predictions without assessing whether the input remains within the detector's nominal operating regime, which we refer to as self-aware object detection. We introduce a degradation-aware framework based on degradation manifolds, which structure a detector's feature space according to image degradation rather than semantic content. Our method augments a standard detection backbone with a lightweight embedding head trained via multi-layer contrastive learning, where images sharing the same degradation composition are pulled together while differing configurations are separated. Unlike prior contrastive IQA approaches, our method performs detector-aligned input-fidelity monitoring: it uses task-backbone features and a nominal prototype to detect degradation-induced shifts, rather than estimating perceptual image quality in a standalone representation. To anchor the representation, we estimate a pristine prototype from clean training embeddings, defining a nominal operating point in feature space. Self-awareness is then derived as geometric deviation from this reference, providing an intrinsic image-level signal of degradation-induced shift that is independent of detection confidence. Experiments on synthetic corruptions, cross-dataset zero-shot transfer, and natural weather-induced shifts show strong pristine-degraded separability, consistent behavior across detector architectures, and robust generalization across datasets with substantial content variation. These results suggest that degradation-aware detector representations provide a reliable signal for monitoring input-fidelity shifts.

authors.name: Stefan Becker, Simon Weiss, Wolfgang H\"ubner, Michael Arens

papers.title: Evaluation of Visual Processing Should Be Human-Centered, Not Metric-Centered
papers.summary: This position paper argues that the evaluation of modern visual processing systems should no longer be driven primarily by single-metric image quality assessment benchmarks, particularly in the era of generative and perception-oriented methods. Image restoration exemplifies this divergence: while objective IQA metrics enable reproducible, scalable evaluation, they have increasingly drifted apart from human perception and user preferences. We contend that this mismatch risks constraining innovation and misguiding research progress across visual processing tasks. Rather than rejecting metrics altogether, this paper calls for a rebalancing of evaluation paradigms, advocating a more human-centered, context-aware, and fine-grained approach to assessing the visual models' outcomes.

authors.name: Fanghua Yu, Jinfan Hu, Zhiyuan You, Xiang Yin, Hongyu An, Xinqi Lin, Chao Dong, Jinjin Gu

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Active Perception for Embodied Question Answering in Dynamic Human-Populated Scenes
papers.summary: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) couples active visual perception, vision-language reasoning, and sequential decision making, and has traditionally been evaluated in temporally stable environments where visual evidence can be accumulated reliably. In realistic multimedia settings such as dynamic human-populated scenes, however, moving people and transient occlusions introduce human-induced perceptual variations: task-relevant multimodal cues become transient, viewpoint-dependent, and incompletely captured in individual views. Conventional store-then-retrieve strategies generate redundant visual evidence and incur high inference cost, making them ill-suited to such variations. This exposes two core problems for embodied agents: resolving viewpoint-dependent ambiguity, and maintaining compact evidence for efficient inference. To address these challenges, we present DIVRR (Dynamic-Informed View Refinement with Relevance-guided Rotation and adaptive memory selection), a training-free active evidence-acquisition framework for EQA. DIVRR combines question-conditioned room guidance with relevance-triggered view augmentation to guide exploration and additional observation. Selective memory admission uses the same relevance signal as view augmentation to retain high-scoring evidence, reducing stored entries while keeping the retrieved visual context compact. To evaluate EQA under human-induced perceptual variations, we introduce DynHuman-EQA, a dynamic human-populated EQA dataset constructed in Habitat, comprising dynamic and static subsets under shared scene layouts. Experiments on DynHuman-EQA and HM-EQA show that DIVRR outperforms existing baselines in both accuracy and memory efficiency. The gains are most pronounced in dynamic human-populated scenes.

authors.name: Xin Lu, Rui Li, Xun Huang, Weixin Li, Jiayuan Li, Chuanqing Zhuang, Zhengda Lu, Jun Xiao

papers.title: PolGS++: Physically-Guided Polarimetric Gaussian Splatting for Fast Reflective Surface Reconstruction
papers.summary: Accurate reconstruction of reflective surfaces remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision, with broad applications in real-time virtual reality and digital content creation. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables efficient novel-view rendering with explicit representations, its performance on reflective surfaces still lags behind implicit neural methods, especially in recovering fine geometry and surface normals. To address this gap, we propose PolGS++, a physically-guided polarimetric Gaussian Splatting framework for fast reflective surface reconstruction. Specifically, we integrate a polarized BRDF (pBRDF) model into 3DGS to explicitly decouple diffuse and specular components, providing physically grounded reflectance modeling and stronger geometric cues for reflective surface recovery. Furthermore, we introduce a depth-guided visibility mask acquisition mechanism that enables angle-of-polarization (AoP)-based tangent-space consistency constraints in Gaussian Splatting without costly ray-tracing intersections. This physically guided design improves reconstruction quality and efficiency, requiring only about 10 minutes of training. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of our method.

authors.name: Yufei Han, Chu Zhou, Youwei Lyu, Qi Chen, Si Li, Boxin Shi, Yunpeng Jia, Heng Guo, Zhanyu Ma

papers.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework Combining Inductive and Deductive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Planning
papers.summary: Existing end-to-end autonomous driving models rely heavily on purely data-driven inductive reasoning. This "black-box" nature limits interpretability and makes safety-critical planning challenging in complex, long-tail scenarios. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose a novel neuro-symbolic trajectory planning (NS-Plan) framework, which integrates rigorous deductive reasoning into end-to-end neural networks. Specifically, our framework utilizes a Large Language Model (LLM) to dynamically extract scene rules and employs an Answer Set Programming (ASP) solver for deterministic logical arbitration, generating logically consistent and traceable discrete driving decisions. To bridge the gap between discrete symbols and continuous trajectories, we introduce a decision-conditioned decoding mechanism that transforms high-level logical decisions into learnable embedding vectors, simultaneously constraining the planning query and the physical initial velocity of a differentiable Kinematic Bicycle Model (KBM). By combining KBM-generated baseline trajectories with neural residual corrections, our approach uses the KBM to guide trajectory generation while keeping the decision-making process traceable. On the nuScenes benchmark, our method (NS-Plan) comprehensively outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reducing the average $L_2$ error by 18.3% (to 0.49 m), the collision rate by 22.2% (to 0.07%), and improving the trajectory prediction consistency (TPC) by 13% (to 0.47 m) compared to MomAD. More importantly, in the complex Turning-nuScenes subset, our method reduces the collision rate by 78.1% (to 0.07%) over the baseline.

authors.name: Hongyan Wei, Wael AbdAlmageed

papers.title: TRACE: Structure-Aware Character Encoding for Robust and Generalizable Document Watermarking
papers.summary: We propose TRACE, a structure-aware framework leveraging diffusion models for localized character encoding to embed data. Unlike existing methods that rely on edge features or pre-defined codebooks, TRACE exploits character structures that provide inherent resistance to noise interference due to their stability and unified representation across diverse characters. Our framework comprises three key components: (1) adaptive diffusion initialization that automatically identifies handle points, target points, and editing regions through specialized algorithms including movement probability estimator (MPE), target point estimation (TPE) and mask drawing model (MDM), (2) guided diffusion encoding for precise movement of selected point, and (3) masked region replacement with a specialized loss function to minimize feature alterations after the diffusion process. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate \name{}'s superior performance over state-of-the-art methods, achieving more than 5 dB improvement in PSNR and 5\% higher extraction accuracy following cross-media transmission. \name{} achieves broad generalizability across multiple languages and fonts, making it particularly suitable for practical document security applications.

authors.name: Jiale Meng, Jie Zhang, Runyi Hu, Zhe-Ming Lu, Tianwei Zhang, Yiming Li

papers.title: GATE-AD: Graph Attention Network Encoding For Few-Shot Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Few-Shot Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection (FS-IVAD) is a critical task in modern manufacturing, where automated product inspection systems must identify rare defects using only a handful of normal, defect-free training samples. Existing approaches typically model normality by assessing each patch largely through its individual appearance, e.g., through similarity to stored normal features, reconstruction from support samples, or distance from a learned normal representation. This paper introduces GATE-AD, whose key contribution is to instead model few-shot normality through local contextual relations: a patch is considered normal when it can be consistently recovered from its learned dependencies with its spatial neighbors. To realize this formulation, frozen self-supervised ViT patch tokens are organized on a spatial neighbor graph and processed by a Graph Attention Network (GAT), while representation alignment and a Scaled Cosine Error (SCE) objective enable reconstruction-based anomaly scoring. Node masking and attention dropout further regularize learning in the low-shot regime. On MVTec AD, VisA, and MPDD, GATE-AD achieves strong detection and localization performance across $1$- to $8$-shot settings, attaining the highest image-level AUROC in $10$ of $12$ settings and the highest image-level AP in $8$ of $12$ settings under a unified evaluation protocol, while also achieving the lowest inference latency among the compared methods. In order to facilitate reproducibility and further research, the source code of GATE-AD is available at https://github.com/gthpapadopoulos/GATE-AD.

authors.name: Aggelos Psiris, Yannis Panagakis, Maria Vakalopoulou, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos

papers.title: SIGMA: A Physics-Based Benchmark for Gas Chimney Understanding in Seismic Images
papers.summary: Seismic images reconstruct subsurface reflectivity from field recordings, guiding exploration and reservoir monitoring. Gas chimneys are vertical anomalies caused by subsurface fluid migration. Understanding these phenomena is crucial for assessing hydrocarbon potential and avoiding drilling hazards. However, accurate detection is challenging due to strong seismic attenuation and scattering. Traditional physics-based methods are computationally expensive and sensitive to model errors, while deep learning offers efficient alternatives, yet lacks labeled datasets. In this work, we introduce \textbf{SIGMA}, a new physics-based dataset for gas chimney understanding in seismic images, featuring (i) pixel-level gas-chimney mask for detection and (ii) paired degraded and ground-truth image for enhancement. We employed physics-based methods that cover a wide range of geological settings and data acquisition conditions. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that SIGMA serves as a challenging benchmark for gas chimney interpretation and benefits general seismic understanding.

authors.name: Bao Truong, Quang Nguyen, Baoru Huang, Jinpei Han, Van Nguyen, Ngan Le, Minh-Tan Pham, Doan Huy Hien, Anh Nguyen

papers.title: Video Object Segmentation under Aquatic Domain Shift: A Diagnostic Benchmark and Restoration Adapter
papers.summary: Underwater video object segmentation (VOS) requires temporally consistent dense segmentation in scenes where water acts as a participating optical medium. Wavelength-dependent attenuation, scattering, turbidity, and unstable illumination alter object appearance, weaken mask-level localization cues, and destabilize temporal association, yet existing VOS benchmarks provide limited support for diagnosing these aquatic factors. We introduce UW-VOS, a large-scale diagnostic benchmark with 1,431 video sequences, 307,267 mask annotations, 411 semantic categories, and 16 fine-grained attributes. UW-VOS supports both standard VOS evaluation and factorized analysis of aquatic appearance degradation, spatial localization ambiguity, and temporal identity discontinuity. We further propose the Aquatic Restoration Adapter (ARA), a physics-derived parameter-efficient module that transfers the inverse structure of underwater image formation into bottleneck feature space and can be instantiated in different VOS backbones. Experiments show that representative open-air VOS methods suffer an average 13-point $\mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F}$ drop on UW-VOS. ARA matches or surpasses full fine-tuning in both Transformer- and memory-based VOS backbones, and outperforms standard PEFT counterparts under a matched setting. These results establish UW-VOS as a diagnostic platform for underwater video perception and ARA as a compact feature-restoration module for aquatic domain adaptation. Project repository: https://github.com/hszh/UW-VOS.

authors.name: Hongshen Zhao, Jingkang Tai, Yuhang Wu, Wenkang Zhang, Xi Lan, Shangyan Wang, Tianyu Zhang, Wankou Yang

papers.title: Enhancing Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning via Hierarchical Feature Optimization
papers.summary: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a compelling paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning, allowing multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model by transmitting locally computed gradients to a central server without exposing their private data. Nonetheless, recent studies find that the gradients exchanged in the FL system are also vulnerable to privacy leakage, e.g., an attacker can invert shared gradients to reconstruct sensitive data by leveraging pre-trained generative adversarial networks (GAN) as prior knowledge. However, existing attacks simply perform gradient inversion in the latent space of the GAN model, which limits their expression ability and generalizability. To tackle these challenges, we propose \textbf{G}radient \textbf{I}nversion over \textbf{F}eature \textbf{D}omains (GIFD), which disassembles the GAN model and searches the hierarchical features of the intermediate layers. Instead of optimizing only over the initial latent code, we progressively change the optimized layer, from the initial latent space to intermediate layers closer to the output images. In addition, we design a regularizer to avoid unreal image generation by adding a small ${l_1}$ ball constraint to the searching range. We also extend GIFD to the out-of-distribution (OOD) setting, which weakens the assumption that the training sets of GANs and FL tasks obey the same data distribution. Furthermore, we consider the challenging OOD scenario of label inconsistency and propose a label mapping technique as an effective solution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve pixel-level reconstruction and outperform competitive baselines across a variety of FL scenarios.

authors.name: Hao Fang, Wenbo Yu, Bin Chen, Xuan Wang, Shu-Tao Xia, Qing Liao, Ke Xu

papers.title: CROWD: A global dataset of continuous urban dashcam driving
papers.summary: We introduce CROWD (City Road Observations With Dashcams), a manually curated dataset of ordinary, variable duration, temporally contiguous, unedited, front facing urban dashcam segments screened and segmented from publicly available YouTube videos. CROWD is designed to support cross-domain robustness and interaction analysis by prioritising routine driving and explicitly excluding crashes, crash aftermath, and other edited or incident-focused content. The release contains 107,407 segment records spanning 36,204.26 hours (82,484 unique uploads), covering 10,538 named inhabited places in 238 countries and territories across all six inhabited continents (Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America and Oceania), with segment level manual labels for time of day (day or night) and vehicle type. To lower the barrier for reproducible baseline analysis, we provide per-segment CSV files of automatic detections for all 80 MS-COCO classes produced with YOLOv11x, together with segment-local multi-object tracks generated with BoT-SORT; e.g. person, bicycle, motorcycle, car, bus, truck, traffic light, stop sign, etc. CROWD is distributed as video identifiers with segment boundaries and derived detection and tracking pseudo-labels, enabling reproducible research without redistributing the underlying videos. To support leakage-free evaluation, we also provide canonical splits grouped by source channel or by locality, and weights that balance the contribution of localities and countries.

authors.name: Md Shadab Alam, Olena Bazilinska, Pavlo Bazilinskyy

papers.title: Stitch4D: 4D Urban Reconstruction from Sparse Multi-Location Observations via Spatio-Temporal Interpolation
papers.summary: Dynamic urban environments are often captured by cameras placed at spatially separated locations with little or no view overlap. However, most existing 4D reconstruction methods assume densely overlapping views and struggle under sparse multi-location observations, producing unstable reconstructions in unobserved intermediate regions. To address this practical yet underexplored setting, we propose Stitch4D, a unified 4D reconstruction framework that compensates for missing spatial coverage in sparsely observed urban environments. Stitch4D synthesizes intermediate \emph{bridge views} between distant camera locations and jointly optimizes real and synthesized observations in a unified coordinate frame with inter-location consistency constraints. By recovering intermediate spatial coverage before optimization, Stitch4D mitigates geometric collapse and improves reconstruction stability in sparse regions. To evaluate this setting, we introduce Urban Sparse 4D (U-S4D), a controlled CARLA-based benchmark for free-viewpoint reconstruction under sparse multi-location configurations. Experiments on U-S4D show that Stitch4D consistently outperforms representative 4D reconstruction baselines in image-quality metrics. These results suggest that recovering intermediate spatial coverage is an effective strategy for stabilizing 4D reconstruction in sparse urban environments. The project page is provided in https://stitch4d-project-page.vercel.app/.

authors.name: Hina Kogure, Kei Katsumata, Taiki Miyanishi, Komei Sugiura

papers.title: Fundus-R1: Training a Fundus-Reading MLLM on Public Data
papers.summary: Fundus imaging such as CFP, OCT and SLO is crucial for the early detection of retinal anomalies and diseases. Fundus image understanding, due to its knowledge-intensive nature, poses a challenging vision-language task. An emerging approach to addressing the task is to post-train a generic multimodal large language model (MLLM), either by supervised finetuning (SFT) or by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), on a considerable amount of in-house samples paired with high-quality clinical reports. However, these valuable samples are not publicly accessible, which not only hinders reproducibility but also practically limits research to few players. In this paper, we make a novel attempt to train a reasoning-enhanced fundus-reading MLLM, termed Fundus-R1, using exclusively public datasets, wherein over 94% of the data are annotated with image-level labels only. Our technical contributions are two-fold. First, we propose a RAG-based method for composing image-specific, knowledge-aware reasoning traces. Such auto-generated traces link visual findings identified by a generic MLLM to the image labels in terms of ophthalmic knowledge. Second, we enhance RLVR with a process reward that encourages self-consistency of the generated reasoning trace in each rollout. Extensive experiments on three fundus-reading benchmarks, i.e., FunBench, Omni-Fundus and GMAI-Fundus, show that Fundus-R1 clearly outperforms multiple baselines, including its generic counterpart (Qwen2.5-VL) and a stronger edition post-trained without using the generated traces. This work paves the way for training powerful fundus-reading MLLMs with publicly available data.

authors.name: Yuchuan Deng, Qijie Wei, Kaiheng Qian, Jiazhen Liu, Bangxiang Lan, Qingwei Shen, Jianfeng Dong, Weihong Yu, Xirong Li

papers.title: Resource-Constrained UAV-Based Weed Detection for Site-Specific Management on Edge Devices
papers.summary: Weeds compete with crops for light, water, and nutrients, reducing yield and crop quality. Efficient weed detection is essential for site-specific weed management (SSWM). Although deep learning models have been deployed on UAV-based edge systems, a systematic understanding of how different model architectures perform under real-world resource constraints is still lacking. To address this gap, this study proposes a deployment-oriented framework for real-time UAV-based weed detection on resource-constrained edge platforms. The framework integrates UAV data acquisition, model development, and on-device inference, with a focus on balancing detection accuracy and computational efficiency. A diverse set of state-of-the-art object detection models is evaluated, including convolution-based YOLO models (v8-v12) and transformer-based RT-DETR models (v1-v2). Experiments on three edge devices (Jetson Orin Nano, Jetson AGX Xavier, and Jetson AGX Orin) demonstrate clear trade-offs between accuracy and inference latency across models and hardware configurations. Results show that high-capacity models achieve up to 86.9% mAP50 but suffer from high latency, limiting real-time deployment. In contrast, lightweight models achieve 66%-71% mAP50 with significantly lower latency, enabling real-time performance. Among all models, RT-DETRv2-R50-M achieves competitive accuracy (79% mAP50) with improved efficiency, while YOLOv10n provides the fastest inference speed. YOLOv11s and RT-DETRv2-R50-M offer the best balance between accuracy and speed, making them strong candidates for real-time UAV deployment.

authors.name: Linyuan Wang, Haibo Yao, Te-Ming Tseng, Kelvin Betitame, Xin Sun, Yanbo Huang, Dong Chen

papers.title: High-Speed Vision Improves Zero-Shot Semantic Understanding of Human Actions
papers.summary: Understanding human actions from visual observations is essential for human-robot interaction, particularly when semantic interpretation of unfamiliar or hard-to-annotate actions is required.
