authors.name: Xiaoxing Hu, Wenxi Yao, Chaoyuan Shi, Ziqi Ye, Xiaorong Guo, Peixuan Li, Zhuoran Sun, Ziyang Gong, Peiyuan Zhang, Mingxin Liu, Shuran Ma, Hongbo Liu, Xiaomin Yu, Yu Tian, Wentao Wang, Zhenjie Yang, Jian Hu, Yunhang Shen, Haoyu Cao, Xue Yang

papers.title: FiLM-CAM: Keyed Feature Modulation for Conditional-Access Watermarking
papers.summary: We propose FiLM-CAM; a conditional-access image watermarking approach that enforces authorized encoding, decoding, and removal through keyed feature modulation. A secret key conditions a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) mechanism that transforms the internal representation of the watermark signal before embedding, thereby coupling the payload to the key at the feature, rather than pixel level. The same key must be presented to condition the decoder to correctly recover the payload embedded in an image. To enforce conditional access, we train the system to maximize the performance gap between authorized and unauthorized use, ensuring reliable extraction under the correct key while inducing failure under incorrect keys. In addition, we design our encoder to estimate the watermark residual invariant to the presence of pre-existing watermarks. This design enables conditional watermark removal via simple re-encoding and subtraction of the residual using iterative refinement, contingent on knowledge of the secret key. We evaluate FiLM-CAM across multiple watermarking encoder-decoder backbones, demonstrating that keyed feature modulation serves as an effective, architecture-agnostic conditional access module (CAM) for image watermarking.

authors.name: Yash Kulthe, Shruti Agarwal, Vishal Asnani, Andrew Gilbert, John Collomosse

papers.title: Lightweight Frame Compensation for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation under Frame Skipping
papers.summary: Real-time polyp segmentation in computer-assisted colonoscopy is hampered by the difficulty of deploying high-accuracy models under strict latency budgets. Frame skipping, which performs inference every K frames and reuses or interpolates the rest, improves throughput but introduces motion blur and lesion misalignment that degrade temporal consistency. To close this gap, we propose the Lightweight Frame Compensator (LFC), a 77K-parameter plug-and-play module inserted before a frozen segmentation backbone. Operating on a three-frame window, LFC fuses consecutive frames via spatio-temporal attention into a single compensated frame, and is trained only on pseudo-labels generated by a differently seeded model, without any expert annotation. Experiments on three polyp video benchmarks show that LFC recovers most of the accuracy degraded by direct frame skipping and, in several settings, reaches the accuracy of frame-by-frame inference, while retaining a 2.05X--2.55X throughput gain. We further evaluate the temporal stability of three backbones spanning CNN, pyramid Transformer, and global-attention Transformer architectures, revealing a spectrum of sensitivity to frame skipping that arises from how locally or globally each architecture aggregates misaligned input. The compensation gain of LFC follows this spectrum: it is largest for high-capacity Transformer backbones, which achieve the best static accuracy but suffer the most under skip-frame inference. LFC thus offers a lightweight, pluggable, and deployment-friendly route to real-time polyp segmentation.

authors.name: Weihao Gao

papers.title: Ask About the Right Moment: Training-Free Object Identity Reasoning for Video-Language Models
papers.summary: Many questions about a video concern one physical object. Where does the ball end up after the cups are shuffled? Which card is the queen? How often was the mug covered? Open video-language models (Video-LMs) recognise such objects in single frames but do not keep them apart over time. On shuffled shell games, open models from eight families stay near chance, and so do published tool agents. We separate semantic identity binding from temporal identity maintenance. Binding should happen at a moment when the evidence for the object is visible, and maintenance should be left to a tracker. Track, Then Bind implements this principle without training. A promptable video tracker follows every candidate object and draws it with a track number. A frozen vision-language model (VLM) answers one question about the identifying evidence, which binds the target to a track. The answer is then derived from a text description of the tracks. With Qwen3-VL-32B, the agent solves both VET-Bench tasks, where a fine-tuned trajectory model reaches 92% and 90%. On real cup games from the Perception Test, it raises accuracy from 35.5% to 52.3%. Without retuning, the same configuration also solves VET-Bench with Gemma 4 and GPT-5.5. Its track-derived visibility timelines add 8.8-17.9 points on TOC-Bench for open models. GPT-6.1 already answers 92.5% of the real cup games directly but 71.0% through our pipeline, while our timelines still raise its TOC-Bench accuracy from 52.5% to 57.7%. The benefit of external tracking thus depends on the underlying model and the task.

authors.name: Di Yang, Xiaochang Li, Muyang Liu, Yufei Wang, Yanhai Xiong

papers.title: TrackTok: Object-Centric Video Tokenization with Semantically Persistent Tokens
papers.summary: We introduce TrackTok, an efficient video tokenization framework that produces object-centric tokens, i.e., tokens that consistently encode the same semantic object across time, even as it moves, deforms, or undergoes partial occlusion. Conventional patch-based or existing holistic tokenizers produce token identities often tied to fixed image locations. In contrast, our approach learns temporally persistent object-centric representations that bind visual features across frames into stable semantic units. This enables substantially more compact, continuous latent video representations, reducing the number of tokens required for downstream generative modeling with state-of-the-art flow models, while preserving the semantic structure needed for high-quality synthesis. Our tokenizer offers a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off. TrackTok achieves comparable class-conditional generative FVD on UCF-101 dataset at 8 times fewer latent tokens and better latency, and outperforms existing 1D tokenization baselines on frame prediction task on Kinetics-600 across low token budgets. These results suggest that object-aligned and temporally persistent tokenization is a promising direction for scalable video generation, where reducing latent token counts is critical for efficient modeling. Our code for this work is available at https://github.com/phamleyennhi/tracktok.

authors.name: Nhi Pham, Christopher Wewer, Bernt Schiele, Jonas Fischer, Jan Eric Lenssen

papers.title: Understanding and Repairing Cooperative Perception under Adverse Weather
papers.summary: A cooperative detector can lose a correct vehicle detection when surrounding LiDAR measurements change, even if the returns on the vehicle remain unchanged. We study this failure as Weather-Induced Context Interference. On our CoInfra development set, controlled removal outside annotated object boxes turns 22.1% of V2X-ViT's previously correct detections into misses. Restoring network features around the objects to their values before removal recovers 98.6% of these misses. The same restoration in each of three equally sized regions excluding the objects recovers none. Candidate analysis finds accurate boxes that are not selected, while other targets lack well-localized candidates. With paired reference features unavailable at inference, Adverse-Weather Cooperative Repair (AWCR) repairs candidates from current observations. A lightweight Local Correction head generates bounded alternatives, and Quality Selection ranks them alongside original boxes with a correction weight. In V2X-R simulation, AWCR also filters peer returns before detection using Point Classifier trained on generated-point labels. Candidate repair improves mean car BEV AP@0.7 by 4.22 points across three fits on natural adverse-weather CoInfra development inputs and vehicle AP@0.7 by 5.00 points on a rain-affected public recording. It also improves released HEAL, FadeLead, and V2X-DGW detectors with their pretrained weights fixed. On the full V2X-Radar-C validation benchmark, HEAL with AWCR achieves state-of-the-art LiDAR-only cooperative detection performance of 68.22 vehicle BEV AP@0.7.

authors.name: Mengxu Ma (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Linshan Yan (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Kailong Zhang (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Ruiyang Guo (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Dagang Shen (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Yichen Fan (Northwestern Polytechnical University), Hongping Gan (Northwestern Polytechnical University)

papers.title: GIFT: Representation Geometry Matters for Single-Domain Generalized Object Detection
papers.summary: Single-Domain Generalized Object Detection (S-DGOD) aims to generalize from a single source domain to unseen domains under distribution shifts. Existing efforts mainly focus on simulating unseen domains or suppressing domain-specific factors. However, they largely overlook the intrinsic generalization capability embedded in Vision Foundation Models (VFMs). In this work, we show that unconstrained fine-tuning disrupts the geometric structure of pre-trained representations, which encodes domain-invariant semantics. Motivated by this, we propose Geometric-Invariance Fine-Tuning (GIFT), a geometric-aware fine-tuning method for VFMs. Specifically, we introduce a series of learnable Householder reflections to the pre-trained weights to encourage geometry-consistent adaptation under domain shift. In addition, we propose a lightweight channel-wise scaling to facilitate effective task-specific adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GIFT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches on two S-DGOD benchmarks. Notably, by introducing fewer than 1% additional trainable parameters into the frozen backbone, the proposed method achieves improvements of +7.9% and +2.9% in mPC over the previous SOTA on the Cityscapes-C and Diverse Weather Dataset, respectively. This finding highlights that preserving representation geometry is crucial for robust cross-domain generalization, establishing GIFT as a principled and efficient solution to domain shift.

authors.name: Yin Zhang, Yaoyue Zheng, Yongqiang Zhang, Bogdan Raducanu, Dan Liu

papers.title: MVRCap: Towards Comprehensive Video Captioning via Hierarchical Multi-Dimensional Verifiable Rewards
papers.summary: Despite significant progress, current models struggle to generate comprehensive video captions, constrained primarily by coarse-grained supervision, which often fails to capture spatial-temporal dynamics and the underlying logical intent. To address this issue, we introduce MVRCap, a novel framework that reformulates video captioning as a reinforcement learning task steered by structured verification. Central to our approach is a Fine-Grained Verifiable Reward mechanism, serving as dense supervision to enforce rigorous visual-semantic alignment. Specifically, we construct this reward system anchored by three complementary pillars: a Hierarchical Concept Coverage Reward utilizing our newly constructed MVRCap-QA dataset to ensure multi-dimensional completeness and semantic depth, a Factuality Verification Reward to enhance factual consistency, and a Conciseness Constraint to maximize semantic density. Furthermore, we curate the high-quality MVRCap-SFT dataset, providing structured annotations across six key dimensions, to serve as a robust foundational initialization for the RL policy in this training pipeline. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MVRCap achieves state-of-the-art performance on authoritative benchmarks including VDC, CAPability, and VC4VG.

authors.name: Weihuang Lin, Xianing Chen, Zhibin Wang, Congzhi Zhang, Yiwei Ma, Jiayi Ji, Miao Chen, Jun Song, YuCheng, Bo Zheng, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rongrong Ji

papers.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features constrains all directions equally, providing broad coverage without semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance. We therefore propose Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG), which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local variations in input embeddings. TRAG constructs anchor-level constraints from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregates them using pre-trained image--anchor relevance, yielding an image-adaptive constraint. Extensive experiments across architectures and tasks demonstrate state-of-the-art clean and robust performance. Further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image--text relationships.

authors.name: Yubo Cui, Xianchao Guan, Zheng Zhang

papers.title: A Unified Benchmark for Aerial-Enhanced Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Aerial Dataset
papers.summary: Aerial imagery provides complementary spatial context for autonomous driving by exposing road structure beyond the immediate perception range of onboard sensors. Yet map construction from aerial imagery, aerial-assisted online HD mapping, and cross-view localization are typically studied on separate data and benchmarks. We introduce KITScenes Aerial, an extension of the KITScenes Multimodal dataset that augments synchronized onboard sensor data, vehicle poses, and rich Lanelet2 map annotations with spatially associated aerial imagery and higher-resolution neural representations, providing a common basis for a variety of research tasks. Our mapping evaluation focuses on all 53 KITScenes map classes across different model designs, spatial ranges, and aerial resolutions, while retaining compatibility with the widely used three-class setting. Representative baselines show that aerial context is particularly beneficial for fine-grained and extended-range mapping, more than doubling 53-class mAP at the larger mapping extent. Higher-resolution aerial imagery yields a further 4.3 mAP (+24 %) improvement, with gains extending to challenging map elements such as traffic lights. We additionally evaluate cross-view localization under geographically disjoint conditions, where an adapted fine-grained feature-matching baseline achieves a mean translation error of 5.13 m. KITScenes Aerial thus enables unified study of aerial and ground-level information across complementary mapping and localization tasks. Project page: https://kitscenes.com/aerial

authors.name: Daniel Lengerer, Richard Schwarzkopf, Jonas Merkert, Fabian Immel, Rupert Polley, Frank Bieder, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, J. Marius Z\"ollner, Klaus Bogenberger, Christoph Stiller, Carsten Markgraf

papers.title: SketchDirector: Complex Scene Sketching via Agentic Layout Reasoning and Detail Refinement
papers.summary: Existing sketch generation methods often rely on image guidance and are largely limited to individual objects or simplified scenes, leaving text-guided complex scene sketching underexplored. We present SketchDirector, an agentic framework that mimics the human sketching workflow for automatic multi-concept scene sketching. Given a scene-level text prompt, SketchDirector first employs a large language model~(LLM) to decompose the scene into multiple draft assets, where each is represented by a set of B\'ezier curves. Then, an agentic reasoning loop iteratively plans and executes their spatial arrangement, guided by self-evolving memory. Finally, a detail refinement module leverages diffusion priors to enhance sketch quality while preserving geometric structure. To support future research and applications in multi-concept scene sketch generation, we further introduce the MCSketch8K dataset, comprising editable vector assets, compositional layouts, and object-level manipulation annotations. Extensive experiments show that SketchDirector outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in semantic and compositional quality while effectively preserving overall contour organization during refinement.

authors.name: Yiqi Liang, Xiaodong Cun

papers.title: OCRia-1 Technical Report
papers.summary: We introduce OCRia-1, a 4B vision-language model (VLM) for document parsing that excels at preserving table structure, extracting chart data and retaining text formatting. OCRia-1 handles content that has traditionally been challenging in document parsing: merged cells and spanning headers, tables with thousands of cells, chart data, and meaningful text formatting such as bold, italics, subscripts and superscripts, preserving details needed for business-critical document analysis. At the time of this report, it achieves the highest scores on tables, charts and text formatting among the systems evaluated, including a 35B model and Mistral OCR 4.1. Its mean ParseBench score over the four dimensions we evaluate is 0.87, against 0.75 for the next-best system. We emphasize data quality and reward design in training OCRia-1. Synthetic pages provide exact ground truth for long tables and rich formatting, while real pages are transcribed using a pipeline grounded in the PDF text layer. We attribute OCRia-1's performance primarily to careful data curation that prioritizes quality and diversity over quantity. Dimension-specific rewards evaluate table reconstruction, chart-data extraction and text-formatting fidelity. We train the model on the curated data using supervised fine-tuning (SFT), then refine it through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). To our knowledge, OCRia-1 is the fastest published document-parsing VLM in its class, decoding at about 4,700 tokens per second with a single request on one B200 GPU, about nine times faster than the base model on stock vLLM. This is achieved through a block-diffusion speculator, quantization and custom kernels.

authors.name: Aman Rangapur, Antonio Jimeno Yepes, Daniel Bustamante, Nutchapol Dendumrongsup, Sebasti\'an G. Acosta, Pierre-Lo\"ic Doulcet, Simon Suo

papers.title: Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending for Training-Free Style Personalization
papers.summary: Reference-based style personalization should reproduce the appearance of a style reference while preserving the subject specified by a content prompt. In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can also carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage. We propose Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending (CoPFB), a training-free method that estimates a low-rank content basis from a clean generation branch and removes the content-aligned component of the style residual. CoPFB applies rank-one blending at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. On 1,900 combinations of Parti content prompts and FineStyle reference images, CoPFB improves text alignment from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393 over PFB+SAC, while style similarity decreases from 0.590 to 0.577. CoPFB requires no fine-tuning or learnable parameters.

authors.name: Le-Hoang Bui, Hoang-Nguyen Cao, Trung-Nghia Le, Minh-Triet Tran, Dinh-Khoi Vo

papers.title: The DynaCell Evaluation Suite for Dynamic 3D Virtual Staining of Live Cells
papers.summary: Understanding how cells respond to perturbations over time is central to cell biology and drug discovery. Live-cell imaging captures the dynamics of perturbation-induced phenotypes in individual cells. While fluorescence imaging can visualize specific molecular phenotypes, labeling and repeated illumination often affect cell health. Virtual staining offers an alternative by predicting these fluorescence images from images acquired without fluorescent labels. Although many virtual staining models have been developed, their performance on volumetric time-lapse data remains poorly characterized. We address this gap with an evaluation suite for 3D time-lapse virtual staining of live cells. The suite combines paired 3D time-lapse images acquired with and without fluorescent labels, a set of baseline models, and three metric tiers measuring pixel-level fidelity, organelle segmentation performance, and single-cell phenotype similarity. Using this evaluation suite, we study metric and model behavior across 3 cell types, 2 microscopes, 4 organelles, and 3 perturbation states. We find that regression baselines better predict the spatial localization of target organelles, whereas the generative baseline better captures the distribution of phenotypes across cells. These differences expose trade-offs between structural and phenotypic fidelity that are obscured by single-metric evaluation and suggest how virtual staining models can be developed for diverse downstream tasks such as localization, segmentation, tracking, and phenotypic profiling. We release the curated datasets, baseline checkpoints, and evaluation code as part of DynaCell, a broader framework for image-based profiling of cell-state dynamics.

authors.name: Alexandr A. Kalinin, Dihan Zheng, Taylla Milena Theodoro, Ivan Ivanov, Eduardo Hirata-Miyasaki, See-Chi Lee, Aofei Liu, Sricharan Reddy Varra, Talon Chandler, Soorya Pradeep, Chad Liu, Manuel D. Leonetti, Carolina Arias, Bo Huang, Shalin B. Mehta

papers.title: Discovering Semantic Granularity in Images through Clustering of Pretrained Visual Representations
papers.summary: Semantic granularity, which refers to the levels at which visual representations organize image content into meaningful entities, is fundamental to image understanding. However, whether pretrained visual representations inherently encode semantic structures at multiple granularities remains poorly understood. This paper presents a representation-driven approach for discovering semantically meaningful image regions at different granularities through clustering of pretrained visual representations without task-specific training. Specifically, we concatenate feature maps from appropriately deep layers of a pretrained visual model and apply a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based projection to derive a pixel-wise principal representation map (PRM) tensor. The resulting PRM tensor captures latent semantic structures embedded in pretrained visual representations, making them accessible for subsequent semantic clustering. We then introduce the semantic continuity ratio (SCR) and analyze the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of SCR profiles to assess the suitability of PRM tensors for semantic granularity discovery. Our results indicate that PRM tensors exhibiting a higher proportion of relatively high SNR values over an initial range of cluster numbers tend to yield more semantically meaningful regions across multiple granularities. Furthermore, once a suitable PRM tensor is identified through SNR-profile analysis, pixel-wise hierarchical clustering enables the level of semantic granularity to be controlled by varying the number of clusters. We evaluate the proposed approach on the COCO-2017 and VOC-2012 validation datasets using Hungarian-matched intersection over union (HIoU). The results suggest competitive segmentation performance among the compared methods, supporting the feasibility of the proposed approach.

authors.name: Ying Dai

papers.title: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation
papers.summary: Sign language generation (SLG) maps written sentences into signing motion while preserving both lexical content and fine-grained articulation. This requires a model to decide what signs should be expressed and to realize them through precise handshape, trajectory, facial expression and body coordination. Existing pose-based systems and reconstruction-only motion tokenizers often entangle these two decisions, leaving the generator without an explicit text-aligned intermediate target for what to sign before refining how to sign it. To address this issue, we introduce Semantic Residual Vector Quantization (SRVQ), a framework for SLG that frames generation as a two-level process moving from semantics to kinematics. The newly introduced SRV Quantizer learns a hierarchy in which the first residual level encodes sign content and subsequent levels refine pose, handshape, trajectory, and body coordination, all within a single quantizer and without separate semantic representations or external planning stages. Through word-aware conditioning for hierarchical code generation, a masked semantic generator predicts semantic codes and a kinematic generator completes the residual codes for full SMPL-X motion synthesis. We evaluate using retrieval and FID in a shared text-motion embedding space, alongside standard geometric metrics. On CSL-Daily and Phoenix-2014T, SRVQ achieves R@1 of 82.3 and 70.3, outperforming the previous SOTA by 30 and 46 points, respectively.

authors.name: Chang Liu, Ke Han, Niccol\`o Biondi, Gloria Isotton, Elisa Ricci, Davide Talon, Nicu Sebe

papers.title: From Pixels to Actions--Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.summary: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a flow-matching action expert to draw from instruction-conditioned visual representations at different depths. This simple change reveals a consistent pattern. Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons; full fine-tuning reduces but does not erase the gap, and additional scale alone cannot recover it. More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control. Together, these results suggest that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.

authors.name: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu, Siyuan Hu, Ziqi Huang, Tianqi Liu, Mingze Sun, Ziyi Wang, Zhongang Cai, Hanming Deng, Quan Wang, Lei Yang, Lewei Lu, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Dahua Lin, Ziwei Liu

papers.title: ArtCrafter: Feed-Forward Generation of Articulated 3D Object with Analytic Joint Derivation
papers.summary: Articulated 3D assets are essential for robotic simulation and training, yet their generation from casual images poses a key challenge: recovering part geometry and kinematics that remain mutually consistent. We present ArtCrafter, a novel feed-forward generative model for controllable generation of articulated 3D objects from a pair of images, one depicting the object in the rest state and the other in the open state. At the core of ArtCrafter is a DiT-based generative model that jointly produces part-level meshes for both articulation states in a single forward pass. Inspired by Slot Attention, its denoising process operates on a $1+2N$ slot layout comprising one shared base slot and $N$ paired rest/open slots, encouraging each pair to bind to the same kinematic part. To ensure geometrically consistent and disjoint part generation, we introduce Triplet Attention to enforce cross-state geometric consistency between paired rest/open slots anchored through the shared base slot, and a repulsion loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rep}}$ on decoded part point clouds to prevent inter-part penetration throughout denoising. Given the resulting paired meshes, URDF joint parameters---type, axis, origin, and range---are derived analytically from the rigid transformation between each rest/open pair, providing an interpretable alternative to learned joint-parameter regression. Extensive experiments on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets demonstrate that ArtCrafter outperforms existing method under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision, while remaining competitive with methods operating under different input settings and paradigms.

authors.name: Minh Canh Tu, Quang-Binh Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen

papers.title: FATE: Fault-Aware Transfer Error for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: We study unsupervised industrial anomaly detection in the single-class setting, where a detector learns only from normal images of one product category. Reconstruction-based detectors model normal features from a frozen encoder, but their target layers are usually chosen by architectural convention. We instead ask what information one block can pass to another. Treating depth as a sequence of discrete transitions, we train eight directed, token-wise predictors from block 1 and blocks 21-23 to blocks 7 and 14. Adjacent-layer cosine similarity drops at four repeatable fault lines in DINOv2 ViT-L, separating stable depth segments. The deepest blocks retain semantic context but lose local detail, so the residual of a source-to-sensitive prediction measures information that cannot be transported. The fault structure constrains the source and target roles, and the same rule transfers to ViT-B and RADIO-B. A bounded foreground prior, calibrated only on normal training images, suppresses background residuals while retaining a positive floor for evidence outside the estimated foreground. With the same eight channels and a common training-only calibration procedure in every single-category model, category-averaged image AUROC reaches 99.75 on MVTec-AD, 99.42 on VisA and 94.27 on Real-IAD; object-level AUROC on Real-IAD is 96.26. For the 448x448 runs, category-averaged P-AUROC/P-AUPRO on a common 256x256 evaluation grid is 98.46/95.97 on MVTec-AD, 99.21/96.12 on VisA and 99.26/96.59 on Real-IAD.

authors.name: Tao Wang

papers.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
papers.summary: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision. To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SplatAnything

authors.name: Hao Yu, Zhenwei Wang, Yongzhen Hu, Yuning Gong, Junta Wu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Tengfei Wang, Chunchao Guo, Sida Peng

papers.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
papers.summary: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation for egocentric manipulation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video learning, making metric motion usable as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target. Cross-stream action-video coupling establishes close correspondence between metric motion and visual dynamics through lightweight adaptation while preserving the pretrained visual prior. Together, these designs establish a generalist framework spanning six action-video tasks. With only narrow-domain data, EgoGeneralist generalizes to diverse unseen scenes and interactions with effective action control and visual quality, bridging pretrained visual knowledge and metric 3D human motion.

authors.name: Yanlin Jin, Bowen Yang, Cheng Zhang, Yifan Yang, Zhe Li, Jianfei Cai, Kai Zhu

papers.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
papers.summary: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

authors.name: Zheng Wang, Zhengwei Gong, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang

papers.title: Look Closer, Align Better: Explicit Visual Attributes for Robust EEG-to-Image Decoding
papers.summary: EEG-to-image retrieval commonly aligns neural responses with representations from pretrained vision encoders. However, these representations may underrepresent fine-grained visual details needed to distinguish semantically similar images. To address this limitation, we first investigate the EEG decodability and complementary predictive value of explicit visual attributes, identifying visual cues that capture EEG-relevant information beyond pretrained representations. Building on these findings, we propose AttrEcho, a framework that enriches pretrained visual representations with complementary, spatially aligned visual attributes. Specifically, Region-Aligned Visual Attribute Fusion (RAVF) integrates EEG-relevant local visual attributes with spatially corresponding pretrained features through a learnable signed residual gate. We further employ Feature Token Aggregation (FTA), which learns dimension-specific weights across regions to aggregate refined visual features for contrastive alignment with EEG representations. Experiments on THINGS-EEG demonstrate that AttrEcho achieves 94.8% Top-1 and 99.7% Top-5 accuracy in intra-subject 200-way retrieval, while maintaining 82.1% Top-1 accuracy as the gallery expands to 1,600 images with same-concept distractors. AttrEcho also achieves 25.3% Top-1 and 53.0% Top-5 accuracy in inter-subject retrieval. These results highlight the importance of EEG-relevant visual attributes and spatially aligned fusion for fine-grained EEG-to-image retrieval.

authors.name: Ke Xiao, Banghua Yang, Wenbin Guo, Fenqi Rong

papers.title: Autonomous Apple Fruitlet Sizing and Growth Rate Tracking using Computer Vision
papers.summary: In this paper, we present a computer vision-based approach to measure the sizes and growth rates of apple fruitlets. Measuring the growth rates of apple fruitlets is important because it allows apple growers to determine when to apply chemical thinners to their crops in order to optimize yield. The current practice of obtaining growth rates involves using calipers to record sizes of fruitlets across multiple days. Due to the number of fruitlets needed to be sized, this method is laborious, time-consuming, and prone to human error. With images collected by a hand-held stereo camera, our system, segments, clusters, and fits ellipses to fruitlets to measure their diameters. The growth rates are then calculated by temporally associating clustered fruitlets across days. We provide quantitative results on data collected in an apple orchard, and demonstrate that our system is able to predict abscise rates within 3.5% of the current method with a 6 times improvement in speed, while requiring significantly less manual effort. Moreover, we provide results on images captured by a robotic system in the field, and discuss the next steps required to make the process fully autonomous.

authors.name: Harry Freeman, Mohamad Qadri, Abhisesh Silwal, Paul O'Connor, Zachary Rubinstein, Daniel Cooley, George Kantor

papers.title: U-WNO:U-Net-enhanced Wavelet Neural Operator for fetal head segmentation
papers.summary: This article describes the development of a novel U-Net-enhanced Wavelet Neural Operator (U-WNO),which combines wavelet decomposition, operator learning, and an encoder-decoder mechanism. This approach harnesses the superiority of the wavelets in time frequency localization of the functions, and the combine down-sampling and up-sampling operations to generate the segmentation map to enable accurate tracking of patterns in spatial domain and effective learning of the functional mappings to perform regional segmentation. By bridging the gap between theoretical advancements and practical applications, the U-WNO holds potential for significant impact in multiple science and industrial fields, facilitating more accurate decision-making and improved operational efficiencies. The operator is demonstrated for different pregnancy trimesters, utilizing two-dimensional ultrasound images.

authors.name: Pranava Seth, Deepak Mishra, Veena Iyer

papers.title: JND-Guided Light-Weight Neural Pre-Filter for Perceptual Image Coding
papers.summary: Just Noticeable Distortion (JND)-guided pre-filter is a promising technique for improving the perceptual compression efficiency of image coding. However, existing methods are often computationally expensive, and the field lacks standardized benchmarks for fair comparison. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a twofold contribution. First, we develop and open-source FJNDF-Pytorch, a unified benchmark for frequency-domain JND-Guided pre-filters. Second, leveraging this platform, we propose a complete learning framework for a novel, lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art compression efficiency, consistently outperforming competitors across multiple datasets and encoders. In terms of computational cost, our model is exceptionally lightweight, requiring only 7.15 GFLOPs to process a 1080p image, which is merely 14.1% of the cost of recent lightweight network. Our work presents a robust, state-of-the-art solution that excels in both performance and efficiency, supported by a reproducible research platform. The open-source implementation is available at https://github.com/viplab-fudan/FJNDF-Pytorch.

authors.name: Yangyang Wu, Chenlong He, Yuanheng Chen, Yibo Fan

papers.title: Visual Affect Analysis: Predicting Emotions of Image Viewers with Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for large-scale affect inference from images, but their alignment with human affective ratings remains unclear. We benchmarked 16 proprietary and open-source VLMs on three validated affective image datasets: the International Affective Picture System, the Nencki Affective Picture System, and the Library of AI-Generated Affective Images. In a zero-shot setting, models performed two tasks: (i) top-emotion classification and (ii) prediction of human ratings on 1--7/9 Likert scales for discrete emotions and affective dimensions. We also evaluated rater-conditioned prompting on the LAI-GAI dataset using de-identified participant metadata. Best models showed strong discrete emotion classification (60%--80% on six-emotion tasks; 60%--75% on a 12-category task), with anger and surprise predicted least accurately. For continuous ratings, models aligned moderately to strongly with human judgments ($r > 0.75$) but showed consistent biases, especially weaker performance on arousal and overestimation of response intensity. Rater-conditioned prompting had only small, inconsistent effects. Overall, VLMs captured broad affective patterns but sometimes lacked the nuance, although newer model generations performed better.

authors.name: Filip Nowicki, Hubert Marciniak, Jakub {\L}\k{a}czkowski, Bartosz Wilczek, Krzysztof Jassem, Tomasz G\'orecki, Vimala Balakrishnan, Desmond C. Ong, Maciej Behnke

papers.title: Triple-Phase Sequential Fusion Network with Contrast Enhancement Kinetics for Hepatobiliary-Phase Liver MRI Synthesis
papers.summary: Gadoxetate disodium-enhanced MRI is essential for the detection and characterization of hepatocellular carcinoma. However, acquisition of the hepatobiliary phase (HBP) requires a prolonged post-contrast delay, which reduces workflow efficiency and increases the risk of motion artifacts. In this study, we propose a Triple-Phase Sequential Fusion Network (TriPF-Net) with contrast enhancement kinetics to synthesize HBP images by leveraging the sequential information from pre-HBP sequences: while T1-weighted imaging serves as the indispensable baseline, the model adaptively integrates arterial-phase (AP) and venous-phase (VP) features when available. By modeling the tissue-specific contrast uptake and excretion dynamics across these three phases, TriPF-Net ensures robust HBP synthesis even under the stochastic absence of one or both dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. In addition, clinical variables, including age, sex, total bilirubin, and albumin, are incorporated to enhance physiological consistency. Compared with conventional methods, TriPF-Net achieved superior performance on datasets from two centers. On the first-center dataset, the model achieved an MAE of 10.65, a PSNR of 23.27, and an SSIM of 0.76. On the second-center dataset, the model was trained independently, and the corresponding values were 12.41, 23.11, and 0.78, respectively. Moreover, lesion-level evaluation showed that the synthesized images achieved contrast comparable to that of real HBP images, with no significant difference in CNR (P = 0.2699). Blinded evaluations confirmed synthesized images were visually comparable to real HBP, with TriPF-Net remaining robust to missing input phases. This flexible solution enhances clinical workflow and lesion depiction, and may also serve as an automated quality control reference to flag real HBP acquisitions that warrant closer inspection.

authors.name: Qiuli Wang, Xinhuan Sun, Fengxi Chen, Yongxu Liu, Jie Cheng, Lin Chen, Jiafei Chen, Siwei Miao, Xingpeng Zhang, Yue Zhang, Xiaoming Li, Wei Chen

papers.title: Decoupling Ego-Motion from Target Dynamics via Dual-Interval Motion Cues for UAV Detection
papers.summary: Object detection from Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is challenged by severe ego-motion, camera jitter, and large scale variations. While modern detectors perform well on static images, their direct application to UAV video often fails, particularly for small objects in dynamic scenes. Existing motion-based methods often rely on computationally expensive optical flow. We propose a vision-only motion-guided detection framework that decouples target motion from camera-induced disturbances. Homography-based Global Motion Compensation (GMC) first aligns adjacent frames. We then introduce a Dual-Interval Motion Extraction strategy that captures both short-term and long-term motion cues. To integrate these cues, a lightweight Dual-Interval Motion Injection (DIMI) module enhances feature representations within a Feature Pyramid Network. Experiments on the VisDrone-VID dataset demonstrate consistent improvements over the YOLOv8n baseline under severe ego-motion. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the dual-interval design and DIMI.

authors.name: Liuyang Wang, Feitian Zhang

papers.title: RCT-AD: Reliability-Aware Context and Temporal BEV Reasoning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Reliable temporal representation learning is important for end-to-end autonomous driving, particularly when visual observations are degraded by occlusion, motion blur, illumination variation, and sensor noise. Existing Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) approaches provide a unified representation for perception and planning; however, temporal features are commonly aggregated across frames without explicitly accounting for the reliability of individual observations. Consequently, low-quality or inconsistent features may propagate through temporal representations and degrade downstream perception, prediction, and planning. To address this problem, we propose RCT-AD, a Reliability-Aware Context and Temporal BEV Reasoning framework for end-to-end autonomous driving that explicitly models feature reliability and temporal consistency within a shared BEV representation. RCT-AD introduces a Reliable Context Awareness (RCA) module that estimates frame-level reliability using spatial, semantic, temporal, and visual-quality cues, and selectively preserves trustworthy information through a reliability-guided temporal memory mechanism. When the current observation is unreliable, historical high-reliability features are aligned and integrated to construct a more stable temporal BEV representation. A Temporal Trajectory Planner models long-term temporal dependencies and multi-agent interactions, while semantic segmentation and motion-guided detection provide complementary supervision for refining the shared BEV representation. Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark demonstrate consistent improvements across perception, motion prediction, and trajectory planning. RCT-AD achieves 61.5 NDS, 52.9 mAP, and 52.3 mIoU while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of reliability-aware temporal BEV reasoning for unified perception, prediction, and planning.

authors.name: Argho Dey, Yunfei Yin, Swachha Ray, Md Minhazul Islam, Zheng Yuan, Sijing Xiong, Hongyu Liu, Zhiqiu Huang

papers.title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training
papers.summary: We present DreamTrue, a multi-view, cross-embodiment robot world model for action-faithful and physically plausible video prediction. Training such a model on existing robot datasets faces two obstacles: imprecise calibration can impair action following, while limited coverage of unsuccessful interactions can bias predictions toward successful outcomes. To improve action following across embodiments, we render action trajectories into image-space conditions and introduce offline geometric calibration to align these conditions with the target videos. To broaden interaction coverage, we introduce counterfactual post-training, modifying recorded action trajectories and generating future videos under a wider range of actions and contact configurations. To provide feedback on these predictions without paired ground-truth futures, we construct a human-annotated video dataset covering robot, object, and interaction defects and use it to train an embodied video reward model. Its scores guide reinforcement-learning post-training toward more physically plausible interaction outcomes. On AgiBot, DreamTrue attains state-of-the-art action following, while reducing the human-assessed interaction defect rate from from 48.12% to 6.25%. Notably, our model ranks first in the world model track of the AgiBot World Challenge 2026. The project page can be found at https://brave-eai.github.io/DreamTrue.

authors.name: Junyan Li, Ruizhi Li, Yu Liu, Xiangshuo Liu, Mingchao Sun, Hongyu Pan, Mu Xu, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

papers.title: Persistent A-homotopy of Complex Networks
papers.summary: We study how loop classes in a network change when cycles up to a prescribed length are declared contractible. The resulting sequence of quotient groups contains the fundamental group of the clique complex at length three and the graph $A$-fundamental group at length four. Its mod-two abelianisation has a barcode whose death scales are the lengths in a minimum cycle basis. This separates the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations and provides a computable connection between persistent $A$-homotopy and persistent homology. We illustrate the construction on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks and nine benchmark networks. Filling the plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the fundamental group of the torus. In the Watts--Strogatz simulations, the normalised largest death scale falls below the normalised mean path length over the sampled range, while most clique-homology classes survive the square relations at small rewiring probabilities. The power grid has fewer surviving classes but a longer tail of death scales than five degree-preserving randomisations. We also examine connectivity graphs of maximal cliques in ego networks. Explicit certificates establish non-trivial $A$-classes even though the original ego clique complexes are contractible. The group construction and its linear summary answer related but distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permit.

authors.name: Milan Rajkovic

papers.title: Stable Configurations of Dark Energy Stars in f(R,L_m,T) Gravity
papers.summary: In the context of $f(R,L_m,T)$ gravity, two analytical solutions are proposed in this study, representing the structure of compact spherical objects whose behavior is dominated by dark energy fluid parameters. The extended field equations are derived using a static interior spacetime under the considered model which characterize a geometric structure including both dark energy and ordinary matter. The field equations are solved using the connections between dark energy with conventional matter, which are governed by different equations of state. This analysis further employs the Kohler-Chao-Tikekar and Durgapal-Fluoria spacetimes as two distinct ansatzes to close the system of field equations, resulting in two independent solutions. For both solutions, the constants are fixed by matching the interior and exterior spacetimes at the boundary using junction conditions. This study also assesses the proposed models using data from SAX J1808.4-3658, and explore the implications of varying the parametric values within the standard modified framework. The analysis concludes that both models fulfil the necessary physical conditions to ensure their candidacy for realistic stellar structures.

authors.name: M. Sharif, Tayyab Naseer, Aqsa Bashir

papers.title: Zeroth law of black hole mechanics in general Horndeski theories
papers.summary: We investigate the validity of the zeroth law in the general class of scalar-tensor theories with second-order field equations, namely Horndeski theories or generalized Galileon theories in four-dimensional spacetime. Assuming that the non-minimally coupled scalar field inherits the spacetime symmetries, we show that the horizon mixed projection of the field equations implies constant surface gravity on a stationary Killing horizon. Our analysis incorporates the most generic non-minimal scalar couplings permitted within the Horndeski framework, which we consider as a perturbative expansion about general relativity. Our results therefore classify the possible cases within this framework of proof for different classes of scalar-tensor theories, including shift-symmetric scalar fields. These results extend the applicability of black hole mechanics beyond Einstein gravity and provide further evidence for the thermodynamic consistency of general Horndeski theories.

authors.name: Ribhu Paul, Krishnakanta Bhattacharya

papers.title: One-Particle Equivalence of Lorentz-Violating and Lorentz-Deformed Theories
papers.summary: Planck-scale departures from special relativity are commonly described by theories that break Lorentz symmetry and theories in which such symmetry is deformed. We prove that, under a global shell-linearizability condition, these two descriptions are physically equivalent for a single particle, corresponding to unitarily equivalent realizations of the same Wigner orbit expressed in different momentum coordinates. This equivalence breaks down for multiparticle systems, except when the momentum-composition law can be reduced to the ordinary addition of momenta. Our results imply that the distinction between Lorentz violating and Lorentz-deformed kinematics can only be tested by genuine multiparticle observables. We discuss Compton edge measurements as a prototype example of such a multiparticle probe.

authors.name: Arshid Shabir, Francesco Marino, Mir Faizal

papers.title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead stars as Factories of the most Extreme Objects in the Universe
papers.summary: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.

authors.name: Ankit C. Khunt, Swagat S. Mishra

papers.title: Prestatability in the Macroscopic Limit
papers.summary: We examine whether the variables required for a future macroscopic description of a given physical system can themselves be stated in advance. Representing macroscopic descriptions as coarse-grainings of a fixed microscopic phase space, we distinguish formal prestatability, concerning the existence of an effective complete vocabulary of admissible macroscopic distinctions, from dynamical prestatability, concerning whether the future relevance of those distinctions is decidable. Both obstructions disappear for finite microscopic state spaces. In the infinite limit, exhaustive formal prestatability can fail, while a restricted predictive architecture may remain formally pre-statable. We construct such an architecture and show that, under universal dynamics, the future relevance of a candidate variable is equivalent to the halting problem. Thus a fixed microscopic phase space can support macroscopic descriptions whose future variables are not fully pre-statable.

authors.name: Andrea Palessandro

papers.title: Standoff chemical identification of harmful aerosols
papers.summary: Aerosols - solid or liquid particles suspended in air - are an effective means of dispersing chemical warfare agents and toxic pharmaceuticals, posing acute risks to public safety and security. Exposure to aerosol particulate matter in the environment and in industrial settings has also been linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease. In both cases, rapid chemical identification is key to generating early warnings and attributing sources. Established methods chemically identify aerosols only after extracting a sample, while standoff techniques such as lidar classify aerosols only into broad categories. Chemical identification at a distance is hindered by aerosol extinction signatures that are weak, spectrally broad, and obscured by far stronger absorption from ambient gases. Here, we demonstrate time-resolved, standoff chemical differentiation of aerosols with dual-comb spectroscopy and machine learning identification algorithms. The high spectral resolution of dual-comb spectroscopy allows ambient gas absorption to be removed, and the algorithms identify chemicals without knowledge of aerosol size and morphology. We demonstrate identification of aerosolized benzyl fentanyl (a fentanyl simulant) in mixtures with other aerosols in a standoff measurement through ambient H2O, CO2, and CH4. Despite the aerosol producing only subtle, <1% changes in the extinction spectrum across hundreds of wavenumbers, we find the limit of identification to be an order of magnitude below lethal concentrations for a 1 m aerosol cloud. This technique provides a new paradigm for performing rapid chemical speciation of aerosols using their infrared absorption signatures without extractive sampling. Together with advances in chip-based mid-infrared dual-comb spectrometry, we anticipate this technique will enable real-time networks for standoff detection of aerosol emissions and aerosolized chemical threats.

authors.name: Garrett C. Mathews, Alyssa Lalko, Anna C. Ziola, Masayuki Takeuchi, Leo C. Bloxham, Douglas A. Day, Anne V. Handschy, Amanda Makowiecki, Kevin Williamson, Nazanin Hoghooghi, Scott Egbert, Peter Chang, Tsung-Han Wu, Anthony Harness, Robert Wright, Jiang Li, Tin Komljenovic, John Bowers, Satoshi Takahama, Daven Henze, Kerry Vahala, Scott A. Diddams, Jose L. Jimenez, Gregory B. Rieker

papers.title: Finite-amplitude wave dynamics in weak-field-equivalent nonlinear electrodynamics in $(2+1)$ dimensions
papers.summary: We examine finite-amplitude wave propagation in $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear electrodynamics using Born-Infeld, logarithmic, and quadratic polynomial models whose Lagrangians agree through quadratic order in the electromagnetic invariant. Despite this weak-field agreement, characteristic and linearized analyses on homogeneous magnetic background reveal distinct propagation speeds and hyperbolicity domains. In the weak-background limit, the first coefficient at which Lagrangians differ also controls the leading nonlinear variation of the simple-wave characteristic velocity. Exact right-moving simple-waves, corroborated by finite-volume evolution, show rigid Born-Infeld propagation but finite-time gradient catastrophes in the logarithmic and polynomial models, substantially earlier in the latter for matched pulses. These catastrophes can occur while the field remains finite and the system remains hyperbolic, showing that weak-field agreement does not determine finite-amplitude dynamics.

authors.name: M. L. Pe\~nafiel, E. Veneros, A. Urquidi

papers.title: Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
papers.summary: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network), a machine-learning framework that learns this decision from experimental outcomes. We compiled 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes spanning 76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants and 25-620 degrees Celsius. Following the ALD cycle, AJIN predicts adsorption from graph-neural-network embeddings of the precursor and substrate with temperature, and deposition by adding the reactant. The best model (CHGNet-MLP) reaches balanced accuracies of 79.2% for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition and transfers partially to unseen precursors. SHAP and ablation analyses show that substrate chemistry governs adsorption, whereas precursor, substrate and reactant all contribute to deposition. Tested against our laboratory's ALD experiments, AJIN correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases, providing an experimentally grounded tool for prioritizing ALD and area-selective ALD chemistries.

authors.name: Bonwook Gu, Trinh Ngoc Le, Zunair Masroor, Minhyeok Lee, Han-Bo-Ram Lee

papers.title: State and spatial completion of 1D premixed flames for hydrogen and methane combustion
papers.summary: Accurate prediction of chemically reacting flows requires resolving the nonlinear coupling among transport and chemical reaction operators, often at substantial computational cost. This work investigates Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) for learning mappings from partial spatial profiles to steady, one-dimensional, freely propagating hydrogen-air and methane-air flame solutions. Using a database of over 15,000 cases generated with Cantera, two different FNO models were trained to reconstruct the complete thermochemical state from a smaller set of input variables. The first model concerns state completion which uses only temperature, fuel, and oxygen mass-fraction profiles to reconstruct the remaining 7 species for hydrogen flames and 51 species for methane flames along with the missing velocity. The second model performs spatial completion, using upstream thermochemical profiles extending into the initial temperature rise to reconstruct the withheld downstream structure. Evaluation on 2,625 test cases per fuel, excluded from training, shows recovery of reaction-zone species profiles, including radicals and intermediates, across the sampled conditions. These results demonstrate reconstruction of species and velocity profiles that are not supplied as inputs, and recovery of downstream structure outside the observed region. Reconstruction with missing species or incomplete spatial coverage suggests potential for using learned operators in estimating inaccessible thermochemical quantities and developing reduced-state representations for combustion applications.

authors.name: Federico Rios Tascon, Ryan F. Johnson, Diego D. Ortiz, Peter J. Schmid, Beverley J. McKeon

papers.title: Magnetohydrodynamic spectra and line invariants in the presence of axions
papers.summary: A new form of the mean-field equations for magnetic fields, which accounts for the interaction with axions, is studied. It is shown that the asymptotic ergodic invariants of magnetic field lines play a key role in the evolution of magnetic fields, which determine the type of the magnetohydrodynamic spectrum of the solutions.

authors.name: P. M. Akhmetiev (IZMIRAN), M. S. Dvornikov (IZMIRAN), A. Yu. Smirnov (IZMIRAN, Moscow State University)

papers.title: Physics in Safety and Safety in Physics: Lessons from the LHC and its Underground Experiments
papers.summary: Large underground particle-physics facilities are usually discussed by separating scientific performance from the systems that make their operation safe. We develop a complementary view in which safety is treated as an intrinsic part of the physical and operational structure of an experiment. Using the LHC, ATLAS, and CMS as principal case studies, we introduce the concepts of physics in safety and safety in physics: physical laws, measurements, and models determine hazards and protective barriers, while those barriers in turn define the machine, detector, access, and intervention states in which physics can be performed. We formulate this relation through a \emph{safe operational phase space} and through admissible trajectories connecting different configurations, emphasizing that safety constrains not only states but also transitions between them. The framework is applied to beam and magnet protection, cryogenic and oxygen-deficiency hazards, detector-specific risk configurations, personnel access, maintenance, and radiation protection, with particular attention to the different architectures of ATLAS and CMS. We argue that validated protection does not merely restrict scientific activity but can enlarge the domain of sustainable operation. This viewpoint provides a unified physical and operational framework for understanding safety at the LHC and for incorporating protection, maintainability, and recoverability into the design of future accelerator and underground facilities such as HL-LHC, FCC and muon collider.

authors.name: Alexander S. Sakharov

papers.title: Beyond node strengths: the topological content of weighted bipartite networks
papers.summary: Weighted bipartite networks encode the topology and intensity of interactions between two disjoint sets of nodes. However, it is unclear whether the observed pattern of connections is already explained by node interaction volumes or contains additional structural information. Here we introduce a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks that preserves node strengths alone, strengths and global density, or strengths and the complete degree sequence. Across economic, technological, ecological, social and lexical systems, we find that strength constraints alone are generally insufficient to reproduce empirical structures. Yet the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single constraint controlling network density frequently provides the most parsimonious description, whereas networks with stronger residual degree heterogeneity require node-specific constraints. Beyond downstream inference, we also show how the choice of topological resolution changes which interactions and projected relationships are identified as statistically significant. Our results indicate that topology is essential, but often compressible, in the statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and provide a scalable computational framework for fitting, sampling, model selection and validation within a common workflow.

authors.name: Daniele Cirulli, Lorenzo Buffa, Giulio Cimini, Dario Mazzilli, Aurelio Patelli, Fabio Saracco

papers.title: Learning the interactions underlying multicellular migration using many-body stochastic inference
papers.summary: Uncovering the interactions that give rise to emergent collective behavior in active and living matter remains a major challenge. Multicellular migration exemplifies this challenge: complex cell-cell interactions shape collective motion, but are difficult to measure directly. Here, we introduce a many-body stochastic inference framework that learns these interactions directly from experimental trajectories. We infer interaction models spanning different dynamical dependencies and complexities from short-time cell dynamics, and select among them based on their ability to predict emergent collective behaviors. Applied across three behaviorally distinct cell types, this approach yields minimal, predictive models of cell-cell interactions underlying multicellular migration. We find that non-cancerous epithelial cells coordinate multicellular migration through reciprocal repulsion and velocity alignment, while cancerous mesenchymal cells additionally exhibit previously unrecognized nonreciprocal interactions that couple to self-propulsion through two distinct mechanisms, which we term velocity inhibition in fibrosarcoma cells and velocity enhancement in breast cancer cells. Conceptually, these nonreciprocal interactions allow cells to tune the onset and speed of flocks, underscoring their role in collective migration and potentially enhancing cancer cell invasiveness at large cell densities. More broadly, our framework offers a general and principled route for extracting interaction laws of active and living systems directly from data.

authors.name: Bram J. Hoogland, Tom Brandst\"atter, Emily Brieger, Joachim O. R\"adler, Chase P. Broedersz

papers.title: Towards in vivo photon dosimetry using radiation-sensitive mixed-core ultrasound phase-change contrast agents
papers.summary: Objective. Advanced radiotherapy applies complex treatment plans that require verification of the beam delivery. Therefore, in vivo dosimetry, measuring delivered radiation doses directly on the patient, has become increasingly important. Radiation-sensitive phase-change nanodroplets were recently proposed for in vivo radiation sensing. The radiation-induced conversion of superheated nanodroplets into microbubbles generates ultrasound contrast from which radiation deposition can be derived. While successful for in vivo proton range verification, previously used nanodroplet formulations were not suitable for in vivo photon dosimetry due to stringent requirements on the degree of superheat of the nanodroplet core. Here, we used a mixed-core strategy, combining different perfluorocarbons in the same nanodroplet core, to modulate the photon response and droplet stability at body temperature. Approach. Lipid-shelled nanodroplets with different cores (pure octafluoropropane, pure decafluorobutane and a 17:4 (v/v) octafluoropropane:decafluorobutane mixture) were dispersed in deionized water in phantom containers and irradiated with a photons at various temperatures. Simultaneous high-frame rate ultrasound acquisition allowed to link ultrasound contrast generation to the radiation delivery. Nanodroplets were characterized using 19F NMR spectroscopy. Main results. Photons induced nanodroplet-mediated ultrasound contrast strong enough for clinical applications at body temperature. A clear trade-off was observed between a stronger photon response and maintaining sufficient droplet stability. Neither octafluoropropane (lacking stability) nor decafluorobutane (lacking photon response) cores proved suitable. On the contrary, the mixed-core formulation exhibited a strong photon response with minimal background already at small radiation doses (0.1 Gy). This paves the way for future in vivo dosimetry.

authors.name: Bram Carlier, Reza Bahrami Gorji, Qingyuan Tan, Meritxell Gamb\'us-Marf\`a, Uwe Himmelreich, Meng-Xing Tang, Koen Van Den Abeele, Sophie V. Heymans

papers.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
papers.summary: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. From this single picture we obtain the blue of the sky and the white of the clouds, transparency and the refractive index, the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem, reflection and the colours of thin films, why metals reflect and what gives metals and semiconductors their colours, polarizers, Brewster's angle and birefringence, the working of mirrors, lenses, microscopes and the eye, the propagation of a few-cycle pulse through a slab, Cherenkov radiation, amplification and second-harmonic generation. Feynman's arrows are made quantitative with the sheet method, and coupled-dipole simulations show the incident wave being cancelled and replaced inside the medium. The connection with quantum theory is discussed where the classical picture stops: the photon, spontaneous emission and the forbidden lines of the aurora, vision and photosynthesis, and the sum over paths. The text is addressed to undergraduate students and their teachers, and to any reader curious about the physics behind everyday optical phenomena; derivations are collected in separate panels, and the animations and the Python codes used for the figures and simulations are provided as ancillary files.

authors.name: Giancarlo Reali

papers.title: Test beam results for machine-learning-based reconstruction of resistive silicon sensors
papers.summary: The advent of Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs) and AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) as candidate technologies for four-dimensional tracking has moved part of the reconstruction burden onto the analog waveforms of the sensor, in which the charge shared between electrodes encodes the impact position well below the electrode pitch. Recovering that position is a continuous, non-linear inverse problem. Transient Current Technique measurements characterize this problem at fixed injected charge and high signal-to-noise, whereas a minimum-ionizing beam adds Landau fluctuations in the deposited charge under detector operating conditions. We report test beam results for full-waveform reconstruction of an AC-LGAD of 500 $\mu$m pitch read out on a $2\times2$ pad matrix, exposed to the 120 GeV pion beam of the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and read out alongside a six-plane MIMOSA-26 telescope. The telescope is aligned, and its per-plane resolutions are calibrated in situ, giving a track pointing resolution of about 2.5 $\mu$m per axis at the device, so that the measured residual is the sensor response rather than a convolution with the reference. We then compare two analytic estimators, the parameter-free charge-imbalance formula and a fitted linear matrix inversion, with the topology-agnostic transformer developed for resistive silicon sensors. Over the full active pad, the transformer reaches a median total position with up to factor 3 improvement. Within the charge-sharing core, the three methods converge to the floor of this sensor at the achieved signal-to-noise.

authors.name: Don C. Wong, Leena Diehl, Spencer Ellis, Marcos Fern\'andez Garc\'ia, Gabriele Giacomini, Vagelis Gkougkousis, Ben Kilminster, Jingyu Luo, Anna Macchiolo, Yajna Mahabeer, Yevhenii Padniuk, Daria Senina, Samantha Sunnarborg, Jessica Tang, Alessandro Tricoli, Lixing Wang, Gaetano Barone

papers.title: Physics-Based Differentiable Beamforming for Deep Learning-Based Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.summary: Ultrasound is widely used for vascular imaging because it is non-invasive, real-time, and cost-effective. However, its spatial resolution remains limited by diffraction to an order of the acoustic wavelength. This limitation is particularly restrictive for imaging of the microvasculature and high-resolution vector-flow-imaging. In this work, we present a multi-channel physics-based deep learning approach to super-resolve monodisperse microbubbles directly from multi-channel radio-frequency (RF) data. We also present a novel image-based metric for model evaluation. The proposed pipeline combines a learnable deconvolution network with a differentiable beamforming layer, enabling a direct deconvolution of the microbubble (MB) signature prior to image formation. By operating on multi-channel RF data, the method aims to improve localization robustness in the presence of dense microbubble populations and deconvolve the lateral direction in a relatively low-frequency regime (1.7 MHz) where MBs exhibit nonlinear behavior. The model is trained and evaluated on simulated data using monodisperse lipid-coated MBs over a broad range of acoustic pressures and microbubble densities. The proposed method improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the single-channel approach. It achieves sub-wavelength axial and lateral resolution while slightly improving robustness to dense microbubble populations outside the training domain. It also demonstrates generalizability across transmit configurations without requiring explicit training on each transmit configuration.

authors.name: Anass Hameddine, Bram de Wilde, Michel Versluis, Jelmer M. Wolterink, Guillaume Lajoinie

papers.title: New Astronomical, Meteorological and Geological Study of the "Torre Spaccata District" - VII district of the Municipality of Rome
papers.summary: This study, part of the NGICS (New Italian City Geological Study) project, analyzes 25 years of multi-disciplinary data to assess long-term environmental, climatic, and geological trends in Torrespaccata, an urban district within Rome's Seventh Municipality (VII Administrative District). Specifically, it investigates the temporal evolution of Heating Degree Days (HDD) by comparing the historical stationary climate period (1961-1989) with the recent multidecadal interval (1990-2014). Statistical analysis reveals a clear climatic transition: while the pre-1989 period showed a stationary trend (m = -1.14 HDD/year), the modern era exhibits a sharp decline in heating demand, characterized by a negative trend of -11.52 HDD/year (R2 = 0.511). This significant reduction of 80.14 HDD between the two periods is robustly validated via Welch's t-test (t = 3.045, p = 0.0039). Concurrently, interannual variability increased by 29.8%, driven by the synergistic feedback between global warming and the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. Furthermore, the correlation between climatic anomalies and local geological events is evaluated using robust statistical imputation to mitigate uncertainties caused by data gaps. These findings provide critical insights into long-term anthropic and natural changes within the urban ecosystem.

authors.name: Diego Tasselli, Stefano Ricci, Pamela Bianchi

papers.title: Reaching separated flow states by release and recapture with learned latent feedback
papers.summary: Targeting a prescribed flow configuration rather than an aerodynamic coefficient is challenging because the desired state may lie outside the natural attractor. We demonstrate cluster-based control in a learned vorticity representation for two-dimensional flow over a NACA0015 airfoil at $Re=500$ and $\alpha=15^\circ$, using a localized streamwise momentum source near the leading edge. An actuation-enriched ensemble is compressed with a variational autoencoder and partitioned into macrostates. We optimize a continuous feedback law interpolating macrostate-dependent amplitudes without an explicit latent dynamical model. For an attached target, the optimized law approaches constant forcing, arrests vortex shedding and maintains the attached state. For a strongly separated target, the law instead establishes attachment, withdraws actuation so that the natural separation transient carries the flow through the target, and restores forcing to recapture attachment. Over the evaluation horizon, the closed-loop trajectory revisits the target approximately every three shedding periods. Companion open-loop calculations isolate the arrest, release and recapture processes.

authors.name: Khalid Rafiq, Aditya G. Nair

papers.title: Density Matrix Renormalization Group Method for Core-excited Electronic States
papers.summary: We present the formulation and implementation of the Core-Valence Separation (CVS) approximation within the Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) framework for the simulation of core-level X-ray spectra. Two symmetry implementations are developed and assessed, identifying a scheme that preserves spin symmetry and remains applicable to multiple core orbitals.
