We attribute this effect to the transfer of the optical angular momentum in the system. While an individual sub-wavelength circular aperture is not expected to alter the total angular momentum, the periodic structure results in a coherent coupling of plasmons wavefronts, giving rise to a collective Bloch-Floquet-like response. The edge of the structure accumulates the helical phase that eventually results in a visible spin-dependent shifting of the plasmonic beam. We systematically study the effects of hole-array size, periodicity and the geometry. The observed phenomenon shows an unprecedented robustness and consistency. These results establish periodic plasmonic arrays as a platform for converting localized helicity-dependent responses into collective chirality, providing a route toward controlling chiral plasmonic wavefronts in structurally achiral systems.

authors.name: Sahil Sahoo, Ahmed Lafeef Ettapuram Naduvilepurayil, Akash Das, Yuri Gorodetski

papers.title: Offline Evaluation of Information-Theoretic Adaptive Bayesian Vector Magnetometry
papers.summary: An information-theoretic adaptive Bayesian framework for jointly estimating the longitudinal and transverse components of a magnetic field from the time-resolved optical response of a cold $^{87}$Rb ensemble is presented. A linearly polarized continuous-wave probe drives the $D_2$ $F{=}1 \rightarrow F'{=}0$ transition, producing coherent population trapping (CPT) lineshapes whose width, contrast, and transient dynamics depend sensitively on the ambient magnetic field. The full temporal signal, including early-time transient signal and the steady-state absorption, is compared against a precomputed Maxwell-Bloch forward model. The joint posterior distributions of the longitudinal and transverse components of the magnetic field are updated sequentially, while marginalizing over instrumental nuisance parameters arising from the finite resolution of the magnetic bias coil supply. At each step, the applied longitudinal bias field is chosen to maximize the expected Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the current prior and the anticipated posterior, the expected information gain. As a proof of principle, the protocol is validated in post-processing on pre-recorded experimental scans, and both field components converge to well localized field estimates with weak correlation between them, consistent with the distinct dependence of the CPT resonance position and lineshape on the field components. These results establish an information-theoretic framework for joint vector field estimation from transient cold-atom spectroscopy. However, there exists a systematic forward-model discrepancy, showing that posterior concentration alone does not establish accuracy and motivating nuisance-parameter inference in future online implementations.

authors.name: Dinesh Ramachandran, Shubham Jaiswal, Goutam Manna, Saikat Ghosh

papers.title: High-sensitivity sensing technology of 10 MHz radio frequency electric field based on Rydberg atoms
papers.summary: To address the pressing need for high-sensitivity, miniaturized electric field sensors in the short-wave communication band (3-30 MHz), this study proposes and demonstrates a radio frequency electric field quantum sensing scheme based on cesium atomic Rydberg states and the electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) effect. The scheme employs an all-infrared optical design, utilizing 852 nm probe light, 1470 nm dressing light, and 780 nm coupling light to efficiently prepare the 49P3/2 Rydberg state in a room-temperature cesium vapor cell, which is then probed non-destructively via ladder-type four-level EIT spectroscopy.

authors.name: Yulong Han, Zhengye Shan, Kan Zhang, Jinfang Sun, Lihua Zhang, Bang Liu, Dongsheng Ding

papers.title: Retrospective Analysis of Team-Following Trading Profitability in Pumpfun Meme Coins Using Funding Networks
papers.summary: If the right token-creation teams had been known, how much could following them have returned, and what is left when only information available before each launch is used? We study ten separately recorded Pumpfun windows (April 2024 to September 2026), each reconstructed independently from real-SOL reserve states and finite-capital accounts that start with one SOL. Teams are directed funding groups ranked in hindsight. When every team exits at its own best reserve threshold, chosen in hindsight, the main account ends above one SOL in all 8 windows that have a qualifying team (1.10 to 11.32 SOL), but free cash exceeds one SOL in only 5, and marks of positions that never reached their threshold make up 17--94% of equity. If teams are recognised online, from tokens whose first hour has completed, 9 of 19 teams become identifiable only after their last launch; the remaining 10 end above one SOL in 10 cases, with free cash above one SOL in 7; funding links in this step still come from the full window, so even these results are not a fully realisable signal. A large model balance, a result above random cohorts that repeat the threshold search, and a statistical rejection in the selection-matched nulls (3 of 40 tests after Holm adjustment) are three different statements, and these nulls condition on the discovered funding graph, so they do not calibrate the whole selection procedure. Midpoint tests describe a further source of apparent opportunity. A detailed analysis of the best and the worst window, with every analysis parameter varied, shows that the worst result, which is close to break-even, rises several-fold with a stop rule or another funding-graph construction. The results are conditional retrospective model accounts, not executable profits, and not evidence of a causal effect of the SOL price.

authors.name: Fail Gafarov

papers.title: A 40 Gbit/s FPGA-based RoCEv2 transport for detector readout: development and performance
papers.summary: Recording the complete input of a detector trigger allows trigger algorithms to be replayed and studied offline. For the BESIII main drift chamber (MDC), this requires moving tens of Gbit/s from trigger FPGAs into server memory without loss. Remote direct memory access over Converged Ethernet (RoCEv2) lets commercial network adapters write such data into host memory. Detector readout also needs record boundaries that the receiver can check, replay from a verified copy, and host buffers that are reused only after consumption. We present a 40 Gbit/s FPGA RoCEv2 transport that provides these functions. Records are aggregated into CRC32C-checked blocks, and unacknowledged data are kept in DDR memory and verified before replay. Acknowledgment-aware retention writes to DDR only the data that are not acknowledged in time. The transport runs on a ZCU102 board and on the 9U VME Trigger Core Board (TCB). With records of 128 B to 4 KiB it comes within 0.4% of the packetization limit of the link, delivering 36.9 Gbit/s of payload at a path MTU of 1024 B, and its block latency is set by the time needed to fill a block. On a direct link, acknowledgment-aware retention cuts DDR writes for large blocks from 106% to 0.03% of the payload, and injected DDR access errors stay within their queue pair. On the TCB, three 16.4 TB transfers through two switches lost at most five packets each, all recovered by replay. An installation at the MDC is under test.

authors.name: Sheng Dong, Jingzhou Zhao, Haoxin Wang, Tingxuan Zeng, Fei Li

papers.title: Extreme temperatures characterization of Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMT
papers.summary: In this work, we fabricate and characterize ultra-wide bandgap Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMTs with Pt/Au gate under a wide temperature range of 20 K to 650 K. The devices retained robust modulation capability throughout the measurement, with excellent on/off ratio of 9.7 * 107 and 6.4 * 107 under 20 K and 650 K. The DC output IV measurement was performed, with Id,max of a device with Lsd = 9 {\mu}m measured to be 240 mA/mm and 120 mA/mm under 20 K and 650 K. In addition, low drain and leakage were observed in multiple devices, and the device robustness was evaluated under room temperature after the extreme temperature measurement with minimal degradation observed in Id,max and Rsheet. Moreover, transfer I-V characteristics of the Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMTs have also been studied, where a relatively small Vth shift was observed. TLM measurement and transconductance analysis both indicate the presence of weak temperature dependent scattering mechanisms in the device channel. The subthreshold swing (SS) was calculated and observed to increase parallelly to SSideal under investigated temperature, indicates a robust gate structure. Finally, the on/off ratio and Ig of the 9 {\mu}m Lsd device were benchmarked and compared favorably against other reported results. While the results offer insight into the extreme temperature performance of AlGaN channel HEMT with Al composition higher than 50%, it also establishes AlGaN channel HEMT as a promising candidate for extreme temperature electronic applications.

authors.name: Shuwen Xie, Jacklyn Zhu, Swarnav Mukhopadhyay, Yi-Chen Liu, Shubhra Pasayat, Savannah Eisner, Chirag Gupta

papers.title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
papers.summary: We present \textit{Hydrograd} v2.0, a significantly improved differentiable 2D shallow-water model written in Python with JAX. The model solves the shallow-water equations on the unstructured meshes of production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving finite-volume scheme that handles wetting and drying. Gradients are tailored to the type of problem. Steady states are found by Newton's method with an exact sparse Jacobian obtained by graph colouring, and their gradients follow from the implicit function theorem at the cost of one linear solve. Unsteady flows are differentiated in reverse mode with checkpointing, or with an implicit time integrator whose gradient costs about two forward runs. All gradients agree with finite differences, to about $10^{-8}$ for steady flows. On the Savannah River case, the steady water surface differs from that of SRH-2D by 4.7\,mm (root mean square). Steady closure learning was 96 times faster than differentiating through time marching and reached a lower loss. An inflow hydrograph was inverted from stage records with a peak error of 2\,\%. In an unsteady roughness calibration, a singular value decomposition analysis of the sensitivity matrix showed that the stage records at the gauges are 70 to 160 times more sensitive to the total resistance of the reach than to its distribution among the roughness zones, which explains why only a gauge layout with gauges in every zone recovered all five roughness values. On one GPU, a mesh of 512,000 cells takes 7.6\,s for a forward run and 51\,s for a gradient.

authors.name: Xiaofeng Liu

papers.title: Comments on: "Optimized thermal control of a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity"
papers.summary: This comment addresses the publication [Appl. Opt. 65, 7090 (2026)] which targets an alleged ``optimization'' of a patented invention conceived by the author. The invention had introduced a multi-temperature management scheme for a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity that optimized the crystal temperature around the beam waist for phase-matching, while utilizing independently adjustable temperatures in other regions of the same crystal to simultaneously satisfy the double-resonance condition. A foundational form of this invention was initially utilized by co-author H. Vahlbruch without the author's prior knowledge during the construction of the squeezed-light laser for the Virgo gravitational wave detector. In their publication, the three authors now propose a variant that reduces the maximum achievable temperature differential. Here, I demonstrate that this approach does not constitute an optimization but, on the contrary, represents a regression that dismantles the invention. In general, a high-quality implementation of this invention fundamentally depends on maximizing the achievable temperature differential. Only then can the problematic phase differences---introduced by dielectric coatings, Gouy phase shifts, and suboptimal poling lengths at the crystal facets---be effectively compensated for, particularly in short crystals. If desired, smaller temperature differences can always be selected dynamically anyway.

authors.name: Roman Schnabel

papers.title: Estimating Permeability of Carbonate Rocks from NMR T2 Distribution and Formation Factor Using a Physics-Based Model
papers.summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logging provides a nondestructive method for characterizing pore structure and fluid distribution in reservoir rocks. Conventional permeability models, such as the Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) and Timur-Coates (TC) equations, have been widely used to estimate permeability from NMR T2 relaxation time distributions. However, these empirical models require calibration against core-measured permeability, and their fitted coefficients often vary substantially across lithologies and pore systems. In this study, we formulate and evaluate an NMR-informed implementation of a physics-based permeability relationship derived from critical path analysis (CPA) by linking the characteristic pore length scale to the dominant NMR relaxation time. We estimate permeability (k) using NMR T2 distributions and electrical formation factor (F) for 14 carbonate rock samples collected from the Morro do Chaves Formation in the Sergipe-Alagoas Basin, Brazil. We compare the predictive performance of this formulation with that of calibrated SDR and TC models. The proposed CPA-NMR formulation achieves a root mean squared logarithmic error (RMSLE) of 0.56 without calibration against measured permeability from the investigated formation. These findings indicate the potential of combining NMR relaxation measurements with electrical formation factor for physics-based permeability estimation. Further evaluation using independent datasets is needed to assess applicability across formations and lithologies.

authors.name: Behzad Ghanbarian, Silvia L. B. Bermudez, Andre Souza, Gabriel S. S. Ribeiro, Maira C. O. Lima, Paulo Couto

papers.title: Hyperelasticity as an efficient regularizer for 2D-3D thoracic motion models
papers.summary: Patient-specific motion models enable real-time volumetric imaging of the thorax from a single x-ray projection, but most existing approaches require hours of training. The VM-DS framework trains in minutes, yet its image-space self-consistency regularizer accounts for 40% of the motion-model fitting time and does not prevent the fitted fields from folding. In this paper, we explore a range of regularization approaches including scaling-and-squaring, bending energy, diffusion, first-order inverse consistency, isotropic total variation, a negative-Jacobian hinge, |log det J|, a control-point injectivity bound and hyperelastic regularization. Hyperparameters were selected on two development cases from the public DIR-Lab 4D dataset under rules fixed in advance, and the regularizers were tested on eight held-out cases. At a fixed number of training steps, the hyperelastic term trained in 5.6 against 8.4 min and gave a lower held-out TRE (2.5 mm). With a quarter of the motion-model budget it matched the baseline (2.7 mm), and at every budget from 2 to 17 min its mean TRE was lower by 0.3-0.5 mm. Hyperelastic fields had no folded voxel in any held-out view, whereas baseline fields folded in 83 % of views, with image similarity unchanged. A hyperelastic volume penalty can therefore replace image-space self-consistency, matching accuracy with 3-5 minutes of training and removing folding, bringing on-the-day motion models closer to routine use in image-guided interventions. Code will be available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap/tree/hyper

authors.name: Nicholas Hindley

papers.title: Toward Self-Evolving Geospatial Algorithms: An LLM-Driven Framework with a Case Study on Spatial Regime Discovery
papers.summary: Geospatial algorithms have been developed through expert-driven discovery: a researcher spots a limitation, proposes a structural fix, and checks it by hand. With LLM-driven multi-agent systems becoming practical, much of the candidate-generation, evaluation, and selection work can now be largely automated, while the researcher's role shifts upstream toward problem formulation, evaluation design, and interpretation. We refer to this paradigm as Self-Evolving Geospatial Algorithms (SEGA) and propose a framework with three required modules: a two-loop architecture with embedded geographic knowledge as the inner-loop engine; an automatic code formatter that converts any raw geospatial algorithm into the standardized triple required by the inner loop; and a simulation-driven training protocol, in which evolution runs only on synthetic data with known ground truth, and the discovered algorithm is applied unchanged to real data, keeping real-world results out-of-sample. We use spatial regime discovery as a case study, seeded with the Two-stage K-Models algorithm. Evolution uses the Rand Index against the ground-truth partition as fitness signal; the frozen algorithm is then evaluated on 150 simulated grids and 11 real-world datasets across climate, health, hydrology, and politics. The evolved algorithm outperforms its seed, knowledge-free baselines, and four classical regionalization methods. Ablations further indicate that the channel of geographic-knowledge injection, structured retrieval versus prompt-level hints, is itself load-bearing. In this case study, LLM-assisted search sped up the inner loop; whether it does so for other seeds and task families remains open. The geographer's role -- asking the right questions, designing trustworthy evaluation -- grows more central.

authors.name: Xiayin Lou, Peng Luo, Liqiu Meng

papers.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability
papers.summary: Variational second-order reduced-density-matrix calculations can dissociate molecules into fractionally charged fragments; Part I largely removed this failure with integer electron-count conditions on fixed partitions. Building on the realizability theory of point processes, we place these conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs (LPs) on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities, the levels tighten under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric $N$-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which they need not reach, even for the Coulomb repulsion. The spin-summed real-space cuts of Part I are its two-cell members. The LP optimum is also a measure: at fixed one-particle density it equals the $L^1$ distance of the coarse-grained candidate from representability and increases under refinement to that of the candidate, with a vanishing coarse-graining error; its primal law constructs a representable approximation, and its dual a violated valid inequality, used as a cut in molecular calculations. The count conditions are not implied by the usual positivity conditions: moment data that satisfy all three-particle positivity conditions, including $T_1$ and $T_2$, give through Gaussian orbitals a smooth pair density that violates an integer count. For atoms at fractional electron number, ensemble relaxations with the integer-count condition lie closer to the exact piecewise-linear energy than the zero-variance fixed-$N$ form.

authors.name: Maho Nakata

papers.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
papers.summary: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse--Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin vanishes with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Exact finite-rotation corners and periodic-cell simulations confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.

authors.name: Oleg N. Kirillov

papers.title: Wavelength-resolved polarization characterization of supercontinuum vector beams
papers.summary: The polarization state of a supercontinuum (SC) vector beam provides a reference for quantitative polarimetry. We characterize an azimuthally polarized SC vector beam generated with an S-waveplate and azimuthal polarizers by wavelength-resolved Stokes imaging. Representative maps show an approximately tangential azimuthal angle and a small ellipticity parameter over much of the beam, together with the degree of polarization. The {\pm} 90{\deg} azimuthal angle boundary shifts by about 21{\deg} between 450 and 766 nm. A linear fit gives 21{\deg} {\pm} 7{\deg}, where the uncertainty is derived from the slope confidence interval and does not include uncharacterized systematic errors. Jones-matrix calculations examine candidate imperfections under specified assumptions. Attributing the measured boundary shift to this mechanism requires an intensity extinction ratio of about 7 or less at 766 nm if the offset at 450 nm is negligible and the shift corresponds to a uniform azimuthal angle change. The origin remains unresolved. The results motivate wavelength-dependent characterization and calibration of this probe for quantitative polarimetry.

authors.name: Shunpei Nara, Hayato Kobayashi, Kousuke Kusano, Yuta Takai, Hiroyuki Kowa, Toshitaka Wakayama, Takeshi Higashiguchi

papers.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
papers.summary: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

authors.name: Xiaohong Zhang, Wenshan Cai, Zhuomin Zhang

papers.title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Large-Angle Structures
papers.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. The system employs coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination to simultaneously acquire information from flat regions and steep slopes. The proposed iterative SFF algorithm achieves high-resolution 3D topography measurement. Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate that the proposed method enables fast scanning and sub-micrometer resolution and significantly extending the measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. This method fills a critical gap in existing technology for fast, natural-color, 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies.

authors.name: Yuchen Lin, Mengrui Wang, Fan Li, Jingxiang Zhang, Manming Shu, Jiajing Yan, Chang Liu, Tianyu Zhao, Yansheng Liang, Ming Lei

papers.title: Origin of devil's staircases and anomalous Arnold tongues of breathing solitons in optical Kerr resonators
papers.summary: Synchronization phenomena are ubiquitous across natural and engineered systems, and optical resonators supporting breathing solitons offer a natural platform for their investigation. In driven Kerr cavities described by the Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE), breathing-soliton dynamics constitute a minimal setting in which such behavior can be systematically analyzed. Despite recent observations of intricate self-synchronization structures in mode-locked lasers-such as subharmonic entrainment, devil's staircases, and holes within Arnold tongues, i.e., regions of unsynchronized dynamics embedded within synchronized domains-their physical origin has remained elusive due to the complexity of laser dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that these phenomena emerge in the universal framework of the LLE. By reducing the problem to this model, we uncover the mechanism responsible for both the devil's staircase and the formation of holes within Arnold tongues. This provides a unified physical picture of synchronization in nonlinear systems, extending beyond optics and providing insight into analogous predictions and observations in fluids and other oscillatory media. In addition, we identify the regimes of high-order synchronization, enabling the generation of ultradense frequency combs, opening new directions for precision photonic applications.

authors.name: Tianhao Xian, Junsong Peng, Sonia Boscolo, Christophe Finot, Heping Zeng

papers.title: Lensless single-pixel imaging through dynamic coded-aperture illumination
papers.summary: We demonstrate a lensless single-pixel imaging (SPI) system combining dynamic coded-aperture illumination with single-pixel detection. Binary digital micromirror device (DMD) masks generate tailored grayscale intensity fields through coherent propagation, without relay projection optics or temporal grayscale synthesis. Six target-field configurations---uniform, Rayleigh speckle, squared-Rayleigh speckle, and sparse binary fields with $p=10\%$, $5\%$, and $1\%$---are evaluated using binary and grayscale objects. Intensity-correlation and nonnegative total-variation-regularized reconstructions reveal that the preferred illumination depends on the object, reconstruction method, and evaluation metric. By combining rapid binary modulation, programmable grayscale illumination, and single-pixel readout, this implementation provides a flexible architecture for lensless computational imaging and joint design of optical encoding and reconstruction.

authors.name: Yuhan Guo, Shilei Li, Tong Zhou, Liming Li

papers.title: GPU acceleration of the numerical-atomic-orbital DFT code OpenMX with GEMMul8: performance and numerical agreement on consumer and HPC GPUs
papers.summary: We integrate GEMMul8, a library that emulates FP64 matrix multiplication on INT8 Tensor Cores, into the GPU version of the numerical-atomic-orbital first-principles code OpenMX 4.0. The GEMMul8 configuration is compared against the cuBLAS FP64 configuration within each of two environments, a consumer GeForce RTX 5080 and an HPC-oriented H100 PCIe, for the four computational paths formed by collinear (CL) or noncollinear (NCL) spin and band or $\Gamma$-point-cluster solvers. In fixed-work measurements that completed 25 SCF iterations, the diagonalization section of a 384-atom CL band calculation on the RTX 5080 is accelerated by a factor of 2.1 and the total run time by 1.8; a 512-atom CL cluster calculation, which uses only real matrix products in contrast to the CL band calculation, still gains a factor of 1.5 in the diagonalization section. On the H100, GEMMul8 provides little additional acceleration of the diagonalization section. In an accuracy test on a 216-atom Si system in which one atom was displaced by 0.05 angstrom, all 24 configurations were converged using an SCF convergence criterion of $10^{-8}$; every configuration converged at the same iteration within each path, and the differences between GEMMul8 and cuBLAS are at most $2\times10^{-12}$ Ha in the total energy and $7\times10^{-12}$ Ha/Bohr in force components.

authors.name: Hiroyuki Kawai, Taisuke Ozaki, Yoshiaki \=Ono

papers.title: Velocity gradient tensor reconstruction from tracer orientations via Jeffery dynamics
papers.summary: The velocity gradient tensor is a local quantity, but methods that obtain it by spatial differencing of the velocities of spherical tracers amplify measurement noise. We propose a method that reconstructs the velocity gradient tensor from the orientations of non-spherical tracers such as flakes and rods. Based on the Jeffery-type equation, we show that, for incompressible flow, all components of the velocity gradient tensor are uniquely determined from the orientations of four tracers and their time derivatives in the neighbourhood of a reference point (orientation-based method). The method uses neither tracer positions nor spatial differencing. It therefore requires orientation measurements only near the reference point, without requiring measurements throughout a three-dimensional region, and measurement noise is amplified only through temporal differencing. Consequently, the minimum achievable error scales as $\sigma^{1/2}$ with the noise level $\sigma$, compared with $\sigma^{1/3}$ for the positional PTV-plus-differencing approach (position-based method). Numerical tests further show that the vorticity is reconstructed more accurately than by the position-based method, whereas the strain rate is reconstructed with comparable accuracy. Finally, applying the method to spherical Couette flow, we find that the reconstruction fails where the neighbouring tracers align, which renders the inversion ill-conditioned, and that this degeneracy appears as the characteristic light-and-dark pattern familiar from flow visualization.

authors.name: Isshin Arai, Tomoaki Itano

papers.title: Work needed to lift a mass in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.summary: We determine the work needed to lift a mass from $r_2$ to $r_1$ in Schwarzschild spacetime in three ways. First we use a winch and a light rope. Then we use a photon collision. Finally we let the mass decay into photons and reconstruct it at the higher radius. All three methods give the same local work at $r_1$, $W_1=mc^2[1-N(r_2)/N(r_1)]$, where $N(r)=\sqrt{1-r_s/r}$. Thus, independently of $r_1$, the work tends to $mc^2$ as $r_2$ approaches the horizon. The rope example also gives a useful general-relativistic version of a simple machine: a rope in equilibrium need not have equal local forces at its two ends. The redshift factor plays the role of the lever arm. For a real rope the energy conditions prevent the tension from decreasing with height, so this lever advantage is confined to the idealization. The examples are intended as teaching material for undergraduate relativity courses.

authors.name: Anamta Asif, Andrzej Czarnecki

papers.title: Ensemble Covariance Propagation with Machine Learning Weather Prediction Models in a Realistic Data Assimilation System
papers.summary: Integrating machine learning weather prediction (MLWP) models into classical data assimilation (DA) workflows requires that they accurately evolve ensemble covariances. We evaluate this capability in a two-way coupled DA system, where an ensemble variational (EnVar) component evolves the mean and an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) evolves the covariances. The system is cycled over one month and assimilates a wide range of real-world observations, including microwave radiances. Using the MLWP model GraphCast for the EnKF and the physics-based MPAS model for the EnVar yields ensemble spread and covariances comparable to a reference configuration in which MPAS evolves both components. The resulting EnVar mean achieves consistently lower RMSE against GFS analyses, except near the model top, where spurious correlations degrade performance. These results demonstrate that MLWP models can propagate covariance information in a realistic DA cycling system and provide a proof of concept for their integration into future operational ensemble systems.

authors.name: Simon Toedtli, David Ahijevych, Wei Wang, Chris Snyder

papers.title: Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
papers.summary: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system's effective temperature with density.

authors.name: Yaocai Liu, Rui He, Da Wei, Longfei Li, Mingcheng Yang, Junhua Yuan, Yi Peng

papers.title: Robust Implicit Neural Representation for Multiparameter Elastic Full-Waveform Inversion
papers.summary: Multiparameter elastic full-waveform inversion (EFWI) provides a powerful means of reconstructing subsurface elastic properties, but its practical application remains challenging because of strong nonlinearity, parameter crosstalk, and the different sensitivities of seismic data to individual elastic parameters. We develop a robust implicit neural representation (INR) framework for multiparameter EFWI, using continuous neural representations to parameterize the subsurface model and provide an effective model-space constraint during inversion. Within this framework, we systematically investigate different elastic parameterizations and demonstrate that parameterization plays a critical role in controlling parameter coupling and inversion stability. Among the tested formulations, combining P-wave velocity (Vp), P-wave impedance (Ip), and the Vs/Vp ratio provides the most robust overall performance, yielding improved parameter separation and more reliable reconstruction of elastic properties. We evaluate the proposed approach on the Marmousi and Overthrust models under increasingly challenging inversion conditions and further apply it to the field Volve ocean-bottom-node dataset. Both synthetic and field-data results demonstrate that the INR-based formulation, together with the Vp-Ip-Vs/Vp parameterization, improves inversion stability, suppresses parameter cross-talk and inversion artifacts, and produces geologically coherent multiparameter models. These results highlight the importance of jointly considering model representation and physical parameterization in multiparameter EFWI and demonstrate the potential of robust INR-based inversion for complex synthetic and field seismic applications.

authors.name: Chao Li, Yangkang Chen

papers.title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
papers.summary: Most turbulent flows are sustained by inertia, which transfers energy across scales and produces characteristic power-law spectra. Yet dilute polymer solutions also exhibit turbulence when inertia is negligible: in this state, known as elastic turbulence, the velocity field remains spatially smooth while both the velocity and the polymer conformation exhibit robust power-law spectra. How a smooth flow, lacking a hierarchy of eddies, generates such multiscale structure has remained unexplained. Here we show that the missing mechanism is elastic frontogenesis, whereby the flow spontaneously organizes polymer stress into thin sheets that are stretched within their plane and compressed across their thickness, causing their amplitude to grow as they become thinner. Because the fronts are sheet-like structures, this amplification-thinning law uniquely determines the polymer conformation spectrum, while the Stokes response transfers the same geometric scaling to the velocity field, reconciling broadband spectra with spatial smoothness. Being geometric rather than model-specific, elastic frontogenesis provides an organizing principle for viscoelastic flows and the viscoelastic analogue of vortex stretching in inertial turbulence.

authors.name: Marco Edoardo Rosti, Andrea Mazzino

papers.title: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source
papers.summary: Trapped ions is one of the promising platforms for realizing quantum information processing and quantum simulation. Selective and rapid loading of a specific isotope lays the critical foundation for such purpose particularly when scaling up the system size. Here we demonstrate a new method for rapid isotope-selective loading of $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ or $^{135}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$, two types of promising ion qubits, from naturally abundant source using a three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme. Neutral atoms are selected on the narrow 791 nm $6s^2\,{}^1S_0\rightarrow6s6p\,{}^3P_1^o$ transition, resonantly transferred at 554 nm to $6s6d\,{}^3D_1$, and ionized using an existing 532 nm Raman beam. A spectral-overlap analysis based on isotope and hyperfine shifts shows relayed selectivity that the second step can further suppress undesired-isotope excitation and no contaminant ion is detected during our entire experiment. Besides, the resonant drive of the second step excitation yields a prominent loading rate of the selected species. This strategy using multi-step excitations to establish relayed selectivity can be extended to high-purity loading of other species of ions.

authors.name: Zichun Zhou, Xuhui Yao, Jiaze Li, Yuncheng Xie, Haozhe Shi, Yanxin Liu, Weibin Chu, Lei Feng

papers.title: A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
papers.summary: The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.

authors.name: Daniele Telloni, Sabrina Guastavino, Michele Piana

papers.title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
papers.summary: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.

authors.name: Timothy Sereda, Pallas Chou, Morris Hsieh, Emerson Hsieh

papers.title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
papers.summary: Direct numerical simulations examine the phase-dependent turbulence dynamics of pipe flow driven by cardiac-cycle-inspired waveforms. Four cases with and without a low-flow plateau span two Reynolds-number ranges. The response follows four stages of turbulent--turbulent reorganisation. Strong acceleration suppresses transverse fluctuations and vortical activity. During acceleration and early deceleration, streamwise-normal-stress production recovers ahead of pressure--strain redistribution and radial momentum transport, allowing energy to accumulate in elongated streaks. In early deceleration, near-wall high-speed streaks develop predominantly varicose disturbances associated with Q4 sweeps, whereas outer-buffer-layer low-speed streaks develop predominantly sinuous disturbances associated with Q2 ejections. The transition exhibits distinct radial sequences: Q2-based local onset occurs progressively later towards the wall, whereas Q4-based onset is nearly simultaneous across the viscous sublayer and buffer layer, with peaks occurring successively outwards. The two responses overlap between the drag minimum and recovery maximum as redistribution intensifies markedly and multiscale momentum transport recovers rapidly. Turbulence then decays and its scales readjust. Where present, the plateau prolongs this decay and weakens the turbulence inherited by the next acceleration stage. It further delays local instability and lengthens the onset-to-peak intervals of the shear contributions. An unsteady friction decomposition links these phase-dependent dynamics to the drag response, highlighting the role of delayed turbulent shear recovery in sustaining the low-drag interval.

authors.name: Xinyu Wang, Yan Bao, Benlong Wang

papers.title: Extending the reach of real-space real-time TDDFT: new developments in the Octopus code
papers.summary: Octopus is an open-source package implementing time-dependent density functional theory in a real-space, real-time formulation. Here we report on the developments since our previous contribution to the Special Topic Issue on Electronic Structure Software [J. Chem. Phys. 152, 124119 (2020)]. New exchange-correlation functionals extend the range of systems that can be treated, while advances in relativistic and all-electron methods open the door to core-electron spectroscopy. New capabilities for lattice dynamics - stress-tensor calculation, geometry optimization, support for machine-learned force fields, and phonon calculations - enable a fully ab initio description of light-induced lattice dynamics in real time. We also present developments that move beyond the dipole approximation, capturing light-matter interaction more faithfully. Improved methods for exciton dynamics complement a set of algorithmic advances - new propagation schemes, imaginary-time evolution, and a refactored grid handling more than a billion points - that together substantially improve performance and scalability. Combined with technical improvements such as AMD GPU support and a modernized build system, these developments consolidate Octopus as a versatile, high-performance platform for exploring electronic excitations, light-matter interaction, and nonequilibrium dynamics in molecules, nanostructures, and extended systems.

authors.name: Nicolas Tancogne-Dejean, Martin L\"uders, Esra Ilke Albar, Heiko Appel, Franco P Bonaf\'e, Alexander Buccheri, Alessandro Casalino, Benshu Fan, Hans Fangohr, Umberto De Giovannini, Henning Glawe, Hannes H\"ubener, Simon V. B. Jensen, Christian J\"ons, Lukas Konecny, Martin Lang, Ruipeng Li, I-Te Lu, Jehferson Mello, Henri Menke, Sumit Naskar, Zhengwei Nie, Sebastian T. Ohlmann, Micael J. T. Oliveira, Subhojit Pal, Jonas Reimann, Rajarshi Sinha-Roy, Jiuyu Sun, Francesco Troisi, Angel Rubio

papers.title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
papers.summary: We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.

authors.name: Guglielmo Padula, Antonio Colanera, Gianluigi Rozza

papers.title: Aircraft speed and height from Doppler-shifted sound and flight-track data
papers.summary: The changing pitch of a passing aircraft is a familiar example of the Doppler effect. We use audio recordings of 40 aircraft passages to estimate the speed and height by two methods based on the Doppler effect. The endpoint method is an analytical model that uses the limiting frequencies at the start and end of each recording and the slope near the middle of the frequency-time curve. The second method fits the whole curve. Results from both methods are compared with independent flight-tracking data. The endpoint method consistently underestimates speed and height because the recorded frequencies have not approached their limiting values. The full curve fit agrees with the tracking data within about 3% in speed and 12% in height for steady passages, with poorer agreement when speed or height changes. Software developed with AI assistance made it practical to analyze this many passages. The comparison offers undergraduate students an example of testing model assumptions and identifying systematic errors in real measurements.

authors.name: Praveen Pathak, David Rakestraw, Vijay Singh

papers.title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
papers.summary: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2~mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450~mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured $S_{21}$ at 2.45 GHz was $-$18.8~dB, versus $-$60.9~dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint $\pm$5~mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE~802.11n test demonstrated a 65~Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at $-$20~dBm transmit power through the coupler link. These results establish high-rate, placement-tolerant on-skin Wi-Fi communication through an SSPP waveguide textile.

authors.name: Akihito Noda, Ryo Takahashi

papers.title: Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality
papers.summary: Variational principles for dissipative processes come in two families: minimum principles at nonequilibrium stationary states (Helmholtz, Kirchhoff, Prigogine) and maximum principles for relaxation in continuum mechanics (Ziegler, Hackl, Fischer). We contribute to the understanding of the thermodynamic extremal principle (TEP) by investigating its extremal properties, and uncover the connection between the two families, whose distinction was recently made precise for diffusion: the extremal character is decided by the regime, which is either relaxation at frozen state, as in a closed system (maximum dissipation), or a driven stationary state in an open system (minimum dissipation), while the underlying Rayleighian functional is convex and minimized in both cases. We further examine the Reynolds transport theorem, a useful tool for fixing the energy rates of continua, and the role of inertia, recently argued to lie beyond the reach of Rayleighian principles. With inertia the driving force must be held fixed during the variation, which is less elegant than in the inertialess case, where it is a state function. Writing the energy rate as rates times driving forces still yields the correct equations, and an extremal statement survives whenever the frozen force does not depend on the varied rate. This holds directly for unsteady Stokes flow, and for Navier-Stokes flow after a change to material coordinates, in which the particle acceleration is the second time derivative of the state and the convective term, nonvariational in the Eulerian description, does not appear. The framework is tested on the Navier-Stokes family (Stokes, unsteady Stokes, and Navier-Stokes flow, in order of increasing complexity) and on dissipative Lagrangian mechanics.

authors.name: Wolfgang Flachberger, Lukas Einkemmer

papers.title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.summary: Mobile ion migration strongly influences the electrical response and current-voltage hysteresis of perovskite solar cells. However, quantitative determination of ionic transport parameters typically requires transient measurements, extensive numerical simulations, and/or fitting procedures involving multiple uncertain parameters. Here, we present an analytical model that establishes a direct relationship between capacitance-frequency (C-f) characteristics and ionic transport properties in perovskite solar cells, while accounting for interlayer effects. The model describes the transition from the ion-screened depletion capacitance at low frequencies to the geometric capacitance at high frequencies and demonstrates that the characteristic transition frequency provides a direct measure of the dielectric relaxation time for ions. Furthermore, the model establishes a quantitative connection between C-f characteristics and scan-rate-dependent current-voltage hysteresis, enabling prediction of the scan-rate window in which maximum hysteresis occurs. Drift-diffusion simulations show excellent agreement with the analytical predictions over wide ranges of ion density, ion mobility, transport-layer mobility and doping concentration. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted correlation between capacitance and hysteresis. By providing a direct, physically transparent, and computationally efficient route for extracting ionic transport parameters from routine impedance measurements, this work offers a practical tool for quantifying ion migration and understanding dynamic phenomena in perovskite solar cells.

authors.name: Manjeet Kumar, Changzeng Ding, Mathias Nyman, Yongqi Sun, Chang-Qi Ma, Ronald \"Osterbacka, Oskar J. Sandberg

papers.title: Silicon and silicon nitride photonic ring resonator arrays for photonic trimming metrology
papers.summary: Proposed silicon on silicon oxide 4x4 matrix multiplier for use in refractive index measurements, based on the Advanced Micro Foundry deep ultraviolet process. Agreement between simulated spectra and analytic design spectra demonstrate the intended performance of the components given a 1550 nm wavelength spectrum analysis. Intended purpose of the design includes optical damage analysis of the cladding, and photonic chip refractive index analysis following sub-threshold laser ablation. Femtosecond multi-shot tuning of refractive index is not a recommended application, due to round trip-losses causing quality factor and transfer function degradation.

authors.name: Cael Warner

papers.title: Heterogeneous Acceleration of TRIMEG++ code using OpenMP for Gyrokinetic Simulations
papers.summary: Turbulent transport largely determines the performance of magnetic-confinement fusion devices such as tokamaks, and gyrokinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations are a principal tool to predict it. Advancing up to hundreds of millions of markers and solving large sparse field systems at every time step makes whole-device simulations among the most expensive in plasma physics. GPUs can accelerate this workload, but porting a complex code requires restructuring its parallelism and memory traffic, ideally without a separate version per vendor. In this work, the gyrokinetic code TRIMEG-C1, whose unstructured triangular mesh and high-order finite elements cover both the confined core and the open-field-line edge of the plasma, is rewritten in C++ as TRIMEG++ and fully offloaded to GPUs with OpenMP target directives, so that one portable code base runs on both AMD and NVIDIA hardware. The particle-to-grid projection is offloaded in its standard and field-aligned formulations, the PETSc-based field solver runs on the GPU through the library's backends, and, together with the previously offloaded particle pusher, every stage whose cost scales with the marker count runs on the GPU. All speedups are node-to-node comparisons against a 256-core CPU node (2x AMD EPYC 9754). On the TCV-X21 tokamak reference case, the offloaded kernels reproduce the CPU results to a relative accuracy of 1e-11, and the full simulation runs 4.1-6.1x faster on a node with two AMD MI300A and 2.1-3.0x faster on a node with four NVIDIA A100, with the speedup growing with problem size. The MI300A, with shared CPU-GPU memory, needs no explicit data transfers, whereas the A100 needs them managed by hand. These results show that directive-based offloading can accelerate a complex gyrokinetic code across GPU vendors, making whole-volume tokamak simulations with hundreds of millions of markers practical on a single GPU node.

authors.name: Nicola Noventa, Giorgio Daneri, Zhixin Lu, Matthias Hoelzl

papers.title: Fluctuation-Response Relations and Memory in Tissue Cell Number Dynamics
papers.summary: The longevity of multicellular systems requires finely tuned feedback mechanisms to control the balance of cellular proliferation and loss. To understand the microscopic details governing feedback during homeostasis, it is crucial to quantify the feedback using a robust, minimally invasive method. Existing methods typically depend on perturbing the system to quantify the response. Such perturbations may alter cell physiology and are often technically challenging to implement. We propose a steady-state fluctuation-analysis framework to measure the dynamic response coefficient of cellular tissues. Under the minimal assumption of crowding feedback and Markovian noise, we derive a corresponding theoretical description. We validate this framework against three models of increasing complexity: a simple stochastic simulation, an agent-based mechanical model of tissue growth, and a multi-scale model of membrane-potential-regulated growth. These tests reveal the suitability of using passive fluctuations to characterize the tissue response parameters. Furthermore, this approach can help discover novel phenomena; in particular, we uncover memory effects arising from the non-equilibrium nature of growth. This work opens new avenues to quantify growth parameters in living tissues.

authors.name: Jens Elgeti Johannes C. Kr\"amer

papers.title: Tunable Near-Unity Light Absorption via Surface Exciton-Polaritons in Periodic Gratings of Anisotropic Polarizable Materials
papers.summary: Near-perfect light absorption in ultrathin films is hindered by two fundamental obstacles: the momentum mismatch that prevents resonant excitation of surface exciton-polaritons (SEPs) under ordinary illumination, and the 50% absorption ceiling imposed on free-standing conductive sheets by geometric symmetry. Here we show that both obstacles can be overcome simultaneously in a simple, planar geometry. A one-dimensional periodic grating of anisotropic polarizable ribbons composed of J-aggregates supporting bright molecular excitons provides the reciprocal lattice momentum needed to excite SEPs without employing an attenuated total reflection configuration, while a metallic mirror beneath a dielectric spacer folds the reflected field back onto the absorber, breaking the $50\%$ limit through interference between the incident and reflected waves. We develop a semi-analytical matrix formulation to compute the full optical response of such structure, and demonstrate that the absorptance at the first-order SEP resonance can be continuously tuned from near-unity to near-zero by varying the spacer thickness alone. The grating period and filling factor offer additional spectral control, and oblique incidence unlocks a second, out-of-plane polariton branch. These results establish periodic gratings of excitonic media as a versatile, practical and integrable platform for spectrally selective, near-perfect light absorption.

authors.name: M. V. Rodrigues, M. S. Barreiro, M. I. Vasilevskiy, N. M. R. Peres

papers.title: X-ray parametric down-conversion probes radiation-induced dynamics in hybrid perovskite MAPbBr3
papers.summary: We report minute-timescale time-resolved measurements of X-ray parametric down-conversion (PDC) of X-rays into ultraviolet photons in a MAPbBr3 single crystal under continuous irradiation. Despite the known radiation sensitivity of hybrid perovskites and the high photon flux required to detect the intrinsically weak PDC signal, the nonlinear response remains measurable throughout the irradiation sequence. Both PDC and Bragg diffraction exhibit a slow decay consistent with diffusion-driven damage dynamics on timescales reported for bromide-vacancy and proton migration. However, despite their similar decay rates, the PDC and Bragg signals evolve toward markedly different steady states, while an additional fast decay component is observed in the Bragg response but absent in the PDC signal. Density functional theory calculations identify N 2s states of the methylammonium cation as the most likely contributors to the measured PDC response and show that their Fourier component is only weakly affected by bromide-vacancy formation. These results establish nonlinear X-ray diffraction as a channel-selective probe of radiation-induced dynamics and demonstrate that radiation damage can couple differently to nonlinear and linear X-ray responses.

authors.name: S. Sofer, O. Sefi, G. J. Man, H. N. Barad, N. P. Jasti, D. Cahen, S. Shwartz

papers.title: Bayesian Kinetic Model Selection in Dynamic PET via Consistency Models
papers.summary: Accurate voxel-wise parametric imaging in dynamic positron emission tomography (PET), particu- larly with total-body PET (TB-PET) scanners, requires se- lecting the appropriate kinetic model for diverse organs and lesions. Conventional nonlinear least squares fitting paired with the Akaike or Bayesian Information Criterion (NLS+AIC/BIC) is computationally slow, sensitive to lo- cal minima, and prone to selecting simple models under high voxel-level noise, whereas classical Bayesian methods such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) and Approx- imate Bayesian Computation (PET-ABC) are too slow for whole-body imaging. In this work, we propose a consis- tency model (CM) that performs simultaneous Bayesian kinetic model selection and parameter posterior estimation. By combining the continuous kinetic parameters and dis- crete model index into one target vector conditioned on the measured time-activity curve (TAC) and input function, the CM samples from the joint posterior distribution p({\theta}, m|y) in seconds per slice with a GPU workstation of 4 NVIDIA A100. We validated the framework on two simulated and clinical applications: whole-body [18F]FDG TB-PET across seven compartment models, and brain [11C]raclopride PET for detecting smoking-induced dopamine release between two neurotransmitter models. In simulations, the CM achieved 97.97% model selection accuracy in the [18F]FDG applica- tion (vs. 58.67% for NLS+AIC) and 91.4% accuracy in the [11C]raclopride application (vs. 73.5% for NLS+BIC), while closely matching reference MCMC parameter posteriors. In clinical applications, CM generated whole-body FDG model selection maps, in which each regions was assigned litera- ture established sensible kinetic models; CM also success- fully mapped voxels in the brain where dopamine release was induced by smoking.

authors.name: Yun Zhao, Qinlin Gu, Andrew J. Reader, Yanan Fan, Georgios I. Angelis, Katya Amadita, Gaelle Emvalomenos, Evan D. Morris, Guobao Wang, Steven R. Meikle

papers.title: Off-focus detection for SNR enhancement in coherent single-pixel imaging
papers.summary: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. We show that appropriately selected off-focus Fourier-plane positions can improve reconstruction performance by suppressing fluctuation-sensitive coherent backgrounds while preserving spatially encoded signals. Experimentally, using a programmable liquid-crystal terahertz spatial light modulator and coherent heterodyne detection, we demonstrate improved amplitude and phase reconstruction from selected off-focus channels compared with focal detection. A symmetric off-focus pair with complementary transverse-wave-vector weighting further enhances image fidelity, contrast, and compressive-sampling robustness through coherent channel fusion. These results establish detector-position engineering as a new strategy for enhancing the robustness and information efficiency of CSPI.

authors.name: Wei Zhu, Hui Yuan, Hangbing Guo, Sheng Wang, Da Tian, Benwen Chen, Kebin Fan, Caihong Zhang, Huabing Wang, Biaobing Jin, Jian Chen, Peiheng Wu, Hartmut G. Roskos, Jingbo Wu

papers.title: One2N: Recursive refinement breaks the resolution barrier for Earth-system AI
papers.summary: Earth-system AI models approach kilometre-scale resolution, but halving grid spacing quadruples the grid-point count and end-to-end training cost. We introduce One2N, a recursive incremental framework extending a coarse model through $N$ levels of cross-resolution residual correction. At each level the parent is frozen and excluded from backpropagation, so its activations and optimizer states are never retained; only a tier-specific module is trained. A single refinement level on the NeuralGCM-0.7$^\circ$ baseline yields the two-level One2N-0.07$^\circ$, trained on one 80 GB GPU. Against HRES-0.07$^\circ$ and ERA5-0.25$^\circ$ analyses it matches its parent's tropospheric skill while reducing upper-stratospheric errors and resolving finer structure. Tropical-cyclone track errors nearly match the parent's and are lower than Pangu-Weather-0.25$^\circ$ at medium range; RMSE is lower than that model's on 93.46% of common targets. One2N thus turns an existing forecasting system, or an inexpensively trained coarse baseline, into a reusable foundation for high-resolution development, breaking the resolution barrier.

authors.name: Yanyan Tan (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Xiangjun Tian (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Can Wang (College of Mathematical Science, Beijing Information Science and Technology University, Beijing, China), Hongqin Zhang (Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Yinhai Luo (Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Min Zhao (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources), Zhe Jin (Institute of Carbon Neutrality, College of Urban and Environmental Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, China), Xingchao Yang (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources), Zaifei Wang (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources), Banglin Zhang (College of Meteorology and Oceanography, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China), Aiwen Wang (College of Mathematical Science, Beijing Information Science and Technology University, Beijing, China), Jing Zhou (State Key Laboratory of Physical Oceanography, Institute of Oceanographic Instrumentation, Qilu University of Technology), Tao Wang (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources), Baosheng An (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources), Xuliang Zhuang (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Shilong Piao (Institute of Carbon Neutrality, College of Urban and Environmental Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, China), Tandong Yao (State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources)

papers.title: Predictability of Collective Behavior in Networks of LLM Agents
papers.summary: As AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly interact at scale, anticipating their collective behavior becomes necessary. Unlike humans, individual LLM agents can be probed in {controlled scenarios}; however, the predictability of their collective outcomes hinges on what such measurements capture. We study information cascades on networks of LLM agents that decide whether to share a post given how many of their contacts have shared it. At the same fraction of sharing contacts, an agent's response depends on how many contacts it has and on the post. Responses that ignore the number of contacts mispredict the cascades, increasingly on heterogeneous networks, by an error we derive analytically and that network topology alone cannot reveal. Measured in context, the response predicts, through mean-field theory, the cascades of full LLM simulations, tipping points included. Anticipating the collective behavior of AI agents thus requires evaluating them in their local network context.

authors.name: Fabian Baumann, Michele Starnini

papers.title: Variational free complement method with Gaussian expanded complement functions: extensions of general atomic framework including helium and lithium ground states with geminal induced expansion length
papers.summary: We expand the previous framework of hierarchical-decontraction Gaussian expanded complement functions approach (arXiv: 2603.16262v2) of the free complement (FC) method to $N$-electron atomic systems including general permutations. We consider the possibility that the Gaussian expansion length depends on the presence of the geminal $g$ function. To be more specific, fewer expansion length shall be used when the two-electron $g$ function is combined with the initial wavefunction. The present approach is applied to the ground states of the helium and lithium atoms. The complement function generations via 2s$\rightarrow$1s channel in the lithium ground state are discussed. Symmetries for the associated $N$-electron integrals are analyzed.

authors.name: Cong Wang

papers.title: Modelling socio-economic effects of the pandemic in a metropolitan area
papers.summary: One of the most notorious measures taken by authorities in every country trying to prevent the uncontrollable spread of the Covid 19 pandemic was to impose severe measures to diminish the mobility of people. In recent publications we proposed a mathematical model to address the consequences of these measures and to predict the infections under different scenarios, for various different countries. In this paper we extend the model, called the BTH--SEIRS-model, to deal with the reduction of mobility in an urban area. The chosen region was the densely-populated metropolitan area around Helsinki, the capital of Finland. This choice obeyed to the fact that there are precise data related to mobility from a mobile telephone company, and that this region was completely isolated from the rest of the country for a short period during the pandemic. We also used public transport data from railways and the accommodation occupation rates in the area of interest. We show that the BTH--SEIRS model is capable of simulating the real infection data as well as the mobility-related economic activity, exhibiting the main trends present in the three indicators used for comparison. Our calculations allow us to highlight the difference of the behaviour of the pandemic in a totally different spatial scale, and to discover the hidden factors that govern the behaviour of people who are forced to commute every day from home to work.

authors.name: Jan E. Snellman, Rafael A. Barrio, Cecilia I. Ventura, Tzipe Govezensky, Kimmo K. Kaski, Maarit J. Korpi-Lagg

papers.title: Probabilistic wavefield decomposition from array covariance
papers.summary: Inter-sensor coherence loss carries information about the wavefield that conventional array processing discards. The array-covariance matrix is modelled using a mixture of energy distributions over slowness with analytical characteristic functions, e.g., skew-normal and angular-harmonic distributions, and inverted using variational Bayesian inference. The posterior supports uncertainty quantification, experimental design, model comparison and hypothesis testing. For a synthetic hydroacoustic T-phase, information is increased by an additional sensor and decreased by noise; the data favour a distributed source over a point source. For an observed thermospheric infrasound return, energy is skewed back towards the source. The method is implemented in the software Topophone2.

authors.name: Jack-Andrew Smith, Claudia Elijas-Parra

papers.title: Optical frequency combs on thin-film lithium niobate: from principles to applications
papers.summary: Optical frequency combs, consisting of mutually coherent and equally spaced spectral lines, provide a powerful means of synthesizing, distributing, and processing optical frequencies on chip. Among integrated photonic platforms, thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is particularly attractive for comb generation because it combines strong electro-optic (EO) functionality, accessible $\chi^{(2)}$ and $\chi^{(3)}$ nonlinearities, low-loss nanophotonic confinement, and versatile dispersion engineering. This review summarizes the physical foundations and representative realizations of TFLN combs, and discusses their applications in optical communication, microwave photonics, optical computing, and precision metrology. The integration of nonlinear functionality, EO control, and passive photonic components is expected to advance compact, energy-efficient comb sources and broaden the utility of TFLN in integrated photonics and quantum optics.

authors.name: Xiangzhi Xie, Tianqi Lei, Zeyu Luo, Binbin Nie, Yanyun Xue, Yikun Chen, Qi-Fan Yang, Yaowen Hu, Cheng Wang

papers.title: Efficient sensitivity analysis for combustion problems via reformulation and adjoint methods
papers.summary: Numerical simulations of combustion processes rely on chemical kinetic models, whose predictive capability is typically assessed by comparing measurements of quantities of interest (QoIs) in idealized experimental configurations with the corresponding simulated values. Sensitivity analysis quantifies the influence of model parameters on QoIs, making it a key tool for model development and optimization. Given the large number of parameters involved in detailed kinetic models compared to the number of QoIs, adjoint methods are a promising approach for efficient sensitivity analysis. Ignition delay times (IDTs) and extinction strain rates (ESRs) are among the QoIs of primary importance. However, applying adjoint methods to these quantities is not straightforward and is addressed in this work. The system of governing equations is reformulated via a coordinate transformation that makes the QoI an explicit component of the solution vector. This reformulation enables the application of adjoint sensitivity analysis for both IDT and ESR. A computational complexity analysis demonstrates that the proposed formulation significantly improves algorithmic efficiency compared to conventional approaches. The methodology is verified by comparing adjoint sensitivity coefficients with those obtained from other methods. Execution time measurements show computational cost reductions of up to two orders of magnitude relative to standard direct sensitivity analysis. A benchmark study is conducted across kinetic models of increasing size to assess how far theoretical efficiency gains are realized in practice. While the results show that implementation details can limit performance for smaller problem sizes, the expected asymptotic scaling is observed for larger models. The benchmark thus provides a reference framework for identifying key performance bottlenecks and guiding subsequent optimization efforts.

authors.name: Francesca Loffredo, Raymond Langer, Marco Vivenzo, Sanket Girhe, Heinz Pitsch

papers.title: Usage of GPUs for ALICE Reconstruction in the ALICE Online Compute farm and in the Grid
papers.summary: ALICE, the dedicated heavy-ion experiment at the LHC, records Pb-Pb collisions at an interaction rate of up to 50 kHz. It was the first LHC experiment to leverage GPUs for online data processing during LHC Runs 1 and 2, and its Run 3 online event reconstruction is now almost fully based on GPUs. In order to use its online processing server farm also for offline processing in an efficient way while the LHC is not operating, ALICE has been running the offline TPC tracking on GPUs since 2023. Since then, ALICE has been working on offloading more offline reconstruction steps to GPUs. In particular, porting the track model decoding and ITS tracking to GPUs has improved the throughput by 29%. Starting in 2026, ALICE can use the GPUs at external grid sites beyond the ALICE online computing farm for offline reconstruction.
