A first production campaign ran on the NVIDIA GPUs of the NERSC Perlmutter cluster, marking the first use of GPUs for LHC offline reconstruction at an external grid site.

authors.name: David Rohr for the ALICE Collaboration

papers.title: The role of administrative costs in policies to improve cooperation
papers.summary: We use an agent-based model for studying policies of an abstract government to increase the level of cooperation. In situations where defection is the rational choice, agents receive a bonus if they choose to cooperate. The government taxes agents' payoffs from a repeated prisoner's dilemma game to establish a budget that covers the payment of bonuses, but also the administrative costs involved. We consider costs to identify cooperators, and costs to mitigate the consequences of defective behavior. Governmental interventions are fallible, i.e. cooperators and defectors are correctly identified only with a certain accuracy. Hence, the critical bonus needed to let agents cooperate depends on the accuracy, but also on the current level of cooperation. We analyze the cost constraints for the government to pay the critical bonus and different policies to adjust the accuracy dependent on the level of cooperation. We find that perfect cooperation becomes impossible. Instead, high levels of cooperation can be achieved with optimal adjustment policies.

authors.name: Giacomo Vaccario, Luca Verginer, Frank Schweitzer

papers.title: Why fluid relaxation modes matter: Nonlinear frequency response, dynamical integrity, and dynamic pull-in of electrostatic microbeams with squeeze-film damping
papers.summary: The squeeze film between an electrostatically actuated microbeam can both induce damping and add stiffness to the structure. In addition, the dynamics of the film can interact with the nonlinear response of the microbeam. This paper extends a reduced-order model built on the complex modes of the coupled fluid-structure problem to the computation of periodic responses and their stability for clamped-clamped microbeams. Periodic orbits are continued in the frequency domain, and their stability is determined from their Floquet multipliers. The robustness of the response is assessed through basins of attraction, integrity measures, and dynamic pull-in maps in the plane of the excitation parameters. The model is validated against the measured and computed frequency response of a microswitch. Closed-form expressions are derived for the fluid relaxation modes, together with a correction for strongly coupled films, and define a parameter that characterizes the regime of the film. The approach is applied to different microbeams including cases where fluid modes relax on the timescale of the oscillation. For all simulated devices, a single fluid mode is necessary and sufficient, whereas adding coupled modes cannot replace it, whether the fluid modes respond quasi-statically or carry their own dynamics. Removing the fluid mode displaces both bifurcations that bound the pull-in band, changes the size of the basins of attraction and the position of the attractor within them, misses an abrupt erosion of the safe basin under increasing excitation, and shifts the whole region of dynamic pull-in in the excitation plane. The reduced model, with three real unknowns, makes these global analyses affordable for a fully coupled fluid-structure system.

authors.name: Fehmi Najar

papers.title: Boosting bottom-up milling of glass with GHz laser bursts
papers.summary: Burst-mode laser processing has gained increasing attention in material machining due to its potential to enhance processing efficiency and quality. However, most studies have focused on conventional top-down machining strategies, while investigations of bottom-up milling (BUM) remain limited. In this work, we optimize processing parameters for high-efficiency glass milling using a bottom-up approach with GHz bursts. The results show that the highest BUM efficiencies are achieved when employing high pulse counts ($\geq$ 20). To the best of our knowledge, we report the highest glass milling efficiency, reaching more than 250 $\mu$m$^3$/$\mu$J for both soda-lime glass and fused silica. Furthermore, increasing the burst repetition rate while maintaining a parameter set associated with high milling efficiency enables a material removal rate larger than 8 mm$^3$/s.

authors.name: Migl\.e Mackevi\v{c}i\=ut\.e, Juozas Dudutis, Aleksandras Kondratas, Paulius Ge\v{c}ys

papers.title: VNA-Only Calibration of Waveguide Thermistor Mounts with Self-Consistent Determination of the Thermistor-Port Impedance
papers.summary: A method is presented for determining the calibration factor and the effective efficiency of waveguide thermistor mounts from vector-network-analyzer reflection data alone, without a microcalorimeter, extending the three reflection-coefficient method of the coaxial case. In waveguide the thermistor is coupled to the line through a matching structure and the reference impedance of the thermistor port, $Z_0$, is not known a priori; it is inferred through a power-consistency relation between pairs of states, under the convention that it is real. The method reproduces the factory certificates (U = 2 %) of four K486A mounts within 1.0 % rms and the PTB-traceable values (U = 0.85 to 0.98 %) of a fifth within 0.34 % rms; its expanded measurement uncertainty is 0.5 to 1.16 % (k = 2) for the best specimen and below 2 % for the five. A mount with its waveguide-to-coaxial adapter is calibrated directly, without characterizing the adapter, from the model factor of the mount and the geometric factor measured through the adapter. The scattering matrix implied by the solution is not passive; a minimum-norm correction of the thermistor impedances along the two directions invisible to the calibration factor - the ratios of the efficiencies of the three states - brings it to the floor of passivity, where the efficiency depends on the load only through its mismatch factor, leaves the result unchanged, and gives the sensitivity of the efficiency to the bias resistance in closed form: below $4\times10^{-5}$ $\Omega^{-1}$ in band mean, proportional to the mismatch of the operating state and to the loss of the mount.

authors.name: Patricio Greco

papers.title: Longitudinal beam dynamics II. Lecture 1: single and double rf systems
papers.summary: In the first part of this lecture, the main characteristics of synchrotron motion, namely, synchronous particle and phase, bucket area and emittance, are introduced. The equations of longitudinal particle motion in a single rf system of a proton synchrotron are rederived and the phase equation is analyzed for small and large amplitude particles. The particle motion below and above transition energy is also considered. The main applications and operation modes of a double rf system are discussed in the second part of the lecture. The intensity effects and beam instabilities are the subject of the following lecture.

authors.name: Elena Shaposhnikova

papers.title: Retweeting patterns reveal partisan asymmetries in information sharing and signal state-level electoral outcomes in the 2020 US presidential election
papers.summary: As social media has become a primary source of political information, concerns are growing that online information consumption may intensify political polarization and reshape democratic processes. Yet how large-scale online information consumption organizes polarized political ecosystems and relates to offline voting remains unclear. Here we reconstruct partisan information ecosystems from more than 500 million tweets generated during the 2020 US presidential election, integrating information diffusion across media outlets, influencers, and social peers. Contrary to the conventional expectation that broader information exposure promotes moderation, we find that retweeting a wider range of political information is associated with stronger political polarization. We further show systematic asymmetries in political information ecosystems: the Republican ecosystem is highly concentrated and ideologically biased, whereas the Democratic ecosystem is more dispersed and primarily organized around relatively moderate left-leaning sources. Finally, we demonstrate that several shared retweeting signatures robustly map onto state-level electoral outcomes despite cross-state heterogeneity. Our findings reveal asymmetric political information ecosystems as a key organizing principle of online political communication and identify collective retweeting patterns as a scalable signal of real-world voting behaviours.

authors.name: Dawei Li, Qinjun Wan, Xin Wang, Dahe Jiang, Junyu Lu, Shitong Wang, Zhelun Zhang, Zhenyu Guan, Shaoting Tang, Feng Fu

papers.title: Longitudinal beam dynamics II. Lecture 2: intensity effects and beam instabilities
papers.summary: In this lecture, dealing with intensity effects, the equations of longitudinal motion with induced beam voltage are analyzed. This allows us, first, to describe the single-bunch potential well distortion and the loss of Landau damping. Then the linearized Vlasov equation is used to derive step-by-step the Lebedev equation. This matrix equation is then applied to find the thresholds, growth rates and spectra of an unstable multi-bunch beam. The lecture is concluded by a discussion of possible beam-instability cures.

authors.name: Elena Shaposhnikova

papers.title: HFR distorted-wave photoionization of Te III: a preliminary benchmark for large-scale atomic data production to model nebular-phase kilonovae
papers.summary: The shortage of photoionization cross sections for heavy elements remains an obstacle to non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) modeling of nebular-phase kilonova ejecta, where hydrogenic prescriptions have often been adopted in the absence of ion-specific calculations. We present a first preliminary benchmark of direct photoionization cross sections for doubly ionized tellurium, obtained using the distorted-wave (DW) approximation within the pseudo-relativistic Hartree-Fock (HFR) method implemented in the Cowan codes, in which a semi-empirical adjustment based on the observed energy levels is performed. For the photoionization from the ground level of Te III to the ground level of Te IV, comparison with Dirac R-matrix data shows encouraging agreement in the magnitude and overall decrease of the non-resonant background in the lower photon-energy region, approximately below 4 Ry (autoionizing resonances are absent from the present direct treatment). These preliminary results support HFR distorted-wave calculations as a promising and computationally tractable approach for large-scale production of photoionization cross sections, with lanthanides and actinides as longer-term targets, in light of their importance to kilonova modeling and of the severe lack of atomic data for these species.

authors.name: J\'er\^ome Deprince, Lucas Maison, Charlie Guillaume, Exauc\'e Bokamba Motoumba

papers.title: Physics design of a dual-ring light source toward MHz-rate free-electron laser radiation
papers.summary: Combining the high peak brilliance and short pulse duration of free-electron lasers (FELs) with the high repetition rate of diffraction-limited storage rings (DLSRs) is a promising direction for accelerator light sources. In this paper, we propose a dual-ring light source concept that, at MHz repetition rates, delivers pulses with a pulse durations and peak power intermediate between those of FELs and DLSRs. Such a light source can be realized as an upgrade of an existing DLSR by adding an isochronous ring equipped with transverse gradient undulators (TGUs) and connecting the two rings via bunch compression and decompression systems. We present the conceptual layout and show that bunch compression shortens the electron bunches to ps-scale durations; multi-turn radiation in the isochronous ring raises the repetition rate to 1.36 MHz from a single TGU; and the long TGUs enhance the brilliance, delivering $10^{7}$--$10^{9}$ photons per pulse across the soft and hard X-ray range, an increase of 2--4 orders of magnitude over the original DLSR. The dual-ring light source thus provides a cost-effective route to MHz FEL operation based on existing storage-ring infrastructure, combining the high repetition rate of a DLSR with the short pulses and high brilliance of a linac-driven FEL.

authors.name: Fancong Zeng, Yi Jiao, Weihang Liu, Yu Zhao, Weilun Qin

papers.title: Data-Driven Conservation Laws for Newtonian Systems: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Eisenhart-Duval Geometry
papers.summary: We introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network approach for the data-driven reconstruction of the symmetries and conservation laws of Newtonian dynamical systems, based on the geometrization of the dynamics through the Eisenhart-Duval lift. Within the Eisenhart-Duval lift, the symmetry conditions reduce to the linear Killing or Conformal Killing equations of the extended metric. We combine a Hamiltonian neural network, which reconstructs the potential function from the data, with a random-feature neural network, which solves the symmetry conditions for the collineations of the extended geometry. From the learned vector fields we construct the Lie algebra and, through Noether's theorem, the corresponding conserved quantities, while the derivation of the curvature invariants for the extended geometry provide allow us to perform an independent consistency test. We apply the method to the one-dimensional Ermakov-Pinney equation and to the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator, with and without a quartic perturbation, by using different level of noise in the phase-space data. For the Ermakov-Pinney equation, the three Killing vectors of the flat extended plane, and the corresponding nonlocal conservation laws, are recovered for, while for the harmonic oscillator, the ten conformal Killing vectors which form the $so(3,2)$ Lie algebra are determined for noise levels up to $10\%$. When the quartic term is added, the broken symmetries are identified as approximate symmetries.

authors.name: Andronikos Paliathanasis

papers.title: Frequency tuning capability of self-powered piezoelectric tuned mass dampers
papers.summary: Tuned mass dampers suffer from frequency shift sensitivity. This paper investigates the use of tunable piezoelectric tuned mass dampers (PE-TMD) by studying their behavior with tunable resistive and capacitive loads to adapt their resonant frequency. An analytical model is developed to assess the influence of key dimensionless parameters-electromechanical coupling coefficient, mass ratio, and quality factoron vibration attenuation, frequency tuning capability, and energy harvesting. The study reveals trade-offs between attenuation, tunability, and energy harvesting. It provides design guidelines for autonomous PE-TMDs and identifies key challenges for their practical implementation, including the interest of high coupling coefficients, whose the implication is limited is with growing mass ratio. Notably, it highlights the necessity of high coupling coefficient, the influence of which on frequency tuning is limited as the mass ratio grows.

authors.name: David Gibus (SYMME), Omar Larhlid (SYMME), Ahmed Guerine (SYMME), Adrien Badel (SYMME)

papers.title: Magnetized plasma modulator for polarization-tunable ultrahigh-power single-cycle lasers
papers.summary: Ultrahigh power lasers with tunable polarization and few-cycle duration have long been considered the holy grail of high-power laser science, as they push light-matter interactions into an entirely new physical regime. Yet such pulses remain far beyond the reach of conventional solid-state optics and technologies. Here, we introduce a novel magnetized plasma modulator that boosts linearly polarized lasers from petawatt to exawatt powers while simultaneously enabling tunable polarization, offering a promising approach for high-power laser development. This is achieved in density-tailored plasmas by combining dispersive compression of a chirped picosecond laser pulse with magneto-chiral group-velocity splitting in a few-Tesla magnetic field. It can generate circularly or elliptically polarized pulses with extremely high compression ratios (over 1000) and extremely short durations (down to the single-cycle level) in a compact and efficient manner. These findings demonstrate a feasible pathway toward exawatt-class few-cycle lasers with tunable polarization, opening new avenues for a wide range of cutting-edge research and applications.

authors.name: Li-Jia Shuai, Xing-Long Zhu, Zheng-Ming Sheng

papers.title: Sensitivity of diffusion MRI to white matter pathology: a comparison between ROI-based effect size and TBSS analysis under different diffusion protocols, field strengths and post-processing strategies
papers.summary: We investigated how much more advanced diffusion MRI acquisitions and more complex processing increase sensitivity to group-wise white matter (WM) differences due to pathology, and how the choice of statistical analysis affects this sensitivity. Data were acquired with DTI and DKI protocols at 3T and 7T in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), athletes with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS), and healthy controls (HC). Seven processing pipelines combining denoising, Gibbs removal, eddy current and motion correction, and Gaussian smoothing were applied. Sensitivity was assessed with two methods: a region-of-interest-based (ROI-based) effect size analysis over 72 WM tracts segmented by TractSeg, quantified by Cohen's d, and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), quantified by the fraction of significant voxels in the WM skeleton. The ROI-based analysis found significant group differences for both SLE versus HC and PPCS versus HC, whereas TBSS found differences only for SLE versus HC. Both analyses agreed that the diffusion protocol affected sensitivity more than field strength or post-processing. Regardless of pipeline, DTI-derived fractional anisotropy (FA) yielded a 0.26 higher effect size and 25% more significantly different voxels between SLE and HC than DKI-derived FA, and 3T yielded a 0.2 higher effect size and 21% more significant voxels than 7T. Smoothing reduced sensitivity in both analyses (by up to 12% in TBSS for SLE versus HC). Overall, TBSS appears less suited to localized pathology such as neurotrauma, whereas the ROI-based analysis showed no bias with respect to the nature of the pathology. Advanced protocols such as 3T-DKI and 7T-DTI may need further optimization before surpassing conventional 3T-DTI in sensitivity to WM pathology in SLE.

authors.name: Evgenios N. Kornaropoulos, Theodor Rumetshofer, Anna Gard, Linda Knutsson, Niklas Marklund, Pia C. Sundgren, Markus Nilsson

papers.title: Mechanisms of Zener diode and ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction: A novel explanation in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect resulting from infrared self-emission at room-temperature
papers.summary: In textbooks, a quantum-mechanical tunneling mechanism based on electron-wavefunction is used to explain Zener diode as well as ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction. In this study, an attempt in particle description is made to explain these devices. Any object at room-temperature emits infrared (IR) photons. The process of heavy doping can cause many defects. The self-absorption of the IR emission could be achieved through sub-band-gap excitations due to defects, creating carriers. In a heavily doped p-n junction device, some of the IR-generated carriers diffuse into the junction which has a built-in field. The built-in field sweeps out the carriers, creating IR photocurrent. The reverse leakage current of the p-n junction is regarded as the IR photocurrent according to a precedent where impurity-photovoltaic-effect is used to explain circuit devices (arXiv:2510.18226). Heavy doping results in not only a great many IR-generated carriers but also an avalanche effect at low voltage, producing Zener breakdown. Additionally, the impurity-photovoltaic-effect can make a reasonable contribution to explaining the temperature dependence of Zener breakdown. If the doping is very heavy, the heavily doped p-n junction can be altered to create an ohmic contact, which can also be explained in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect. Not only quantum mechanics, but also this photovoltaic mechanism in particle description can explain the above devices. Considering the wave-particle duality, the combination of quantum-mechanical and photovoltaic mechanisms is suggested to explain these devices. Each mechanism plays a big or small role in the explanation.

authors.name: Jianming Li

papers.title: N-Layer quasi-geostrophic modons in a vertically sheared flow
papers.summary: Modons, or dipolar vortices, are a form of propagating vortex solution consisting of two counterrotating regions of fluid and moving together under self-advection. They are common features of the upper ocean that can remain stable over long times, thereby transporting fluid over large distances. Here, we present a semi-analytical method for finding modon solutions in a vertically-sheared background flow using the multi-layer quasi-geostrophic framework. This method works for arbitrarily many fluid layers and builds on our previous studies of multi-layer modon solutions. We present three example of modons in a background flow, highlighting the effect of varying relative potential velocity between layers and the impact of depth-dependent potential vorticity gradients arising from surface deformation and velocity shear.

authors.name: Matthew N. Crowe

papers.title: Efficient high-order Discontinuous Galerkin simulations of multi-species high-enthalpy flows
papers.summary: Numerical simulation of hypersonic vehicles is an attractive approach to investigate the complex phenomena involved in such technologies. For this, second-order finite volume methods (FVM) are the established method in computational fluid dynamics, with the cost of high dissipation in affordable meshes, thus needing refined ones or adaptive mesh refinements techniques to obtain accurate results. An alternative is to make use of high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods, in particular discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM), once it achieves higher formal order of accuracy on element-local polynomial bases. Therefore the goal of this work is to present the numerical simulations of a two-dimensional scramjet configuration to test and verify the applicability of the DGSEM approach for a complex hypersonic flow where shock-shock interactions occur. Results revealed to be in agreement with reference FVM solvers, thus verifying the code implementation.

authors.name: Beatriz Fag\'a, Georgii Oblapenko, Yiyang Zhu, Daniel Doehring, Manuel Torrilhon

papers.title: Is AMOC collapse too unstable in climate models?
papers.summary: It has been a long-held paradigm that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation in coupled climate models is too stable, underestimating the possibility of a collapse. A recent analysis of extended simulations to year 2300 in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project, CMIP6, demonstrated a partial AMOC collapse where the deep circulation completely vanishes. This collapse was simulated by at least one model in all emission scenarios, and it occurred in every model forced by the highest emission scenario when extended to year 2300. Given the modelling community's previous emphasis on stability in climate models, in this perspective, we explore the alternate possible mechanisms by which the AMOC in CMIP6 might have become too unstable. This is motivated by the lack of evidence of downward trends in the AMOC in the observational records, and a subset of CMIP6 models displaying too high climate sensitivity and too strong sensitivity to aerosol removal, both of which could predispose them toward a spurious collapse. For these reasons, it is critical to evaluate the mechanisms by which CMIP6 models simulate AMOC collapse, to be able to develop programs further investigating the trustworthiness of simulated AMOC collapse scenarios.

authors.name: Sybren Drijfhout, Alejandra Sanchez-Franks

papers.title: Dynamics of singular-jet formation during the collapse of drop-impact craters
papers.summary: The collapse of a drop-impact crater that bypasses the pinch-off singularity produces exceptionally thin, high-velocity jets, often referred to as singular-jets. We perform 2D axisymmetric DNS using Basilisk, employing adaptive mesh refinement to capture the intricate flow features. The numerical results for a drop diameter of $3.64$ mm at ambient pressure match the experiments well under different impact conditions. During the crater collapse, qualitatively different dimple shapes form, including an entrapped bubble beneath the dimple. Quantitatively, an entrapped bubble with a diameter of ~210 \mu m and a jet velocity of 61.7 m/s for the singular-jet case during cylindrical dimple collapse is obtained from simulations. Subtle morphological changes in crater evolution distinguish the jetting regime, with a critical angle of 109.2 between the crater side wall and its base in the singular-jet case. The simulation provides insight into the internal flow fields, enabling us to delineate the observed phenomenon. The pressure and velocity fields reveal that the high jetting velocity is associated with the formation and rapid collapse of a nearly cylindrical dimple. The resulting pressure distribution drives a strongly upward flow near the dimple base, while the nearly parallel dimple side walls redirect radial liquid motion towards the axis. We extend the simulations into the post-entrainment region and identify another singular-jet near the upper boundary of the entrainment region. The jet reaches a velocity of 63.93 m/s and exhibits morphological characteristics similar to the first singular-jet case. A regime map is constructed from simulations spanning Weber numbers ranging from 100 to 200 and Froude numbers from 45 to 92; the updated lower and upper boundaries for the entrainment region, based on singular-jet formation, are We = 45.5\, Fr^{0.237} and We = 53.5\, Fr^{0.251}, respectively.

authors.name: Nivesh Mishra, Anikesh Pal

papers.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
papers.summary: Most frameworks for teams of large language model (LLM) agents fix the team's shape inside the software: who talks to whom, how much is passed along, and what a human can do once a run has started. Human-team research has long asked those questions: where team phenomena live (in members or in their interaction), how team-level properties arise, and what separates what a team does from how a team is. I propose using that theory as the organizing lens for configuring, observing and intervening in LLM-agent teams, without assuming its findings transfer. I introduce teamknitt, a framework and open reference implementation in which a user configures a team of 1-16 AI agents for task completion, solution generation, achieving a goal or a research mission; selects one of fourteen deterministic routing topologies or a custom directed graph; chooses a sharing profile that limits what may travel along permitted routes; and binds sources, representations, work dependencies, handoffs and an expertise directory. The recorded process can be observed through non-system views (member reports and behavior) and system views (distributed problem-solving, differentiated transactive memory, interactive coordination, team dynamics). Interventions are explicit and human-led: reviewed reconfiguration between runs, planned disturbances, and private feedback, pause, resume or stop applied at dependency-wave boundaries, with "queued", "applied", "assembled", "understood" and "improved" kept as separate claims. Emergent states such as trust and shared understanding are declared unmeasured. This is an idea and system-description paper with falsifiable hypotheses on topology, information flow and intervention timing, including whether the fractal scaling of communication output between members, and between members on different models, relates to task and team performance. No comparative result is reported.

authors.name: Goran Mitevski

papers.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
papers.summary: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

authors.name: Brendan M. Unikewicz, Joseph E. Bonavia, Ekaterina L. Koelliker, Abigail Klein, Katie C. Spaeth, Hannah M. Varner, S. Kiana Naghibzadeh, Yoav Horev, Sareh Parangi, Tal Cohen

papers.title: Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics-Guided Machine-Learning Potentials for Mapping Nitric Oxide Interactions with Oxygen-Covered Graphite
papers.summary: Exploratory ab initio molecular dynamics is used to construct machine-learning interatomic potentials for NO interactions with highly oriented pyrolytic graphite at 33\% bridge-site oxygen coverage. Representative configurations sampled across surface temperatures and incidence energies provide reference energies and forces for training and validation. The selected potential enables relaxation of 300 adsorption configurations and construction of spatial and angular interaction maps. These maps reveal increasingly restricted attractive regions during vertical approach and reduced short-range repulsion upon molecular reorientation. The resulting adsorption geometries and interaction landscapes guide further first-principles sampling toward refining potentials for NO oxidation dynamics.

authors.name: Yaideny Rodriguez Linares, Gilberto A. Alou Angulo, Samuel Del Fr\'e, Maurice Monnerville, Alejandro Rivero Santamar\'ia

papers.title: Vendor-Agnostic Pseudocontinuous Arterial Spin Labeling Using Pulseq: Cross-Vendor Quantitative Evaluation
papers.summary: Purpose: Inter-scanner variability in cerebral blood flow (CBF) quantification limits reproducibility in multi-center arterial spin labeling (ASL) studies. We developed and validated a vendor-agnostic pseudo-continuous ASL (PCASL) sequence using the open-source Pulseq framework, and assessed its extensibility to advanced perfusion imaging. Methods: A vendor-independent PCASL sequence was implemented in Pulseq and deployed on 3T scanners from Siemens, GE, and United Imaging. Seven healthy volunteers underwent single-post-labeling-delay (PLD) PCASL on all platforms, including test-retest scans. An in-house adapted Siemens vendor-based PCASL sequence served as reference. Reproducibility was assessed using within-subject coefficient of variation (CVwithin), root mean square error (RMSE), regional CBF correlation, and voxel-wise variation ratio maps. Multi-PLD PCASL and planning-free VE-PCASL were implemented as proof-of-concept extensions. Results: Mean gray matter (GM) CBF was similar across implementations. Test-retest GM CVwithin was below 4% on all platforms; Siemens-Pulseq had the lowest value (2.65%), versus 3.64% for the native sequence. GM RMSE between Siemens-Vendor and Pulseq implementations was comparable to test-retest RMSE, and all inter-scanner CVwithin values were below 3%. Voxel-wise variation ratio distributions were centered near 100%, suggesting cross-vendor variability comparable to physiological baseline fluctuations. Multi-PLD and VE-PCASL ran successfully on all platforms, yielding consistent CBF/ATT maps and vascular territory delineations. Conclusion: Pulseq-based PCASL enables vendor-agnostic perfusion imaging with low inter-scanner variability. This open-source approach provides a reproducible, standardized solution for multi-center ASL studies and facilitates deployment of advanced ASL techniques in clinical research.

authors.name: Jianing Zhang, Jun Wang, Joseph G. Woods, Shaoyou Ye, Shuai Ming, Hongwei Li, Wei Hu, Wei Wei, Xiaohu Li, Thomas W. Okell, Yang Ji

papers.title: Effects of pulse durations in atom interferometry with double Raman diffraction
papers.summary: Double Raman diffraction is a key enabling technique for future space missions relying on atom interferometry that offers enhanced sensitivity and intrinsic suppression of systematic effects. This diffraction mechanism naturally arises when employing a retro-reflection configuration in microgravity, but then accelerations can no longer be determined through a frequency-chirp scan. As a consequence, measurements become much more sensitive to systematic effects associated with pulse timing and duration. Indeed, the finite pulse duration can introduce additional phase shifts and small modifications of the arm trajectories, which are critical sources of error in high-precision measurements. In this work, we present the first complete analytical results of these effects for double Raman diffraction, building upon previous work for single diffraction and extending the standard literature. Our analysis determines the impact of finite pulse durations on the full interferometer sequence, quantifying the shifts of the atomic wave packets' trajectories and the acquired phases. The description relies on a comprehensive framework describing matter-wave propagation in terms of central trajectories and centered wave packets, and can be easily incorporated into relativistic treatments. Furthermore, we make use of group theoretic methods that are particularly useful when accounting for residual accelerations and frequency chirps, which are also relevant for ground-based applications. Our study includes time-dependent accelerations and frequency chirps, gravity gradients, retardation effects, AC Stark shifts induced by the Raman pulses, and external forces such those due to magnetic fields or temperature gradients in the black-body radiation.

authors.name: Nadja Augst, Albert Roura

papers.title: Consistent Mapping for Fluid Structure Interaction with Geometrically Nonlinear Isogeometric Beams
papers.summary: Isogeometric beam formulations provide an efficient reduced-dimensional representation of slender structures, combining accurate geometry and high-order continuity with few structural degrees of freedom. Their application to fluid--structure interaction (FSI) requires transferring motion and loads between the one-dimensional beam centerline and the surrounding fluid interface. While mapping strategies exist for conventional finite element beams, geometrically nonlinear isogeometric formulations require operators consistent with their spline-based kinematics and distinct descriptions of cross-sectional rotation. This work develops consistent beam-to-surface mappings for geometrically nonlinear isogeometric Bernoulli and Timoshenko beams in partitioned FSI. Fluid-interface points are attached to the beam in the reference configuration and reconstructed using the nonlinear kinematics of each formulation. Consistent linearization yields a configuration-dependent mapping operator whose transpose ensures work-conjugate load transfer. The formulations are verified through analytical deformation tests, convergence studies, and virtual-work checks, and evaluated in beam-based adaptations of the Mok and Turek--Hron benchmarks and the Goland wing flutter benchmark. The results confirm accurate interface reconstruction and work-conjugate load transfer under large deformations, while demonstrating the applicability of both beam formulations to coupled FSI problems.

authors.name: Juan Ignacio Camarotti, Ricky Aristio, Roland W\"uchner

papers.title: A Dual-Frequency-Constrained Structure-Function Kirchhoff Model for Near-Nadir Ocean Backscatter -- Part I: Theoretical Framework
papers.summary: Most operational near-nadir geophysical model functions (GMFs) are empirical and fitted one radar band at a time, and do not explain the difference between Ku and Ka band. This paper derives a backscatter model in which one local description of the sea surface serves both bands. The near-nadir Kirchhoff integral is written in terms of the elevation difference between two surface points separated by a horizontal lag. The surface then enters through the structure functions of that difference, and the scattering kernel selects the lags each band samples, about 2.5-1.4 cm at Ku and 1.0-0.5 cm at Ka band. Geometric optics is recovered as the quadratic, isotropic limit, without a spectral cutoff. With a logarithmic second-order structure function, one wind-dependent log-slope sets both the incidence shape and the Ku-Ka shape difference, and band transfer reduces to evaluating one curve at a second lag. Same-footprint dual-frequency radar data show that one band alone does not determine this transfer. The log-slope is the level of the short-wave saturation range and grows about as the square of the wind speed; a physical short-wave spectrum reproduces this growth but overestimates the level. Dual-frequency radars thus measure the centimetre-scale roughness level, although they do not separate a scale-dependent structure function from non-Gaussian surface statistics. A companion paper delivers and evaluates the resulting GMF, KuKa-Mod.

authors.name: Alexey S. Mironov, Fr\'ed\'eric Nouguier, Bertrand Chapron

papers.title: Analytic $GW$-Bethe--Salpeter Gradients with Quasiparticle Response in the Resolution of the Identity
papers.summary: Analytic nuclear gradients for excited states from the Bethe$-$Salpeter equation (BSE) in the static screening approximation are presented within this work. The response of the screened interaction to nuclear displacements is treated within the resolution-of-the-identity (RI) approximation, in close analogy to RI random phase approximation gradients, and is folded into the Lagrangian formalism of time-dependent density functional theory gradients. Quasiparticle gradients enter via the full analytic derivative of the corrections for RI contour-deformation $G_0W_0$ and ev$GW$, also taking into account that incomplete quasiparticle spectra are typically supplied. Comparisons to earlier approaches using a geometry-independent fixed quasiparticle correction are made. For the latter, the orbital-rotation terms are derived exactly, too. The implemented gradient scales as $\mathcal{O}(N^4)$, and the three-index integrals are processed in batches with a memory demand of $\mathcal{O}(N_\mathrm{aux}^2 + N_\mathrm{occ}^2 N_\mathrm{aux})$. Excited-state geometries of a set of small molecules are compared to EOM-CCSD references and to TD-DFT. It is shown that the full quasiparticle gradient removes most of the systematic underestimation of the bond lengths in singlet excited states. A comparison along the C$-$C stretch of acetylene shows that the neglected derivative of the quasiparticle corrections is modest, but becomes erratic for $G_0W_0$ near poles of the self-energy, which ev$GW$ avoids.

authors.name: Christof Holzer

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Ising-Bloch Transition in Polarization Cavity Solitons
papers.summary: Polarization cavity solitons in coherently driven Kerr resonators undergo a sequence of dynamical bifurcations as the cavity detuning is increased. Here we show that a stationary localized state containing an Ising wall first becomes a fixed breather and then develops finite chirality and drift motion through a spontaneous non-equilibrium Ising-Bloch transition. Stability analyses identify the modes responsible for the breathing and the motion, revealing controllable dynamics of polarization cavity solitons.

authors.name: Juan Diego Mazo-V\'asquez, Lewis Hill, Flore K. Kunst, Gian-Luca Oppo

papers.title: Frequency-selective membrane-based metamaterial filters for low-insertion-loss harmonic crosstalk suppression in sub-harmonic THz receivers
papers.summary: Parasitic reflections and standing waves fundamentally limit amplitude stability and phase fidelity in coherent continuous-wave (CW) terahertz (THz) systems. We report a complementary metamaterial filter pair designed for frequency-selective isolation at 300 GHz and 600 GHz in sub-harmonic heterodyne architectures. Fabricated on ultra-thin polyimide membranes, the filters provide more than 30 dB stopband isolation while maintaining insertion losses below 1 dB in the passband. System-level coherent-imaging experiments demonstrate effective suppression of spurious-reflection-induced interference effects and improved spectral baseline stability. The filters mitigate wavefront distortions resulting from such interferences and enhance reconstruction robustness. These results establish membrane-based metamaterial filters as compact frequency-selective isolation elements for sub-harmonic heterodyne THz detection and highlight their potential for phase-engineered imaging and sensing applications.

authors.name: Hui Yuan, Meng Zhang, Almila Kura, Daniel Erni, Hartmut G. Roskos

papers.title: A Dual-Frequency-Constrained Structure-Function Kirchhoff Model for Near-Nadir Ocean Backscatter -- Part II: The Practical GMF, KuKa-Mod
papers.summary: Near-nadir radars, from altimeters and rain radars to wave scatterometers, need a geophysical model function (GMF) relating backscatter to wind, yet most operational models are empirical and specific to one band. This paper delivers KuKa-Mod, an operational near-nadir GMF for wind retrieval at Ku and Ka band, built on one physical description of the sea surface, and evaluates it. Following the companion paper (Part I), the additive coefficient and log-slope of a logarithmic surface structure function are fitted jointly to the Ku-band incidence profile of the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) radar and to the same-footprint Ku-Ka shape difference. The model reproduces the Ku profile and reaches the azimuth-averaged Ka profile with no additional shape parameter and one fitted level, largely explained by the seawater dielectric and the clear-sky attenuation. Against scatterometer winds the Ka-Ku difference holds to within 0.3 dB up to 25 m/s, whereas the near-nadir Ka wind sensitivity is about 20% too weak. An empirical correction measured against the same winds sets the operational high-wind level of both bands, validated to 20 m/s. Without a sea-state coefficient, a long-wave tilt predicts where the response to significant wave height changes sign at Ku band, a tilt that CFOSAT/SWIM confirms, and the azimuth harmonics are reproduced once a sensor-dependent offset is removed. The operational model is released as parameters, an evaluator and look-up tables ready for retrieval processors.

authors.name: Alexey S. Mironov, Fr\'ed\'eric Nouguier, Bertrand Chapron

papers.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
papers.summary: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

authors.name: Dusan Sarenac, Charles W. Clark, Owen Lailey, Muhammad Arif, Wangchun Chen, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, Joachim Nsofini, Dmitry A. Pushin

papers.title: Damped polarizability and first hyperpolarizability of large systems with hybrid functionals: self-consistent and Lanczos solvers
papers.summary: We present a damped coupled-perturbed Kohn-Sham method to compute the dynamical polarizability and first hyperpolarizability of finite systems, implemented in the CRYSTAL code for semi-local, global and range-separated hybrid functionals. The approach is based on the adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory for the complex-valued (hyper)polarizabilities, describing optical phenomena such as absorption, and the nonlinear second-harmonic generation, rectification and Pockels effect. These are obtained either at individual frequencies with a self-consistent solver based on Pulay extrapolation, or at an arbitrary grid of frequency and damping factors with a Lanczos solver, from which the first-order amplitudes required in the hyperpolarizability can be reconstructed. With hybrid functionals, the self-consistent solver tends to become impractical at some point beyond the absorption onset, where there are many excitations for which the external frequency lies between their energy and those of their contributing single-particle transitions, and its convergence eventually stalls for large systems. In contrast, the convergence of the Lanczos method is essentially independent of size, hence the cost of the dynamical response calculation scales with system size as the hybrid ground-state calculation. The implementation is validated in a small molecule and, as an application, we study the first and second-order optical response of a series of hexagonal boron nitride flakes of up to 324 atoms. The use of range-separated hybrid functionals allows to capture the strongly-bound first excitation of the monolayer, and evidences the failure of the self-consistent method to converge excitations with strong electron-hole attraction.

authors.name: A. Garc\'ia-Bl\'azquez, A. Erba, A. Boccuni, J. K. Desmarais

papers.title: The Weight Is in the Reading: Hidden States in Memristors, Memlumors, and Electrochemical Transistors
papers.summary: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. Building on Chua's formulation of memristive systems, we separate the state variable, which evolves with the excitation history, from the observation map that converts it into a measured signal, and we define the weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol. Three platforms show the consequences: a memristor, in which the same voltage writes and reads; a memlumor, in which light both modifies the state and produces the photoluminescence that reports it; and an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT), in which the gate writes and the channel reads. In the transistor, two states prepared by different histories give the same channel current at a specific drain bias and become distinguishable again when the bias is changed, while the stored charge persists and the gate current continues to separate them. Published experiments provide precedents: a drain-bias-dependent cancellation of the OECT transient, and trapped charges in perovskite memlumors that are invisible to conventional time-resolved photoluminescence but revealed by a read-write-read sequence. A synaptic weight is therefore not a property of the material alone but of the material together with its readout, and reports of synaptic behavior should specify what is stored, what is measured, and how one is inferred from the other.

authors.name: Gonzalo Rivera-Sierra, Heyi Zhang, Daiki Nishioka, Takashi Tsuchiya, Juan Bisquert

papers.title: OCEAN: A Five-Phase Framework for Meaningful Change
papers.summary: Managing meaningful change requires more than motivation, insight, or isolated techniques. This paper introduces OCEAN, a five-phase conceptual framework for structuring nonclinical developmental conversations and change-oriented work in coaching and in the practice of leaders and HR professionals. The five phases are Observe, Create, Expose, Awaken, and Nurture. In Observe, individuals develop a systemic, present-oriented understanding of the situation. In Create, they turn that understanding into goals that are meaningful and actionable. In Expose, they identify the attempted solutions that maintain the difficulty they are meant to remove, along with the resistances, biases, and self-deceptions that keep them in place. In Awaken, they activate new behaviors through planning, reframing, paradoxical movement, and emotionally significant experiences. In Nurture, they consolidate progress through repetition, habits, connection, and sustainable contexts. OCEAN integrates insights from systemic and interactional thinking, goal construction, emotional awareness, and habit consolidation into a structured process.

authors.name: A. Fronzetti Colladon

papers.title: First demonstration of long-distance electron drift in liquid xenon with the Xenoscope time projection chamber
papers.summary: Xenoscope is a dual-phase xenon time projection chamber operated at the University of Zurich to investigate electron transport over distances relevant to the next-generation XLZD (XENON-LUX-ZEPLIN-DARWIN) observatory. We demonstrate electron drift over $2.6$ m in liquid xenon using cosmic-muon-induced ionization signals. External muon tagging provides a timing reference for charge produced at known depths, while the endpoint of the average electroluminescence waveform probes transport over the full drift length. We measure electron drift velocities of $(1.320 \pm 0.006)$ mm/$\mu$s at $(80.92 \pm 0.36)$ V/cm and $(1.436 \pm 0.001)$ mm/$\mu$s at $(96.00 \pm 0.42)$ V/cm. These results establish detectable charge transport over meter-scale distances and provide an experimental benchmark for the development of future large liquid-xenon time projection chambers.

authors.name: N. Angelides, M. Babicz, E. E. Barillier, L. Baudis, H. Birch, C. Capelli, J. J. Cuenca-Garc\'ia, S. George, R. N. Hampp, M. A. Hernandez, L. H\"otzsch, F. J\"org, K. Mor{\aa}, M. Noia, S. Ouahada, B. Penning, F. Piastra

papers.title: Experimental Evidence of Cellular Sparing under Single-Pulse Picosecond Irradiation at Extreme Dose Rates
papers.summary: Understanding how biological cells respond to radiation delivered on extremely short timescales is central to resolving the fundamental mechanisms underlying radiotherapy and to defining new regimes of radiobiology. Experimentally accessing these earliest stages of physicochemical response is crucial to benchmark current numerical codes, whose predictions are known to vary substantially with under-constrained early-stage parameters. Using a laser-driven electron source, tunable doses up to 8Gy were delivered to normal and cancer human cell lines, in single pulses of picosecond-scale duration at mean dose rates above 10^10 Gy/s. Clonogenic survival assays and 53BP1 foci formation were compared with conventional X-ray irradiation at 2.4Gy/min. Surviving fractions are found to be comparable to conventional irradiation at doses up to 3Gy. At higher doses, however, all cell lines exhibited a consistent increase in surviving fraction, corresponding to an average RBE at 10% survival of 0.84+/-0.05. This sparing effect is associated with a statistically significant reduction in the beta parameter of the linear-quadratic model, indicating reduced cell killing from accumulated sub-lethal damage. Picosecond irradiation also produced a marked reduction in prompt 53BP1 foci, but no significant difference in residual foci at 24h and foci-size distributions. These results provide the first experimental evidence of cellular sparing following single-pulse picosecond-scale irradiation. Direct comparison with recent work at femtosecond timescales suggests the presence of a previously undetected sharp transition in biological response at the femtosecond/picosecond interface, giving critical insight on the possible mechanisms responsible for this differential response.

authors.name: H. Maguire, C. A. McAnespie, P. Chaudhary, L. Corrigan, T. Foster, S. J. McMahon, D. P. Molloy, G. Nersisyan, N. OConnor, K. M. Prise, G. Schettino, G. Sarri

papers.title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
papers.summary: Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/\Delta t$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $\Delta t$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias: past a turnaround step, refining the step increases the error, in FP64 as in FP32. For a model oscillator the analysis predicts the floor and the FP32-to-FP64 ratios of turnaround step and minimum error within 30%. Our remedy needs no FP64 arithmetic: each state variable is stored as the unevaluated sum of two FP32 numbers, updated with error-free transformations, while every right-hand-side evaluation stays in FP32. Unlike compensated summation, it needs no rewriting of the scheme. In model problems from geophysical flow, mechanical dynamics and celestial mechanics, with five Runge-Kutta and multistep schemes, it restores design-order convergence to the floor. In large-eddy simulations of a high-lift airplane wing on three refined grids, up to 544 million cells, with time steps $\Delta t$, $\Delta t/2$ and $\Delta t/4$, FP32 overpredicts the lift by 2.1, 4.5 and 7.7%, while the two-float lift agrees with FP64 within 0.3% on every grid, and on graphics processing units the production solver runs 1.6 to 2.7 times faster than FP64.

authors.name: Michael F. Barad

papers.title: On the Seven-particle Clusters of Lennard-Jones and Thomson
papers.summary: In this Letter, we develop a graph-geometric framework and prove that the pentagonal bipyramid (PBP) is the unique global minimiser of both the seven-particle Lennard-Jones energy in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the seven-charge Thomson energy on $S^2$, up to rigid symmetries and particle relabelling. For the Thomson problem, this strengthens a recent deterministic global-optimality certificate to numerical tolerance into an exact global-optimality and uniqueness theorem. A weak-interaction graph, defined by thresholding pair geometry, organises configuration space without imposing symmetry or discarding any pair interaction. For Lennard-Jones, pair-energy counting, graph classification, subset bounds, and force balance reduce all possible minimisers to 29 bounded domains; exact geometric certificates exclude 28, localise the survivor near the PBP, and a uniform restoring-energy estimate proves uniqueness. The Thomson proof follows the same progression: graph reduction, geometric localisation, and rigidity, but finalises through whole-domain coercivity and a global localisation theorem. The same fivefold order therefore emerges in two very different physical settings: an unconstrained cluster with a preferred bond length and purely repelling charges confined to a sphere, showing a common geometric organising principle for seven particles that is not tied to either interaction.

authors.name: Li Shen

papers.title: Two-dimensional liquid-like order in a confined population of swimming Eudorina colonies
papers.summary: Swimming microorganisms accumulate at boundaries, but the spatial statistics of the resulting layers are rarely measured. We report a population of colonial green algae, of order 71 $\mu$m across, that accumulates against the rigid upper wall of a closed 1-2 mm chamber and holds a two-dimensional non-contacting arrangement for about 105 min. The pair correlation function has a first shell at $r/\bar{D} = 1.73$, $g = 4.8$; a hard-disc null at the same area fraction reaches only $g = 2.1$, so the ordering is not excluded volume alone. Nearest-neighbour separation is $1.80 \pm 0.13$ diameters. The bond-orientational order parameter is $\langle|\psi_6|\rangle = 0.456$ against 0.385 for the null, only 36% of interior colonies are six-coordinated, and the orientational correlation $g_6(r)$ decays over 1.5 diameters with $\eta_6 = 1.31$ against the hexatic bound of 1/4: the arrangement is a two-dimensional liquid, not a crystal or a hexatic. Colonies execute a persistent random walk with reorientation time 1.4-1.7 s at Reynolds number $\sim 9\times 10^{-4}$. Breakup begins at 127 min. Thermal convection is excluded on Rayleigh-number grounds. Caveats: the length calibration is nominal rather than metrological, and this is a single population observed once. All data and code are deposited.

authors.name: Nicholas Tufillaro

papers.title: Interception Focusing of Colloid Transport in Granular Porous Media
papers.summary: Colloid transport and retention in environmental granular porous media underlie groundwater resource protection from, and remediation using, biological and non-biological nano- and micro-particles (colloids). During transport, colloids periodically intercept grain surfaces and translate along them at separation distances across several tens of nm corresponding to the secondary minimum between the opposing forces of longer-range of van der Waals (VDW) attraction and shorter-range electric double layer (EDL) repulsion. Relatively weak diffusive translation of colloids supports their continued translation in secondary minimum association until they are expelled to bulk fluid at rear flow stagnation zones on grain leeward sides. We herein show that this dynamic focuses colloids into a network of fluid streamlines (incomplete mixing lamellae) that enhances their subsequent likelihood of interception with downgradient grains, i.e., increases the so-called collector efficiency (typically denoted by Greek letter eta). Interception focusing of colloids in granular porous media explains well-observed outcomes of colloid transport under environmental conditions, including nonmonotonic nonexponential profiles of retained colloids and the non-Markovian nature of extended tailing of low colloid concentrations following initial elution. Interception focusing is a fundamental process that distinguishes colloids from solutes and renders inapplicable to colloids the assumption that is often invoked for solutes of complete pore scale mixing in granular porous media.

authors.name: William P. Johnson (University of Utah, Geology and Geophysics, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA), Noah G. Willis (University of Utah, Geology and Geophysics, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA), Luis A. Ullauri (University of Utah, Geology and Geophysics, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA), Bashar M. Al-Zghoul (University of California Davis, Civil and Environ. Eng., Davis, California, USA), Diogo Bolster (University of Notre Dame, Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Sciences, Notre Dame, Indiana, United States)

papers.title: Rapid Antigen Detection Tests Empowered by Cholesteric Spherical Reflectors for Expanded Capabilities
papers.summary: While Rapid Antigen Detection Tests (RADTs) have proved their value in point-of-care detection of respiratory diseases, their poor-contrast readout limits their use at early stages of infection where viral concentrations are low, and most RADTs test only for one disease, leaving a sick patient ignorant in case of a negative result. We explore the potential of Cholesteric Spherical Reflectors (CSRs) as enhanced optical labeling probes for RADTs, leveraging their circularly polarized reflections to maximize contrast by background subtraction and thereby lower the analyte concentration required for detection. Moreover, we demonstrate how the ease in tuning the CSR reflection color and the freedom to choose between right- and left-handed circularly polarized reflection allow us to design CSRs to distinguish optically between multiple diseases, eventually enabling RADTs capable of screening for a set of multiple diseases in a single test. We develop a method for functionalizing CSRs with appropriate antibodies and we propose a new type of RADT specifically designed for use with CSRs as detection label, demonstrating that the comparatively large size of CSRs (tens of microns in diameter) does not prevent viral analytes to tether them to an antibody-coated test surface. The strength of the optical CSR signal quantitatively reflects the antigen concentration.

authors.name: Chih-Chieh Chien, Yan-Song Zhang, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Conrotte, Carole L. Linster, Sivashankar Krishnamoorthy, Jan P. F. Lagerwall

papers.title: Manufacturing Complex Structures Through Interfacial Self-Organization
papers.summary: Conventional manufacturing constructs three-dimensional geometries through localized material deposition, removal, or shaping, with fabrication effort greatly increasing with geometric complexity. Here, we introduce a manufacturing approach in which target geometry is encoded into sparse wireframe scaffolds that guide liquid self-organization through interfacial forces. We apply a computational framework that approximates arbitrary target geometries using constant-mean-curvature surface domains and extracts their boundaries to construct the scaffolds. Under neutral buoyancy conditions, curable liquids injected into these scaffolds self-organize into the prescribed geometries, which are subsequently solidified into mechanically isotropic structures with optically smooth surfaces. We demonstrate the fabrication of complex anatomical models and topology-optimized structures featuring intricate branching geometries, internal cavities, and integrated materials. This approach opens new possibilities for scalable fabrication of complex geometric designs.

authors.name: Jacob Garrett, Abhinit Sati, Edward Chien, Emily Whiting, Valeri Frumkin

papers.title: A liquid implant that grows into a stable scaffold in situ
papers.summary: Endovascular embolization requires materials that can pass through narrow microcatheters yet form stable, conformal occlusions within irregular vascular lesions, but reconciling these competing requirements remains challenging. Here we report a wirelessly activated liquid precursor whose final architecture is constructed only after target localization. A gallium-based liquid metal containing iron microparticles and gas microcavities remains deformable, magnetically navigable, and retrievable before activation. Wireless induction heating activates the internal reactive microenvironment, coupling gas-driven microcavity growth with oxidative mineralization of newly generated gallium interfaces to form a porous, self-supporting scaffold. In aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation models, activation enabled durable occlusion, aneurysm-neck healing, and six-month stability in a porcine aneurysm model. These findings establish post-delivery construction as a strategy for creating stable therapeutic implants from minimally invasive liquid precursors.

authors.name: Wenqiang Li, Qichen Peng, Fuhong Wang, Zhentan Quan, Shengxiang Cai, Zhuoming Zhou, Jin Zhang, Ting Liu, Xuanping Xie, Lin Zhu, Bo Wang, Shuang Wang, Yuan An, Yingtong Zhou, Zirong Liu, Haohui Li, Songshen Li, Ben Wang, Xinjian Yang, Quanshui Zheng, Hongzhang Wang

papers.title: Conductance scaling in nanopore arrays: disentangling roles of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry
papers.summary: The scaling of electrical conductance with the number of nanopores, $N$, in an array is of fundamental importance for applications in membrane separation and ion transport across biological membranes, and has been the subject of longstanding disagreement in the field. Combining finite element calculations with theory, we resolve this disagreement for pores with negligible surface charge by showing that two previously conflicting predictions are each correct in their own limiting reservoir geometry: cuboidal reservoirs commensurate with the interpore spacing, for which the conductance scales linearly with $N$, and infinite reservoirs, for which the scaling is sublinear in $N$ for closely spaced pores. We show the transition between these limits with increasing reservoir size and, for infinite reservoirs, we show that a simple analytical model from electrical contact theory is mathematically equivalent to an existing point-charge capacitance model for nanopore arrays and validate its applicability against finite element and method-of-moments calculations. Using this model, we derive a characteristic coupling length, $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$, the interpore spacing at which the array conductance reaches $95\%$ of that of the same number of independent pores. $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$ scales linearly with pore diameter $d$, and grows with $N$ as $\sim\log N$ for linear arrays and $\sim\sqrt{N}$ for square arrays, so that pore coupling persists to surprisingly large separations in large arrays. Our work provides a general framework for predicting nanopore array conductance as a function of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry, of importance to nanofluidics research and the targeted design of functional devices.

authors.name: Jacob Bair, Zachery Gottshall, Matthias Kuehne

papers.title: Exceptional Topological Bound States in the Continuum
papers.summary: Topological phases, exceptional points, and bound states in the continuum (BICs) are three key concepts in condensed matter and classical wave physics. Their pairwise combinations have yielded a rich variety of intriguing singular modes, but the triple merger--exceptional topological BICs (ET-BICs)--has yet to be explored. In this Letter, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a universal approach for constructing such elusive exceptional structures. The system consists of four coupled topological chains: y-mirror stacking generates pairs of topological BICs, while z-stacking with biased loss yields a generalized mirror symmetry under which each pair--separated in different subspaces until their collapse--merges into an ET-BIC at a critical loss. Experimentally, using an acoustic platform with electrically tunable loss, we not only directly observe the coalescence of eigenenergies but also the coalescence of eigenstates, offering a complete verification of the ET-BIC formation. The triply synergistic ET-BICs may pave the way for wave devices that simultaneously demand robustness, sensitivity, and BIC confinement.

authors.name: Luohong Liu, Qicheng Zhang, Shuaishuai Tong, Chunyin Qiu

papers.title: Pelletization Pressure Engineering of the Superconducting Properties of Fluorine-Doped PrFeAsO
papers.summary: We investigate the influence of the pelletization pressure on the structural, microstructural, and superconducting properties of fluorine-doped PrFeAsO0.7F0.3 (Pr1111). Precursor powders are pressed into pellets at pressures ranging from 174 to 1131 MPa, after which the applied pressure is released and all samples undergo an identical two-step conventional synthesis process at ambient pressure (CSP-AP). All samples predominantly exhibit the tetragonal P4/nmm structure, and the lattice parameter a and unit-cell volume V decrease with increasing pelletization pressure up to an intermediate-pressure range (~900 MPa) before increasing at higher pressures. The actual fluorine-content derived from energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) also increase with pelletization pressure, while Raman spectra show only modest variations in the characteristic vibrational modes associated with Fe and As. The superconducting response exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the pelletization pressure. Among the investigated samples, the sample pelletized at 870 MPa exhibits the most favorable overall superconducting properties, with a superconducting onset temperature of 44.2 K, ~5 K higher than that of the lowest-pressure sample. It also displays a narrower superconducting transition, the highest relative sample density, a favorable effective magnetic critical current density at high fields, and a relatively large effective thermally activated flux-flow activation energy. At higher pelletization pressures, the superconducting response deteriorates, coinciding with increases in the lattice parameters, increased secondary-phase contributions, and reduced relative density. These findings establish the pelletization pressure as a relevant processing parameter for modifying the structural, microstructural and superconducting properties of Pr1111 during CSP-AP.

authors.name: Jayant Kumar, Konrad Kwatek, Tatiana Zajarniuk, Taras Palasyuk, Yaroslaw Konopelnyk, Tomasz Cetner, Cezariusz Jastrz\k{e}bski, Shiv J. Singh

papers.title: Delta-Corrected Shot Reduction for Bypassing Optimization Plateaus in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.summary: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) remains a cornerstone hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for quantum simulation, yet its scalability is fundamentally constrained by heavy measurement overheads. While strategies such as variance-preserved shot reduction (VPSR) mitigates this cost, they suffer from convergence instability and optimization stagnation caused by finite-sample bias in limited pilot shots. To overcome this limitation, we introduce delta-corrected shot reduction (DCSR), an analytically enhanced shot allocation strategy that rigorously mitigates finite-sample instability. Utilizing the multivariate delta method, we derive explicit higher-order bias correction terms for the empirical reduction factor. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations reveal that incorporating higher-order statistical moments, such as skewness and kurtosis, provides the gradient resolution necessary to bypass noise-induced barren plateaus. DSCR significantly accelerates convergence compared to standard VPSR across diverse noise and resource regimes while matching or decreasing cumulative measurement costs, establishing a mathematically rigorous framework for variance-stabilized shot allocation on near-term hardware.

authors.name: Jamie Evander Ghozaly, Pekik Nurwantoro, Gagus Ketut Sunnardianto, Yanoar P. Sarwono, Leong-Chuan Kwek

papers.title: Engineering a digital acoustic black hole
papers.summary: We show how to design and build an analogue black hole as a synchronous digital circuit. We define the sound speed, the flow and the horizon of such a circuit in terms of its own logic, and realise one on a field-programmable gate array, where the black hole is probed electrically with a signal generator and an oscilloscope. We measure the stability of the horizon, its causal cone, the ringdown and rotational superradiance. A single flipped bit inside the horizon leaks out by an amount that falls exponentially with depth. Digital circuits thus form a reconfigurable class of gravitational analogues and realise an analogue black hole as a cellular automaton.

authors.name: Antonino Flachi

papers.title: Is price-impact decay statistically identifiable by propagator estimation? Diffusive prices force the inferred kernel to be transient and fine-tuned
papers.summary: Despite the long memory of market-order flow, price dynamics remain diffusive---a seemingly paradoxical coexistence known in econophysics as the diffusivity puzzle. The propagator model has long been regarded as a promising solution: price impact decays in time, finely balanced against the order-flow memory, and propagators inferred from data have been reported to be consistent with this fine balance. Here we prove a no-go theorem: asymptotic impact decay is not statistically identifiable by propagator estimation, since for diffusive prices the fine-tuned decay is returned whether or not the true impact decays. It rests on universal theorems for the Wiener--Hopf deconvolution by which propagators are inferred under long-memory order flow: (i) the inferred propagator is necessarily transient, even when the true impact is permanent; (ii) under a mild condition, it decays with the fine-balance exponent, fixed by the order-flow autocorrelation alone. The fine-tuned decay is thus a property of the deconvolution, not evidence of impact decay. We demonstrate this with an exactly solvable null model that retains order splitting and the square-root law but whose impact is strictly permanent: the inferred propagator shows an artificial fine-tuned decay although the true impact never decays. Nonlinear propagator estimation, being of Wiener--Hopf type, is subject to the same theorems whenever true metaorders have long memory.

authors.name: Shunta Fujiwara, Yuki Sato, Kiyoshi Kanazawa

papers.title: Stochastic Acceleration Downstream of Astrophysical Shocks
papers.summary: Generation and evolution of turbulence at shock fronts are crucial aspects of the process of particle acceleration in different classes of sources. Here we aim at describing the fate of non-thermal particles and turbulence in the downstream region of an astrophysical shock, both in the case in which turbulence is solely produced upstream and advected through the shock and in the case in which additional turbulence is injected downstream. In particular we will provide an estimate of the effect of stochastic acceleration on particles accelerated at the shock and then advected behind it. The calculations will be specialized to supernova remnant shocks. The temporal evolution of the particle distribution function downstream of the shock and the power spectrum of the turbulent perturbations are both followed by solving numerically the transport equations for the two quantities, accounting for the damping of waves due to the particles that resonantly interact with them, which makes the problem non-linear. Our calculations show that, if waves are only self-generated upstream via Bell instability, they are not able to significantly modify the particle spectrum in the downstream region. Additionally, turbulent cascading in $k$-space quickly drains their energy, further limiting the stochastic acceleration of particles. If, on the other hand, there are additional sources of turbulence downstream, then these waves can contribute meaningfully to second order Fermi acceleration and alter the spectrum of particles. This may reflect in the spectrum of gamma radiation produced through $pp$ scattering downstream. Although second order Fermi acceleration is typically slower than diffusive shock acceleration, particles are expected to stay downstream of shocks for much longer times during which stochastic acceleration can modify their spectrum and affect the spectra of multi-messenger emissions.

authors.name: Antonio Capanema, Pasquale Blasi

papers.title: A new approach to measuring both the steady flow curve and the planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids using exponential shear
papers.summary: We revisit the protocol known as Exponential Shear (ES), first proposed by Doshi and Dealy in 1986. This is a transient strong flow that can be readily imposed in the laboratory using commercial strain-controlled (separate motor and transducer) rheometers which accurately measure both the (exponentially) time-varying torque and normal force exerted by the sample. Numerous studies over the years have proposed competing definitions of an appropriate material function for reporting data obtained from the exponentially time-varying imposed deformation. We revisit this unresolved challenge and carefully reconsider the exponential material kinematics involved and the proper definition of the corresponding material functions. We show that by understanding the time-varying eigenvalues and eigenvectors of both the shearing kinematics and the evolving state of stress in the sample it is, in fact, possible to use an exponential shear test to quantitatively map out \textit{both} the full flow curve (of shear viscosity vs. shear rate) and the steady planar extensional viscosity curve as a function of deformation rate. These findings are supported by numerical simulations of a number of nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive models, asymptotic analysis, as well as experiments with several polymeric liquids.

authors.name: Nicholas King, Eugene Pashkovski, Reid Patterson, Gareth H. McKinley

papers.title: Lifting mechanical zero modes without dispersion
papers.summary: Floppy frameworks carry flat bands of zero-frequency mechanisms with no finite-frequency resonance, and couplings that lift them usually spread them. We show that an on-site tensor lifts a mechanism band without first-order dispersion exactly when, projected onto the mechanisms, it acts as wavevector-independent scalars on orthogonal pieces. Three structures achieve this: local normal modes, invariant symmetry sectors, and a balance law. A mechanism moves both ends of every bond between two vertex classes equally along it, and where the inter-class bond tensors are class scalars this balance law fixes its norm shares and hence the flat value from geometry alone. For the fluorite net the band lies outside the tensor spectrum, at 14/9 of the contact stiffness to first order, and stays flat to all orders in a fixed cage. A placement inside a tiling dual that keeps the common symmetry supplies such tensors, because each contact star inherits its site symmetry. Ten catalogued dual pairs lift flat; half are eigenvalue cases a resolved count matches, and the balance law explains flat bands in random cages too. Duality makes the rigid cage common. In a printable beam-frame lattice, contacts that lock joint rotation remove first-order bending dispersion whenever bonded mechanisms are orthogonal local normals.

authors.name: Joohan Nam

papers.title: A Witness for Quantum Correlations Using Nonlinear Spectroscopy
papers.summary: The ability to detect and quantify entanglement in molecular systems is essential for understanding their quantum correlations and to evaluating molecules as platforms for quantum technologies. Here we show how signals from existing spectroscopic techniques can provide sufficient information to witness entanglement. The main ingredient is a spectroscopic map from admissible quantum states to a finite-dimensional space of signal coefficients, which are expectation values of state-independent effective observables. The molecular response model and measurement protocol determine the effective observables for a fixed system bipartition, and the spectroscopic map defines sets of joint expectation values compatible with all admissible quantum states and their separable subset.
