We illustrate the construction of the effective observables and their expectation value sets using rotational invariants and the spectral structure of optical signals. Fluorescence dynamics and photon coincidences provide a complementary example. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for entanglement certification with established spectroscopic techniques.

authors.name: Julia Liebert, Gregory D. Scholes

papers.title: Odd Darcy Law: Odd Viscosity and Edge Currents in Porous Media
papers.summary: We derive and numerically validate an odd Darcy law for chiral active fluids in porous media, in which an antisymmetric permeability tensor induces a flow transverse to the applied pressure gradient. We identify two distinct mechanisms leading to this odd response: odd viscosity in the fluid or the nonlinear coupling of edge currents to inertia. We then show how the transverse transport depends on porosity, boundary friction, and chirality.

authors.name: Raphael Maire, Ignacio Pagonabarraga

papers.title: Foreshortening of Polarizer Angles in Wide Field Polarizing Imagers
papers.summary: The Polarimeter to Unify Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) is a very wide field polarizing imager covering a 90 degree diameter region of the sky, stitched together from four individual fields of view (FOVs), three of which are supported by Wide Field Imagers (WFIs) with 40 degree diameter individual FOVs. The science objective requires precise measurement of linear polarization. The WFI FOV is sufficiently wide that polarizer angles are foreshortened by projection effects relative to the line of sight of each pixel in the instrument, deviating from their nominal angular positions of -60, 0, and +60 degree relative to the instrument frame of reference. These angles are foreshortened by the very wide WFI field of view, changing their effective angle across the image plane - an effect that is analogous to similar challenges of polarimetric right/left channel separation in large-format 3D cinema, such as the IMAX format. Using a simple geometrical approach we estimated the perceived polarizer angle in the WFI FOV will vary by +/-2.5 degree for +/-60 degree and +/-3.5 degree for 0 degree polarizer angles. We present the effect of this deviation on the polarized brightness to be recorded by WFI, along with how optical distortion will shift the location of foreshortened angles. We also discuss the implications of this effect on upcoming technologies based on polarimetry across in wide fields.

authors.name: Ritesh Patel, J. Marcus Hughes, C. E. DeForest, Daniel B. Seaton, Chris Lowder, Matthew J. West

papers.title: Stanley Deser 19th March 1931 - 21st April 2023
papers.summary: Stanley Deser was Ancell Professor Emeritus at Brandeis University and Visiting Professor at the California Institute of Technology. He was a world-renowned theoretical physicist whose accomplishments include the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) formulation of general relativity, supergravity with Zumino, the dynamics of flat space with Jackiw and 't Hooft and many other contributions to the quantum theory of gravity. In the 1980s he was instrumental in securing National Science Foundation approval of the LIGO gravitational wave experiment against much opposition. He was awarded the Einstein Medal in 2015 for important contributions to general relativity, in particular the development of the ADM formalism. Other awards include: The Dannie Heineman Prize 1994; Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences 1994; Honorary Member of the Torino Academy of Sciences 2001; Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences 1979, Fellow of the American Institute of Physics.

authors.name: M. J. Duff, K. S. Stelle

papers.title: Ergotropy as distance from equilibrium
papers.summary: We show that the ergotropy (a.k.a available energy) of a thermally isolated system is the $1$-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions. Specifically, between the energy profile of the system state, and the energy profile of its associated passive state. We prove this for both classical and quantum systems, and illustrate it with examples. Our result formalises the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium

authors.name: Michele Campisi

papers.title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
papers.summary: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

authors.name: Chunlong Li, Shien Yang, Yiwei Huang, Yu Zhang, Fei Xue

papers.title: Solar cycle variations of meridional flow and differential rotation in a non-kinematic dynamo model
papers.summary: Flux transport dynamo models have emerged as the leading paradigm for explaining the observed solar cycle. However, most of these models are kinematic and axisymmetric. We develop a non-kinematic dynamo model by specifying large-scale flows, such as the differential rotation and meridional flow. Thus, our model does not require the $\Lambda$ effect or other parameterisations of turbulent transport to generate the large-scale flows; it only solves the fluctuating flows and thermodynamics. Our model is inherently 3D by construction, although it is currently operating in axisymmetric mode because the source for poloidal field generation (Babcock-Leighton $\alpha$) is assumed to be axisymmetric. Our model reproduces solar-cycle variations in both the meridional flow and the differential rotation -- specifically, the torsional oscillation in some agreement with observations. The model naturally exhibits some variability in the solar cycle, even without incorporating stochastic fluctuations, offering a new methodology for modelling the non-kinematic solar dynamo in 3D.

authors.name: Bidya Binay Karak, Mark Miesch

papers.title: A Microscopic Model Underpinning Macroscopic QED in Active Media
papers.summary: We establish a microscopic foundation for macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in active media. Starting from a driven three-level system, we derive an effective two-level description with nonequilibrium stationary populations and employ a quantum central limit approach to obtain collective Langevin dynamics. This construction yields the electromagnetic susceptibility and quantum noise-current correlations from the same microscopic stationary state, providing a direct connection to the reservoir operators of conventional macroscopic quantum electrodynamics. We show that the optical response is governed by the population difference, whereas the noise correlations depend separately on the populations of the two levels. Consequently, at optical transparency, the imaginary part of the susceptibility vanishes while quantum fluctuations remain finite. We interpret the resulting noise statistics in terms of an effective reservoir occupation and a purification involving two vacuum modes, and establish a corresponding effective-temperature fluctuation--dissipation relation. Finally, we demonstrate that the residual fluctuations at transparency can induce finite heating of a nearby quantum probe.

authors.name: Daigo Oue

papers.title: The AI research space shapes country academic performance
papers.summary: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have demonstrated great potential across diverse domains, prompting increasing attention to understanding the AI ecosystem. As knowledge production is often perceived as a process of connecting existing pieces of knowledge, mapping the interconnections of AI knowledge is crucial for unraveling the dynamics of scientific production in AI. However, maps created so far have fallen short of capturing knowledge relatedness, focusing instead on citation relationships between subfields. Here, we build an AI research space by connecting pairs of AI research topics based on their proximity measured through author-topic coupling. Projections of country level performances onto the space reveal that countries exhibit distinct baskets of specializations. We further examine the role of the structure of the AI research space in the scientific development of nations. We find that countries are more likely to gain specialization in topics that have high proximity to already specialized neighbor topics, and that publications whose topics align more with the developed topics in the country are more likely to become high impact. Our results highlight the AI development gaps across nations and the path-dependence in the development induced by the AI research space.

authors.name: Siyi Zhou, Tianxing Pan, Qing Ke

papers.title: More particles or the pair? An exact test of how to improve mode-coupling theory
papers.summary: How a dense liquid arrests into a glass remains a central problem in physics. Mode-coupling theory (MCT), the leading microscopic theory of the glass transition, fails to reproduce mean-field caging. Two routes are proposed to repair it: tracking more-particle correlations, or enforcing repulsion within each colliding pair. Testing both on an exact benchmark liquid, we show that MCT lets touching spheres pass through each other at all orders: adding particles dilutes memory and worsens the transition, whereas restoring pair impenetrability recovers mean-field arrest and the cage size.

authors.name: Hu Cang

papers.title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. These approaches include atlas-based label propagation, convolutional architectures, promptable foundation models, and, most recently, vision-language models (VLMs), which integrate clinical text with volumetric segmentation. Each methodological generation has addressed limitations of its predecessor while introducing new ones. A substantial gap remains between research progress and clinical deployment, as routine workflows continue to be dominated by atlas-based and narrow task-specific deep-learning tools, which remain strong baselines in geometric overlap metrics but are highly rigid in terms of application, versatility, portability, and interpretability. As contouring systems further grow in complexity, conventional geometric overlap metrics become insufficient, motivating evaluation paradigms that incorporate surface-based, dosimetric, and prompt-adherence assessment. Emerging agentic architectures that combine large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and vision-language segmentation modules are leading towards more flexible, guideline-aware, interactive contouring workflows. These systems could automate flexible and interpretable knowledge-based contouring and actively support the clinical reasoning underlying target volume definition.

authors.name: Josef A. Buchner, Richard Osuala, Ayhan Can Erdur, Melissa C. Olufs, Stephanie E. Combs, Jan C. Peeken

papers.title: Spatial effects of Kuramoto modeling on the power-grid frequencies
papers.summary: Spatial coupling and heterogeneity can generate complex power-grid frequency dynamics. We investigate the contributions of spatial structure, intrinsic nonlinear dynamics, and external driving using the Kuramoto model (KM), with and without uncorrelated noise, and compare its predictions with real-grid measurements. We analyse one month of 100 ms frequency measurements from 16 Hungarian transmission-grid sites and simulate the KM on a 387-node transmission network and two-dimensional lattices. The measured power spectra exhibit two scaling regimes, with exponents of approximately 1.63 and 2.23. One-second frequency increments decorrelate rapidly, while correlations of their local inverse variance decay slowly, initially as a power law, $\tau^{-0.26(2)}$, up to 15 minutes. A superstatistical Gaussian mixture based on measured local variances captures much of the non-Gaussian increment distribution, but not the rare extreme events. We also estimate the non-stationary long-time frequency autocorrelation exponent. KM simulations on low-dimensional networks exhibit algebraically decaying autocorrelations and power spectra, consistent with the measurements and the Wiener-Khinchin relation in the steady state. On the heterogeneous transmission network, partial synchronization and frequency locking produce persistent spatial patterns and multi-peaked frequency distributions. However, neither deterministic KM dynamics nor independent Gaussian driving reproduces the measured spectra and increment statistics simultaneously. Moreover, empirical frequency fluctuations are largely shared across substations, whereas simulated fluctuations mainly reflect relative node motion. These findings suggest that spatially coupled nonlinear dynamics contribute to observed frequency fluctuations alongside external driving, including 15-minute power dispatches.

authors.name: Krist\'of Benedek, Michelle T. Cirunay, Sangita Dutta, Attila Balogh, B\'alint Hartmann, G\'eza \'Odor

papers.title: Detecting space objects with Earth-observation radar satellites
papers.summary: Millimetre-to-centimetre orbital debris poses a hazard to spacecraft, but its abundance remains difficult to measure. Spaceborne radars offer a substantial sensitivity advantage at close range: received echo power decreases with the fourth power of distance, so an otherwise identical object ten times closer produces a 10,000 times stronger echo. We investigate this opportunity using openly available Sentinel-1 radar voltages recorded on six calendar days. Catalogue-assisted processing identifies a manually validated sample of 76 objects at ranges of 41.7--492.9 km, including satellites, rocket bodies and debris fragments. A blind search recovers two selected debris transits without using their orbital predictions during detection. A short debris encounter also demonstrates how precise range and Doppler measurements can refine a catalogue orbit. Ground scatter increases the effective background and is the principal sensitivity limitation in Earth-looking observations. An ideal receiver-noise sensitivity comparison predicts detectable conducting-sphere diameters of approximately 3.4 mm for Sentinel-1 and 0.6 mm for EarthCARE at 10 km range, assuming coherent integration limited by beam transit time and a 10 ms cap. These results establish the feasibility of space-object detection using existing Earth-observation radars and motivate statistical debris surveys and targeted orbit refinement following collision warnings. Observations directed away from Earth and receive windows adapted to nearby objects could improve sensitivity to small debris.

authors.name: Juha Vierinen, Laura-Kristin Scholtz, Ulrik Noer, Theresa Rexer, Daniel Kastinen, P{\aa}l Gunnar Ellingsen

papers.title: Amortized Transport-Map Likelihoods for Hierarchical Inverse Problems with Application to Wetting
papers.summary: Hierarchical Bayesian models pool measurements, but with the forward model in the likelihood every posterior evaluation costs one forward solve per cell. To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular transport-map likelihood, trained once per design, serves every cell. We apply it to infer wetting properties from photographs of a stable hole in a thin liquid film. The hole's radius depends, through the nonlinear Young-Laplace equation, on the contact angle and capillary length. One photograph gives rank-one information about them, so we pool many in a hierarchical model whose cells, each a substrate at one volume setting, share the apparatus geometry and the noise scale. A design fixes the number of substrates, the volume settings and the photographs per cell. The map's posteriors agree with direct sampling of the forward model in the wetting properties at a synthetic validation design, and less closely at a larger synthetic scaling design. At the validation design, simulation-based calibration detects no departure for any parameter. There, the map needs several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. On real photographs its posterior agrees with direct sampling and is consistent with the measured radii. Trained offline, the amortized map turns new photographs into a posterior with no forward solve. It is thus a major step toward measuring wetting properties in situ without disturbing the liquid.

authors.name: Henning Bonart

papers.title: Topological phases and scattering protected by projective chiral symmetry
papers.summary: The bulk-boundary correspondence states that topological properties of a bulk material guarantee the existence of protected edge modes, oftentimes associated with the attractive property of backscattering immunity. In this Letter, we consider a time reversal invariant classical system with both translation and chiral, or sublattice, symmetries. We show that when these two symmetries anti-commute, the material exhibits a topological phase protected by the same invariant as type D topological superconductors. We realize such a system experimentally and observe the existence of the associated edge modes in an acoustic network. Our measurements are in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions from discrete lattice models. Finally, we show that these edge modes are immune to backscattering for perturbations consisting in two subsequent identical defects.

authors.name: Th\'eo Torres, Renaud C\^ote, Marc Pachebat, Antonin Coutant

papers.title: Beam-beam effects on measurements at electron-positron colliders: LEP neutrino counting and Higgs factories
papers.summary: Beam-beam electromagnetic interactions affect the luminosity, collision energy, polarization, and particle backgrounds relevant to precision measurements at electron-positron colliders. We investigate these effects using Fast $e^{\pm}e^{\pm}$ Beam and Luminosity (FeeBL), a new beam-beam simulation framework, and compare its predictions with published results from LEP and proposed future colliders. We reproduce the analytical field-integration calculations of LEP Bhabha scattering and identify an approximately 2% bias in previously published beam-deflection simulations. Applying the corresponding luminosity correction and a revised uncertainty assessment motivated by the observed agreement among the four LEP experiments yields ($N_\nu = 2.9965 \pm 0.0040$), compared with the previously reported ($2.9963 \pm 0.0074$). The revised uncertainty is conditional on an assumed common rescaling of experiment specific uncertainties and motivates further investigation of the original uncertainty budgets. We identify and correct implementation errors in the modeling of Breit-Wheeler, Bethe-Heitler, and Landau-Lifshitz pair production, with implications for detector backgrounds at Higgs factories. Simulated beam depolarization and luminosity spectra are compared with existing ILC and HALHF predictions. Finally, we investigate collision energy monochromatization for direct Higgs production, obtaining sub-MeV collision energy peak widths in exploratory linear collider configurations at substantial luminosity cost, while finding significantly weaker narrowing for the FCC-ee configurations studied. We derive a rigid Gaussian beam overlap model and estimate that FCC-ee needs roughly 10 m of horizontal only dispersion to reach widths of $\approx1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

authors.name: Brendon Madison

papers.title: Ultrafast Liquid Jet X-ray Total Scattering
papers.summary: X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide the temporal resolution needed to extend total scattering and pair distribution function (PDF) analysis to investigate structural dynamics on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We recently demonstrated that high-quality total scattering data and PDFs can be obtained from individual XFEL pulses; here, we take the next step towards time-resolved studies of structural dynamics in solution. Using the Materials Imaging and Dynamics (MID) instrument at the European XFEL, we obtain total scattering data up to $Q_{\max} = 16.4\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-1}$ from both conventional capillary samples and, critically, from samples delivered by a liquid jet. Despite the large air and solvent backgrounds inherent to this setup, PDFs suitable for quantitative structural analysis are recovered from liquid dispersions and molecular clusters in solution. We further demonstrate pump-probe total scattering from $\mathrm{CsPbBr}_3$ nanocrystals in a liquid jet, resolving a fluence-dependent photoinduced isotropic lattice strain. Additionally, empirical potential structure refinement (EPSR) of XFEL total scattering data from an aqueous Keggin cluster reveals site-specific hydration environments and enables three-dimensional mapping of the surrounding solvent structure. Together, these advances open the door to tracking not only ultrafast structural changes in solution, but also the evolving solvent environments that govern molecular behaviour and reactivity.

authors.name: Adam F. Sapnik, Philip A. Chater, Dean S. Keeble, Tobias A. Bird, John S. O. Evans, Federica Bertolotti, Antonietta Guagliardi, Norberto Masciocchi, Daniel T. Bowron, Lise J. St{\o}ckler, Elodie A. Harbourne, Anders B. Borup, Rebecca S. Silberg, Viktoria A. Kaznelson, Stefanie Punke, Mariia Svyrydenko, Maryna I. Bodnarchuk, Dmitry N. Dirin, Simon C. Boehme, Maksym V. Kovalenko, Bo B. Iversen, Emil S. Bozin, Kirsten M. {\O}. Jensen, Gabriele Ansaldi, Karen Appel, Alexander Gierke, J\"org Hallmann, Aliaksandr Leonau, Anders Madsen, Johannes M\"oller, Jan-Etienne Pudell, Angel Rodriguez-Fernandez, Andreas Schmidt, Roman Shayduk, Cornelius Strohm, Joana Valerio, Ulrike Boesenberg, David A. Keen

papers.title: Hidden Distances: How Likert-Scale Spacing Shapes Algorithmic Voting Advice
papers.summary: Voting Advice Applications (VAAs) are algorithmic recommenders that match voters with political candidates on policy preferences. They are widely adopted across many multi-party democracies; in Denmark, 62\% of eligible voters used a VAA ahead of the 2022 general election, and 45\% of VAA users reported following its advice. VAAs typically ask voters and candidates to respond to policy statements on a Likert scale, from ``strongly disagree'' to ``strongly agree'', and recommend candidates whose responses are closest to the voter's. Computing these distances requires assigning numbers to response options, a design choice without an empirical basis, since it is unknown how people perceive the distances between options. Here we show that this seemingly technical choice substantially changes whom voters are matched with. We parameterize the distance between ``(dis)agree'' and ``strongly (dis)agree'' relative to the distance between ``neutral'' and ``(dis)agree'' as $\alpha$, and quantify how it changes recommendations for a popular Danish VAA. We find that moving from equidistant options to doubling this distance can change $37.7\%$ of top candidate matches and $21.9\%$ of top party matches, although no answers change. Low $\alpha$-values favor candidates with strong positions, with some parties receiving up to $ 19.6\%$ more recommendations, while high $\alpha$-values favor moderates. Similarly, female candidates receive fewer recommendations at low $\alpha$ and more at high $\alpha$-values. Our findings demonstrate that undisclosed quantification choices in algorithmic recommenders can carry considerable electoral consequences, and they call for transparency and sensitivity analysis in VAA design. As Likert-based matching also underpins dating platforms and roommate allocation systems, these implications extend well beyond elections.

authors.name: Thomas Broholt Knudsen, Christian H{\o}st-Madsen, Vedran Sekara, Jonas L. Juul

papers.title: Parker Solar Probe Flies Through the Sun's Magnetic Poles Near 10 Solar Radii
papers.summary: During the peak of the Sun's magnetic cycle, the solar corona can be complex and dominated by dynamics, while hidden below, the dipole component of the its photospheric magnetic field steadily reverses with respect to the rotational axis. Here, we use Parker Solar Probe (\emph{Parker}) data from two of its closest approaches in mid-2025 to show that the large-scale field at solar maximum resembled a simple tilted dipole. Similar to how Ulysses provided a complete scan of the solar rotation-aligned dipole at solar minimum, \emph{Parker} sampled the full range of magneto-latitudes, probing both magnetic poles below the Alfv\'en surface. Concurrent in situ data at larger distances reveal that both hemispheres contain solar wind with asymptotic speeds near 800 km s-1, yielding a picture similar to the Ulysses latitude scans but now in the equator near solar maximum. This contrasts with the disordered structure observed by Ulysses during its solar maximum latitude scan, which we attribute to the long timescale of data collection. Overall, we find the coronal field is organized as a dipole, but the fast solar wind streams are deformed by non-dipolar substructure: the positive dipole axis is aligned with one coronal hole, the negative centers over a pseudostreamer, and significant mass flux enhancements are observed at magnetic separatrixes. Our measurements suggest that even at solar maximum, the solar corona can still exhibit structure nearly as ordered as solar minimum. Moreover, by sampling rapidly and close to the Sun, the detailed imprint of source region structure can be determined in the solar wind.

authors.name: Yeimy J. Rivera, Adam J. Finley, Samuel T. Badman, Olga A. Panasenco, Kristopher G. Klein, Srijan Bharati Das, Edward E. DeLuca, Kristoff Paulson, Tatiana Niembro, Michael Terres, Federico Fraschetti, Michael L. Stevens, Nour E. Raouafi, Tamar Ervin, Ali Rahmati, Orlando M. Romeo, Christopher J. Owen, Zesen Huang, Marco Velli, Stuart D. Bale, Davin Larson

papers.title: Deriving Tsallis Entropy from First Principles
papers.summary: The kinetic approach for q-distribution is extended through a "bottom-up" procedure to the corresponding entropic formula. In this way, the validity of Tsallis' formula, S_q(W) = k_B ln_q(W), is established from first principles. The resulting q-entropy is additive and the zeroth law of thermodynamics is automatically satisfied because the conventional identification beta = 1/(k_B T) remains valid. Entropy, energy, and all relevant quantities for both discrete and continuous cases are evaluated using standard (linear) averages. The "bottom-up" and "top-down" approaches yield the same q-distribution for velocities. The standard results are naturally recovered in the limit q -> 1.

authors.name: J. A. S. Lima, M. H. Benetti

papers.title: Scalable operating currents in amorphous W-N/FePt superconducting rectifiers
papers.summary: We demonstrate high-efficiency, field-free superconducting diode behavior in W-N/FePt bilayers fabricated entirely by sputtering at room temperature. The devices combine amorphous W-N superconducting thin films with a 48-nm-thick FePt layer exhibiting remanent stripe-domain magnetization. We used lithographically patterned microbridges to compare W-N/FePt bilayers with single-layer W-N reference films at three nominal W-N thicknesses (18, 24, and 28 nm). The bilayers exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of approximately 4.1-4.3 K. At zero applied magnetic field, the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics exhibit pronounced nonreciprocity, controlled by the orientation of the in-plane remanent FePt magnetization relative to the transport current. The diode response is maximized for perpendicular alignment, reverses polarity upon magnetization reversal, and is strongly suppressed when the magnetization is aligned with the current. This behavior is consistent with asymmetric vortex entry and motion governed by the magnetic stray fields generated near the bridge edges. At 3 K with the remanent magnetization perpendicular to the current, increasing the W-N thickness from 18 to 28 nm widens the current interval between the dissipation thresholds for opposite polarities from about 0.3 to 1.55 mA. All three bilayers exhibit diode efficiencies of approximately 75-80% in this configuration.

authors.name: S. Russo, A. Sanson, Yeonkyu Lee, Jeehoon Kim, N. Haberkorn

papers.title: Memory in biological L\'evy walks from the dynamic-entropy formalism
papers.summary: L\'evy walks are recognized by the histogram of their flight lengths, while the renewal hypothesis on which the textbook model rests, that every flight is drawn afresh, is seldom tested. We test it with the dynamic-entropy formalism. Maximizing the causal entropy of a sequence of logarithmic flight lengths at fixed lagged correlations yields a chain of continuous spins on a compact interval, whose depth, selected by the data, tells a renewal walker from a Markovian one and from one with a longer memory. With one lag the chain is exactly solvable. A duality that exchanges long and short flights locates a first-order condensation of the flights at the upper cutoff, with the logarithmic range of the flights in the role of system size, and a positive memory makes the histogram heavier-tailed than the rule that generates each flight. For groups, the same construction separates the memory of each individual from delayed interactions and from drives common to all units, which an analysis of the group average confounds, and it gives the collective speed a critical point. On open data, renewal is rejected in seven of ten conditions of Drosophila larvae and in every termite, whose memory reaches a few flights back and lowers the exponent of the histogram by more than half a unit below that of the one-step rule. Wild baboons align with where their nearest neighbors, those ahead above all, were heading 10 to 30 s earlier, and homing pigeons are coupled across their small flocks. Zebrafish T cells, a negative control, remember their own speed, but no delayed coupling between the speeds of different cells survives the controls.

authors.name: Adriano Barra, Andrea Ladiana

papers.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
papers.summary: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. We predict magnetoresistance ratios in the range of 1.14-1.20 for the charge-transfer device and up to $10^3$ in the single-electron transistor.

authors.name: Jan Phillips, Joaqu\'in Fern\'andez-Rossier

papers.title: A Hierarchy of Fast and Strong Signatures for Vertex Orbits
papers.summary: The defining features of a physical system are its symmetries and its invariants. For a network, the symmetries are the automorphisms, and the invariants are the vertex orbits they define. Two vertices of a graph may appear structurally indistinguishable without being interchangeable under any graph automorphism. Distinguishing apparent similarity from genuine symmetry lies at the heart of the vertex-orbit partition problem. In this work, we develop a hierarchy of increasingly expressive, automorphism-invariant signatures that draw on the spectral properties of the graph Laplacian and the Dirac operator to reveal subtle structural differences. Guided by a sequence of counterexamples, we progressively strengthen these signatures, ultimately incorporating probing techniques, which are temporary structural perturbations, that expose the hidden distinctions in the original unperturbed graph. We evaluate our approach across diverse benchmark families, recovering exact orbit partitions in challenging instances, including graphs that resist low-dimensional Weisfeiler--Leman refinement. We also examine the computational and numerical limitations of our constructions, distinguishing empirical success from theoretical completeness. Our findings highlight the potential of spectral and probing-based methods for uncovering the structural distinctions that define vertex orbit.

authors.name: Joe Germany, Mohamad Al Sayed, Rana Dbouk, Amer E. Mouawad, Sara Najem

papers.title: Renewal Bias in Parallel Simulations of Absorbing Processes
papers.summary: Asynchronous parallel simulations of stochastic processes with absorbing states can exhibit systematic sampling bias when trajectory durations depend on their eventual absorbing outcomes. Workers that continuously restart upon absorption preferentially record rapidly terminating trajectories within a fixed computational budget, distorting the observed ensemble statistics. We investigate this effect using a minimal renewal model with two absorbing states and state-dependent exponential durations. Renewal theory yields exact expressions for the expected number and composition of completed trajectories, showing that the resulting bias decreases algebraically with execution time but persists as the number of parallel workers increases at fixed budget. We compare continuous sampling with First-Trajectory Filtering, which retains only the initial trajectory attempted by each worker. Although finite execution deadlines introduce residual censoring bias, this bias decreases exponentially with the computational budget. An analytical mean-squared error calculation reveals budget-dependent crossover worker allocations beyond which First-Trajectory Filtering becomes more accurate despite collecting fewer trajectories. We also examine the limitations of statistical inference under severe censoring when the absorbing-state probabilities and characteristic durations are unknown. Finally, simulations of the Axelrod model near its nonequilibrium transition demonstrate the preferential sampling of rapidly absorbing fragmented configurations, illustrating the relevance of the renewal mechanism in a spatially interacting system. Our results show that increasing computational throughput does not necessarily improve statistical accuracy and highlight the importance of accounting for trajectory-duration heterogeneity in parallel simulations of absorbing processes.

authors.name: Sandro M. Reia, Jos\'e F. Fontanari

papers.title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
papers.summary: The method of projection onto localized states intended for describing reactions and clustering is examined. In particular, the method offers a simple extension of the no-core shell model to continuum- and clusterized bound states. A critical analysis of a previous realization of the method is provided. A way to minimize the number of basis functions required for convergence is given. An easy way to obtain exactly unitary and symmetric $S$ matrix from calculations is pointed out. The method is tested in one- and two-channel $np$ scattering problems with the Daejeon $NN$ interaction. It is shown that excellent convergence can be reached even when only oscillator states with low number of excitation quanta are retained.

authors.name: V. D. Efros

papers.title: Catalysis-induced phase separation of enzymes via diffusivity contrast
papers.summary: Catalysis can drive phase separation by coupling local chemical composition to molecular transport, even in the absence of attractive interactions. Here, we demonstrate such catalysis-induced phase separation in a microscopic particle-based model of enzymes catalyzing the interconversion of substrate and product molecules with different diffusivities. We derive an analytical instability criterion in the dilute limit, showing that a homogeneous mixture becomes unstable when the nonequilibrium chemical drive and the diffusivity contrast are sufficiently large, and the substrate and product concentration exceeds a threshold set by the enzyme volume. Brownian-dynamics simulations confirm the predicted instability and reveal macroscopic coexistence of enzyme-rich and enzyme-poor phases, including in regimes where equilibrium depletion interactions cannot account for demixing. Finally, we show that, upon eliminating the fast chemical degrees of freedom, the reactive ternary mixture maps onto an effective binary mixture nonreciprocal interactions. Our results establish an explicit microscopic mechanism for catalysis-induced phase separation and connect chemically driven phase separation to the physics of motility-regulated and nonreciprocal matter.

authors.name: Marie Jardat, Jacques Fries, Vincent Dahirel, Jaime Agudo-Canalejo, Pierre Illien

papers.title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
papers.summary: At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH$_{10}$ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)$_2$, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

authors.name: Henricus R. A. ten Eikelder, Florian Knoop, Florian Trybel

papers.title: MarsNet: Learning the Martian Atmosphere from Observations Alone
papers.summary: We present MarsNet, a machine-learned model of the Martian atmosphere trained only on observations. Existing reanalyses assimilate spacecraft retrievals into general circulation models (GCMs), so where observations are sparse their fields largely reflect the model. We therefore use extant reanalyses only for evaluation. MarsNet alternates a two-hour forecast with an update that assimilates the observations of each window, and both steps are learned jointly. Because the Martian record is too sparse for an unrestricted network, learning is confined within a fixed physical structure: the state is in physical units, the forecast uses physical tendencies of fixed form and learned strength, and the update is a bounded Kalman update. MarsNet is trained on Mars Years (MY) 24--31 and evaluated on independent observations. On three seasons of MGS radio-occultation temperatures assimilated by no dataset, MarsNet matches or improves on the three reanalyses in the lowest three scale heights, with a near-surface root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 4.2 K against 4.4--5.4 K, but is less accurate aloft. The model's surface pressures are the most accurate of the four products (RMSE 10 Pa against Curiosity in MY32, compared with 20--46 Pa). On withheld Mars Climate Sounder profiles of MY32, its temperatures beat an observed climatology and persistence, including in ten-sol forecasts without new observations, and its stated uncertainty is close to calibrated. Much of the temperature skill is present before training and appears to come from the structure and tables fitted to the observations, while training mainly improves the surface pressures, at some cost to dust. The model cycles stably through nine Mars years, and the influence of each observation can be traced. Its speed makes experiments on the observing record practical, and it offers an independent reference for GCMs and reanalyses.

authors.name: Sebastian Mengwall, J. Michael Battalio

papers.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.summary: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

authors.name: Jiaxi Wu, Elias R. Most

papers.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
papers.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

authors.name: Jinzheng Li, Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

papers.title: A regularization-independent Information Criterion for correlated data
papers.summary: We generalize the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to allow model and data subset selection when regularized fits are performed on correlated data. While the standard generalization to regularized fits is inherently dependent on the type of regularization applied to the data covariance matrix, our definition, the RIAIC, is, on average, regularization-independent. The regularization-independence is achieved by defining the new Information Criterion as an estimator of the model-dependent contribution to the correlated Kullback--Leibler divergence. The Bayesian extension is derived as well. We test the new criterion on lattice QCD data by performing regularized fits and show that it reproduces the selection properties of the standard correlated AIC, with fluctuations which are compatible with the expected statistical uncertainties. These results enable the application of subset and model selection techniques to cases where regularizations are applied to the covariance matrix of the fitted dataset.

authors.name: Davide Laudicina

papers.title: Cavitation near the oscillating piezoelectric plate in water
papers.summary: Gas and vapor bubbles at a wall can reduce the skin friction of a liquid flow. We estimate whether an oscillating piezoelectric plate mounted flush with the wall can create such a near-wall bubble layer by acoustic cavitation. Once the cavitation threshold is reached, the liquid can no longer follow the receding plate, and the excess plate displacement is accommodated by cavitation bubbles forming at the wall; this kinematic argument gives the bubble volume generated per stroke and its energy cost. Homogeneous cavitation in pure water (about -30 MPa) requires pressure amplitudes far beyond those of flat piezoelectric plates and produces submicron bubbles that collapse within nanoseconds. Heterogeneous cavitation on wall and gas nuclei (-0.1 to -1 MPa) is within reach of piezoceramics and concentrates the void on fewer, larger wal-attached bubbles, which survive between strokes if they exceed a few micrometres at 5 MHz. The acoustic power needed to sustain a bubble layer in a turbulent boundary layer at 10 m/s is about 20 kW/m2 for heterogeneous and about 0.4 MW/m2 for homogeneous cavitation.

authors.name: M. N. Shneider, M. Pekker

papers.title: Design and Formulation of a Hydromechanical Fin for AUV Operations and Wave Parameter Estimation
papers.summary: Ocean dynamics play a crucial role in global climate, ecosystems, and human activities, necessitating accurate and efficient methods to characterize ocean currents and waves. This paper presents the development of a novel bio-inspired hydrofoil system for detecting and characterizing ocean currents and waves based on a dolphin's flipper foil design. The prototype's performance was assessed through controlled experiments, demonstrating the system's ability to quickly and accurately orientate itself in the direction of flow. Wave mechanics and a geometric proof were applied to estimate wave parameters such as wave height and current from the hydrofoil's positioning. The proposed hydrofoil system shows potential for use in various marine applications, including oceanographic research, environmental monitoring, and navigation. The bio-inspired hydrofoil system offers a promising approach to ocean current and wave characterization, with the potential to significantly impact our understanding and monitoring of ocean dynamics without greatly impacting vehicle performance or increasing power utilization in operation.

authors.name: Brendan M. Unikewicz

papers.title: Viral Lattice Theory: A Biophysical Framework for Collective Virion Motion
papers.summary: Viral Lattice Theory develops a testable framework for collective motion and mechanical response of virions and virus-like particles (VLPs) in viscoelastic environments. Its central problem is observational ambiguity: distinct interparticle forces, material relaxation processes, and hydrodynamic couplings can produce similar particle trajectories or equilibrium measurements. We ask which additional measurements can distinguish these mechanisms. Combining lattice dynamics, stochastic mechanics, and linear response theory, the framework derives memory-dependent forces and, under thermal-equilibrium assumptions, fluctuation-dissipation-consistent noise. Explicit observation models account for finite camera exposure and support parameter-identifiability tests and experimental design. In a synthetic response-fluctuation benchmark, models with matching equilibrium covariance and nearly matching response magnitude differ by approximately 28 degrees in response phase and 40% in spectral density at a selected crossover, demonstrating the discriminating value of complementary observables. A crystal-response example uses satellite tobacco mosaic virus geometry and published acoustic summaries to calibrate a spectral peak and test a separately reserved linewidth. An HPV-inspired VLP model extends the framework to classical stochastic transport between intact, reversibly deformed, and damaged structural states, illustrating recovery and delayed damage after delivery. Path-survival and driven-cycle calculations distinguish transient loading from sustained nonequilibrium behavior. A separate viral-phonon quantization postulate is presented as a conditional quantum extension, not an established biological effect. The results provide synthetic and conditional comparisons that specify experimentally testable distinctions.

authors.name: Lillian St. Kleess

papers.title: High-quality electron beam generation from laser wakefield accelerators for driving compact free electron lasers
papers.summary: Despite the successful demonstration of compact free electron lasers (FELs) driven by laser wakefield accelerators (LWFAs), the pursuit of further enhancements in high-gain compact FELs presents a challenge due to the limitations in electron beam quality. In this work, we pinpoint the pivotal physics and optimization strategies for high-quality single-stage LWFAs that are crucial for high-gain FELs. We have delved into the synergistic injection mechanism, where the self-evolution injection threshold is far from reached at the injection position, with both the shock front and self-evolution of the laser playing a role in the injection process. A thorough discussion has been provided on the beam-quality degradation and optimization strategies, in terms of global (slice) energy spread and projected (slice) emittance. With the goal of achieving high-gain FELs driven by LWFAs, we have also explored the synthesis quality of the electron beam to determine an optimized power gain length. A comprehensive start-to-end simulation has been conducted, demonstrating the effectiveness of compact FELs powered by these high-quality electron beams. The resulting radiation reaches the saturation regime after a 4.5-meter-long undulator, with an energy of 17.4 {\mu}J and a power of 6.0 GW at a wavelength of 23.9 nm. This proposed scheme offers not only a framework for optimizing beam quality in LWFAs, but also a promising path for future compact LWFA-driven FELs to achieve saturated regimes, opening up new possibilities for widespread applications.

authors.name: Ke Feng, Kangnan Jiang, Runshu Hu, Chen Lv, Xizhuan Chen, Hai Jiang, Shixia Luan, Wentao Wang, Ruxin Li

papers.title: Simulation of Micro-Void Development within Large Scale Additively Manufactured Polymer Composite Deposition Beads
papers.summary: Despite the growing level of technology advancement that characterizes extrusion deposition additive manufacturing technology, there remains significant knowledge gap in fully understanding the process-structure-property relationship involved in this technology. The ability to effectively and efficiently control the manufacturing process provides an opportunity for optimizing the complex microstructure of the polymer composite prints which can lead to significant improvement of the associated print properties and in-service part performance. Modeling the polymer melt flow extrusion-deposition process is important in understanding the development of the inherent microstructural formation. The current research presents a computational-based approach for investigating process induced micro-voids and their impact on print properties. We develop a multiscale FEA simulation tool to predict the global and local flow-fields during the polymer-melt flow process to investigate underlying mechanisms that may promote the micro-void development within the bead microstructure and determine potential process related factors that can be controlled to mitigate micro-void formation and growth. The research also presents a computational based method for assessing the impact of the micro-voids on the effective print properties. The direct implication of a reduced part voidage levels is the development of high-quality functional components for specialized applications such as light weight & high strength integrity composites widely used in a variety of industries particularly the automobile, aerospace, renewable energy and defense industries.

authors.name: Aigbe E. Awenlimobor

papers.title: Galerkin reduced order model for two-dimensional Rayleigh-B\'enard convection
papers.summary: In this work, Galerkin projection is used to build reduced-order models (ROM) for two-dimensional Rayleigh-B\'enard (RB) convection with no-slip walls. We compare an uncoupled projection approach that uses separate orthonormal bases for velocity and temperature with a coupled formalism where the equations are projected onto a single basis combining velocity and temperature components. Orthonormal bases for modal projection are obtained as the eigenfunctions of the controllability Gramian of the linearized RB equations, eliminating the need for DNS snapshot databases required by traditional POD-based approaches. Various coupled and uncoupled ROMs with different numbers of modes are generated and validated against direct numerical simulations (DNS) over a wide range of Rayleigh numbers. One of the objectives is to determine their domain of validity as a function of the system dimension and the Rayleigh number. DNS and ROM results are compared in terms of mean vertical profiles, heat flux, flow structures, dynamical regimes and energy spectra. Crucially, unlike previous POD-based Galerkin models for thermal convection, these ROMs do not require closure models and remain numerically stable. The coupled approach shows better agreement with DNS in terms of mean vertical profiles and Nusselt number scaling. The capabilities of these models are exploited to conduct a detailed bifurcation analysis at $Pr = 10$ using Poincar\'e sections and Lyapunov exponents, precisely identifying the transitions between periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic states with significant reductions of computational cost.

authors.name: Enrique Flores-Montoya, Andr\'e V. G. Cavalieri

papers.title: A Heuristic Mirror-Bulk Model of Schwarzschild Black Hole Interiors
papers.summary: Schwarzschild -- non-rotating and chargeless -- black holes (BHs) are classically understood to be voids of extreme gravitation, with modern and contemporary apporaches having involved string-theoretical black branes and superfluid analogs. In this study, we reconsider Schwarzschild BHs by letting its black brane be a closed spherical surface, within which a mirror-bulk fluid is contained, mirrored by surface-dwelling Hawking radiation quanta. By employing a once-used variational method of solving the Einstein field equations, the eneregtic output is approximated by the metric Ansatz input. Here, we consider a Tangherlini-like black 2-brane metric Ansatz in 3+1 spacetime, and via $G_{\mu\nu}=8\pi GT_{\mu\nu}$ the geometric information of the time-time component $G_{00}$ determines the corresponding (effective) energy density $T_{00}$ and the respective energy profile $E:=T_{00}V$. These are found to be functions of the radial coordinate, which also applies to the BH interior $r\in[0,~r_S]$. We explore and discuss the mirror-bulk energy content, internal pressure, and the mass- and pressure-gradients of a mirror-bulk BH.

authors.name: Noah M. MacKay

papers.title: Atom Interferometer Phase Shear and Spacetime Sectional Curvature
papers.summary: Atom interferometry is a natural laboratory for precision tests of general relativity, but there are no known simple relationships between atom interferometer phase and geometric properties of spacetime. Here we show that a different atom interferometer observable, the phase shear, can be expressed directly as the integrated sectional curvature over a spacetime surface enclosed by the interferometer arms and final beamsplitter, which follows from a generalized Gauss-Bonnet theorem. This interface of quantum mechanics, relativity, and geometry is manifestly coordinate-free and representation-free and can provide a useful computational tool for predicting atom interferometer properties in arbitrary background spacetimes.

authors.name: Hunter Swan, Jason M. Hogan

papers.title: Light in Slices: How to Enable Precise Laser Processing?
papers.summary: Ultrashort (femtosecond, fs) laser pulses have fascinating properties as they allow to confine optical energy on extreme scales in space and time. Such fs-laser pulsed beams can be seen as spatially thin slices of intense light that are radially and axially constrained to the micrometer scale, while simultaneously propagating at the extremely high speed of light. Their high peak intensities and their short time lapse makes such laser pulses unique tools for materials processing, as their duration is shorter than the time required to transfer absorbed optical energy, via electron-phonon coupling, from the electronic system of the solid to its lattice. Hence, the laser pulse energy remains localized during the interaction and does not spread via diffusion into the area surrounding the irradiated region. As one consequence, the fs-laser thus offers increased precision for material modification or ablation accompanied by a reduced heat-affected zone of only a few hundred nanometers. On the other hand, the high laser peak intensities can enable nonlinear material interactions that are rendering unique material excitation and relaxation pathways possible. In this chapter, we briefly review the reasons for the enormous success of ultrashort pulse lasers in materials processing - both for the processing of the surface or in the bulk of solids. We identify the underlying fundamental processes that can limit the precision or the up-scaling of the laser processing towards large volumes, areas, or processing rates. Strategies to overcome such limitations will be outlined and questions on the ultimate limits of laser material processing will be answered.

authors.name: Stefan Nolte, J\"orn Bonse, Nadezhda M. Bulgakova

papers.title: Active learning and explicit electrostatics enable accurate modeling of electrolytes
papers.summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) combine near-ab initio accuracy with the computational efficiency of classical force fields, making them promising tools for modeling molecular liquids and electrolytes. Their predictive accuracy depends strongly on the diversity of the training set, while the explicit treatment of electrostatics is increasingly recognized as an important factor in improving their performance. In this work, we assess the impact of incorporating explicit electrostatics and environment-dependence of atomic charges by comparing short-ranged Moment Tensor Potentials (MTPs) with electrostatics-augmented MTPs, including fixed-charge and environment-dependent charge models. To this end, we employ D-optimality-based active learning (AL) to train short-ranged MTPs and extend the AL procedure, previously unavailable for long-range electrostatics-augmented MTPs, to these models, enabling largely automated generation of diverse training sets for pure ethylene carbonate (EC) and ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), their mixtures, and LiPF6 solutions. For EC, EMC, and their mixtures, electrostatics-augmented MTPs achieve accuracy comparable to or better than that of their short-ranged counterparts while requiring fewer machine-learned parameters. For LiPF6 solutions, however, a notable improvement in accuracy is achieved only with environment-dependent charges, which also enhance stability in large-scale molecular dynamics simulations, unlike the fixed-charge model. The resulting short-ranged MTPs and environment-dependent-charge models reproduce experimental densities with mean absolute deviations of 0.2-6% and ionic conductivities with deviations of 11-15%, while capturing the experimentally observed temperature dependence of conductivity.

authors.name: Olga Chalykh, Mikhail Polovinkin, Dmitry Korogod, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev

papers.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. II. Bead-Fourier RPMD
papers.summary: Feynman path integrals (PIs) have found many uses in approximate quantum dynamics methods for efficiently calculating real-time quantum correlation functions. The PIs typically take the form of discrete imaginary-time slices along a closed path, where the slices form the ``beads'' of a ring polymer (RP) necklace. Some methods, such as centroid molecular dynamics (CMD), use the RP to generate an effective potential for the dynamics, while others, like RP molecular dynamics (RPMD), directly utilize the RP in real-time dynamics in order to incorporate approximate quantum effects. The standard, discretized bead forms of CMD and RPMD may require a large number of RP beads to obtain accurate results for systems with strong quantum effects and at low temperatures. In Paper I (J. Chem. Phys. 2025, 163, 144123), we introduced the bead-Fourier (BF)-CMD method, where we utilized the inclusion of a Fourier sine series to reduce the number of beads needed to converge the CMD effective potential up to eightfold. In this work, we extend RPMD to incorporate BF-PIs in the form of BF-RPMD. We study several implementations of the BF-RPMD method through the calculation of correlation functions for both linear and nonlinear operators. We found that the effectiveness of this method is sensitive to both the type of system and the form of the operators being studied. Our results show that this method is able to produce results on par with standard RPMD, with at worst a twofold and up to an eightfold reduction in the number of beads by including two to three Fourier components.

authors.name: Nathan London, Mohammad R. Momeni

papers.title: Distributed Acoustic Fiber Sensing for Research Campuses and Large Scientific Infrastructures -- The Hamburg WAVE proto-network
papers.summary: Here, we demonstrate and investigate how Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) can be utilized on research campuses and in large scientific infrastructures to study environmental vibrations and reduce their impact on high-precision experiments. We first discuss the potential of DAS in the context of particle accelerators, gravitational wave detection experiments and research campuses. Next, we present the results of our seismic measurement campaign conducted with our proto-network, which involved the probing of over 12 km of fiber, in May 2021. This campaign was conducted by the Hamburg WAVE initiative in Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld and included DESY, the European XFEL, PETRA III and the University of Hamburg. Our proto-network confirms the ability to observe natural, anthropogenic, and infrastructural vibrations and how and where these couple into different parts of the heterogeneously set up fiber network. We also present results on a study of noise and motion coupling aspects of DAS probing double-redundant fiber loops in a unique environment, the European XFEL. Our results show that DAS can greatly benefit research campuses and large scientific infrastructures and they highlight the opportunities and challenges of implementing and operating such seismic networks.

authors.name: Oliver B\"olt, Luigia Cristiano, Sandy Croatto, Dirk Gajewski, Erik Genthe, Oliver Gerberding, C\'eline Hadziioannou, Conny Hammer, Markus Hoffmann, Katharina-Sophie Isleif, Antonia Kiel, Charlotte M. Krawczyk, Regina Maass, Ingra Barbosa, Norbert Meyners, Reinhardt Rading, Holger Schlarb, Roman Schnabel, Wanda Vossius, Christopher Wollin

papers.title: New approach to approximate analytical solutions for a harmonic oscillator subject to combined linear and nonlinear damping
papers.summary: We introduce a new approach to deriving approximate analytical solutions of a harmonic oscillator damped by purely nonlinear, or combinations of linear and nonlinear damping forces. Our approach is based on choosing a suitable trial solution, i.e. an ansatz, which is the product of the time-dependent amplitude and the oscillatory (trigonometric) function with a reduced frequency (due solely to linear damping) and an initial phase shift (due to both linear and nonlinear damping) compared to the undamped case. We derive the amplitude decay equation using the connection of the energy dissipation rate with the power of the total damping force. By matching our ansatz to the initial conditions, we obtain equations for its initial amplitude and initial phase. We demonstrate the validity of our approach for quadratic damping, a combination of linear and quadratic damping, and finally a combination of linear, quadratic, and Coulomb damping. For pure quadratic damping and for a combination of linear and quadratic damping, we compare our approximate analytical solutions with the corresponding numerical solutions and find that they describe the oscillator dynamics well in the regime of weak to moderately strong damping. For the combination of all three types of damping, our solutions agree well with the numerical solutions until the last half-period or the last few half-periods of the motion (primarily depending on the strength of the Coulomb damping). In addition, we show how to use our solutions to determine damping constants from given displacement vs. time data, demonstrating that they can be applied to the analysis of experiments.

authors.name: Karlo Lelas, Robert Pezer

papers.title: Collisionless relaxation as the origin of the anisotropic, non-thermal, and multi-temperature momentum distributions observed in space plasmas
papers.summary: Anisotropic, non-thermal, and multi-temperature distributed particle momenta are commonly observed in collisionless space plasmas, such as the solar wind. Using Liouville's theorem, we argue that anisotropic compression or expansion of the plasma, followed by a relaxation of the resulting anisotropic stress must lead to non-equilibrium states that exhibit either anisotropic, non-thermal distribution functions, different electron and ion temperatures, or a combination of these effects. We present arguments showing that a plasma in thermal equilibrium undergoing anisotropic compression or expansion cannot return to thermal equilibrium in the absence of particle collisions. Since most astrophysical plasmas are practically collisionless and experience significant anisotropic compression or expansion, we expect anisotropic, non-thermal, and multi-temperature particle distributions to be ubiquitous, in agreement with solar wind measurements.

authors.name: Torsten En{\ss}lin, Christoph Pfrommer

papers.title: Generative deep learning improves reconstruction of global historical climate records
papers.summary: Instrumental observations from the early twentieth century are sparse and uncertain, limiting estimates of historical climate variability and change. Existing reconstructions rely largely on statistical interpolation, smoothing spatiotemporal variability and leading to underestimation of local extremes. Recent deterministic machine-learning approaches focus primarily on spatial inpainting of coarse-resolution temperature fields but do not explicitly quantify uncertainty or enforce spatiotemporal consistency. Here, we present GenCRest, a generative deep-learning model that reconstructs globally complete temperature and precipitation fields from sparse, uncertain observations using a generative prior learned from Earth-system models and reanalyses. GenCRest preserves accuracy, temporal persistence, and higher-order variability of climate dynamics, consistently outperforming statistical and machine-learning benchmarks. Applying GenCRest to observational records that underpin climate assessments, we find stronger early-twentieth-century ENSO variability and identify approximately 50% more El Ni\~no events documented in the literature, which are not represented in established datasets. Our reconstructions reveal a more spatially heterogeneous history of temperature change during 1900--1980, with pronounced regional warming and cooling contrasts, particularly in the Arctic. For 1981--2024, our results suggest that recent assessments overestimate Arctic-mean warming due to interpolation smoothing, while underestimating warming in the Greenland, Barents, and Kara Seas. Furthermore, based on our seamless global reconstruction that infers precipitation variability across the oceans and under-monitored regions, we identify more widespread wet extremes over land in the early twentieth century and intensified regional wetting and drying across land and ocean in recent decades.

authors.name: Zhen Qian, Teng Liu, Duo Chan, Sebastian Bathiany, Shangshang Yang, Philipp Hess, Nils Bochow, Christian Burmester, Maximilian Gelbrecht, Brian Groenke, Niklas Boers

papers.title: g4chargeit: Geant4-based kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of charging in dielectric materials
papers.summary: We present g4chargeit, a kinetic Monte Carlo framework built on Geant4 for self-consistent simulation of time-dependent electrostatic charging in dielectric materials. The model explicitly incorporates stochastic particle transport and scattering processes using validated Geant4 cross-sections, while self-consistently evolving the electric potential and field. As a representative application, we simulate the charging of regolith grains under average dayside conditions on the Moon. The surface of the Moon, in addition to other airless planetary bodies, are regularly exposed to solar ultraviolet photons and solar-wind plasma, creating a radiation environment in which electrostatic interactions among regolith grains become significant. Until now, simulations of regolith charging have often relied on analytical approximations that oversimplify grain geometry and interaction mechanisms. Our Geant4-based simulations reveal charge accumulation within intergrain micro-cavities, leading to repulsive electrostatic forces consistent with experimental observations. The framework establishes a multiscale approach that links microscopic scattering events to the continuity equation of surface charge density and to the formation of macroscopic surface charge patches in complex grain geometries. Although demonstrated here for planetary regolith, the method is general and applicable to a broad range of dielectric charging problems. The code is openly available at https://github.com/kgandhi63/g4chargeit.git.

authors.name: Kush P. Gandhi, Advik D. Vira, William M. Farrell, Nikolai Simonov, Alvaro Romero-Calvo, Thomas M. Orlando, Phillip N. First, Zhigang Jiang

papers.title: Natural Lithopanspermia to Earth: Transport, Shielding, and Survival Limits for Solar-System and Extrasolar Donor Classes
papers.summary: Natural panspermia is a transport-and-establishment hypothesis, not a theory of abiogenesis. The Earth-specific question is whether any nonterrestrial donor remains competitive with terrestrial origin once launch, planetary-system escape, transit, Earth interception, atmospheric entry, terminal loading, and post-delivery establishment are imposed. We formulate this problem as a donor-class dependent Earth-directed transport-survival kernel, supplemented by a minimum protected-depth envelope d_{min}(t_{flight}) and a survival-weighted buried-volume fraction F_{bur} for the low-shock spall population. The resulting hierarchy is strongly ordered under current transport and survival constraints. Hard panspermia is physically credible only on Solar-System scales: early Mars combines demonstrated lithic exchange with Earth, low escape speed, early aqueous habitability, and a rare 10^2-10^4 yr transfer tail, whereas the more common 10^5-10^7 yr martian transfer regime requires lightly shocked meter-class carriers. Beyond the Solar System, low-v_{inf} capture and long-duration survival fail simultaneously; even the Solar birth-cluster channel yields only ~3 x 10^{-5} f_{seed} expected Earth-seeding events, where f_{seed} is the conditional probability that a viable arrival establishes life on Earth. Indigenous terrestrial origin therefore remains the default inference, early Mars is the only quantitatively serious external hard-panspermia alternative, and extrasolar or intergalactic hard panspermia is not competitive for Earth's actual origin history. Soft panspermia is much more plausible as chemical enrichment of early terrestrial abiogenesis.

authors.name: Slava G. Turyshev

papers.title: Fluctuations in Aharonov-Bohm Electrodynamics
papers.summary: We consider the application of the Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem (FDT) to the electrodynamics of Aharonov-Bohm (ABE), which differs from Maxwell's in that it allows for local non-conservation of charge. For the case of a system of non-conserved charges at thermal equilibrium we obtain the same spectral distribution of energy of the electromagnetic field as in Maxwell electrodynamics. However, the electric field contribution to that energy doubles that in Maxwell case, while the magnetic contribution is the same as in Maxwell theory, the electric excess energy is compensated by a negative contribution arising form the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) scalar field. For a conductor with local non-conservation of charge described by the $\gamma$ model, we derive the spectrum of current correlation at first order in $\gamma$, which results in a violet noise contribution added to the classical Johnson-Nyquist white noise result for the voltage fluctuations in a conductor.

authors.name: F. Minotti, G. Modanese

papers.title: Localized Tornado Outbreak at the Upstream of a Tropical Easterly Wave in Camarines Norte, Philippines (13 September 2025)
papers.summary: (Abridged) On 13 September 2025 at around 22 UTC, a localized tornado outbreak affected Camarines Norte in the eastern Philippines. The event developed within an atypical easterly severe weather regime, with warm, moist southeasterly low-level flow and modest low-level shear ahead of an approaching easterly wave. Convective initiation was focused along the upstream segment of the inverted trough, within a vorticity convergence zone that may have enhanced low-level rotation. MUCAPE reached 2167 J kg$^{-1}$, LCLs were below 200 m, and modestly curved but strongly streamwise hodographs favored supercells and tornadogenesis. At least five vortices were identified, three of them tornadoes from semi-discrete supercells. The Magang tornado, confirmed by a ground damage survey and Doppler radar, was rated IF2.5 along a $\sim$1.4 km path; the radar-identified Cahabaan ($\sim$2.1 km path) and Napilihan tornadoes were rated IF1, and the remaining two vortices IF0. The near-simultaneous Magang and Cahabaan storms were close enough that inflow-outflow interactions may have aided tornadogenesis. Dual-polarization radar revealed Z$_\mathrm{DR}$ and K$_\mathrm{DP}$ columns, a tornadic debris signature co-located with the Magang velocity couplet, and a bounded weak echo region in the Cahabaan supercell. To our knowledge, this is the first well-observed tornado outbreak with simultaneous tornadic supercells documented in the Philippines within an easterly severe weather regime.

authors.name: Generich H. Capuli

papers.title: A stochastic agent-based extension of the GSM$^2$ model for particle therapy: cell-cycle dynamics, dose-rate dependence, and fractionation effects
papers.summary: We present a stochastic agent-based extension of the Generalized Stochastic Microdosimetric Model (GSM$^2$) that links microscopic energy deposition by ionizing radiation to population-scale response. Each cell is represented as an agent whose DNA damage, cell-cycle phase, and fate evolve as a continuous-time Markov process. Particle arrivals, repair, misrepair, division, death, and migration are treated as competing stochastic events in an event-driven algorithm, enabling track-structure simulations of spheroids with up to $1.5\times10^5$ cells in minutes on a single workstation. For static populations, the model reproduces the Lea--Catcheside dose-rate dependence of survival for proton and carbon-ion irradiation over four orders of magnitude in dose rate. Dose-rate sparing decreases with increasing LET and disappears for low-energy carbon ions. After calibration to a single survival curve for aerobic X-ray irradiation of V79 spheroids, the model predicts without further fitting survival under anoxia and after carbon-ion irradiation in aerobic and anoxic conditions, reproducing measured oxygen enhancement ratios and relative biological effectiveness. Applied to three-dimensional tumor spheroids, the framework resolves responses to single, split, and fractionated irradiations, separates the effects of repair, reassortment, and repopulation, and quantifies stochastic variability between realizations. The model provides a mechanistic single-cell framework for studying time-dependent effects and uncertainty in particle irradiation.
