authors.name: Francesco G. Cordoni, Marco Battestini, Marta Missiaggia

papers.title: High Frame-Rate Mid-Infrared SPAD Camera
papers.summary: Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays have enhanced optical imaging capabilities by enabling a distinctive combination of photon-counting sensitivity, nanosecond-scale gating, and high frame-rate operation. These capabilities, however, have remained mostly confined to the visible and near-infrared, leaving the mid-infrared, the spectral region hosting the fundamental vibrational signatures of most molecules, largely devoid of these benefits. Here, we demonstrate the first mid-IR SPAD imaging system by integrating broadband adiabatic frequency upconversion with a 512 X 512 Silicon SPAD array. This architecture extends the SPAD functionality to the mid-IR, enabling room-temperature, low-noise, broadband photon-counting imaging. We achieve spectrally resolved mid-IR imaging at frame rates of up to 60,000 frames per second and capture nanosecond-scale laser-induced thermal dynamics via weak mid-IR blackbody emission, revealing spatial-temporal behavior predominantly indistinct to existing technologies. These results establish a potential platform for photon-resolved, ultrafast thermal and chemical imaging in a spectral range with more limited high-speed low-light detection capabilities

authors.name: Ziv Abelson, Daniel Beitner, Ziv Livne, Eyal Hollander, Moshe Cohen Erner, Edoardo Charbon, Haim Suchowski

papers.title: Numerical quality factor statistics for superconducting rf cavities with spatially inhomogeneous multilayer coatings modeled by Gaussian random fields
papers.summary: Bulk niobium has long been the material of choice for superconducting radio-frequency applications. An alternative approach is the superconductor-insulator-superconductor multilayer structure, which enables the use of brittle high-$T_c$ materials such as NbTiN. At present, SIS coatings are limited to flat samples, with the single-cell TESLA cavity representing a key milestone. Extending coating processes to non-flat geometries is expected to introduce macroscopic inhomogeneities in coating thickness. We model these variations using Gaussian random fields parametrized by a length scale, and generated by solving a stochastic partial differential equation. The resulting field is incorporated into the boundary condition of the cavity eigenvalue problem, from which quantities of interest -- such as resonant frequency and quality factor -- are computed. This procedure is repeated for eight length scales, with \num{2048} samples per length scale, where the resulting quality factors are recorded. Our results show that the quality factors follow a normal distribution. The standard deviation increases with the length scale and can be statistically distinguished. In contrast, the mean values remain largely unchanged, with only a few significant differences. In extreme cases, depending on the length scale, the quality factor may differ from the uniform case by \SIrange{2}{6}{\percent}.

authors.name: Aaron Gobeyn, Wolfgang Ackermann, Herbert De Gersem

papers.title: Significant heat transfer enhancement via polymer additives in two-dimensional sheared convection
papers.summary: Heat dissipation is critical in modern engineering and polymer additives offer a potential route to improve fluid-based cooling. We study elasticity-enhanced heat transfer in two-dimensional, thermally stratified Poiseuille flow. At Reynolds numbers $Re \lesssim 1000$, we observe two linearly unstable modes: the recently identified elasticity-induced centre mode (Khalid \textit{et al.}, \textit{J. Fluid Mech.}\@\ \textbf{915}, 2021) and the classical buoyancy-driven convective mode (Kelly, \textit{Adv. Appl. Mech.}\@\nobreakspace\textbf{31}, 35--112, 1994). Direct numerical simulations show that the centre mode develops into a nonlinear `arrowhead' state but yields negligible heat transfer enhancement (typically $\approx 0.03\%$ above the conductive state). By contrast, polymers can enhance the heat flux associated with the convective mode by up to $1100\%$. The nonlinear convective-mode states are periodic orbits or travelling waves, dominated by hook-like polymer-stress structures that can attach to channel walls. Both unattached and attached hooks act as `polymer walls', steering flow along rather than across them. Unattached hooks deflect fluid vertically around them in the channel interior and reduce flow rate, whereas wall-attached hooks travel more slowly, reorganising the flow into strong counter-rotating rolls and triggering extreme enhancement. The elasto-buoyant nature of these states is confirmed by perturbation kinetic energy budgets, showing that polymer and buoyancy sustain the states synergistically. Wall-attached hooks enable rapid thermal equilibration but impose a large hydraulic penalty, making them suitable for process streams requiring fast temperature adjustment. Unattached hooks provide a more thermally efficient regime for heat transport. These results highlight the potential of elastic fluids for future heat transfer enhancement technologies.

authors.name: Guanhan Li, Lu Zhu, Rich. R. Kerswell

papers.title: Endogenous drivers of gender disparity in online dating
papers.summary: In its early days, online dating was heralded as a great equalizer, removing biases built into heterosexual courtship. However, as repeatedly observed, that prophecy was never fulfilled, and some biases have even become exacerbated. In this paper, we identify a general endogenous mechanism that can amplify a small initial gender gap in first-contact rates of heterosexual dating, even when women and men follow identical behavioral rules. This mechanism relies on assumptions about the participants' expectations of new contacts and their time constraints. We formulate this symmetry-breaking mechanism as a system of differential equations and analyze its fixed points and their stability. The mechanism explains the amplification of a gap, not its origin or direction, which may stem from social norms, preferences, or platform design.

authors.name: Huaiyu Tan, Chenyu Li, Taha Yasseri, Lei Shi, Petter Holme

papers.title: Second stability region for gyrokinetics and the L-H transition
papers.summary: Using a simple circular tokamak geometry, we show the well-known `second stability region' of MHD-ballooning modes exists for linear gyrokinetics too---whether electrostatic or electromagnetic---and we suggest that the plasma enters this region in H-mode as a consequence of the bootstrap current and Shafranov shift altering the magnetic field, which may occur if the normalised pressure gradient is $\alpha_{\rm MHD} \simgt 1$ and collisionality is low. By performing simulations in more realistic magnetic geometries, we demonstrate a large reduction in collisionless, electrostatic turbulent transport when going from density and temperature profiles typical of L- and H-mode, respectively. This reduction is shown to be a consequence of both the bootstrap current lowering the global magnetic shear, and the pressure gradient altering the local magnetic shear, pushing the plasma towards the second-stability region. A path connecting the L- and H-mode equilibria is constructed, along which the energy and particle fluxes exhibit non-monotonic behaviour as a function of the pressure gradient.

authors.name: R. J. J. Mackenbach, A. Zocco, P. Helander

papers.title: Quasi-DNS with chemical kinetics for a single multiple-injection burner element under stable lean conditions for future gas turbine applications
papers.summary: We develop a Quasi-DNS with chemical kinetics for a stable lean condition in a single multiple-injection burner element for future gas turbine applications, as a reusable workflow for a coaxial mixing-tube burner. Here, Quasi-DNS denotes a high-resolution, turbulence-model-free calculation; it is not DNS in the strict sense. The OpenFOAM-based method includes: (i) a simplified 30deg sector geometry capturing vortices at the mixing tube outlet, (ii) boundary conditions reproducing coaxial jets and preheated air, (iii) a reduced Correa methane-air mechanism compared with GRI 3.0 using Cantera, (iv) mesh-development and grid-sensitivity assessment based on flame structure and the squared gradient of mixture fraction, and (v) post-processing with methane-based flame index. Demonstration at an equivalence ratio phi = 0.45 shows limited in-tube mixing and strong outlet vortices, yielding a more extended heat release region than the RANS solution. - A reusable high-resolution, turbulence-model-free Quasi-DNS workflow with detailed methane-air chemistry is developed for a coaxial mixing-tube burner. - The workflow combines a reduced methane-air mechanism, refined sector-domain meshes, and scalar-field diagnostics for characterizing mixing and heat release regions. - The workflow enables analysis of mixing and flame stabilization under stable lean conditions, and provides a high-resolution numerical reference under the stated assumptions for comparison with RANS-based calculations.

authors.name: Kazuki Abe, Youhi Morii, Kaoru Maruta

papers.title: Fundamental limits in photonics and electromagnetics: a tutorial
papers.summary: Theoretical limits and physical bounds across many areas of science, mathematics, and technology -- including Shannon's information-capacity limits, Bennett and Landauer's thermodynamic limits on computation, and G\"odel's incompleteness theorem in formal logic -- serve as defining pillars of their fields. In photonics and electromagnetism, numerous physical bounds and constraints have likewise been uncovered over the past several decades. In this Tutorial, we first review the fundamental principles that constrain light-matter interactions, and then discuss limits at different hierarchical scales, from optical material responses to wave propagation, scattering, and related optical phenomena and functions, relevant to a wide range of applications. By providing a more unified treatment of these results and highlighting the many open questions that remain, our goal is to help readers rapidly get up to speed with the frontier of this research area and contribute to advancing the broader vision of a universal framework for fundamental limits of light interactions with matter.

authors.name: Owen D. Miller, Francesco Monticone

papers.title: Joos-Weinberg covariant field with mass and spin $\frac{3}{2}$
papers.summary: We present the explicit theory of the Joos-Weinberg covariant field with spin $\frac{3}{2}$ which is a eight-dimensional massive covariant field transforming according to the representation $(\frac{3}{2},0)\oplus(0, \frac{3}{2})$ of the group $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. As the transformation matrices of this representation are still unknown, we apply a new method for deriving them using exclusively maximally reducible representations, e. g. $(1,0)\otimes(\frac{1}{2},0)$ instead of the irreducible one $(1,\frac{1}{2})=(1,0)\otimes(0,\frac{1}{2})$ we meet in usual frameworks. After applying this method, we obtain a $12$-component covariant field transforming according to the representation $[(1,0)\otimes(\frac{1}{2},0)]\oplus [(0,1)\otimes(0, \frac{1}{2})]$ which is maximally reducible, up to subspaces of irreducible representations of the $SU(2)$ group. Consequently, after developing the theory in the direct product basis of the representation $(1,0)\otimes(\frac{1}{2},0)$, we can separate the sector of spin half revealing thus the genuine Joos-Weinberg covariant massive field of spin $\frac{3}{2}$. The theory of this field is build naturally deriving the field equation and associated matrices, Lagrangian formalism, inner product and the closed expressions of the orthonormal mode spinors.

authors.name: Ion I. Cotaescu

papers.title: State estimation of Rayleigh-B\'enard convection with reduced-order models
papers.summary: In this work, we develop a state estimation framework for two-dimensional Rayleigh-B\'enard (RB) convection that combines a stable Galerkin reduced-order model (ROM) with an extended Kalman filter (EKF). The ROM, constructed from controllability modes of the linearized Boussinesq equations, provides the nonlinear dynamical model for the filter prediction step. Direct numerical simulations (DNS) are used to generate synthetic measurements for data assimilation. We assess filter performance across periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic regimes, demonstrating that the filter tracks the most energetic modes with high fidelity and achieves time-averaged reconstruction errors below $16\%$ for velocity and $19\%$ for temperature. We apply the ROM-based EKF to a hybrid simulation scenario where the system state is assimilated from velocity measurements. It is shown that velocity observations alone suffice to reconstruct the state, including the temperature field. Finally, we exploit the Kalman gain matrix to develop a greedy sensor placement strategy that progressively removes the least informative sensors. The algorithm reveals a clear hierarchy among sensor types and can be used to derive skeletal observation configurations. It also provides guidance on which measurement variables and spatial locations are most informative for state correction. The present framework is general, and may be applied to other quadratic Galerkin ROMs for state estimation.

authors.name: Enrique Flores-Montoya, Andr\'e F. C. da Silva, Andr\'e V. G. Cavalieri

papers.title: The Optics of Shadow Bands
papers.summary: Shadow bands are transient, rippling patterns of light and dark that may appear in moments before and after totality in a solar eclipse. Despite centuries of reports, their physical origin has remained unresolved. This article develops a geometric-optical solution in which the Sun's extended structure produces a celestial analog of Young's double-slit experiment, generating an interference and fringes on the ground. The analysis combines solar limb geometry and a wave-based formulation that yields quantitative predictions for fringe width and spacing. Some other properties of shadow bands are also analyzed.

authors.name: Branko Sretenovi\'c

papers.title: Midlatitude cloud radiative effects reinforce storm tracks on seasonal timescales
papers.summary: Midlatitude storm tracks play a central role in Earth's climate by transporting heat from low to high latitudes. Their strength is therefore set by the meridional temperature gradients, traditionally linked to differential solar heating. This framework predicts a substantial seasonal reduction in storm activity, as meridional insolation gradients vanish during summer. Yet in the Southern Hemisphere, storm activity decreases by only about 40% from its seasonal maximum. Here, we show that cloud radiative effects contribute to the seasonal maintenance of storm activity by reinforcing the temperature gradients that sustain it. Satellite observations reveal that sunlight reflected by midlatitude clouds in early summer creates a substantial meridional gradient in surface heating, despite the nearly uniform summer insolation. Idealized aquaplanet simulations then show that shortwave cloud radiative effects reinforce meridional sea-surface temperature gradients, thereby strengthening storm activity primarily during late summer and autumn, while longwave cloud effects partly offset this response. To interpret these results, we develop a simple theoretical model linking storms, clouds, and sea-surface temperature gradients. The model captures the seasonal response and demonstrates the importance of two emergent cloud properties: the maximum attainable cloud albedo and the sensitivity of cloud cover to storm activity. Together, these findings indicate that cloud radiative feedbacks help maintain the thermal gradients that sustain storm activity on seasonal timescales. More broadly, they reveal a strong coupling among storms, clouds, and the ocean spanning distinct spatial and temporal scales.

authors.name: Or Hadas

papers.title: Tuning Plasma Frequency of Nested Wire Media
papers.summary: We study nested wire media possessing $C_6$ and $C_4$ rotational symmetries whose plasma frequencies can be controlled through breathing deformation. Numerical simulations reveal tunability exceeding $80\%$ and $60\%$ for the considered $C_6$ and $C_4$ breathing geometries, respectively. To describe these structures, we develop an analytical model based on the local field approach within the thin-wire approximation, which confirms the high tunability of the studied wire structures. We also propose an approximation for dense wire media. The developed framework is applicable to the general case of nested wire structures -- wire media with an arbitrary parallelogram lattice and multiple wires per unit cell.

authors.name: Denis Sakhno, Pavel A. Belov

papers.title: Generalization of Rayleigh's high-frequency theory for the 2D Helmholtz equation in a half-space subject to a radiation condition at infinity and a Dirichlet condition on a 1D periodically-uneven boundary
papers.summary: The 2D Helmholtz equation, radiation condition and Dirichlet boundary condition, are the translation, in mathematical terms, of (at least) three physical 2D problems for the prediction of the total scalar wavefield on one side of an impenetrable 1D periodically uneven boundary when: a) a plane TE electromagnetic wave propagating in the vacuum strikes the boundary the other side of which is occupied by a perfectly-conducting medium, b) a plane SH elastic elastic wave strikes a rigid boundary, c) a plane acoustic wave strikes a pressure-release boundary. The first attempt to solve such problems in a non-heuristic manner was made by Lord Rayleigh (in his book, 'The Theory of Sound' which appeared in 1896). My task will be to revisit Rayleigh's theory of diffraction by a sinusoidal-shaped, impenetrable boundary, and more specifically, his perturbation method for obtaining a mathematically-explicit solution to the diffraction problem in the high-frequency regime. In so doing, I shall correct and generalize Rayleigh's method to obtain solutions for arbitrary angles of incidence as well as for 1D periodic impenetrable boundaries of quite-general shape.

authors.name: Armand Wirgin

papers.title: Continuous 3-D Latent Diffusion for Medical Image Generation and Reconstruction
papers.summary: High-resolution three-dimensional (3-D) medical latent diffusion remains limited by the cost of decoding full volumes, which existing latent autoencoders (AEs) handle through overlapping sub-volume decoding. We propose a continuous 3-D latent diffusion model framework for computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) generation and measurement-guided reconstruction, built on a coordinate-rendering autoencoder (CoRe-AE). Its decoder applies its convolutional stage once on the compact latent grid and renders voxel intensities from spatial coordinates through a lightweight implicit head, evaluated in memory-bounded chunks. This design avoids overlapping sub-volumes and remains differentiable with respect to the latent, so that the decoder can be used inside measurement-guided reconstruction. The framework was evaluated on CT volumes of 512\textsuperscript{3} voxels and MRI volumes of 256\textsuperscript{3} voxels. At 512\textsuperscript{3}, the decoder was 4--18 times faster than the MAISI and 3D MedDiffusion AEs and required the lowest peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory, including when its gradient was computed. CoRe-AE also achieved the highest peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) among the evaluated AEs on both modalities. The resulting frozen 3-D latent prior generated full volumes without patch seams and, without retraining, reconstructed sparse-view CT and accelerated MRI through hard data consistency, within 2.4--4.9 dB PSNR of the pixel-domain decomposed diffusion sampler (DDS). A single volumetric latent prior thus supports both generation and reconstruction of high-resolution medical volumes on one GPU. Our code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/Mellak/continuous-3d-latent-diffusion.

authors.name: Youness Mellak, Antoine De Paepe, Dimitris Visvikis, Alexandre Bousse

papers.title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
papers.summary: In fluid-fluid displacements in porous and fractured materials, viscous friction in microscale interfacial (Haines) jumps is intimately linked to macroscale energy dissipation and the associated pressure-saturation (retention) hysteresis. The mode of control (flow rate vs. pressure) and the driving rate (from quasistatic to finite) can substantially affect hysteresis. Despite the significance of hysteresis and dissipation in various technological and natural processes, a quantitative understanding of the link between the micro- and macro-scales, and of the impact of the inherent heterogeneity of porous media, remains elusive. An ``imperfect'' Hele-Shaw cell of variable aperture is a simple model system which allows to study all these in details. However, simulating fluid-fluid interface evolution in heterogeneous media, even in such a simple system, is computationally prohibitive, as multiple length and time scales need to be resolved simultaneously. We develop here a spectral computational approach for interface evolution and energy dissipation and validate it via comparison to computational fluid dynamics simulations and experiments. Computational efficiency is demonstrated by following interface evolution in a cell with a single ``defect'', as well as with random roughness; in both, disparate length scales lead to nontrivial dynamics over many orders of magnitude in time. We also show theoretically that, in the quasi-static limit, while viscous forces during Haines jumps fully account for the energy dissipated between consecutive metastable equilibria, viscosity does not change the total dissipated amount, merely the relaxation time. Our approach provides a stepping stone towards upscaling of fluid-fluid flows in porous media.

authors.name: Mykyta Chubynsky, Jordi Ortin, Marco Dentz, Ran Holtzman

papers.title: From populations to absolute binding affinities in molecular simulations: exact volumetric terms and practical estimators
papers.summary: Biomolecular simulations of binding commonly confine the unbound ligand with volumetric restraints to accelerate convergence. However, a general account of how such restraints enter the volumetric term of the standard binding free energy, and of how this term should be evaluated from histogram data, is currently lacking. We take as our starting point the established relation, in the dilute limit, between the binding constant $K$ and the relative populations of the bound and unbound states, which we re-derive from the canonical partition function of molecular solutes in explicit solvent. Building on this relation, we show that a restraint that leaves the bound state unaffected and confines a homogeneous unbound region modifies the volumetric term in a single way, by replacing the system volume with the volume of the region over which the unbound population is evaluated. This yields closed-form estimators for restrained simulations, computable from histograms of any suitably defined reaction coordinate, with the volumetric term kept explicit. Previous expressions based on the potential of mean force are recovered as a special case. The analysis also exposes two distinct errors in current practice: single-bin estimators, which reduce the bound state to one histogram bin and are not valid estimators of $K$, and working formulas that omit the bin width entering the volumetric term, which make the result depend on the unit of length. We apply the estimators to a Lennard-Jones dimer, the cucurbit[7]uril/1-adamantanol host--guest complex, and the galactonate--DgoT ligand--protein complex.

authors.name: Davide Mandelli, Emiliano Ippoliti, Charles Plate

papers.title: Evaluation of the Ambipolar Diffusion Approximation in Partially Ionized Rarefied Hypersonic Flows
papers.summary: Accurate numerical simulation of rarefied hypersonic plasmas is increasingly important for optimization of re-entry spacecraft design and the development of advanced aerospace technologies. For kinetic simulation methods, it is convention to enforce ions and electrons to diffuse at the same rate, known as the ambipolar diffusion approximation. This approach circumvents costly resolution of fast electron motion, but neglects the complex plasma dynamics of ions and electrons. Almost all studies that investigated the efficacy of the ambipolar diffusion approximation in hypersonics report noticeable differences in flowfield properties when electrostatic modeling is used, including increases in vehicle surface heat flux and decreases in electron temperature. However, studying the ambipolar diffusion approximation in multi-species hypersonic flows (such as air flows) makes it challenging to isolate the origin of these differences. Kinetic hypersonic flow simulations with electrostatic modeling are performed with argon to quantify the validity of the ambipolar diffusion approximation along a one-dimensional stagnation streamline. Three different plasma diffusion regimes are studied under two sets of rarefied freestream flow conditions. The approximation is evaluated in terms of predicting plasma density distributions, electron temperature, and stagnation point heat flux. New criteria are proposed for identification of plasma diffusion regimes in hypersonic flows and use of the ambipolar diffusion approximation.

authors.name: Marisa Petrusky, Iain D. Boyd

papers.title: Validating direct solvers for Newton's gravitational N-body problem, and the systematic comparison between IEEE floating point and Posits
papers.summary: We present a systematic comparison between arbitrary precise arithmetic and integration, IEEE-754 compliant floating point arithmetic (fp16, bfp16, fp32, double precision fp64, and quadruple precision fp128), and two implementations of Posits (type III unum) for solving Newton's chaotic N-body problem. Each implementation is benchmarked with arbitrary precise calculations to objectively evaluate their performance in precision as well as speed. We rely on hardware and compiler implementations for fp64, and software implementations for arbitrary-precision arithmetic and Posits. Half precision arithmetic (fp16, bfp16, and Posits$$) are insufficiently precise for solving Newton's equations of motion. Single precision (fp32, and Posits$$) could be used for statistical ensemble calculations, but lead to relatively large errors in any individual strong encounter. All 64-bit implementations fp64 as well as Posits (Posits$$) experience difficulty in our tests. One of the implementations of Posits (Universal) gives precision comparable to fp64 but is slow (by at least an orders of magnitude compared to fp64 after correcting for the more efficient hardware support for the latter). The other (CPPPosits) has a speed comparable to fp64 but has systematically larger errors (by about an order of magnitude compared to fp64 with excesses exceeding two orders of magnitude). As a consequence, this implementation leads to a systematic drift in the result space and has difficulty resolving close encounters. Posits and fp64 have difficulty when integrating a dynamical system in a moving reference frame; testing Galileo invariancy. In their current implementation, Posits do not seem to be the ideal alternative for fp64 when integrating chaotic or stiff ordinary differential equations, such as Newton's equations of motion.

authors.name: Simon Portegies Zwart (Leiden Observatory)

papers.title: Investigation of the Asymptotic Properties of Active Impedance in Large Finite Array Antennas
papers.summary: This paper presents an improved full-wave solver for finite array antennas, and uses this solver to examine asymptotic properties of active impedance for large regular arrays. The improved solver is based on a preconditioning scheme that has been adapted for use on more general finite geometries, and an improved data structure. These two improvements result in a fast and stable solver with a lower memory footprint. By investigating the active impedance of the center element in finite arrays it is found that, even for arrays with 1000 elements, asymptotic behavior may differ appreciably from infinite arrays. Tied to these properties, different predictors on how the active impedance of the center element in the array behaves are presented. The two best predictors work very well for the wideband arrays investigated, and may be used to decide when array approximations, such as unit cell methods, are appropriate, rather than general statements on array size.

authors.name: Harald Hultin, Lucas {\AA}kerstedt, B. L. G. Jonsson

papers.title: Simple data fusion from several ocean and atmosphere hindcast models improves surface drifter trajectory prediction
papers.summary: Simulating the trajectory of surface drifters in the ocean matters for search and rescue, pollution tracking, oil and chemical spill response, and marine risk analysis. Accurate prediction remains difficult, as widely acknowledged in the literature, and also illustrated by the ``Forecasting Floats in Turbulence'' challenge issued by the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) in 2021, and which ultimately led to this paper. The main source of error usually comes from uncertain ocean currents, while errors in wind forcing and object drift properties are often smaller [Dagestad and R\"ohrs, 2019]. Here, we use an open one-year dataset of Sofar Spotter trajectories together with several ocean and atmospheric hindcast products to test data-driven drift models at scale. We compare three approaches: i) a standard (baseline) drifter trajectory simulation based on one ocean model and one atmospheric model, ii) linear regression (LR) models that fuse all available predictors, and iii) neural networks (NN) using similar inputs. A simple LR model that combines all predictors performs equally well as the NN. Because LR is simpler, cheaper, and more robust, we retain it as the preferred approach. In 2-day trajectory prediction, this improves the Liu-Weisberg skill score by around 40\% relative to the baseline. These findings apply to hindcast mode; applying this methodology for forecast mode remains for future work.

authors.name: Jean Rabault, Knut Frode Dagestad, Gaute Hope

papers.title: Multiphysics simulation of all-optical switching and sequential magneto-optic readout in an integrated Si$_3$N$_4$/GdFeCo waveguide
papers.summary: Femtosecond pulses guided in a silicon nitride waveguide have recently switched a Co/Gd magnetic element patterned on top of it, a step towards magnetic memory built into photonic circuits. The guided mode heats such an element non-uniformly, and, to our knowledge, no calculation has yet followed the written state from this heating to an optical readout. Here we model both steps for an 8 nm GdFeCo film inserted across a Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguide. A three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain calculation gives the absorbed pump energy. This energy drives a four-temperature model and calibrated stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch dynamics, and a later probe pulse reads the recovered state. At the reference fluence, a single pump pulse reverses 86% of the film from either saturated state, and this fraction changes little over a 2.4-fold range of incident fluence. The unswitched cells lie where the absorbed fluence stays below the single-cell threshold, and a threshold rule applied to the absorption map reproduces the full calculation. When the film starts from zero magnetization, thermal noise sets the direction of each recovered local moment at random. Between the saturated and random states, the probe energy fractions change by at most 0.02. The magnetic Faraday and Kerr rotations are far more sensitive and become about 12 and 130 times smaller, respectively, in the random state than in a saturated film. The reflected signal also contains a magnetization-independent geometric background, which can be removed by subtracting a reference signal. The model therefore predicts that a guided probe can distinguish the written states through its polarization. It assumes a homogeneous film and omits heat flow and exchange between neighbouring cells.

authors.name: Muhammad Arief Mulyana, Budi Adiperdana, Ayi Bahtiar

papers.title: Dark matter deformations of photon-ring echoes in horizon-scale interferometry
papers.summary: Photon-ring echoes can probe the delayed light paths near rotating black holes, even when their main ring scales agree. We study an effective rotating geometry with a strong dark matter spike and compare it with a separately ring-matched Kerr control. At $a/M_B=0.8$, $i=70^\circ$, and $M_H/M_B=10$, the remaining angular critical-parameter fingerprint is $1.49\%$. The first two higher image orders have median delays of $13.33M$ and $33.06M$, with spike--Kerr shifts of $1.192M$ and $0.378M$. Finite-order ray transport, slow-light synchrotron images, and complex very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) visibilities show distinct delay and interference patterns. Direct and higher-order images contribute differently to the complex visibility signal. With the same emitting source, the model difference survives controlled station noise. Independent synthetic-source tests show that the signal depends strongly on source variability: EHT-like held-out closures give an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of $0.658$ (95\% interval $0.497$--$0.807$), while two source-conditioned tests give AUC values close to $0.5$. Published general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) light curves of Sgr A* illustrate how electron physics changes variability on the relevant time scales. Together these results connect environmental photon transport to interferometric observables and quantify the importance of source information for future echo studies.

authors.name: Mohsen Fathi

papers.title: The Minimal Persona: Rarer and Shared Labels Both Skew Allocation Among AI Agents
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents built on large language models increasingly work in teams, where one agent divides tasks or resources among others that the software marks with a team, a role or a similar label. A model that simply up-weights any recipient sharing a string with its own context would favor same-label peers, so a shared-label tilt alone says little about groups. Borrowing the minimal-group paradigm of social psychology, we had six language models divide 100 points among 19 peers that differed only in carrying one of two invented words, in groups of unequal size (32,400 decisions). Varying group size separates two effects. In five of the six models, at the most unequal split, a recipient with the rarer label received 1.3 to 3.3 times the points of one with the common label even when the decider was not told its own label: a rarity effect that involves no match to the decider. In four of them it accounts for 35% to 55% of the extra favoritism that agents in the smaller group show their own group, and for more in the fifth. Telling the decider its label adds an own-group effect, positive in every model and in five of the six indistinguishable from label matching. With the labels hidden, neither appears. Because the labels mean nothing, bias tests built on lists of named social groups are not designed to detect either effect.

authors.name: Messi H. J. Lee

papers.title: Dual-polarized, mid-infrared nonreciprocal absorption
papers.summary: The emission and absorption of thermal radiation are usually coupled via reciprocity and Kirchhoff's law, stated as the equality of spectral directional emissivity and absorptivity. Magneto-optical materials have recently been identified as a promising route to lifting the constraint of reciprocity for thermal emission and absorption, with multiple experimental demonstrations using doped InAs, which is described by an antisymmetric, nonreciprocal dielectric tensor under an applied magnetic field. However, these demonstrations have been limited to p-polarized light in the Voigt configuration, whereas thermal radiation from a blackbody is unpolarized and thus comprised of both s- and p-polarized light. This means existing nonreciprocal emitter and absorber designs underutilize available power by 50%. Here, we report a photonic crystal slab-based structure that exhibits nonreciprocal absorption for both s- and p-polarizations in the mid-infrared spectral range. The structure operates from 11-20 $\mu$m and consists of an a-Si photonic crystal slab on top of a doped InAs substrate. The photonic crystal slab supports eigenmodes that couple to both s- and p-polarized plane waves, resulting in absorption peaks that, because of the applied magnetic field, spectrally shift in opposite directions for forward- and backward-propagating light$\unicode{8212}$a signature of nonreciprocity in planar, subwavelength systems. We fabricate the designed structure, then experimentally demonstrate dual-polarized nonreciprocal absorption by measuring its room-temperature absorptance using magnetic-field-integrated absorptance spectroscopy. Our design is a step toward the complete control of light as heat, which could improve photonic energy conversion, thermal management, and mid-infrared optical isolation and circulation.

authors.name: Simo Pajovic, Yiting Zhao, Yae-Chan Lim, Ruzan Sokhoyan, Harry A. Atwater

papers.title: Broad-angle photon-pair generation from high-$Q$ flatband resonant 3R-MoS$_{2}$ metasurfaces
papers.summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in ultrathin optical resonant metasurfaces offers a promising platform for integrated quantum light sources. However, conventional resonances suffer from steep momentum dispersion, limiting photon-pair generation to narrow excitation and emission angles. Here, we demonstrate a high-$Q$ flatband resonant 3R-MoS$_{2}$ metasurface for high-efficiency, broad-angle SPDC photon-pair generation. By combining Brillouin zone folding with in-plane symmetry breaking, we engineer a high-$Q$ flatband resonance in the near-infrared regime, maintaining a robust $Q$-factor across a wide range of incident angles. Exploiting the strong local electric field enhancement of resonance and the large second-order susceptibility of 3R-MoS$_{2}$, the metasurface boosts the degenerate SPDC pair-generation rate with orders of magnitude enhancement over an unpatterned film of identical thickness. Crucially, the near-zero band dispersion extends the effective emission angle to $\pm 5^{\circ}$ with negligible spectral drift $\sim 0.1$ nm and high directional tolerance. Under pulsed excitation with a finite spectral bandwidth, the metasurface maintains a substantial bandwidth-averaged photon-pair yield, while demonstrating strong spectral locking of the resonant emission channel against pump wavelength detuning despite the expected trade-off in generation efficiency. This work establishes a versatile strategy for momentum-independent quantum light sources, opening new avenues for scan-free quantum ghost imaging and quantum information processing.

authors.name: Tingting Liu, Huifu Qiu, Xintong Shi, Jumin Qiu, Shuyuan Xiao

papers.title: Transferable reconstruction of equilibria in network dynamics from sentinel nodes
papers.summary: Reconstructing the state of a large networked system from measurements at only a few nodes is a challenge for monitoring, prediction, and intervention. Here we ask whether such reconstruction is possible for equilibrium states and whether it can transfer across different nonlinear dynamics. We study this question across various networks and across $17$ nonlinear dynamics on networks from different domains. For each network, we observe only a vanishingly small fraction of sentinel nodes and train either a neural network or linear decoder. We find that accurate reconstruction is often possible, and that transferability is structured rather than universal. Eleven dynamics with adjacency-matrix-type coupling form a robust transferable class. By contrast, six diffusively coupled dynamics form isolated transfer components. Non-random sentinel selection is consistently important, and linear decoders often approach neural-network performance. These results show that sparse node observations can encode enough information to reconstruct full network equilibria across broad families of nonlinear dynamics, while also revealing sharp limits to universal transfer.

authors.name: Naoki Masuda, Bisna Mary Eldo, Tharusha Bandara

papers.title: Skyrmion topology of scalar waves in real and momentum space
papers.summary: Generalizations of magnetic skyrmions to the context of other areas of physics, such as plasmonics, optics (including microcavity polaritons) and even water waves have become an important research topic. However, the generalization of the skyrmion number in such systems is still the subject of active research. While magnetic skyrmions textures are inherently formed by vectors (magnetic spin vectors), recent developments in other areas of physics have generalized the concept of skyrmions and skyrmionic patterns to the case in which scalar fields are used to define 3-component pseudo-spin vectors. This gives rise to a wide variety of skyrmion-like textures, depending on the detailed functional forms of the scalar fields. For example, steady-state outgoing waves in driven-dissipative polariton systems fail to have a well-defined global skyrmion number in real (configuration) space but can have one in momentum space. We classify the skyrmion integral for various scalar fields with different asymptotic behaviors in real space as well as momentum space, and in both cases give conditions for the skyrmion number not to exist, or be integer, half-integer or non-integer. Examples of physical systems to which our analysis can be applied include polariton condensates, water waves and gain-guided lasers.

authors.name: Nai H. Kwong, Ewan M. Wright, Jan Wingenbach, Roman Lebs, Harald Giessen, Stefan Schumacher, Rolf Binder

papers.title: Bianisotropic Space-Time Metasurfaces
papers.summary: We experimentally demonstrate bianisotropic space-time metasurfaces based on varactor-loaded omega-shaped meta-atoms. Full-wave simulations reveal coexisting electric and ring-associated magnetic responses at the operating frequency, while a traveling-wave modulation drives reactive loads embedded in both responsive regions of the meta-atom. The resulting space-time modulation generates a reconfigurable polychromatic spectrum with directional sideband radiation governed by Floquet phase matching. Under free-space illumination, the same metasurface preferentially couples the received field toward one guided port, producing modulation-controlled directional routing. The measurements characterize the collective bianisotropic response rather than independently retrieving its electric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric susceptibility components. These results establish bianisotropic space-time metasurfaces as a platform for jointly controlling frequency generation, directional radiation, and wave routing within a single dynamically modulated aperture.

authors.name: Sajjad Taravati, Ya-Adama Kabia

papers.title: Detuning-Controlled Vibrational Autler--Townes Passage toward Single-Sublevel Orientation of Nonpolar Molecules
papers.summary: Single-sublevel preparation would give collision and surface-scattering experiments access to oriented molecules, yet established orientation methods either require a permanent dipole moment or select only partially. We introduce all-optical Autler--Townes state-selective adiabatic passage (ASAP), in which a detuned infrared field dresses a rovibrational transition, and the selected dressed branch is mapped adiabatically onto one magnetic sublevel as the field vanishes. We resolve the magnetic-sublevel-selected rovibrational Autler--Townes doublet of the R(0) transition of $^{13}$CO$_2$ and show that the coupling strength and detuning set both its separation and the partition of the bare-state composition between its two components. The spectral selectivity of the target dressed branch reaches 97\% at a coupling detuning of $-1.2$~MHz. A density-matrix model calibrated against these spectra returns, for the dressed molecules, a target-sublevel population approaching 0.9 over a broad range of coupling powers and detunings.

authors.name: Meng-Yi Yu, Ya-Nan Lv, Cun-Feng Cheng, Shui-Ming Hu

papers.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
papers.summary: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $\mu$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

authors.name: Shelby Klomp, Shafaq Gulzar Elahi, Scott Grudichak, Chethn Galla, Zhiyuan Wang, Mark Nguyen, George Winstone, Katarina Boskovic Guy, Emma Derrick, Maddox Wroblewski, Jacob Sprague, Andrew Laeuger, Jackson Larsen, Nancy Aggarwal, Shane L. Larson, Andrew A. Geraci

papers.title: Phase-Stabilization-Free Information Processing on Unstable Photonic Processors
papers.summary: Hadamard-coded optical receivers commonly require stable interference conditions for absolute codeword discrimination. Here we encode four symbols as differential Hadamard operations: no phase change or a $\pi$ shift on exactly two of three non-reference input modes. The information is carried by the selected phase-change operation, rather than the absolute optical codeword. We investigate a fixed eight-port intensity-only receiver that reconstructs six coupled trigonometric observables from simultaneous power measurements. Their deterministic sign transformations allow an analytical decoder to identify the applied operation from successive measurements without continuous optical phase stabilization or knowledge of the initial absolute codeword label. An earlier measured signature and sufficiently limited inter-measurement drift remain necessary. We establish exact observable reconstruction, characterize exceptional phase configurations and conditional noise sensitivity, and compare ideal four- and eight-port detection under an equal-photon budget. Experiments on programmable photonic processors yield 96.19\% analytical decoding accuracy; a separate machine-learning analysis reports 98.31\% on a held-out experimental trace. The results demonstrate differential, intensity-only Hadamard operation decoding under the tested conditions.

authors.name: G\"okhan Elmas, Igor A Litvin, Janis N\"otzel

papers.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
papers.summary: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.

authors.name: Joseph T. A Peterson, Manoranjan Majji, John L. Junkins

papers.title: Dysfunctional Functionals and their Therapies in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
papers.summary: The exchange-correlation functional in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) is known to have dependence on past densities and initial states, and yet this memory-dependence is ignored in practical calculations which almost always use an adiabatic approximation. We discuss the dysfunction that arises due to this deficiency and point to therapies that go beyond the adiabatic approximation. Still, adiabatic TDDFT has had success in a wide range of systems for response properties and for fully non-equilibrium dynamics, and why this is so is only partially understood. This, together with the rigorous foundation of the exact theory and its favorable system-size scaling, provides tremendous impetus for continuing to strive towards improved approximations to the exact functionals, and a deeper understanding of the impact of approximations in applications.

authors.name: Neepa T. Maitra

papers.title: Implementation Science Driven Identification of Barriers to AI Diagnostic Decision Support: A Stakeholder-Informed Concept Mapping Study
papers.summary: The clinical translation of artificial intelligence (AI) is a critical step toward precision medicine. The implementation study presented here focuses specifically on barriers to AI adoption in the diagnostic medicine workflow. Successful clinical adoption of AI requires more than technical performance; it depends on addressing real-world organizational, ethical, infrastructural, and workflow-related barriers that may prevent promising systems from moving beyond research settings. To examine these barriers, we used structured concept mapping (CM) to operationalize stakeholder engagement and to integrate a knowledge translation (iKT) approach within the Knowledge-to-Action (KTA) framework. Stakeholders co-generated 96 statements describing barriers to AI implementation and organized them into 11 clusters, including infrastructure limitations, ethical and legal concerns, workflow integration challenges, and distrust in algorithmic reasoning. These findings provide actionable knowledge for supporting AI implementation in the diagnostic chain. We additionally position digital twins (DT) as a related, forward-looking context, as they are increasingly discussed as future extensions of AI-enabled care. As such, our findings offer preliminary insights for future DT deployment, as many DT systems are expected to rely on AI-driven prediction, multimodal data integration, and iterative model refinement. Addressing the identified barriers early may help AI-based clinical tools, and eventually DT-enabled applications, progress from prototypes toward evidence-based standards of care.

authors.name: Ali Fathi Jouzdani, Arman Gorji, Mohammad Zahedi, Morteza Alizadeh, Babak Saboury, Arman Rahmim, Mohammad R. Salmanpour, Ahmad Fayaz-Bakhsh

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moir\'e Flatband Superlattices
papers.summary: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moir\'e superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moir\'e modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moir\'e superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moir\'e superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

authors.name: Amin Zamani, Lihang Feng, Jianji Liu, Ze Zheng, Gabriel Sanderson, Mohsen Rahmani, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu

papers.title: A Multidimensional Evaluation Framework for Artificial Intelligence-Based Ocean State Forecasts
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) based ocean state forecasts now approach or surpass those produced by operational ocean forecasting systems as measured by conventional pointwise metrics. However, these metrics may favor spatially smoothed forecasts and cannot determine whether forecast variables remain physically coherent. Forecast evaluation should therefore move beyond overall pointwise accuracy toward assessing forecast trustworthiness. We propose a multidimensional framework comprising overall pointwise accuracy, physical consistency, and distributional consistency. Overall pointwise accuracy summarizes forecast and reference agreement over all valid samples; physical consistency evaluates dynamical balances using model outputs alone; and distributional consistency evaluates distribution tails and multiscale spatial structures. Three AI models were deployed as representative testbeds in a unified operational environment. This comprehensive assessment shows that lower overall pointwise errors cannot preclude substantial dynamical imbalances and suppressed fine-scale variance. Conversely, higher pointwise errors may arise from spatial displacement of coherent structures rather than a poor representation of their amplitude. The results demonstrate that the evaluation of AI ocean forecasting models should be based on the multi-dimensional assessment of forecast trustworthiness, rather than solely relying on a single metric. The study provides a preliminary framework for AI model intercomparison, which is also informative for targeted model refinement and operational implementation.

authors.name: Ziqing Zu, Ye Yuan, Tiejun Ling, Zhi Chen, Xiang Li, Zhiqiang Li, Qiang Wang, Jiangjiang Xia, Jiuke Wang, Yongjun Jia, Shinan Wang, Zhi-Yuan Zhang, Renbo Pang, Xiaojuan Lin, Yu Zhang, Huier Mo, Ang Li

papers.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
papers.summary: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window; the infrared photon of a pair probes the excited sample at a set delay after excitation, and the transient response is read out from the count rate of its visible partner. We resolve picosecond carrier dynamics in a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror near 1529 nm with a picowatt-level probe, unaffected by thermal background and by sample IR photoluminescence 50 times stronger than the probe. The approach is applicable to the mid-infrared, fingerprint region, where infrared detection is hardest, and to the terahertz region.

authors.name: Jasleen Kaur, Yu Mukai, Ryo Okamoto, Shigeki Takeuchi

papers.title: Convection in the interior of Cepheid variable stars
papers.summary: This paper is associated with a poster winner of a 2025 American Physical Society's Division of Fluid Dynamics (DFD) Gallery of Fluid Motion Award for work presented at the DFD Gallery of Fluid Motion. The original poster is available online at the Gallery of Fluid Motion, https://doi.org/10.1103/APS.DFD.2025.GFM.P005.

authors.name: Maxime Stuck, Jane Pratt

papers.title: Graph Symbolic Distillation: Decoding Graph Data into Interpretable Formulas across Materials and Chemistry
papers.summary: Graph data provide a natural representation of the interconnected structures and interactions underlying many chemical and materials systems. Graph neural networks (GNNs) can learn complex relationships from such data, yet translating these representations into interpretable descriptors and scientific insights remains challenging. Here we introduce graph symbolic distillation (GSD), a framework for decoding graph data into interpretable symbolic formulas. GSD identifies task-relevant message-passing architectures and distills their learned transformations while preserving graph connectivity and aggregation operations. Across three case studies spanning bulk materials, molecules, and surfaces, GSD not only recovers expert-defined descriptors from elementary node and edge features, but also reveals relationships emerging from their organization in complex graphs: extremal local geometric descriptors for band gap variations in $\gamma$-CsPbI$_3$, a local polarity--size relationship underlying hydration free energy, and site-specific electronic-connectivity coupling in multidentate adsorption. GSD thus provides a general route from graph data to interpretable descriptors and new, testable scientific insights.

authors.name: Yuxuan Yao, Karsten Reuter, Wenbin Xu

papers.title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data
papers.summary: Reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse and irregular measurements remains challenging because the underlying inverse problem is severely underdetermined. Here we present MANTRA, a manifold-based tensor framework that represents each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space while constraining its coefficient tensor to a low-rank Tucker manifold. This structure provides a compact, data-adaptive representation without requiring gridded observations or governing equations. Riemannian optimization and adaptive selection of rank and basis complexity enable the model to exploit coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations. In simulations of forced isotropic turbulence and flow over a cylinder, MANTRA recovers multiscale structures at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and remains accurate under Gaussian noise up to 20% of the peak velocity. It also recovers leading coordinate-wise correlation structures from sparse observations. Applied to experimental particle-tracking velocimetry of an oscillating impinging jet, MANTRA reveals time-evolving structures that are not apparent from the scattered measurements alone.

authors.name: Nazmus Sakib, Alexander G. Mychkovsky, Hessam Babaee

papers.title: Shaking the causal tree: On the faithfulness and minimality assumptions beyond pairwise interactions
papers.summary: Higher-order mechanisms can make genuine causes invisible to causal discovery, but whether this reflects fine tuning or a structural limitation remains unclear. We prove, for a binary causal family, that the failure of faithfulness is not a measure-zero pathology: it persists for every nonzero coupling vector, even though every active edge remains causally minimal. Experiments with established causal-discovery methods show how this separation propagates into algorithm-dependent failures. A Partial Information Decomposition then identifies the lattice supports probed by faithfulness and minimality, placing the two premises at opposite ends of a single conditioning hierarchy. This exposes a two-sided obstruction: synergy can erase faithfulness, while redundancy can make the positive margin protecting minimality arbitrarily weak. Exact causal premises and practical discoverability can therefore point in different directions

authors.name: Tiago Martinelli, Diogo O. Soares-Pinto, Francisco A. Rodrigues

papers.title: Global MHD simulations of the solar convective zone using a volleyball mesh decomposition. I. Pilot
papers.summary: Solar modelling has long been split into `internal' and `surface' modelling because of the lack of tools to connect the very different scales in space and time, as well as the widely different environments and the dominating physical effects involved. Significant efforts have recently been put into resolving this disconnect. We address the outstanding bottlenecks in connecting internal convection zone and dynamo simulations to the surface of the Sun, and conduct a proof-of-concept high-resolution global simulation of the convection zone of the Sun, using the task-based DISPATCH code framework. We present a new `volleyball' mesh decomposition, which has Cartesian patches tessellated on a sphere with no singularities. We use our new entropy based HLLS approximate Riemann solver to model magneto-hydrodynamics in a global simulation, ranging between 0.655---0.998 R$_\odot$, with an initial ambient magnetic field set to 0.1 Gauss. This paper describes the methods and the pilot runs of the setup. The mesh decomposition exhibits neither unwanted artefacts, nor noise build-up. The simulations develop convective motions with complex, turbulent structures. Small-scale dynamo action twists the ambient magnetic field and locally amplifies magnetic field magnitudes by more than two orders of magnitude within the initial run-time.

authors.name: Andrius Popovas, {\AA}ke Nordlund, Mikolaj Szydlarski, Yixiao Zhou

papers.title: Origins of suppressed self-diffusion of nanoscale constituents of a complex liquid
papers.summary: Understanding and ultimately controlling the transformations and properties of nanoscale systems, from proteins to synthetic nanomaterial assemblies, is limited by the inability to uncover their dynamics on their characteristic length and time scales. Here, we nevertheless demonstrate this ability using MHz X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) -- directly elucidating the characteristic microsecond-dynamics of density fluctuations of semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs), not only in a colloidal dispersion but, more importantly, in a liquid phase consisting of densely packed, yet mobile, NCs with no long-range order. We find the wavevector-dependent fluctuation rates in the liquid phase are suppressed relative to those in the colloidal phase and relative to observations of densely packed repulsive particles. We show that the suppressed rates are due to a substantial decrease in the self-diffusion of NCs, which we attribute to explicit attractive interactions. Using coarse-grained simulations, we find that the extracted shape and strength of the interparticle potential explains the stability of the liquid phase, in contrast to the gelation observed via XPCS in many other charged colloidal systems. This work opens the door to elucidating fast, condensed phase dynamics in complex fluids and other nanoscale soft matter, such as densely packed proteins and non-equilibrium self-assembly processes, in addition to designing microscopic strategies to avert gelation.

authors.name: Christian P. N. Tanner, Vivian R. K. Wall, Mumtaz Gababa, Joshua Portner, Ahhyun Jeong, Matthew J. Hurley, Nicholas Leonard, Jonathan G. Raybin, James K. Utterback, Ahyoung Kim, Andrei Fluerasu, Yanwen Sun, Johannes Moeller, Alexey Zozulya, Wonhyuk Jo, Felix Brausse, James Wrigley, Ulrike Boesenberg, Jan-Etienne Pudell, Joerg Hallmann, Wei Lu, Roman Shayduk, Mohamed Youssef, Anders Madsen, David T. Limmer, Dmitri V. Talapin, Samuel W. Teitelbaum, Naomi S. Ginsberg

papers.title: Metastable phase separation and information retrieval in multicomponent liquids
papers.summary: Liquid mixtures can separate into phases with distinct composition. This phenomenon has recently come back to prominence due to its role in complex biological liquids, such as the cytoplasm, which contain thousands of components. For simple two-component mixtures phase-separated states are global free energy minima. However, local free energy minima, i.e., metastable states, are known to play a dominant role in complex systems with many components. For example, Hopfield neural networks can retrieve stored information from partial cues via relaxation to metastable states. Under what conditions can phase separated states be metastable, and what are the implications for information retrieval in multicomponent liquids? In this work we develop the general thermodynamic formalism of metastable phase separation. We then apply this formalism to an illustrative toy example inspired by recent experiments, binary mixtures with high-order interactions. Finally, as core application of the formalism, we study metastability in Hopfield liquids, a class of multicomponent mixtures capable of storing information on the composition of phases. We show that these phases can be nucleated from partial cues via metastable phase separation. Spatial simulations of liquids with a large number of components match our analytical solution. Our work suggests that complex biological mixtures can retrieve information through metastable phase separation.

authors.name: Davide Marcato, Rodrigo Braz Teixeira, Izaak Neri, Pablo Sartori

papers.title: Characterizing sleep stages through the complexity--weighted-entropy plane in human intracranial data and in a whole-brain model
papers.summary: Approaches based on symbolic information, such as entropy and complexity, have shown that sleep reorganizes the temporal structure of brain activity. However, most of this evidence comes from scalp EEG and group averages. In this work, we characterized sleep stages in intracranial recordings from 65 patients during wakefulness and the REM, N2, and N3 stages, using weighted permutation entropy (WPE) and the statistical complexity measure (SCM). In the complexity--entropy plane, the states formed a clear trajectory from wakefulness to REM, N2, and N3, with decreasing entropy and increasing complexity as sleep deepened. This organization was observed individually in most patients and was recovered more consistently by WPE than by conventional permutation entropy. The trajectory, however, was not the same throughout the cortex. All regions shifted in the same direction, but the occipital cortex followed a much shorter path than the parietal cortex. This result reflects the spatial heterogeneity of the brain during sleep and shows that cortical regions differ not only in the position they occupy in the plane, but also in the path they follow between states. Finally, a whole-brain model based on the human connectome showed that increasing neuronal adaptation shifts the simulated dynamics in the same direction observed in the empirical data, pointing to adaptation as one of the candidate mechanisms involved in this reorganization.

authors.name: Helena Bordini de Lucas, Leonardo Dalla Porta, Alain Destexhe, Maria V. Sanchez-Vives, Osvaldo A. Rosso, Cl\'audio R. Mirasso, Fernanda Selingardi Matias

papers.title: Protocols for a many-body phase microscope: From coherences and d-wave superconductivity to Green's functions
papers.summary: Quantum gas microscopes probe quantum many-body lattice states via projective measurements in the occupation basis, enabling access to various density and spin correlations. Phase information, however, cannot be directly obtained in these setups. Recent experiments went beyond this by measuring local current operators and local phase fluctuations. Here we propose how Fourier-space manipulation in a matter-wave microscope allows access to various long-range off-diagonal correlators in experimentally realistic settings, realizing a many-body phase microscope. We demonstrate in particular how the fermionic d-wave superconducting order parameter in arbitrary Hubbard-type models, the non-equal time Green's function yielding the spectral function, or the hidden order of composite bosons in a fractional Chern insulator can be directly measured. Our results show the great potential of matter-wave microscopy for accessing exotic correlators including phases and coherences and characterizing intriguing quantum many-body states.

authors.name: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt

papers.title: Scaling signatures of near-critical dynamics in large-scale human resting-state electrophysiology
papers.summary: From 1/f noise to neuronal avalanches, evidence of scaling in brain activity has been increasingly linked to tuning to or near criticality. The concept of scaling is intimately related to the renormalization group (RG), in essence providing coarse-grained, simplified descriptions that generalize to classes of diverse physical systems. Following the RG idea, scaling laws have been reported in populations of spiking neurons at microscopic scales. Whether similar scaling principles govern large-scale neural activity in the human brain and how they relate to underlying neural physiology remains unresolved. Here, we analyze large-scale electrophysiological recordings (MEG) of human resting-state brain activity and apply a RG-inspired coarse-graining approach to track collective neural dynamics across spatial scales. We find that multiple observables exhibit robust scale-invariant behavior under coarse-graining: activity variance and correlations grow according to power laws, covariance eigenspectra follow a characteristic scaling relation, and neuronal avalanche statistics and scaling relationships are conserved. Using an analytically tractable neural network model with parameters inferred from data, we show that the observed scaling signatures arise close to, but slightly below, criticality, and that the scaling exponents can be modulated by network inhibitory drives. These findings demonstrate that RG-inspired scaling analysis can uncover signatures of critical dynamics in non-invasive human electrophysiology and suggest a principled route toward estimating excitation-inhibition balance from large-scale brain recordings.

authors.name: Irem Topal, Anna Poggialini, Marco Dal Maschio, Daniele De Martino, Oren Shriki, Fabrizio Lombardi

papers.title: On deep squeezing or cooling a parametric resonator using feedback
papers.summary: Here we analyze ways to achieve deep subthreshold squeezing or cooling of fluctuations in a parametric resonator enhanced by a lock-in amplifier feedback loop. The main advance and novelty of this paper is that we analyzed the full impact of this feedback on the response of the parametric resonator to an ac drive or to additive noise. Due to this feedback, the dynamics of the parametric resonator becomes more complex and, in addition to a saddle-node bifurcation (SNB), a Hopf bifurcation (HB) at the instability threshold can also occur. We calculate the phase-dependent amplification gain in the response of the resonator to an added ac signal with three independent techniques: approximately using the averaging method (AM) or the harmonic balance method (HBM), and more precisely using Floquet theory (FT) and Green's functions. The HB was predicted by the AM, FT, and a modified version of the HBM that takes into account quasi-periodicity. In our analysis of fluctuations, we were able to calculate the noise spectral density and the squeezing or cooling of fluctuations using Fourier techniques and FT. Deamplification and cooling occur near the HB, whereas deep squeezing and heating occur near a SNB. Furthermore, we show that there is an optimal amount of parametric pumping and feedback to reach the strongest cooling. The theoretical framework presented here is general and could be applied to a wide range of physical implementations.

authors.name: Adriano A. Batista, Raoni S. N. Moreira, A. A. Lisboa de Souza

papers.title: High Purity OAM Entangled Photons from SPDC with Reduced Spatial Spectral Correlations
papers.summary: Entanglement generated by Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) involves multiple, often mutually correlated degrees of freedom. These degrees of freedom are often treated independently, overlooking the intrinsic correlation between them. We focus on the spatial-spectral correlations that, if left uncontrolled, introduce distinguishability and reduce coherence, undermining applications such as high-dimensional OAM encoding. We analyze the spatio-spectral structure of the biphoton and identify conditions enabling a strong reduction of such correlations. We then quantify how spatial-spectral coupling degrades OAM spatial purity, mapping high-purity regions as functions of OAM order, crystal length, and pump/collection waists. The resulting design parameter regime enables engineering bright, high-purity OAM-entangled sources, reducing the need for additional loss-introducing filtering and therefore supporting scalable high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.

authors.name: F. Crislane V. de Brito, Sylwia Kolenderska, Piotr Kolenderski

papers.title: Discovery of the Solution to the "Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Paradox"
papers.summary: In 1935, Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky and Nathan Rosen (EPR) published a thought experiment that is entirely correct, has been demonstrated in real experiments, and is now the most famous in quantum physics. Their pioneering work described, for the first time, quantum correlations and can be regarded as a very early glimpse into today's `deep' quantum technologies, by which I mean those that enhance functionality by making use of quantum correlations. However, their work also produces a paradox that Erwin Schr\"odinger had already recognised as such in 1935 and which has since been cemented by the so-called Bell experiments. Here, I can now pinpoint the cause of the paradox in the EPR line of reasoning. It boils down to a single assumption by EPR, which I prove to be false. I show that this resolves the paradox.

authors.name: Roman Schnabel

papers.title: Quantum Optical Signatures of Band Geometry in Solid-State High Harmonics
papers.summary: We develop a general theory of high-harmonic generation (HHG) in solid-state systems, based on a weak-correlation expansion of photonic and matter degrees of freedom. Unlike standard HHG theories, which treat light-matter dynamics through the Schrodinger equation, our approach employs density-matrix evolution, naturally capturing the mixed-state character of both the field and the matter - a critical aspect for describing complex solid-state band structures. We show explicitly that the properties of the emitted fields are governed by the quantum statistics and quantum geometry of the underlying solid. Taking the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model in a one-sided optical cavity as a paradigmatic example, we demonstrate the change in HHG response and quantum-light signatures due to the presence of the cavity. Furthermore, we show that cavity-matter interaction gives rise to squeezed high-harmonic quantum light, whose properties are directly imprinted by the current- current fluctuations and conductance in the material system. Crucially, the observed squeezing does not rely on a separate quartic Kerr mechanism. In the mesoscopic regime, the genuine quantum Kerr term is higher order in the light-matter coupling strength and negligible, while the relevant non-classical effect is governed by current-current fluctuations encoded in the complex susceptibility of the material. Additionally, non-trivial cross-correlations between different far-field emitted modes appear and show bunched and anti-bunched mode pairs. This work establishes a direct link between band geometry and photon statistics, opening new avenues for geometry-sensitive quantum light generation and photon statistics based spectroscopy of solid-state systems.

authors.name: Denis Ilin, Alexander S. Solntsev, Ivan Iorsh

papers.title: Dissipation of Spekkens' Generalised Contextuality under Decoherence: The Classical Limit
papers.summary: When does a decohering quantum system become classical? Generalised noncontextuality gives one criterion, for scenarios rich enough in preparations: a system is classical once its statistics admit an underlying model in which operationally indistinguishable procedures are physically identical. Where it crosses depends not on the state and channel alone but on which preparations, transformations and measurements the experiment offers, and if every measurement is allowed there is no crossing. For any pairwise unbiased bases in any dimension, given preparations holding their eigenstates and surrounding the maximally mixed state, the question reduces to a finite linear program; for a qudit of odd prime dimension $d$ restricted to the stabiliser subtheory, with one depolarised magic state, we solve it in closed form. With preparations and measurements alone the qutrit strange state is classical at zero noise; with the Clifford gates added, each channel represented once, it crosses at 3/5; and with a random gate represented, as Spekkens' treatment asks, by the matching mixture of stochastic maps, at 3/4. A Clifford orbit of assignments supports such a representation only if it has $d^2$ members, leaving, in every odd prime dimension, only Gross's discrete Wigner function: the crossing sits where it stops being negative.

authors.name: Enrico Bozzetto, Jonte R. Hance

papers.title: Exploring the near-kernel sector of quantum reduced loop gravity
papers.summary: We study the near-kernel sector of the Hamiltonian constraint operator in the one-vertex model of quantum reduced loop gravity using exact diagonalisation methods and variational Monte Carlo methods with neural quantum states. The analysis is based on the symmetric Hamiltonian containing both Euclidean and Lorentzian contributions, and on the variational minimization of the positive quadratic operator $\hat{Q}=\hat{C}^2$, where $\hat{C}$ is the symmetric Hamilton constraint, in truncated Hilbert spaces with spin cutoff up to $j_\text{max}=1001$. In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.

authors.name: Ilkka M\"akinen, Hanno Sahlmann, Waleed Sherif

papers.title: The $L^p$ spectrum of the Stokes operator on hyperbolic 3-space and exponential decay for the Navier-Stokes equations
