Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.

authors.name: Yu-Qi Chen, Hai-Shan Liu, Hong Lu

papers.title: Deep Inelastic Scattering and Proton Structure Functions in AdS/QCD models
papers.summary: In this work we study the holographical fermionic deep inelastic scattering in a deformed AdS model. Imposing that the potentials that emerge from the Schr\"odinger-like equations for the fermionic chiral left and right modes are SUSY partners to preserve isospectrality, we implement a systematical truncation of such potentials. Then, we show that in the quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model, the fermionic DIS and the proton structure functions $F_{1,2}(q^2,x)$ are identical with the results obtained from the soft wall model. Further, we obtain and compare high-order approximations for the fermionic potentials with the full solution of the deformed AdS model and show, as expected, that as greater the order of approximation, the better are the results for $F_{1,2}(q^2,x)$ when compared with experimental data explicitly for the Bjorken parameter values $x=0.85, 0.75$ and $0.65$.

authors.name: Rafael A. Costa-Silva, Henrique Boschi-Filho

papers.title: On Thermodynamic Role of the Gauss-Bonnet Topological Term
papers.summary: We revisit the thermodynamic implications of the Gauss-Bonnet topological term in four spacetime dimensions. It has been previously claimed in the literature that this term, although it does not modify the equations of motion, shifts the black hole entropy by a contribution proportional to the Euler characteristic of the horizon. We argue that this conclusion is sensitive to the choice of the boundary action on the horizon. We then identify a choice for which the Wald entropy expression naturally reproduces the Jacobson-Myers entropy, even for non-stationary black holes. We also show that there are no further contributions to conserved quantities from smooth outer boundaries, regardless of the choice of boundary conditions there and of the asymptotic behaviour of the spacetime. Moreover, we demonstrate that the topological Gauss-Bonnet term changes the critical temperature of the Hawking-Page phase transition, opening, in principle, a way for detecting its presence in the gravitational action. In fact, for a positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant, we observe a zeroth-order Hawking phase transition at high temperatures and pressures. While our discussion focuses on the case of the Gauss-Bonnet term in 4D, the results are more general and qualitatively apply to other Lovelock Lagrangians in their respective critical dimensions.

authors.name: Marek Li\v{s}ka, David Kubiznak

papers.title: Boundary Formula for Volume Response of Entanglement Wedge Polygons
papers.summary: The vacuum volume of an entanglement wedge polygon is topological. We determine its semiclassical quadratic response to time-symmetric coherent scalar matter in AdS$_3$. A contrast of six interval entropies measures a nonnegatively weighted energy integral, whereas volume depends on the unweighted integral. For negative mass squared above the stability bound, perturbations with the same quadratic coefficient of global energy can match all six vacuum entropies through second order yet have opposite volume responses. A continuum of narrowing quartets reconstructs the volume response with controlled noise. An independent CFT calculation for a dimension-$3/2$ primary reproduces an exact polygon edge formula.

authors.name: Chen-Te Ma

papers.title: M-theory anomaly localization and holographic $c$-extremization
papers.summary: We compute the cubic and $C_3\wedge X_8$ caracteristic class contributions to the trial anomaly polynomial of supersymmetric $AdS_3\times M_8$ backgrounds with $M_8=P(\mathcal O \oplus \mathcal L)\to B_6$. Including the Abelian currents descending from $C_3$, we identify the projective invariant $J$ as the denominator arising from their elimination by $c$-extremization and recover the central charge $c^{(0)}=-I_3+3I_+I_-/J$. The $X_8$ push-forward determines the pure R-symmetry, mixed R--Betti and gravitational anomalies. Evaluating it at the classical extremum gives the associated central-charge corrections, linear in the overall unshifted flux. The mixed term contributes equally to both central charges and is required in general. We evaluate these formulae for three flux-quantized backgrounds, including non-polynomial solutions. Direct projective fibre integration reproduces the mixed coefficient obtained by localization. On the wrapped-$M5$ $S^4$ bundle, the same couplings reproduce the independently known field-theory anomaly through orders $N^3$ and $N$. Their interpretation as full CFT central charges requires a unitary SCFT with a normalizable vacuum, suitable supersymmetric boundary conditions, a complete mixing sector of global currents and control of omitted anomaly sectors. A conditional Euclidean relative-equivariant interpretation is discussed separately.

authors.name: Carolina Matt\'e Gregory

papers.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
papers.summary: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.

authors.name: Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

papers.title: Covariance and the use of the Schrodinger equation in quantum field theory
papers.summary: The Schrodinger equation is not covariant. Nevertheless, quantum field theory is often formulated using the Schrodinger equation to describe the time evolution of the system, which is equivalent to using Feynman path integrals. It is well known that scattering theory gives covariant results provided that the interaction vanishes in the asymptotic limit of $t \rightarrow \pm \infty$, but there are other situations of interest that do not satisfy those conditions. As an example, the Aharonov-Bohm effect is derived here using second-quantized field theory to describe all the electrons as well as the electromagnetic field, which allows the effects of retarded vector potentials to be calculated in a straightforward way using the Feynman propagator. The results are in agreement with the usual expression for the Aharonov-Bohm effect when the retardation of the electromagnetic field is negligible, but they predict a fractional phase shift, a lack of covariance, and violations of causality when retardation effects are significant. These results suggest that quantum field theory based on the Schrodinger equation or Feynman path integrals is incomplete in the sense that it cannot give a correct description of all observable phenomena.

authors.name: J. D. Franson

papers.title: Twisted Compactification, Quotient Quantum Codes and Logical Gates
papers.summary: Many quantum codes, including balanced-product, bivariate-bicycle and genon codes and the five-qubit code, are quotient codes: a larger code folded onto itself by identifying each check with its image under a deck transformation composed with a symmetry. We show that this is the lattice form of twisted compactification, in which a theory on $X\times F$ carries a symmetry background along $F$, and we use the correspondence in both directions. For monomial quotients of Pauli stabilizer codes, a transfer theorem gives the logical qudits, logical operators and distance bounds from those of the parent, with a Tate cohomology group counting the logical operators that are new. For higher-form and cup-product symmetries the twist is an entangling diagonal circuit; when a finite cover trivializes the background, the code is a dressed quotient, so abelian Pauli codes give non-abelian topological order such as $D(D_4)$. The dressings have Clifford level at most one less than the degree of the twist, and for cubic twists the code dimension is a count of solutions of quadratic equations in cup products, which certifies that the code is not a Pauli stabilizer code when it is not a power of two; on tori and slabs the distance is linear in the size. Twists also create logical gates: three toric codes on $S^3$ have no logical qubits, but on $\mathbb{RP}^3$ the same circuit is a logical $CCZ$. A quarter-turn twist of the 3D fermionic toric code gives codes of linear distance, from $[[768,2,9]]$ up, whose $p+ip$ pump is an explicit finite-time quasi-local evolution that preserves the code space exactly; using the spin-topological response formula of Barkeshli, Hsin and Kobayashi, we identify its logical action as $T$ up to Clifford factors. Finally, twisting abelian gauge theories reach only the quantum doubles $D(G)$ with $[G,G]$ central.

authors.name: Po-Shen Hsin

papers.title: Analogue Gravity: the Subcritical Case
papers.summary: We focus on the subcritical case in Analogue Gravity for a subluminal dispersion relation, and investigate the problem of pair creation in the absence of an horizon analytically, for the subcritical white hole case. We limit our attention to weakly dispersive media. In particular, we take into account for simplicity the Corley model and adopt an approach inspired by quantum mechanics in the so-called overbarrier scattering. The presence of complex turning points is shown to play a fundamental role in allowing a mode conversion which would be absent in a naive WKB approach. We show that there is still a pair creation phenomenon, which, in the subcritical case, is non-Planckian and without a Hawking partner. Our fully analytical results are qualitatively in agreement with the literature at hand. Furthermore we confirm the existence of a critical regime betwen the subcritical and the transcritical ones where no pair creation occurs.

authors.name: F. Belgiorno, S. L. Cacciatori, A. Vigan\`o

papers.title: Quantum Open Effective Field Theory: anomalous decoherence
papers.summary: We study decoherence of a scalar field coupled to ``anomalous'' environments with critical behavior with the Schwinger-Keldysh including the influence functional, and the quantum master equation (QME) up to second order in the coupling. The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation yields a Langevin equation and the Lindblad (QME) includes \emph{time dependent rates} allowing to study transient dynamics. We focus on three examples featuring non-Markov dynamics that cannot be described with S-matrix/Fermi's golden rule rates \textbf{i) Unparticle physics:} a conformal sector beyond the Standard Model at an infrared fixed point featuring correlation functions with anomalous scaling dimensions, \textbf{ii) Threshold and infrared enhancement:} when the mass shell of the field coincides with or is near to a kinematic threshold of the spectral density of the bath, \textbf{iii) Critical environments:} the bath is at a critical point, correlation functions scale with anomalous dimensions and long-wavelength fluctuations feature critical slowing down. In all cases the reduced density matrix undergoes decoherence in the energy basis of the probe, and off-diagonal matrix elements decay as $e^{-\Phi(t)}$ with $\Phi(t)>0 $ the \emph{decoherence function} and $\Gamma(t) = \dot{\Phi}(t)$ the decoherence rate. In all cases we find that either transient or asymptotically $\Phi(t) \propto t^{-\mu}~;~ \mu>0$ with $\mu$, determined by the behavior of the spectral density at threshold and the anomalous scaling dimensions of the correlation functions, or $\Phi(t) \propto \ln(t)$ for the infrared case. For a critical environment there is a new dynamical scaling exponent. A probe of frequency $\omega_q$ is resonant with a \emph{critically slow} quasiparticle for $q_*\propto \omega^{1/z}_q$ at which decoherence is strongly \emph{enhanced}.

authors.name: Gabriela Barenboim, Daniel Boyanovsky

papers.title: Shallow-water black holes and lattice superradiance
papers.summary: Rotating black holes can amplify waves that scatter off them, a process known as superradiance that fluid analogues bring into the laboratory. Separating the horizon's role from dissipation in the surrounding fluid remains difficult. Here we realise a rotating analogue black hole in a lattice fluid: a shallow-water vortex whose horizon is set by a topographic sill, so that the only sink lies behind a supercritical layer that lets nothing out. We measure superradiance as energy extraction: the flux at the horizon is outward for co-rotating waves whose pattern rotates more slowly than the horizon, and inward for faster waves, counter-rotating waves and a non-rotating hole. A scan over three lattice viscosities separates the extraction at the horizon, which is inviscid, from that of the viscous fluid inside the corotation radius: well below the band edge the horizon is the absorber; near the edge the viscous share is half at the operating viscosity and vanishes at the lowest. A drain-anchored horizon, as in water-tank experiments, gives the same signs. Our analysis gives insight into the mechanism of superradiance and offers a cheap, flexible platform for designing analogue-gravity experiments.

authors.name: Antonino Flachi

papers.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
papers.summary: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

authors.name: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima

papers.title: ERG, axions, and a PT-symmetric accelerating Universe
papers.summary: In conventional quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian is required to be Hermitian, ensuring real energy eigenvalues. Certain non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also possess entirely real spectra when they are invariant under the combined action of parity ($\mathcal P$) and time reversal ($\mathcal T$). Such Hamiltonians are called unbroken parity--time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric. We conjecture that, in a string-inspired scenario, a repulsive phase of gravity may be due to a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric gravitational theory, characterised by anomalous Chern-Simons terms, coupled to axion fields. The conjecture is based on the behaviour of the chiral anomalous couplings of these axions to electromagnetic potentials. Within the Exact Renormalisation Group (ERG) framework in the modified local potential approximation, we argue that singularities in the ERG beta functions for such couplings may indicate an infrared phase transition. At the energy scales of these singularities, we conjecture that the field theory transitions from the Hermitian phase to a ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal T}$-- symmetric theory, of gravity, characterised by a repulsive Netwon's ``constant''. This may induce the acceleration observed in the Universe at late eras, without the need for a dark--energy component.

authors.name: Nick E. Mavromatos, Sarben Sarkar

papers.title: Scalar-tensor reconstruction of coherent quantum black holes
papers.summary: We construct a scalar-tensor realisation of spherically symmetric black hole geometries that effectively arise from quantum coherent states characterised by a finite core and finite extension. We determine the non-minimal coupling to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, kinetic coupling, and scalar potential and show that the kinetic term is positive only in finite domains. For fixed black hole mass, the boundaries of these domains provide a natural mechanism that relates the core size and spatial extension to the dynamics of the scalar-tensor realisation. We further show that the same geometry can also be obtained from a Horndeski action with derivative coupling and determine its domain of validity. Neither reconstruction includes the event horizon nor can it simultaneously reproduce arbitrarily large portions of the interior and exterior of the black hole, whose quantum origin therefore appears to remain partially outside the regime of applicability of semiclassical theories of gravity.

authors.name: R. Casadio, A. Giusti, R. da Rocha

papers.title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
papers.summary: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

authors.name: Kyriakos Destounis

papers.title: The Energy-Momentum Tensor of a Compact Object in General Relativity to all Multipole Orders
papers.summary: In effective field theory approaches to compact object motion in general relativity, spin and tidal effects are encoded by operators formed from the Riemann tensor and its derivatives. Many such operators contribute degenerately to observables, with a single one often affecting several multipole moments of the body. Using the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon formalism, we construct a natural basis of independent tensors which are each canonically conjugate to precisely one multipole. We find the novel exact distributional formula for the energy-momentum tensor of a compact object in terms of its reduced multipole moments and these tensors.

authors.name: Trevor Scheopner, Felix Lichtner

papers.title: Variational Approach to the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon Equations of Motion for Extended Objects in General Relativity
papers.summary: The exact motion of a finite size object in curved spacetime is captured by the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations. They associate a unique worldline, momentum, and spin to that object and determine the evolution of such in terms of its fully independent multipole moments. We provide a thorough review of this theory and show how to build it directly via a manifestly gauge invariant variational principle well-suited for effective descriptions of relativistic compact objects. We discuss conditions under which the covariant spin supplementary condition can be enforced and identify the natural basis of curvature tensors conjugate to the object's multipole moments.

authors.name: Trevor Scheopner, Felix Lichtner

papers.title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
papers.summary: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

authors.name: Suraj Prasad

papers.title: Thermodynamic, Optical, and Wave Signatures of Charged Letelier AdS Black Holes with PFDM and Quintessence
papers.summary: We study a four-dimensional charged Letelier--anti-de Sitter (AdS) black-hole metric containing a cloud of strings, a phenomenological perfect-fluid-dark-matter (PFDM) source, and a Kiselev-type quintessence term. We derive the curvature invariants, horizon temperature, entropy, electric potential, and horizon-based mass function, and analyze local thermal response and the associated extended-phase-space identities. A rectangular benchmark cycle gives $W=0.095000$ and $\eta\simeq15.39\%$ for the explicitly stated geometric-unit parameters; these values are model- and cycle-specific and are not presented as a universal efficiency enhancement. For geometric optics, we derive the photon-sphere condition, critical impact parameter, and finite-radius shadow angle. For a massless, minimally coupled scalar field, we obtain a radial-coordinate Helmholtz equation and identify frequency-dependent barriers, evanescent intervals, and candidate trapping regions; the eikonal barrier-top scale approaches the photon-sphere capture scale. Two qualifications delimit the interpretation. First, with the stated PFDM stress-tensor convention, $\rho_{\rm PFDM}=-\beta/(8\pi r^3)$, so positive $\beta$ describes a negative-density effective source. Second, the mass function follows from the horizon equation, but identifying it with a conserved asymptotic AdS mass requires a separate charge and boundary-normalization analysis. The potential-well analysis likewise does not determine complex quasinormal frequencies. We therefore present the results as a consistent, parameter-specific analysis of the adopted phenomenological geometry, while distinguishing algebraic thermodynamic identities from conclusions requiring asymptotic-charge or spectral calculations.

authors.name: B. Eslam Panah, S. Gurtas Dogan, A. Guvendi, O. Mustafa

papers.title: Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model
papers.summary: For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.

authors.name: Bertrand Eynard

papers.title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
papers.summary: This work investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson interferometry within the nonminimal Standard-Model Extension. Employing methods of chiral perturbation theory for mass dimension d=5, a connection between the quark-level and the meson effective pseudoscalar Lagrangian is established. The resulting phenomenological signatures in neutral-meson oscillations with particular focus on the detector geometry are explored. This analysis permits the interpretation of such CPT tests within the d=5 quark sector of the Standard-Model Extension. Existing data are used to extract first constraints on two coefficients and to estimate achievable sensitivity gains over published bounds of up to 18 orders of magnitude.

authors.name: Ralf Lehnert, Agnes Roberts

papers.title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
papers.summary: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2\Omega_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

authors.name: Haotian Huangfu, Tianjun Li, Qi Sun, Rui Sun, Wenxing Zhang

papers.title: Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry
papers.summary: We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.

authors.name: Martin A. Guest

papers.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
papers.summary: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.

authors.name: Jiabao Liu, Lucas Johns, Hiroki Nagakura

papers.title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.summary: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4\pi \bmod 1/2\pi$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.

authors.name: Sonali Patnaik, Rajeev Singh

papers.title: A geometrical approach for obtaining exact analytical solutions for a scalar field in a one-dimensional dynamical cavity
papers.summary: The dynamical Casimir effect was first predicted by G. T. Moore in 1969, who considered a real scalar field inside a cavity with a moving mirror in ($1+1$)D, satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moore wrote the general solution for the field in terms of a function that satisfies a functional equation nowadays known as the Moore equation.In the literature, exact analytical solutions to the Moore equation form a rather small set, restricted to specific classes of laws of motion. Cole and Schieve (1995) developed a geometrical approach that yielded a general formula for the solution of the Moore equation for cavities initially at rest. However, its application has always been done through numerical calculations, and their approach has therefore long been regarded solely as a numerical method. In this work, we show that their method can also be employed as a powerful method for deriving exact analytical solutions, and show the applicability of this approach to deriving analytical solutions to the Moore equation. We obtain original exact analytical solutions for an expanding cavity with a uniformly moving mirror, a contracting cavity with a mirror that approaches the static one asymptotically, and, in addition, we recover the first analytical solution to the Moore equation for a resonant mirror motion, originally obtained by Law in 1994. Moreover, we extend the Cole-Schieve approach, showing that exact solutions can be constructed from any spacetime region where the Moore function has already been determined. We show that this extended geometrical approach allows us to expand the set of known analytical solutions to the Moore equation from the few classes of motion reported in the literature to an infinite set, as it enables the treatment of new classes of laws of motion obtained by combining those presented here with each other as well as with previously known classes of trajectories.

authors.name: Maxwell F. de Ara\'{u}jo, Odemar Juli\~{a}o do N. Neto, Stanley S. Coelho, Jeferson Danilo L. Silva, Alessandra N. Braga, Danilo T. Alves

papers.title: Projective symmetries and differential recursions for the large-$N$ Gross--Witten--Wadia and one-dimensional QCD matrix models
papers.summary: We compare the fixed-charge planar Gross--Witten--Wadia (GWW) model with source-free one-dimensional QCD at large $N$ and $N_f/N$ fixed. In both models the resolvent and one-cut condition give an algebraic equation for a derivative of the free energy: a quartic for GWW and a sextic for QCD. Finite-$N$ Toeplitz determinants independently check the selected QCD branch. Signed permutations of homogeneous parameter triples realize $S_4$; the resulting action on the algebraic branches and operator labels gives a common projective description of the two models. For QCD, the sextic yields a differential recurrence linking small-charge rows two apart. The same second-order PDE gives a finite-width column recursion that reconstructs the coefficient pyramid from its GWW boundary. A distinct boundary, obtained from the first resummed coefficient, is the Narayana triangle. A formally collapsed slice counts decorated bipartite plane trees and admits an exact symmetric product formula. The many-flavor scaling reduces the sextic to the quartic and retains transverse projective data: the QCD divided-difference triple coalesces at this boundary, whereas the limiting quartic satisfies the full standard GWW third-order system. We distinguish algebraic degree, mixed differential order, and fixed-parameter ordinary differential order throughout.

authors.name: S. Voloshyn

papers.title: Nonlinear Scalarization of Reissner-Nordstr\"om Black Holes in Scalar-Torsion-Maxwell Teleparallel Gravity
papers.summary: We investigate the nonlinear scalarization of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in scalar-torsion-Maxwell teleparallel gravity, in which the scalar field is nonminimally coupled to the Weitzenb\"ock invariant. We consider polynomial coupling functions that avoid tachyonic instabilities at the linear level, thereby exploring a scalarization mechanism driven by nonlinear effects. In the decoupling limit, we study the nonlinear evolution of finite-amplitude scalar perturbations and show that the inclusion of a sixth-order coupling term allows the scalar field to dynamically evolve toward nontrivial stationary configurations. This behavior can be understood in terms of the effective potential, which develops nontrivial local minima that provide a mechanism for nonlinear saturation. By numerically solving the fully coupled field equations, we construct asymptotically flat charged black hole solutions endowed with scalar hair. We classify these solutions according to the number of nodes in the scalar field profile, identifying multiple branches whose structure and multiplicity depend on the coupling parameters. We further show that the higher-order coupling progressively suppresses higher-node branches and characterize the scalar backreaction through deviations of the metric functions and the torsion scalar from the Reissner-Nordstr\"om background.

authors.name: Joaqu\'in Robledo, Yerko V\'asquez, P. A. Gonz\'{a}lez

papers.title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
papers.summary: Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\to\eta h^+$, $D\to\pi\pi$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $\Xi_c^+\to\Sigma^+h^+h^-$ and $\Lambda_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=\pi,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $\eta h^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\to\pi\pi$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.

authors.name: Jaeyoung Kim (on behalf of the Belle II Collaboration)

papers.title: Naturalness in the Past from a Time-Dependent Supersymmetry Scale
papers.summary: We consider the possibility that electroweak naturalness may be epoch dependent. In no-scale supergravity, a rolling quintessence modulus can control the supersymmetry-breaking scale, allowing superpartners to be much lighter in the early universe while remaining heavy today. Fifth-force and varying-constant effects can be suppressed via correlated modular weights in the visible-sector K\"ahler metric and modulus-dependent superpotential Yukawa couplings, while radiative stability of the quintessence potential requires additional tuning of the field-dependent vacuum energy. The resulting effective theory has distinctive implications for early-universe phase transitions, relic abundances, and gravitational waves.

authors.name: Tony Gherghetta, Kunio Kaneta, Wenqi Ke

papers.title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
papers.summary: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.

authors.name: Chongying Dong, Kaiwen Sun, Haowu Wang

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear, quadratic, and conformal gravity
papers.summary: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity, general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, and one of the recently proposed higher-dimensional extensions of conformal gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory and, in quadratic gravity, on the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$-dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We further examine conformal relations to linear-gravity solutions, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Particularly noteworthy is that standard static black-hole geometries are absent from the direct-product sector of the considered form of conformal gravity for $n>4$. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

authors.name: Petr Jizba, Tereza Lehe\v{c}kov\'{a}

papers.title: Real-Time Path Integral Resurgence: Which Classical Path Contributes?
papers.summary: Which complex classical paths contribute to a real-time Feynman path integral? Picard-Lefschetz theory answers this question with the intersection numbers of the thimbles, which are notoriously hard to compute in infinite dimensions. We show that resurgence provides a practical alternative. We compute the asymptotic series of the real and complex classical paths to high order, with Feynman diagrams and with a transport recursion for the cumulants, and read off the adjacency of the classical paths from the divergent tails of the series with Borel-Pad\'e methods. The South-East rule then turns adjacency into relevance. For a particle meeting a Rosen-Morse barrier, we identify the relevant complex classical paths in front of and behind the barrier, including the complex path that carries quantum tunnelling, follow ordinary and higher-order Stokes phenomena as the final point moves, and verify the predictions with the exact propagator. The resummed series reproduce the propagator with exponential accuracy. Finally, we outline how the expansion extends to relativistic path integrals governed by a Hamiltonian constraint.

authors.name: Job Feldbrugge

papers.title: Pentagon Functions for Two-Loop Leading-Colour $pp\to t\bar{t}H$ Amplitudes with a Light-Quark Loop
papers.summary: We present a basis of special functions and an efficient numerical implementation for the planar two-loop master integrals that enter the leading-colour amplitudes for $pp\to t\bar{t}H$ with a closed light-quark loop. We provide analytic results for the special functions at transcendental weight one and two in terms of logarithms and dilogarithms, while higher weights are evaluated as one-fold integrals. We focus on the nested roots that arise, studying their analytic structure on the physical region and constructing numerically stable representations of letters and $\mathrm{d}\log$ forms that involve them. We find that a number of $\mathrm{d}\log$ forms have an antiderivative that cannot be represented by a single logarithm over the physical region and tackle them numerically with adaptive Chebyshev approximation. We implement the functions in \texttt{C++} as an extension of the \texttt{PentagonFunctions++} library. We study the performance of our implementation over physical phase-space points and find that the evaluation is accurate and fast enough for phenomenological application. This provides an important building block for NNLO studies of $t\bar{t}H$ production at the LHC.

authors.name: Simone Devoto, Manfred Kraus, Ben Page

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
papers.summary: The non-asymptotic flatness of charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the horizon electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics automatically satisfied, but also both the CR relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.

authors.name: Chang-Xu Yan, Zili Mou, Yu Tian, Hongbao Zhang

papers.title: A possible signature of neutrino spin precession in the J-PARC muon $g-2$ experiment
papers.summary: We examine a possible signature of the neutrino angular-momentum contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly measurement in the J-PARC E34 experiment. In previous papers we argued that the angular momentum carried by the unobserved neutrino pair may leave an uncertainty in the anomaly inferred from the time modulation of detected positrons. At Fermilab the highly relativistic muons make the forward-emission approximation suitable for this estimate. The lower muon momentum at J-PARC requires the decay kinematics to be treated explicitly. We integrate the longitudinal momentum of the neutrino pair using the positron energy distribution and asymmetry derived from the theoretical weak-decay spectrum, and the same event-counting weight $N(E)A(E)$ is employed for both experiments. For positron energies between $1.5$ and $2.9$ GeV at Fermilab and between $200$ and $275$ MeV at J-PARC, the proposed correction is smaller at J-PARC by $0.415\pm0.176$ ppm, when the most optimistic E34 precision is assumed. The expected difference amounts to $2.36$ standard deviations if the future measurement is centred on this value. The calculation thus identifies an experimental comparison which may test the proposed effect independently of the hadronic contribution to the Standard Model prediction. We also examine the possibility of testing the effect by comparing measurements at two different muon momenta. With a fixed positron energy threshold of 200 MeV, the maximum sensitivity is obtained at a muon beam energy of 245 MeV. The predicted difference relative to the nominal J-PARC configuration has significance of $4.88\sigma$ for the most optimistic experimental sensitivity.

authors.name: S. Carneiro, F. C. Sobrinho

papers.title: Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
papers.summary: Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. We focus on electrically charged matter and magnetic gauging in a five-dimensional circle compactification where the axion arises from an Abelian gauge field and the radius is dynamical. We discuss two mechanisms for stabilising the radius/radion using Casimir energy from fields neutral under the Abelian gauge field, with and without an additional periodic scalar winding around the compact circle. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. At the Minkowski minima (with radion masses of $100$--$170\,\mathrm{TeV}$), electrically charged matter induces a residual strong CP angle of order $10^{-17}$ and shifts the radius negligibly. Magnetic gauging remains compatible after including its additional degree of freedom in the Casimir spectrum, provided its coupling is sufficiently small. We observe that increasing the radius suppresses charged-matter breaking relative to QCD but increases magnetic breaking contribution. We also determine the radion decay channels, including the graviphoton, and study reheating from a possible radion-dominated era without scalar winding or magnetic gauging. For a non-minimal Higgs-curvature coupling $\xi=7$, the visible-sector reheating temperature is about $85\,\mathrm{MeV}$ with a dark-radiation contribution of $\Delta N_{\rm eff}\approx0.02$. The entropy released during radion decay dilutes the axion abundance, allowing axions with $f_a=10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and an initial misalignment angle $\vartheta_i\approx0.43$ to account for the entire observed dark matter abundance. For the same decay constant, reproducing this abundance in radiation domination requires $\vartheta_i\approx0.065$.

authors.name: Falguni Biswas, Yeshan Juberi, Ahmed Rakin Kamal

papers.title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
papers.summary: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.

authors.name: Isaac Zhu, Fernando Romero-L\'opez, Phiala E. Shanahan

papers.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
papers.summary: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $\Delta^2_{h,2}/\Delta^2_h\simeq0.04\,\Delta^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $\Delta^2_\zeta=c_w\Delta_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4\epsilon$, and $n_T=-2\epsilon$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $\zeta$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $\Omega_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $\mu$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.

authors.name: Daniele Bertacca, Raul Jimenez, Sabino Matarrese, Mariam Abdelaziz, Marisol Traforetti

papers.title: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
papers.summary: Estimating out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in individual instances of random quantum circuits has been proposed as a candidate for verifiable quantum advantage, and demonstrated to be hard for conventional classical algorithms such as tensor networks and Monte Carlo. Using insights from quantum chaos, we develop and implement a polynomial-time classical algorithm for the four-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and the eight-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in typical instances of one-dimensional (1D) quantum circuits. Our results demonstrate average-case classical tractability of estimating OTOCs in the sensitive regime where circuit-to-circuit fluctuations are large. Our algorithm organizes the OTOC into a rapidly converging series, where the leading term includes contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom in the replicated Hilbert space, and subleading terms arise from excursions outside this space. Although chaos is often viewed as an insurmountable barrier to classical simulation, our algorithm exploits a form of dephasing caused by chaos, which suppresses the subleading terms. We provide strong theoretical and numerical evidence to support this suppression. Further, we demonstrate that practical implementations of our algorithm estimate ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in 1D circuits with high accuracy, achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio at larger circuit depths compared to recent 2D experiments by Google. Extending our algorithm to higher dimensions, and resolving the status of quantum advantage in 2D OTOCs, remain open problems.

authors.name: Yunchao Liu, Yihui Quek, Shreya Vardhan, Tianci Zhou

papers.title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
papers.summary: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the M\"uger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.

authors.name: Justin Asher, Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham

papers.title: Scalar quasinormal modes of the exact spinning Morris--Thorne wormhole
papers.summary: We study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a minimally coupled massless scalar field on the exact spinning Morris-Thorne wormhole. The problem is posed on the complete two-ended geometry, whose asymptotic rest frames rotate relative to each other. After extracting the axis behaviour and the outgoing phases at both infinities, we compactify the radial coordinate and construct a quadratic eigenvalue problem by two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation. The analytic background yields exact constraints on the spectrum. At fixed azimuthal number $m$, the frequencies $\widehat{\omega}=r_0\omega$ are mirror symmetric about $\operatorname{Re}\widehat{\omega}=3\pi jm/2$, where $r_0$ is the throat radius and $j=J/r_0^2$ is the dimensionless angular momentum. Each multipole family depends on $m$ and $j$ only through $mj$ and three angular Chebyshev polynomials represent exactly the multipoles $L=|m|,|m|+1,|m|+2$. A conserved flux confines nonthreshold real quasinormal frequencies to the superradiant window $0<\omega/(m\Omega_-)<1$, where $\Omega_-=3\pi J/r_0^3$. For the sampled sectors $m=1,2,3$ and spins up to $j=19$, every converged frequency is damped and lies outside this window. Independent integration verifies the low-lying modes, while Kerr spectra provide a separate benchmark for the two-dimensional solver. A limiting radial equation explains why the computed mode frequencies approach the upper edge of the superradiant window with frequency offsets proportional to $(mj)^{-1/2}$ at large $mj$. A complete stability assessment requires further analysis of the unresolved scalar spectrum and of perturbations of the coupled metric-matter system.

authors.name: Mark Sukaiti, Davide Batic, Denys Dutykh

papers.title: Thermal Krylov complexity and entropy of inflationary modes with different comoving-wavenumber dependences
papers.summary: We study thermal Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy for primordial scalar modes in three inflationary models with different comoving-wavenumber dependences. These models are canonical single-field inflation, a non-trivial sound speed model, and a modified dispersion relation model. We construct a purified two-mode thermal state and first study its unitary Krylov evolution in an ideal closed system. In the parameter range considered here, the sound-speed correction increases the mean values and oscillation amplitudes of the Krylov quantities. The modified dispersion relation produces a stage-dependent oscillatory structure. We then introduce an independent effective open-system parametrization. The normalized Krylov distribution is controlled by a geometric ratio that combines thermal occupation, coherent spreading, and effective attenuation. We derive explicit expressions for Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy. We also obtain their low- and high-temperature limits. The sound-speed correction enhances the geometric ratio in the adopted parameter range. For the modified dispersion relation, coherent spreading and effective attenuation compete. These results show how thermal occupation and modified mode frequencies control Krylov-space spreading in the three inflationary models.

authors.name: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu

papers.title: Scattering and bound observables for spinning particles in Kerr spacetime with generic spin orientations
papers.summary: We derive the radial action of a spinning probe particle in Kerr spacetime from the worldline formalism in the first-order form, focusing on linear in spin effects. We then develop a novel covariant Dirac bracket formalism to compute the impulse and the spin kick directly from the radial action, generalizing some conjectural results in the literature and providing ready-to-use expressions for amplitude calculations with generic spin orientations. This allows, for the first time, to find new covariant expressions for scattering observables in the probe limit up to $\mathcal{O}(G^6 s_1 s_2^4)$. Finally, we use the action-angle representation to compute the fundamental frequencies for generic bound orbits, including the intrinsic spin precession, the periastron advance and the precession of the orbital plane.

authors.name: Riccardo Gonzo, Canxin Shi

papers.title: The Weight of $Spin(32)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ Little Strings: T-duality and Hasse Diagrams
papers.summary: We study the worldvolume theories of stacks of $Spin(32)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ heterotic NS5-branes probing a transverse singularity $\mathfrak{g}$. We revisit and extend the original classification by Blum and Intriligator, and show that the resulting 6d Little String Theories (LSTs) are naturally labeled by affine dominant coweights of the singularity $\mathfrak{g}$. This in turn enables us to efficiently arrange these theories into groupings satisfying all known necessary conditions to be T-dual. Using this formulation, we then study the partial order of those coweights, and extend a recently proposed slice-subtraction algorithm to construct Hasse diagrams for LSTs directly from their six-dimensional generalized quivers, allowing us to probe certain properties of their Higgs branch. Along the way, we exploit these techniques to show that the number of duality orbits at maximal flavor rank is determined by the center of the transverse singularity $\mathfrak{g}$, and provide a simplified proof of a monotonicity theorem for this class of theories. Finally, we show how some of our techniques can be extended to other classes of 6d theories, such as Type-II LSTs and SCFTs.

authors.name: Hamza Ahmed, Florent Baume, Paul-Konstantin Oehlmann

papers.title: Three-charge black holes from the worldsheet
papers.summary: We consider the general asymptotically flat, doubly-rotating, three-charge black hole uplifted to a family of NS5-F1-P black brane solutions of Type IIB supergravity. We construct a null-gauged WZW model whose target-space geometry reproduces this background in the NS5 decoupling limit, and show that the gauging parameters precisely satisfy the appropriate consistency conditions on the perturbative string spectrum. Through an analytic continuation and an appropriate limit, this model relates to a recently studied construction describing strings on smooth, horizonless geometries. We further analyze the supersymmetric and extremal three-charge configuration, corresponding to the ten-dimensional uplift of the (NS5-decoupled) BMPV black hole, and show that it requires a novel class of null-gauged WZW models. Our construction provides explicit examples of worldsheet CFTs that capture string dynamics on certain black hole geometries with linear dilaton asymptotics.

authors.name: Stefano Massai, Enrico Turetta

papers.title: New Projection Operators for Planar Electrodynamics
papers.summary: In this article, we provide a new construction of a set of projection operators and apply it to obtain the propagator of three-dimensional models of electrodynamics; in particular, we consider the Maxwell-Lee-Wick-Chern-Simons, Maxwell-Deser-Jackiw electrodynamics and nonlocal infinite derivative electrodynamics. In order to prove the efficacy of these operators, we perform a causality and unitarity analysis to investigate the presence of ghosts and tachyons.

authors.name: Fl\'avio P. Cruz, Jos\'e A. Santos, Victor J. V. Otoya

papers.title: On theta function expressions of cyclic products of fermion correlation functions in genus two
papers.summary: In arXiv:2211.09069, significant progress was made in decomposing simple products of fermion correlation functions, and in summing over spin structures of superstring amplitudes in genus two under cyclic constraints. In this manuscript we consider part of the same subject using a framework in which one of the branch points of the genus two curve is fixed at infinity. This framework is a direct generalization of the popular one in the case of genus one. We address some of the issues that remained unresolved in our previous paper arXiv:2209.14633. We show that the spin structures of the simple products of fermion correlation functions with cyclic conditions depend only on the Pe-function values at the half-periods of the genus two surface, for any number of factors in the products. Similar to the genus one case, we can provide basis functions to decompose the product. Consequently, the trilinear relations found in arXiv:2211.09069 can be derived from the known set of differential equations of genus two Pe-functions by setting the variables equal to the half-periods of the non-singular and even spin structures, as is the case for genus one. Based on these considerations, we present a procedure for expressing the results of decomposed formulae in terms of the unique genus two theta function for two, three, and four point cases, and discuss a realistic approach for calculating six point function. A general formula for the expression of the results in terms of the theta function for the product of an arbitrary number of the fermion correlation functions is not yet derivable.

authors.name: A. G. Tsuchiya

papers.title: Spinning States and Unitarity in 3D Gravity
papers.summary: We revisit the proposal to cure the negative density of states in the three-dimensional gravitational path integral by adding spinning states whose spin scales with the central charge. We show that sub-extremal and extremal spinning states below the black hole threshold can cancel the known negativities, and interpret these states as bulk spinning defects. Additionally, certain overspinning states above the black hole threshold can cure these negativities while preserving the spectral gap. The overspinning states were previously interpreted as classical spinning strings; we instead identify them as overspinning BTZ geometries, which are smooth pure gravity quotients of AdS$_3$ with no fixed points. All of these spinning geometries exhibit causal pathologies in their Lorentzian continuations. Moreover, the overspinning geometries arise from mixed elliptic-hyperbolic identifications and contain a formally real chiral temperature. We also generalize the computation of scalar correlators to the extremal background and propose a quotient-motivated image expression for the overspinning geometries.

authors.name: Ziyi Li

papers.title: On Generalized Statistics and Stability in $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-Graded Supersymmetric Yang-Mills Theory
papers.summary: In the standard formulation of relativistic quantum field theory, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded structure is assumed to realize locality and the boson-fermion dichotomy. While $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$-graded extensions are known to be allowed at the level of symmetry, their realization in interacting quantum field theories remains unclear. In this paper, we construct a classical minimal $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. We derive the invariant action and show that all kinetic terms have the correct sign, indicating the absence of classical ghost-like instabilities. Moreover, the positivity of the Hamiltonian follows from the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded supersymmetry algebra. As a result, we show that $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded generalized statistics can be realized at the classical level in a stable interacting supersymmetric gauge theory.

authors.name: Ren Ito, Akio Nago, Shou Tanigawa

papers.title: Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
papers.summary: We develop a Wilsonian description of perturbative D-terms in 4d $\mathcal N=1$ gauge theories on $\mathbb R^3\times S^1$ with chiral Kaluza--Klein spectra. A closed-form, one-loop-exact coefficient of the auxiliary D fields, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos parameters and globally valid throughout the holonomy space, determines the leading holonomy potential away from massless thresholds. We establish uniform weak-coupling control there and match across thresholds by retaining the light fields. Gauge-anomaly cancellation renders the Coulomb-slice vacuum equations affine within each chamber bounded by the thresholds, enabling exact linear analysis of their zero sets and numerical reconstruction through DBSCAN clustering of approximate zeros, LPCA denoising, and RANSAC hyperplane detection. Complementing the rank-one applications of the accompanying Letter, we study flavor-twist dependence in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $\mathcal N=4$ theory, and illustrate the numerical reconstruction in higher-rank R-twisted Argyres--Douglas reductions of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence. We also relate the same D-term data to leading stationary-phase equations of supersymmetric partition functions and a decompactification limit of the torus twisted superpotential.

authors.name: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Daniel J. Resnick

papers.title: Background-independent one-loop renormalization of tensor and scalar primordial spectra
papers.summary: We present a background-independent renormalization framework for one-loop primordial spectra. We apply it to two observables: the scalar-induced tensor spectrum sourced by a minimally coupled spectator field, and the scalar spectrum generated by potential self-interactions. In both cases, the UV part of the loops is isolated and, using the universal WKB behavior of the internal modes, the UV poles are extracted analytically and absorbed into local counterterms without having to specify either the background evolution or the full dynamics of the field running in the loop. This yields finite model-independent expressions for the renormalized spectra amenable to numerical analysis.

authors.name: Guillermo Ballesteros, Jes\'us Gamb\'in Egea, Flavio Riccardi

papers.title: Projections and topological classification of black hole thermodynamics
papers.summary: Black hole thermodynamic topology has evolved from classifications based on global topological numbers to more refined schemes including boundary behavior. This development motivates a deeper question: how are different topological manifestations connected within the complete thermodynamic structure? In this paper, we propose the thermodynamic projection conjecture, which seeks to address this question by examining different topological manifestations in the context of the complete thermodynamic structure and exploring their underlying physical connections and formation mechanisms. As a representative application of this idea, we investigate temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions, in which the topological number varies with temperature while the physical parameters are held fixed. We examine how the complete thermodynamic structure gives rise to different topological outcomes on different temperature slices. Our results demonstrate that temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions arise from boundary effects, whereas the pairwise generation or annihilation of equilibrium states in the interior leaves the total topological number unchanged. These results establish that, at fixed physical parameters, the topological differences observed on different temperature slices originate from the same complete thermodynamic structure and can be understood within a unified framework of thermodynamic projections. Furthermore, this study offers a new approach to understanding black hole thermodynamic structures and their rich physical behavior through the interplay between global structures and their local manifestations.

authors.name: Di Wu

papers.title: Perusing confining pseudoreal theories: hints of emerging massless spin-1 bosons
papers.summary: Solving quantum field theory, which is at the basis of the standard model of particle interactions, is one of the main tasks of contemporary theoretical physics. Minimal asymptotically free pseudoreal theories, containing one or two species of massless Weyl fermions in pseudoreal representations of the gauge group, flow towards a poorly understood infrared dynamics. We provide a comprehensive study of all non-supersymmetric pseudoreal theories, first identifying the ones that likely flow towards a conformal dynamics. Assuming that the remaining ones confine, we find that tumbling hints the possible formation of a non-trivial condensate dynamics, consistently with other symmetry considerations. All but one one-species theories may feature at least one massless spin-1 state. Instead, the only confining two-species theory likely features two massless spin-1 states and one Nambu-Goldstone boson. These expectations must be further tested, for instance by use of Lattice simulations, the functional renormalization group, and supersymmetric analogs.

authors.name: Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Konstantinos Kollias

papers.title: Magnetic corrections to the fermionic Casimir effect with Lorentz symmetry violation and a compactified extra dimension
papers.summary: In this work I study the effect of a magnetic field on the Casimir effect due to a massive, charged fermion field that violates Lorentz invariance in an aether-like manner while maintaining CPT, in a space with one toroidally compactified extra dimension. I take the fermion field to obey MIT bag boundary conditions on two identical square parallel plates. I do this investigation using the zeta function technique that enables me to calculate the Casimir energy and pressure for a massless fermion, and one with a light mass, in the presence of a constant magnetic field perpendicular to the plates. I examine the cases of timelike Lorentz violation, of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction of the magnetic field, of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field, and of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction of the compactified extra dimension. In all scenarios, I find simple and accurate analytic expressions of the magnetic field dependent Casimir energy and pressure.

authors.name: Andrea Erdas

papers.title: Krylov complexity and spectral density of BMN matrix model
papers.summary: We use Krylov complexity as a typical diagnostic of quantum many body dynamics in the context of BMN matrix model at large mass gap. We calculate several physical entities, for example, the moments and return amplitudes at large mass deformation. We calculate them for both spread complexity of states as well as Krylov growth of operators in the matrix model. We propose a general expression for the moments at any given order $n$. We also discuss orthogonal polynomials for spread as well as operator Krylov complexity. In the context of the Krylov operator growth we further compute the spectral function and the density of states. A careful analysis of the spectral function near the resonance reveals various IR divergences in addition to the physical collective modes. These collective modes appear to be exceptionally stable due to large mass gap. On the other hand, the UV of the theory appears to be extremely damped due to higher scattering rates. We carefully diagnose these IR divergences near resonance which reveals that these collective modes are in fact non-propagating and should be thought of as diffusion modes or relaxation modes with infinite relaxation time. We also calculate the Krylov variance and Krylov entropy for the matrix model and in particular at early time. The linear early time growth of the Krylov entropy confirms the onset of quantum chaos in the matrix model at large mass gap.

authors.name: Dibakar Roychowdhury

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Multiple Cosmic Superstrings and the Overshoot Problem
papers.summary: Post inflationary string cosmology can feature an initial population of multiple species of cosmic superstrings whose tension is controlled by a modulus rolling over a steep potential toward a late-time minimum. We perform a full analysis of the associated dynamical system, finding that overshooting the minimum is prevented by the friction of a radiation background of gravitational waves produced from the early decay of effective strings arising from NS5- and D3-branes wrapped around internal cycles. On the other hand, fundamental strings survive longer and decay when the modulus is oscillating around the minimum and they have about $1/3$ of the total energy density. The spectrum of gravitational waves generated by the decays of these multiple cosmic superstrings, even if diluted by a late epoch of modulus domination, can still result in a high-frequency, multi-peaked signal, offering an observational signature of generic features of string theory.

authors.name: Luca Brunelli, Michele Cicoli, Muhammad Hassan, Seyed Ehsan Qoreishi, Francisco Gil Pedro

papers.title: Critical and multicritical Kasner scaling in holographic phase transitions
papers.summary: We study how holographic phase transitions imprint their scaling laws on the local Kasner geometry inside Einstein-scalar black holes. At fixed double-trace coupling, we derive the near-critical scaling of the deviation of the first-epoch Kasner exponent from the Schwarzschild value: $p_t^{(1)}+\frac{1}{3} \propto O^2 \propto (T_c-T)^{1/r}$, where $O$ denotes the boundary condensate and $r$ labels ordinary criticality ($r=1$), tricriticality ($r=2$), and higher multicriticality ($r\geq3$). A super-exponential scalar potential generates a sequence of Kasner epochs separated by scalar-field bounces. We further find that any later epoch that can be tracked continuously across the transition inherits the same temperature exponent, while its coefficient depends on the epoch. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions for the ordinary and tricritical cases. Finally, we show analytically that the leading irrelevant exponent of the infrared fixed point governs the low-temperature Kasner scaling, and verify the resulting scaling numerically for the first Kasner exponent.

authors.name: Ling-Long Gao, Yan Liu, Hong-Da Lyu

papers.title: Cosmological Collider Signals From a Triangle Loop
papers.summary: Triangular loop signals appear frequently in cosmological collider models but their analytical forms remain unknown due to multiple technical challenges. Here, we determine for the first time the leading analytical cosmological collider signals generated by a massive scalar triangle loop in inflationary bispectrum and trispectrum. Combining a directional cutting rule with partial Mellin-Barnes representations, we obtain both the local and nonlocal trispectrum signals in a soft limit and derive the leading signal in the squeezed bispectrum. Remarkably, all these signals are reproduced by the corresponding bubble diagram with a single effective pinched coupling. Signals beyond leading order and cases with arbitrary internal masses, spins, and interactions can be generated within the same framework. Our approach also provides a systematic route to extracting analytical loop signals from general cosmological correlators.

authors.name: Zhehan Qin, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu

papers.title: Metric Source Completions and Integrability in Celestial Gravity
papers.summary: Opposite-helicity soft limits carry ordering information, whereas a metric generating functional has a symmetric mixed response. We compare these structures for Einstein tree amplitudes, retaining the full momentum-conservation distribution. Normalized transport of primary sources fixes the metric response, and a common Banerjee--Pasterski prescription fixes the two ordered scattering currents on compact regular hard packets. At the reference metric, both ordered scattering responses agree with the transport Hessian, so the two matching defects vanish separately. A four-hard-particle example displays the same nonzero recoil coefficient in both orders and in the transport Hessian; an overlapping-source packet resolves the lower-order spin-frame contact. Six-graviton factorization independently tests the recoil and undifferentiated coefficients of the ordering difference. At seven points, angular integration produces a nonzero relative current whose connector variation contains a conjugate bulk term. We derive this term and its cancellation under coherent transport; global cubic scattering matching still requires the physical Ward comparison on the remaining singular overlaps. Transporting the states, kernels and inverse chains together gives a finite Ward identity and coefficientwise reconstruction for that chosen family. Regular packets leave extensions supported solely on excluded hard--hard coincidences undetermined, and the vacuum functional, independent of the hard sources, remains free.

authors.name: Yingnan Xu, Shuangshuang Chu

papers.title: Holography for integrable field theories
papers.summary: We develop a holographic dual to the integrable field theories built from $4d$ Chern-Simons theory. The dual theory is a topological string on a generalized Calabi-Yau manifold, which is entirely encoded in a geometric object we call a planar spectral curve. We describe the RG flow for a planar integrable field theory as a geometric flow on the moduli of planar spectral curves. This description is valid at all orders in the 't Hooft coupling. We compute this flow explicitly up to two loops in many examples, and find an exact match with known field theory results. At one loop this includes a wide class of models. At two loops we reproduce the RG flow for the principal chiral model with WZ term, and for a class of integrable $\sigma$-models with target $U(N) \times U(N)$.

authors.name: Kevin Costello, Joaquin Liniado

papers.title: Relative entropy of entanglement and tripartite minimal surface
papers.summary: We propose a holographic dual of the relative entropy of entanglement for a boundary tripartition $A:B:C$. Our proposal is that, at the leading order, \begin{align} E_R(\rho_{AB}) = \frac{1}{4G_N}\Big[\mathrm{Area}(\Gamma_{\min}) - \mathrm{Area}(\gamma_{AB})\Big] \notag \end{align} where $\Gamma_{\min}$ is the minimal bulk tripartition surface and $\gamma_{AB}$ is the minimal surface homologous to $AB$. For a general random tensor network, we prove the corresponding upper bound by constructing a separable state associated with $\Gamma_{\min}$ and evaluating its relative entropy. We also establish the matching lower bound rigorously for networks of one, two, and three Haar random tensors by bounding the maximal tripartite product-state overlap. In appropriate geometries, the minimal tripartition surface can form a nontrivial tri-junction resembling the Mercedes logo.

authors.name: Takato Mori, Beni Yoshida

papers.title: Trinity of Carrollian Gravity: Dynamically Equivalent Formulations of Magnetic Carrollian Gravity
