u$ corrected by small charged-lepton rotations whose $12$ and $23$ phases are aligned. A single interference relation expresses the observed Dirac phase $\delta$ as the maximal neutrino phase shifted by a calculable charged-lepton correction, and correlates the sign of that shift with the atmospheric octant; this produces a two-branch prediction in the $(	heta_{23},\delta)$ plane: a lower-octant branch with $	heta_{23}\approx 44^\circ$, $\delta\approx 260^\circ$, and an upper-octant branch with $	heta_{23}\approx 46^\circ$, $\delta\approx 275^\circ$. The lower octant contains the strict single-source point of the flavon phase. Both branches place $\delta$ within about $15^\circ$ of $270^\circ$, i.e., near-maximal leptonic CP violation, favored by T2K; a Dirac phase in the first or second quadrant, or more than about $40^\circ$ from maximal, would exclude the framework. The Jarlskog invariant $J_{m CP}\simeq -0.033$ is nearly branch-independent; only precision measurements of the atmospheric octant and Dirac phase at DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande, IceCube, and JUNO can distinguish the two branches.

authors.name: Vernon Barger

papers.title: Determining the NJL Coupling and AMM in Magnetized QCD Matter via Machine Learning
papers.summary: In this study, we investigate the phase structure of magnetized QCD matter by determining the field-dependent parameters of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model through a physics-informed machine learning framework. Specifically, we focus on extracting the optimal functional forms for the running coupling constant $G(eB)$ and the quark anomalous magnetic moment (AMM) ratio $v_2(eB)$, using lattice QCD computation on the chiral transition and condensate behavior. By embedding the NJL gap equation as a differentiable physics-constrained module, our neural network pipeline identifies continuous parameter functions that accurately reproduce the inverse magnetic catalysis (IMC) effect. Our results demonstrate that the magnetic field smoothly suppresses both $G$ and $v_2$. This approach not only bridges the gap between effective models and lattice data but also provides new microscopic insights into the response of the QCD vacuum to strong magnetic fields. As an independent test, the neutral-pion mass is calculated with the mean learned parameters and reproduces the decreasing trend of recent lattice results without a pion-data refit.

authors.name: Zigeng Ding, Fan Lin, Xinyang Wang

papers.title: Applying self-organizing maps to nonresonant searches
papers.summary: An excess of events seen in a nonresonant search at a collider can be difficult to ascribe to a specific hypothesis from amongst several competing ones. We explore a novel approach of applying self-organizing maps to such an excess to uniquely identify a hypothesis. We use a search for vector-like leptons in a trilepton final state to outline the method. We define an approach combining the inherent clustering of these maps and elements of supervised learning. We compare the performance of this approach with a multiclassifying neural network. We find that the method using self-organizing maps competes well (despite not using any standard model processes in the training), and provides additional tools that would help characterize any observed excesses in searches.

authors.name: Vaidehi Tikhe, N. Kirutheeka, Sourabh Dube

papers.title: Exact baryon-meson relation for $b \to s \nu\bar{\nu}$

authors.name: Teppei Kitahara, Manas Kumar Mohapatra, Kota Sasaki

papers.title: Final-state rescattering in $\bar{B}^{0}_{(s)}\to \Lambda^{+}_{c}\bar{\Lambda}^{-}_{c}$ decays
papers.summary: The LHCb Collaboration has recently reported the first observation of the decay \(\bar B_s^0\to \Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-\), along with measurements of the branching fractions for both \(\bar B^0\to \Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-\) and \(\bar B_s^0\to \Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-\). In this work, we investigate these two decays within the framework of final state re-scattering. Our results show that the predicted branching fractions are consistent with the experimental measurements, which indicates the significant role of long-distance final-state interactions in such baryonic $B$ decays. Furthermore, we present predictions for the direct CP asymmetries and the asymmetry parameters. Numerically, both decays exhibit nearly vanishing direct CP asymmetries and suppressed longitudinal polarizations $\alpha$, whereas the sizable values of $\beta$ and $\gamma$ reflect strong interference between the two helicity amplitudes and provide sensitive probes of the decay dynamics.

authors.name: Zhu-Ding Duan, Xiao Huang, Dong-Hao Li, Run-Hui Li, Jian-Peng Wang, Fu-Sheng Yu

papers.title: Semileptonic sum rules in heavy-to-light charm decays

authors.name: Motoi Endo, Syuhei Iguro, Satoshi Mishima, Takeru Uchiyama, Ryoutaro Watanabe

papers.title: Joint probes of dark matter annihilation from neutrino detectors and CMB targets
papers.summary: Dark matter (DM) annihilation into neutrinos provides a promising observational channel targeted by current and forthcoming neutrino detectors. However, the detection of such neutrino fluxes alone cannot uniquely determine their astrophysical or cosmological origin, such as the recent observations from Super-Kamiokande that hint at a small excess of electron antineutrino events. We propose that the effective number of neutrino species and the spectral distortion of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) can serve as complementary observables to probe neutrino signatures from DM annihilation. Using a simple model-independent analysis, we determine the detection windows of these cosmic observables that overlap with the experimental sensitivities from the Super-Kamiokande, Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory, Hyper-Kamiokande, and the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment, showing that joint probes of large DM annihilation to neutrinos with MeV-GeV masses can be achieved by neutrino detectors and CMB experiments.

authors.name: Ruifeng Leng, Shao-Ping Li

papers.title: Taming Symbolic IBP Reduction with Intermediate Bases
papers.summary: Despite many years of development in integration-by-parts reduction, reconstructing all reduction coefficients, which are rational polynomials of kinematic variables and the space-time dimension, remains a non-trivial problem. The main difficulty comes from the large number of unknowns in a general ansatz, which can lead to a linear system that is too large to solve. In this paper, we present an algorithm for reconstructing reduction coefficients through a sequence of intermediate bases. The resulting analytic reduction coefficients are products of a few analytic matrices, whose non-zero entries are simple rational polynomials. We demonstrate the efficiency of this algorithm with two cutting edge examples: a three-point massive box-triangle and a four-point massive pentagon-triangle. Reconstructing all reduction coefficients for the box-triangle (pentagon-triangle) requires 3289 (13013) numerical samplings, significantly fewer than the number of unknowns in the general ansatz, 1407406 (21638331).

authors.name: Qian Song

papers.title: Holographic light-quark energy loss in a spinning plasma
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled plasma described by a spinning black-brane background obtained from the large-black-hole limit of the Myers-Perry geometry. The parameter $a$ characterizes the boost/rotation parameter of the dual fluid in this holographic setup and is related to the angular velocity in the corresponding limit. We employ two complementary probes, the falling-string and shooting-string descriptions, to compute the stopping distance and the instantaneous energy loss of a light quark moving either transverse or parallel to the local tangential-flow direction. The results show that light quarks quench more readily in a hot environment. For parallel propagation, a counter-propagating configuration enhances energy loss, whereas a co-propagating configuration suppresses it. For transverse propagation, increasing the magnitude of the rotational motion promotes energy loss. In addition, the instantaneous energy loss increases along the trajectory of the endpoint. These results describe classical probe dynamics in the local planar limit and do not include intrinsic-spin effects.

authors.name: Yan-Qing Zhao, Zhou-Run Zhu

papers.title: Parametric Resonance of Higgsed Vector Dark Matter: Inflationary Initial Conditions and Sourced Displacements
papers.summary: Parametric resonance in a Higgsed Abelian sector provides an efficient mechanism for producing vector dark matter, but its viability depends crucially on the origin of the initial dark-Higgs displacement that seeds the resonance. In this work, we investigate this initial-condition problem in a weakly coupled Abelian-Higgs theory with potential $V=\lambda_4(\phi^2-v^2)^2/4$, using the calibrated nonlinear broad-resonance relic map together with a stochastic inflationary analysis of the dark-Higgs condensate. We show that a minimal light-spectator realization fails under standard inflationary duration: while broad resonance and isocurvature constraints require \( \phi_0/H_I \gtrsim 3.3\times10^4, \) the stochastic equilibrium and finite-duration random walk produce only \( \phi/H_I=\mathcal O(1). \) This large displacement mismatch is robust against order-of-magnitude variations in the resonance efficiency and broadness threshold, establishing a model-independent obstruction to the stochastic branch. We then identify a distinct classically sourced branch, generated by a negative Hubble-induced mass, in which the condensate tracks a time-dependent minimum, \( \phi_0=\kappa H_*/\sqrt{\lambda_4}, \) and the radial fluctuation remains heavy during inflation. In this case, the fixed-$e/\lambda_D$ relic scaling shifts from \( m_X\propto \lambda_4^{5/8}H_I^{-3/2} \) to \( m_X\propto \kappa^{-3/2}\lambda_4 H_*^{-3/2}. \) We derive the simultaneous consistency conditions for this sourced branch, including broad resonance, adiabatic tracking, perturbativity, sub-Planckian displacement, thermal non-erasure, spectator backreaction, and control of inflationary vector fluctuations. Our results establish that Higgsed-vector resonance is not merely a dark-matter production mechanism, but a sensitive probe of the inflationary and reheating dynamics that determine its initial conditions.

authors.name: Imtiaz Khan, Salvatore Capozziello, G. Mustafa, Niamat Ullah, Farruh Atamurotov

papers.title: Relativistic corrections and high-energy resummation for exclusive heavy quarkonium photoproduction
papers.summary: The $O(v^2)$ correction to the high-energy resummed coefficient function for the exclusive photoproduction of vector ($1^{--}$) heavy quarkonia off hadrons is computed, thereby taking into account corrections of $O(v^2 \alpha_s^n \ln^{n-1}(x/\xi))$. When expressed in terms of the physical vector-meson mass ($M_V$) and the relative heavy-quark velocity ($\langle v^2 \rangle$) using the Gremm-Kapustin relation, the computed correction turns out to be negligible at the scale $\mu_F=M_V$. However, it partially cancels the $\mu_F$ dependence of the $O(v^2)$ correction to the LO coefficient function in $\alpha_s$, thereby improving the robustness of the predictions.

authors.name: Maxim Nefedov

papers.title: Compositeness relations for near-threshold p-wave bound states
papers.summary: We generalize Weinberg's compositeness relations to near-threshold p-wave bound states and derive the relations among the p-wave effective range expansion parameters, binding energy B, and the field renormalization constant Z. Unlike the s-wave case, the field renormalization constant Z for p-wave states depends on the renormalization scale. We obtain the renormalization equation for Z and provide its solution. We find that the negative-norm state reported more than a decade ago in p-wave sector can be avoided by an appropriate choice of the renormalization scale. We also present the general propagator for p-wave near-threshold states. Our results are expected to have broad applications in studying exotic states, as well as the structure of halo nuclei and Fashbach molecules.

authors.name: Guo-Ying Chen

papers.title: Search for active-sterile neutrino transitions using Pierre Auger Observatory data
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of the Pierre Auger Observatory to physics beyond the Standard Model arising from magnetic-moment-induced transitions between active and heavy sterile neutrinos. Such dipole portal interactions can enhance neutrino-nucleon cross sections above a kinematic threshold set by the sterile neutrino mass, leading to observable modifications of neutrino detection rates at ultrahigh energies (UHE). We estimate the impact of these interactions on both down-going and Earth-skimming neutrino detection channels, the contrasting responses of which enable discrimination between an enhanced neutrino flux and a modified interaction cross section. Using the non-observation of UHE neutrino candidates, we derive neutrino-flux-dependent constraints with 90% confidence-level on the transition magnetic moment for sterile neutrino masses in the range 1 TeV-100 TeV. Under the assumed flux scenarios, the resulting flavor-independent limits extend existing bounds into previously unexplored parameter space.

papers.title: High energy probes of Higgs self-coupling via $W$ boson fusion at future lepton colliders
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity to the Higgs self-coupling through $W$ boson fusion di-Higgs production at CLIC with a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=3$~TeV. We study the interplay between the Higgs self-coupling modifier ($\kappa_{\lambda}$) and Higgs-gauge boson coupling modifiers ($\kappa_{V}$ and $\kappa_{2V}$) within the $\kappa$ framework. To enhance the separation between signal and background, we develop a graph neural network (GNN) based classifier that achieves a signal significance of $\mathscr{Z}\approx 20~\sigma$ at $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, substantially exceeding projected HL-LHC sensitivity. Our results demonstrate that high-energy lepton colliders, combined with graph-based machine learning, provide excellent sensitivity to the Higgs self-coupling and offer a powerful probe of new physics in the electroweak sector, potentially disentangling underlying SMEFT-like and HEFT-like structures.

authors.name: Amir Subba, Hrishikesh Deka, Subhaditya Bhattacharya, Abhik Sarkar

papers.title: Finite-Width Dissolution of Radial Spectroscopy in Single-Top Mesonic Correlations
papers.summary: Within the heavy-mass expansion, the pole width of a system containing one unstable heavy constituent inherits the constituent width up to $\mathcal O(\Lambda_{\rm kin}^2/m_Q^2)$ corrections, while radial splittings remain $\mathcal O(\Lambda_{\rm rad})$. The top quark is an extreme realization of this hierarchy. We implement the complex top pole mass in an instantaneous Bethe--Salpeter framework, where a biorthogonal Hellmann--Feynman relation realizes width inheritance at the operator level and an artificial heavy-mass scan confirms the predicted $m_Q^{-2}$ suppression. The low-pole source-projected response has a single broad maximum at the physical top width in the $t\bar b$, $t\bar c$, and $t\bar u$ channels. Full width-dependent non-Hermitian re-diagonalization and a direct full-matrix resolvent evaluation confirm the progressive dissolution of the small-width radial maxima. Thus stable-top eigenvalues survive as reference poles but not as a resolvable multi-peak spectrum; they may instead leave qualitative, process-dependent $Wb\bar q$ signatures, such as a broad threshold enhancement or modified color flow.

authors.name: Bing-Dong Wan, Shuo Yang

papers.title: On-shell renormalization in NREFT: a simplified description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects
papers.summary: We discuss several issues regarding the modern generalization of Weinberg's compositeness criterion. In particular, we demonstrate that the on-shell renormalization in NREFT reproduces Weinberg's result and provides a simple description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects. Additionally, we present the complete propagator, including the charged channel for the near-threshold p-wave states.

authors.name: Guo-Ying Chen

papers.title: Inverse-seesaw and inflationary scale relations in a supersymmetric 331 model from an SU(6) GUT model
papers.summary: We propose a $N=1$ supersymmetric $SU(6)$ theory with an intermediate $(SU(3)_C\times SU(3)_L\times U(1)_X)$ phase, in which common fields and operators relate the neutrinos, gauge mediation, unification, and symmetry-breaking sectors. The antisymmetric Dirac matrix of the inverse-seesaw sector has rank two, yielding one vanishing light-neutrino mass at leading order. A higher-dimensional symmetry-breaking correction lifts this zero mode through its projection onto the left and right null vectors of the Dirac matrix, leading to a quartic suppression in the ratio of the intermediate and ultraviolet scales. Complete unified messenger multiplets preserve the relative one-loop gauge coupling evolution while modifying the unified coupling. When the same supersymmetry-breaking spurion generates the singlet lepton-number-violating parameter, an analytical relation emerges between the messenger scale, the lepton-number mediator scale, and the unified coupling. The two-loop gauge evolution remains perturbative for the assumed heavy-threshold spectrum. In the inflationary sector, the scalar-amplitude normalization determines the coupling governing both the inflationary potential and the radial scalar mass in the broken vacuum. The physical scalar directions transverse to the inflaton are stable within the neutral supergravity subspace, while the combined inflationary and gauge-mediated conditions imply a significant sensitivity of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. An examination of the allowed operators shows that additional ultraviolet conditions are required to obtain the observed active-neutrino mixing, suppress competing lepton-number-violating terms, and complete the heavy-field spectrum. Our analysis establishes the analytical scale relations among the neutrino, messenger, unification, and inflationary sectors and identifies the conditions necessary for their simultaneous realization.

authors.name: Imtiaz Khan, Tianjun Li

papers.title: The decay $\eta_c\to p\bar p\eta$ with meson--baryon final-state interactions
papers.summary: We study the decay \(\eta_c\to p\bar{p}\eta\) by combining the SU(3) flavor structure of the primary production with final-state interactions in the \(p\eta\) and \(\bar{p}\eta\) subsystems, using the chiral unitary approach. The low-energy \(S_{11}\) dynamics, including the dynamically generated \(N^*(1535)\), is incorporated into the complete coupled-channel amplitude, and a phenomenological \(N^*(1895)\) contribution is included coherently. The \(p\eta\) and \(\bar{p}\eta\) invariant-mass distributions are well described, and the \(p\bar{p}\) distribution is predicted as a kinematic reflection of the \(\eta N\) dynamics. The results support the dynamical interpretation of the \(N^*(1535)\) and suggest possible additional \(S_{11}\) strength near \(1.9\)~GeV.

authors.name: Jing Song, Yu-Shan Ren, Eulogio Oset

papers.title: A universal probe of QCD spin physics from fragmentation energy correlator
papers.summary: We study the fragmentation energy correlator (FEC), which combines the nonperturbative fragmentation function with the infrared-safe energy correlator, as a new probe of the three-dimensional dynamics of QCD hadronization. We demonstrate, both theoretically and numerically, that FEC applies universally to inclusive hadron production in lepton-lepton, lepton-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions, without requiring jet algorithms or simultaneous measurements of other heavy objects. Through the nontrivial transverse-spin dependence, FEC provides a sensitive probe of the chiral-symmetry-breaking scale in QCD via its variation with the energy-correlator scale.

authors.name: Qing-Hong Cao, Xiaohui Liu, Zhite Yu, C. -P. Yuan, Feng Yuan, Shu-Tao Zhang, Hua Xing Zhu

papers.title: Regression on high-dimensional phase space
papers.summary: Machine learning tasks in particle physics are typically expressed in terms of regression, or relaxation toward some optimal solution as defined by an objective or loss function. In this paper, we introduce a large multiplicity expansion for analyzing regression tasks, which enables significant analytic understanding. For concreteness, we study regression with energy flow polynomials (EFPs), a complete linear basis of infrared and collinear safe observables on Lorentz invariant phase space. While the expectation value of any EFP scales like a constant in the large multiplicity limit, we prove that the covariance on uniform phase space of any two EFPs is highly suppressed and scales like the inverse of the squared multiplicity. This very unintuitive result relies on detailed cancellation guaranteed by the interplay of permutation invariance, momentum conservation, and rotational invariance. This scaling of the covariance with multiplicity further implies that the coefficients in an expansion of EFPs must scale quadratically in multiplicity. We present an example of regression with EFPs as applied to $e^+e^-\to$ hadrons events, and show how the regression can be solved analytically through the complementary expansions of the large multiplicity limit and of familiar fixed-order perturbation theory of QCD.

authors.name: Andrew J. Larkoski

papers.title: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
papers.summary: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. We identify regions of parameter space in which two-peak GW spectra are observable at LISA and the Einstein Telescope. By way of illustration, we apply our analysis to a realistic conformal dark SU(3) model.

authors.name: Daniel Ara\'{u}jo, Jo\~ao Gon\c{c}alves, Danny Marfatia

papers.title: Electromagnetic Structure of $\Omega_{ccc}^{++}$ and $\Omega_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons from a covariant three-body Faddeev equation
papers.summary: We investigate the electromagnetic structure of the ground-state $\Omega_{ccc}^{++}$ and $\Omega_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons using a Poincar\'e-covariant three-body Faddeev equation within the rainbow--ladder truncation. We calculate the complete set of elastic spin-$3/2$ multipole form factors, $G_{E0}$, $G_{M1}$, $G_{E2}$, and $G_{M3}$. The leading electric and magnetic form factors become markedly harder from the charm to the bottom sector, revealing the substantially more compact electromagnetic structure of the $\Omega_{bbb}^{-}$. For $\Omega_{ccc}^{++}$, the electric form factor and charge radius at low momentum transfer agree well with the available lQCD results. From the magnetic-dipole form factor at zero momentum transfer, $G_{M1}(0)$, we obtain the magnetic moments $\mu_{\Omega_{ccc}^{++}}=1.26\,\mu_N$ and $\mu_{\Omega_{bbb}^{-}}=-0.207\,\mu_N$. For $G_{E2}$ and $G_{M3}$, the electric-quadrupole structure exhibits a stronger charm-to-bottom evolution than the charge-normalized magnetic-octupole structure. Finally, comparison of the charm and bottom systems shows that both $G_{M1}(0)$ and the relation between the electric and magnetic radii move closer to their leading nonrelativistic heavy-quark expectations as the quark mass increases.

authors.name: Zhao-Qian Yao

papers.title: CANTON-$\mu$ Proposal: A Next-Generation Muon $g-2$ Measurement at Sub-0.1 ppm Precision
papers.summary: We propose a next-generation precision measurement of the muon anomalous magnetic moment (muon g-2) at the High Intensity Heavy-Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF) in Huizhou, China. We refer to this proposed experimental programme as CANTON-$\mu$ (Coherent Anomalous magNetic momenT ObservatioN with muon). HIAF's intense, pulsed GeV-scale muon beams, particularly for negative muons, provide a promising basis for this programme. Building on two previously proposed storage-ring concepts, this work develops HIAF-specific experimental schemes that relax the conventional magic-momentum constraint and allow greater flexibility in the choice of beam momentum. We assess the expected muon intensity at HIAF and the corresponding statistical sensitivity. For each scheme, we identify its distinctive systematic effects, examine feasible control strategies, and propose quantitative systematic-uncertainty targets. Together, the statistical projections and systematic-uncertainty targets indicate prospective total precisions of 0.1 ppm in Phase-I, comparable to the current Fermilab precision, with the potential to reach the 0.05 ppm level in Phase-II following the planned HIAF upgrade. At the ultimate projected precision, the measurement would provide a stringent test of the Standard Model and probe new physics at multi-TeV scales. A focus on negative-muon measurements would enable direct comparison with existing high-precision positive-muon results and strengthen tests of CPT symmetry in the muon sector within the Standard-Model Extension, with a projected sensitivity at the $10^{-24}$ GeV level, an order of magnitude beyond current limits.

authors.name: Ce Zhang, Yu Xu, On Kim, Bingzhi Li, Zejia Lu, Saskia Charity, Guodong Shen, Liangwen Chen, Fedor Ignatov, Liang Li, Qiang Li, Xueheng Zhang, Zhiyu Sun

papers.title: Neutron stars with an agnostic Dark sector: Core and Halo configurations from a two-fluid approach
papers.summary: The study of dark matter admixed neutron stars has the potential to advance our understanding of dark matter particle candidates. However, the large parameter space of dark matter particle masses restricts a systematic, model-independent study. In this analysis, we employ agnostic hadronic and dark-matter equations of state to construct dark-matter-admixed neutron stars within a two-fluid formalism. Dark matter is characterized solely by its low-density equation of state and mass and is modeled as a Fermi gas, while hadronic matter is anchored at low and high densities by chiral effective field theory and perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations. A speed-of-sound parametrization describes the intermediate- and high-density regimes of both hadronic and dark matter, enabling an agnostic treatment of the dark matter equation of state that is constrained only by thermodynamic consistency and does not favor softer or stiffer behavior. Within this agnostic framework, we find that dark matter does not generically compactify the star: light dark matter forms extended halos that raise the tidal deformability, while heavy dark matter forms compact cores that lower it. Consequently, the dominant observational constraint shifts from gravitational-wave tidal deformability for light, halo-dominated models to NICER mass-radius data for heavy, core-dominated models. Using current data at $1\sigma$, we constrain the dark matter fraction to $f_{\mathrm{DM}} \lesssim 0.11$ for light dark matter. By treating the medium- and high-density dark matter equation of state agnostically within a fermionic framework, our approach yields conservative and broadly applicable bounds on the dark matter content of neutron stars. Neutron stars with similar masses but very different tidal deformabilities could be a smoking-gun signature of dark matter in neutron stars.

authors.name: Asit karan, Tuhin Malik, Asim Kumar Saha, Constan\c{c}a Provid\^encia, Ritam Mallick

papers.title: Density-induced dark-baryon conversion in $\Delta-$admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
papers.summary: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $\chi$ in cold, charge-neutral, $\beta$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $\Delta(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $\chi$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $\Delta$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $\chi$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_\chi=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+\Delta+\chi$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$ and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_\chi=1400$ MeV, $\chi$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.

authors.name: Niyar Prabhat Kalita, Vivek Baruah Thapa, Bhanu Prakash Pant, Anil Kumar, Partha Konar

papers.title: Luminosity Signatures of Dark Sector Particles from Black Hole Evaporation in Neutron Stars
papers.summary: Microscopic black holes may form at the centers of neutron stars through the accumulation and collapse of dark matter. While Standard Model particles produced by Hawking evaporation are efficiently absorbed by the dense stellar medium, sufficiently weakly interacting and long-lived particles can escape and subsequently decay into high-energy neutrinos, photons, or charged particles, providing an indirect probe of Hawking radiation. We examine the joint energy--angular distribution of these secondary particles, incorporating mediator propagation, energy-dependent decay, and relativistic decay kinematics. For relativistic mediators, the normalized energy-integrated angular profile becomes approximately independent of the black hole temperature, with its characteristic extent controlled primarily by the combination $c\tau_S/D$ of the mediator lifetime and source distance, as the boost enhancement of the decay length is compensated by relativistic beaming. We demonstrate the viability of this mechanism and illustrate its phenomenology with gravitationally coupled scalars, axion-like particles (ALPs), dark photons, and heavy neutral leptons. Comparing with monochromatic mediator production from dark matter annihilation, we find that the energy-integrated angular profiles can be nearly degenerate, while the energy spectra and energy-resolved angular distributions remain distinct. Although the predicted signals may lie beyond the reach of current observatories, these complementary spectral and angular signatures provide potential targets for future high-energy neutrino and gamma-ray searches.

authors.name: Ioannis Dalianis, Anastasios Irakleous

papers.title: Sensitivity to Sterile Neutrinos with Elastic Neutrino-Electron and Highly Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering in the DUNE Near Detector
papers.summary:
The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) is a next-generation neutrino experiment designed for precision measurements of long-baseline three-flavor neutrino oscillations. The DUNE Near Detector (ND) is also sensitive to short-baseline oscillations arising from mixing with an eV-scale sterile neutrino. In this paper, we present a sensitivity study for sterile-neutrino oscillations in the $3+1$ framework using three complementary event samples in the simulated DUNE ND: highly elastic $
u_\mu$ charged-current (CC), highly elastic $
u_e$ CC, and neutrino-electron elastic-scattering ($
u+e$) events. These highly exclusive samples are chosen to reduce neutrino-interaction and flux uncertainties: the low-hadronic-energy CC selections enhance the correlation between reconstructed lepton energy and neutrino energy, while the precisely calculable $
u+e$ cross section provides an independent constraint on the neutrino flux. Residual interaction-model dependence remains in the CC samples. The statistical analysis considers $|U_{e4}|^2$, $|U_{\mu4}|^2$, $|U_{	au4}|^2$, and $\Delta m^2$, with sensitivity results presented as fixed-$\Delta m^2$ slices for $|U_{	au4}|^2=0$. The strongest sensitivity occurs for $4 \lesssim \Delta m^2 \lesssim 10~\mathrm{eV}^2$, where oscillations produce resolvable distortions of the reconstructed-energy spectra. For one year of on-axis forward-horn-current running, the 90\% confidence-level sensitivity reaches approximately $|U_{\mu4}|^2 \simeq 0.01$ and $|U_{e4}|^2 \simeq 0.015$, depending on the value of the other mixing parameter.

authors.name: The DUNE Collaboration

papers.title: Observation of a strange $J^P=1^{-}$ resonance $K^{*}_1(1870)$ in $\chi_{c1}\to K^+K^-\eta^{\prime}$ decays
papers.summary: A partial wave analysis of the process $\psi(2S)\to \gamma\chi_{c1}$, $\chi_{c1}\to K^{+}K^{-}\eta^{\prime}$, with the $\eta^{\prime}$ meson reconstructed in the $\pi^+\pi^-\gamma$ and $\pi^+\pi^-\eta$ decay modes, is performed using a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3)\times10^{6}$ $\psi(2S)$ events collected with the BESIII detector. In the $K\eta^{\prime}$ system, a resonant contribution with quantum numbers $J^{P}=1^{-}$ is observed for the first time and is denoted as the $K_1^*(1870)$ meson. Its statistical significance is $11.0\sigma$, and its mass and width are measured to be $M=(1869.0 \pm 14.6\pm 18.6$) MeV/$c^{2}$ and $\Gamma=(167.3 \pm 34.0\pm 24.2$) MeV, respectively. The branching fraction of the $\chi_{c1}\to K^{\mp}K_1^*(1870)^{\pm}\to K^{+}K^{-}\eta^{\prime}$ decay chain is determined to be $(1.48 \pm 0.30\pm 0.33)\times10^{-5}$. The branching fraction of the $\chi_{c1}\to K^{+}K^{-}\eta^{\prime}$ decay is measured to be $(7.90 \pm 0.48)\times10^{-4}$. Several intermediate scalar, vector, and tensor states are required to provide a good description of the data. These results provide new input for understanding strange-meson spectroscopy and investigating possible hybrid-state candidates.

papers.title: Measurement of the branching fractions for the decays $\chi_{cJ}\to \phi \omega \eta$ and $\chi_{cJ}\to \phi \omega \eta^{\prime}$
papers.summary: Using a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3) \times 10^{6}$ $\psi(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observation and measurement of the branching fractions for the decays $\chi_{cJ}\to \phi \omega \eta$ and $\chi_{cJ} \to \phi \omega \eta^{\prime}$ ($J = 0,1,2$) with statistical significance greater than $5\sigma$. The branching fractions are determined to be $\mathcal B(\chi_{c0} \to \phi \omega \eta) = (5.43 \pm 0.23 \pm 0.52) \times 10^{-4}$, $\mathcal B(\chi_{c1} \to \phi \omega \eta) = (2.51 \pm 0.14 \pm 0.24) \times 10^{-4}$ and $\mathcal B(\chi_{c2} \to \phi \omega \eta) = (3.03 \pm 0.15 \pm 0.28) \times 10^{-4}$ for the $\eta$ mode, and $\mathcal B(\chi_{c0} \to \phi \omega \eta^{\prime}) = (1.23 \pm 0.23 \pm 0.15) \times 10^{-4}$, $\mathcal B(\chi_{c1} \to \phi \omega \eta^{\prime}) = (1.09 \pm 0.17 \pm 0.13) \times 10^{-4}$ and $\mathcal B(\chi_{c2} \to \phi \omega \eta^{\prime}) = (0.98 \pm 0.17 \pm 0.11) \times 10^{-4}$ for the $\eta^{\prime}$ mode, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic.

papers.title: Search for Dark Photon Dark Matter at 74--159 $\mu$eV/$c^2$ Using Broadband Cryogenic Receivers
papers.summary: Dark photons are hypothetical massive vector bosons that couple to ordinary photons through kinetic mixing $\chi$. Dark photon dark matter (DPDM) converts into photons at a metal surface, with a frequency set by its mass. Using cryogenic K- and Ka-band receivers with a broadband spectrometer, we searched for this signal over 74--159 $\mu$eV/$c^2$ (18--38.5 GHz) with an integration time of $4.8\times10^5$ s per frequency bin. We found no statistically significant signal and set upper limits of $\chi<(3.1$--$17)\times10^{-12}$ at the 95% confidence level over 99.8% of the search range, assuming DPDM constitutes all local dark matter. These results improve on previous limits by more than an order of magnitude over most of 74--110 $\mu$eV/$c^2$ and provide the first direct limits over most of 110--159 $\mu$eV/$c^2$, approximately two orders of magnitude below cosmological bounds.

authors.name: Hiroki Takeuchi, Shunsuke Adachi, Shunki Endo, Keigo Hanimura, Michinori Hirose, Shunsuke Honda, Yuki Sakurai, Junya Suzuki, Osamu Tajima

papers.title: Observation of the rare decay $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$e$^+$e$^-$
papers.summary: A first observation of the rare decay $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$e$^+$e$^-$ is reported by the CMS Collaboration at the CERN LHC. The result is based on a proton-proton collision data sample at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 38.0 fb$^{-1}$, acquired in 2022 using a high-rate dimuon trigger. Using the $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\gamma$ decay channel for normalization, the branching fraction is measured to be $\mathcal{B}$($\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$e$^+$e$^-$) $=$ (2.4 $\pm$ 0.8) $\times$ 10$^{-6}$, with the uncertainty including statistical and systematic sources as well as the $\mathcal{B}$($\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\gamma$) uncertainty. This result is about a factor of three smaller than the existing limit, and is consistent with recent theoretical predictions.

authors.name: CMS Collaboration

papers.title: Proposing GRENDEL: GalleRy ExperimeNt for Decays of Exotic LLPs at the LHC
papers.summary: Long-lived particles are a generic prediction of Standard Model extensions that address the hierarchy problem, the origin of neutrino masses, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, and the nature of dark matter. Despite the breadth of theoretical motivation, neutral long-lived particles in the GeV-scale mass range remain difficult to probe at the LHC main detectors, where trigger limitations and challenging backgrounds curtail sensitivity over a wide range of lifetimes. We propose GRENDEL (GalleRy ExperimeNt for Decays of Exotic LLPs), a dedicated detector to be installed in the PX56 drainage gallery at CMS Point~5. The GRENDEL detector will exploit the substantial rock and concrete between the detector and the LHC interaction point as passive shielding in addition to employing active background rejection. Located approximately 24\,m above the interaction point and running largely transverse to the beam, GRENDEL will span around 110\,m and cover the central region $|\eta| < 0.5$. The detector will make use of extruded scintillator bars to achieve competitive sensitivity with other proposed detectors while requiring minimal infrastructure, and without the need for civil engineering. We present the physics case, detector concept, and projected sensitivities to heavy neutral leptons, dark scalars, and axion-like particles covering the $0.2$--$60$\,GeV mass range, for a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $3\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC. The benchmarks span the neutrino, scalar, and axion portals, with production through exotic Higgs boson decays, $B$- and $D$-meson decays, and $W/Z$ decays.

authors.name: Matthew Citron, Federico Redi, Ryan Schmitz

papers.title: Precise Measurement of the Inclusive Cross Sections of Open-Charm Mesons at Energies from 3.80 to 4.95 GeV
papers.summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from $3.80$ to $4.95~\text{GeV}$, the inclusive production cross sections of open-charm mesons, $\sigma(e^{+}e^{-}\to D^{0}/D^{+}/D_{s}^{+}+X)$, are measured by tagging a $D^0$, $D^+$, or $D_s^+$ meson, where $X$ denotes any accompanying particles. Open-charm production dominates the total hadronic yield above threshold. Therefore these measurements provide a vital reference for understanding hadron production and for validating global $R$ value results. The results offer crucial inputs for investigating heavier charmonia and exotic states coupled to open-charm final states, while serving as a benchmark for comparison with the sum of measured exclusive channels. This comparison directly evaluates the completeness of current exclusive datasets and clarifies the underlying hadronization mechanisms in the open-charm region.

papers.title: Simulation Studies For Goodness-of-Fit and Two-Sample Methods For Univariate Data
papers.summary: We present the results of a large number of simulation studies regarding the power of various goodness-of-fit as well as nonparametric two-sample tests for univariate data. This includes both continuous and discrete data. In general no single method can be relied upon to provide good power, any one method may be quite good for some combination of null hypothesis and alternative and may fail badly for another. Based on the results of these studies we propose a fairly small number of methods chosen such that for any of the case studies included here at least one of the methods has good power. The studies were carried out using the R packages R2sample and Rgof, available from CRAN.

authors.name: Wolfgang Rolke

papers.title: Influence of strangeness on the anisotropic flow of prompt D$^\pm_\mathrm{s}$ mesons in PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV
papers.summary: The azimuthal anisotropy of prompt D$^\pm_\mathrm{s}$ mesons produced in lead-lead (PbPb) collisions at a nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV is measured using data obtained with the CMS detector. The dataset corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 0.58 nb$^{-1}$. The azimuthal anisotropy of heavy charmed mesons provides a key constraint on the interactions of charm quarks with the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) medium. These interactions include coalescence mechanisms and parton energy loss in the QGP. The anisotropy is characterized by measurements of the second- ($v_2$) and third-order ($v_3$) Fourier coefficients of the azimuthal distribution of the D$^\pm_\mathrm{s}$ mesons. The $v_2$ coefficient is determined in the transverse momentum range 4 $\lt$ $p_\mathrm{T}$ $\lt$ 40 GeV for three event centrality classes, while the $v_3$ coefficient is measured in the range 4 $\lt$ $p_\mathrm{T}$ $\lt$ 20 GeV for a single event centrality class. The results for the D$^\pm_\mathrm{s}$ mesons are compared to those previously measured for D$^0$ mesons. For their respective $p_\mathrm{T}$ and centrality ranges, the $v_2$ and $v_3$ coefficients for D$^\pm_\mathrm{s}$ and D$^0$ mesons are found to be consistent. This suggests that the strangeness content of the D$^\pm_\mathrm{s}$ meson does not significantly alter its azimuthal distribution, at least within the measured $p_\mathrm{T}$ ranges. Theoretical predictions incorporating heavy-quark transport and hadronization mechanisms in the QGP are compared to the measured anisotropy coefficients.

authors.name: CMS Collaboration

papers.title: Measurement of jet quenching in O+O collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=200$ GeV by the STAR experiment at RHIC
papers.summary: The STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider presents measurements of correlations between charged hadron triggers of high transverse momenta ($7 8$ GeV/$c$) in event--activity selected O+O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=200$ GeV. Yields of associated hadrons and jets, normalized by the number of trigger hadrons, are suppressed by approximately 20\% in high event activity relative to low event activity collisions, with an absence of suppression excluded with high significance. This suppression corresponds to a shift in $p_\mathrm{T}$ of $0.70\pm0.15~(\rm stat.)~\pm0.10~(\rm syst.)$ GeV/$c$ for large--radius charged--particle jets ($R=0.5$), quantifying their energy redistribution due to final--state interactions. These measurements provide strong evidence for jet quenching in O+O collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=200$ GeV, offering new insight into quark--gluon plasma formation in small collision systems.

authors.name: STAR Collaboration

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Perspective on Spectral Reconstruction in Lattice QCD
papers.summary: Assessing the reliability of spectral reconstruction from finite, noisy lattice correlators requires understanding the constraints supplied by the data relative to prior assumptions. We develop an information-theoretic framework using Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences to quantify the information supplied by the data through changes from prior to posterior probability distributions. Our analysis accounts for both changes in the probability distributions of spectral strength at individual energies and constraints encoded in correlations across the spectrum. We smear these information measures over neighboring energies using Gaussian weights to obtain a smoothed assessment at a specified energy scale. We demonstrate this framework using a hierarchical Bayesian reconstruction method with posterior sampling, applied to mock correlator data generated from a three-peak spectrum and a near-physical lattice proton correlator. These calculations show that the information measures help explain the properties of reconstructed spectra. They also provide a semiquantitative criterion for assessing how strongly reconstructed spectral structures are constrained by the data and how reliable they are in light of prior effects.

authors.name: Nan Wang, Long-cheng Gui, Jian Liang, Jun Shi, Han-yang Xing

papers.title: Optimised Distillation for Nucleon Correlation Functions
papers.summary: The calculation and analysis of nucleon correlation functions is essential for understanding the observed spectra and structure of these ubiquitous hadrons. Two challenges arise in their analysis: at early Euclidean times, they are dominated by excited state contributions and at later Euclidean times, the signal-to-noise ratio degrades exponentially. This leads to a common challenge in identifying a reasonable window on which to extract the ground state energy. By modulating the contribution of each Laplacian eigenmode to the correlator via distillation profiles, we build optimised operators which improve the overlap with the nucleon ground state. In these proceedings, we present our progress on constructing optimised distillation profiles for nucleons and their excited state suppression in two- and three-point correlation functions.

authors.name: J. A. Crawford, J. Finkenrath, L. Barca

papers.title: Symanzik Effective Hamiltonian for Lattice Quantum Field Theories
papers.summary: We propose a framework to construct the Symanzik effective Hamiltonian for lattice quantum field theories directly based on dimensional analysis and symmetries in the Hamiltonian formulation. This allows to classify all operators which can contribute at a given order in the spatial lattice spacing. This list can be reduced using the equations of motion and other identities. We exemplify the framework for $\phi^4$ and pure gauge theory, obtaining results consistent with earlier publications for the case of classical improvement. It provides the means to develop a non-perturbative improvement programme in the Hamiltonian formulation of lattice quantum field theories in the future.

authors.name: Fernanda Steffens, Carsten Urbach

papers.title: Counterdiabatic quantum optimization for efficient state preparation in the Schwinger model
papers.summary: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), whose design is underpinned by the adiabatic theorem, is one of the leading variational quantum algorithms for preparing the ground states of gauge theories. A recently proposed variant, DC-QAOA, incorporates counterdiabatic driving to accelerate the adiabatic process, reducing both circuit depth and runtime. In this work, we present a systematic analysis, from both theoretical and computational perspectives, of DC-QAOA and related counterdiabatic variants for preparing the ground state of the Schwinger model, the paradigmatic (1+1)-dimensional lattice gauge theory. Benchmarking these methods against standard QAOA, we show that counterdiabatic driving improves ground-state preparation while lowering circuit depth requirements. Our results establish counterdiabatic protocols as a practical route towards efficient quantum simulation of gauge theories.

authors.name: Ethan Laval, Bipasha Chakraborty, Stefano Cipolla

papers.title: Optimal summary statistics to constrain w0waCDM with the DESI BGS
papers.summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is the first stage-4 spectroscopic instrument installed on the 4-m Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona. It contains 5000 robotically positioned fibers, allowing the measurement of as many galaxy spectra in one observation (~20 minutes). The data acquisition (2021--2028) aims at constraining the cosmological parameters, and especially the parameters describing the evolution of the dark energy with time. However, standard clustering analysis based on 2-point statistics only capture the Gaussian information of the matter density field, while the analytical models used to match these statistical probe are limited to quasi-linear scales, as they are based on perturbation theory. Therefore, the non-Gaussian and non-linear information of the density field is not exploited. To go beyond these limitations, several alternative clustering methods have been developed that rely on a simulation-based pipeline. In this presentation, we focus on the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey, a magnitude-limited sample of bright galaxies in the redshift range of 0.1 < z < 0.4. We present how accessing the non-linear and non-Gaussian information of the density field allows around 40% improvement on the constraints of some $\Lambda$CDM parameters. We are also extending the method to constrain w0waCDM in order to improve DESI's sensibility at low redshift where the Universe is dominated by dark energy.

authors.name: Simon Bouchard

papers.title: What observations are needed to advance our theoretical understanding of galaxy formation at high redshift?
papers.summary: Although significant progress has been made over recent decades, a comprehensive and predictive framework for galaxy formation remains elusive. Starting from cosmological initial conditions, current models cannot a priori accurately predict key galaxy properties such as their structure, size, star formation histories, chemical abundance patterns, or supermassive black hole mass. This challenge stems from the vast range of spatial scales involved, as numerical simulations must simultaneously account for sub-AU processes nearby stars and black holes in addition to Mpc-scale cosmological gas inflows/outflows and environmental effects. Consequently, simulations must rely on subgrid models and approximations. As a result, theoretical progress in galaxy formation remains fundamentally driven by observational data and the iterative testing of model predictions against empirical results. Here we highlight five key open problems in theoretical galaxy formation that require dedicated observations of the high-redshift Universe, beyond what can currently be achieved through GO programs.

papers.title: DMAJOR: A JWST Legacy Survey of Protoplanetary Disks
papers.summary: We propose an infrared imaging survey of resolved protoplanetary disks spanning a range of galactic environments, directly mapping the 3D structure of planet-forming disks across the IR. DMAJOR (Disk Motions and Architectures JWST Observational Reference survey), our legacy survey, will deliver a benchmark sample to reveal structure and connection to environment. The exquisite stability of JWST allows us to probe for variability with a time-scheduled revisit strategy, while its sensitivity and resolution open a window on disks unobservable from the ground. A uniform sample will reveal how small grains and ice are distributed in protoplanetary disks, how scattered light structures relate to large-scale environmental features, and identify new companions. To achieve this, DMAJOR takes advantage of model-based data analysis using telemetry and mutual calibration to enhance processed data products while minimizing telescope overheads.

papers.title: First detection of the forbidden rotational spectrum of H$_3^+$: JWST/MIRI observations of the shocked gas in HH 168
papers.summary: The H$_3^+$ molecular ion is the cornerstone of interstellar ion-molecule chemistry. Its vibrational transitions have long been observed, in absorption along many interstellar sight lines and in emission from the upper atmospheres of the giant planets, but its pure rotational spectrum, which consists only of "forbidden" transitions made possible by centrifugal distortion, had not been observed in the laboratory or in any astronomical source. With JWST/MIRI we have detected this spectrum toward the Herbig-Haro object HH 168 in Cepheus A West. Twenty-six lines are detected above 5 $\sigma$ in one or both of two fields, of which the (J,K) = (5,0) -> (4,3) line at 16.325 $\mu$m is the strongest. The H$_3^+$ lines share the velocity and spatial distribution of the hot shocked H$_2$, not of the ionized gas. A rotation diagram yields a rotational temperature of ~ 730 K, but the level populations are not thermal and are best explained by subthermal excitation in gas at > 2000 K. We compare the observations with models of shocks propagating into mildly irradiated molecular gas. Constrained by the H$_2$ rotational lines, a dissociative J-type shock predicts H$_3^+$ emission within a factor ~1.5 of that observed, while a nondissociative C-type shock, which fits the H$_2$ lines better, underpredicts it by a factor 5-6, although the excitation of H$_3^+$ by energetic collisions is poorly known. Archival MIRI data show the H$_3^+$ forbidden rotational spectrum in the HH 211 bow shock. The H$_3^+$ lines provide a new probe of the ionization in shocked molecular gas.

authors.name: David A. Neufeld (JHU), Joel D. Green (STScI), Dan M. Watson (Rochester), Paule Sonnentrucker (STScI, ESA)

papers.title: First detection of suprathermal CH$^+$ rotational emissions from chemical pumping: JWST/MIRI observations of the HH 168 molecular shock
papers.summary: The methylidyne cation forms in warm or shocked interstellar gas through the endothermic reaction C$^+$ + H$_2$ -> CH$^+$ + H. Because C$^+$, which is common in irradiated and shocked gas, reacts with H$_2$ only when the reactants supply > 0.4 eV, CH$^+$ traces energy deposition in molecular gas. JWST/MIRI observations of HH 168 reveal the pure rotational lines R(17)-R(31) of CH$^+$ at 13.7-21.3 micron, from upper levels J = 18-32 (0.57-1.65 eV). Eleven lines exceed 5 sigma in both of the two fields that we observed and match the hot H$_2$ in radial velocity and spatial distribution. Because collisional excitation is negligible, each ion entering the v = 0 ladder emits one photon in every R(J) line below its entry level, so the line intensities provide the first measured rotational distribution of the ground-state products. The photon intensity falls almost linearly with increasing J, as expected for formation at a similar rate into every level up to J ~ 33; formation in J = 32 requires > 2 eV of reactant energy. The line positions, up to 150 km/s redward of ExoMol predictions, provide the first measurement of the CH$^+$ rotational intervals above J = 16. A Boltzmann distribution at $\phi T$ ~ 6200 K, where $\phi$ is the fraction of the available energy appearing in rotation, fits slightly better, implying reactant energies equivalent to several thousand kelvin. These lines probe the dynamics of a prototypical interstellar ion-molecule reaction.

authors.name: David A. Neufeld (JHU), Joel D. Green (STScI), Dan M. Watson (Rochester), Paule Sonnentrucker (STScI, ESA)

papers.title: A DOLPHOT/Euclid Study of the Resolved, Faint Outer Milky Way Globular Cluster AM-1
papers.summary: We present a resolved star study of AM-1, a distant ($D \simeq 120$ kpc), faint ($M_V \sim -5.1$) Milky Way (MW) globular cluster, based on Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) imaging. To perform photometry of the Euclid VIS and NISP imaging, we develop a Euclid-specific module for the crowded field stellar photometry package DOLPHOT. We construct and present empirical point spread function (PSF) models for VIS and NISP, along with a photometric calibration, entirely from the public Q1 images. Our photometry reaches $5\sigma$ point source depths of $I_E, Y_E, J_E, H_E = 27.1, 25.3, 25.5, 25.3$, $\sim$1-1.5 mag deeper than the public Q1 catalog, as expected for dedicated resolved star PSF photometry. We resolve the cluster to $\sim$1 mag below its main sequence turnoff in all bands. The Euclid photometry agrees with color-magnitude diagram (CMD) modeling of archival HST/WFPC2 imaging and with the 2MASS-anchored VISTA Hemisphere Survey to $\lesssim0.02$ mag in $I_E$, $J_E$, and $H_E$, with a $\sim$0.07 mag offset in $Y_E$. We find that AM-1 hosts an old ($\sim$10.6 Gyr), intermediate-metallicity ([Fe/H] $\sim -1$) population, with a present-day stellar mass of $\sim 2\times10^4\,M_\odot$ and $M/L_V \simeq 2.2$, and has a half-light radius of $\sim$12-16 pc with a round, low-concentration profile. These affirm earlier studies placing AM-1 among the most extended, diffuse outer-halo clusters, which dynamical work identifies as accreted. We describe and publicly release DOLPHOT v2.1, the Euclid module, and its empirical PSFs, which together enable Euclid resolved star studies ranging from faint MW systems such as AM-1 to more luminous galaxies throughout the Local Volume. We anticipate further refinements, including spatially varying PSFs, with Euclid Data Release 1.

authors.name: Daniel R. Weisz, Alessandro Savino, Andrew E. Dolphin, Meredith J. Durbin, Abigail J. Lee, Evan D. Skillman

papers.title: The deuterium-rich atmosphere of a mature super-Jupiter
papers.summary: The deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio (D/H) has provided key insights into the origin and evolution of the Solar System. Using the James Webb Space Telescope, we detected deuterated methane at $48\sigma$ in a mature giant exoplanet, $\epsilon$ Ind Ab. We measure the planet's D/H ratio to be $(4.4 \pm 0.7) \times 10^{-5}$, which is similar to those of Uranus and Neptune but about twice those of Jupiter, Saturn, and the protosolar nebula. $\epsilon$ Ind Ab's heavy elements (C, O, N, and S) are uniformly enriched to a level similar to Jupiter's. These measurements require $\epsilon$ Ind Ab to have accreted solids with $\mathrm{D/H} \gtrsim 1\%$, at least 30 times more deuterium-rich than typical Solar System comets. Such D/H values are found in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS and in organic molecules in star-forming regions, indicating that $\epsilon$ Ind Ab accreted pristine solids formed in a very cold environment.

papers.title: Classical Cepheids in the 4MOST era I: Methodology for 4MOST variable stars and NLTE abundance gradients in the Milky Way
papers.summary: Classical Cepheids (CCs) are key distance indicators and tracers of young stellar populations in the Milky Way. Their period-luminosity-metallicity (PLZ) relation also makes them calibrators of the Hubble constant $H_0$. Despite their importance, chemical composition, especially non-LTE (NLTE) effects, remains a significant source of systematics in PLZ applications. In preparation for the large CCs sample expected from the 4MIDABLE-HR (4MOST Consortium Survey 4: Milky Way Disc and Bulge High-Resolution) survey, we present a method for deriving Cepheid atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances in NLTE. Using the Payne artificial neural network (ANN) trained on NLTE spectra, we derive atmospheric parameters and abundances for 17 elements: O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Sr, Y, Ba, Eu in NLTE and C and Cr in LTE. We apply the new method to archival spectra of Cepheids and derive radial chemical gradients in the Milky Way. We derive robust NLTE stellar parameters and abundances for Cepheids spanning metallicities from $\sim -0.87$ to $\sim +0.35$ dex. For stars with multi-epoch spectra, we find that NLTE abundances are consistent across the pulsation cycle, whereas LTE values show larger dispersions and biases. The resulting abundance distributions and gradients align well with Galactic disk expectations from chemical evolution models. We confirm that the gradients flatten in the outer disk beyond $R_{\rm GC} \sim 15\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and provide the first NLTE gradients for Co, Ni, Y, and Eu. We show that our NLTE astrophysical analysis yields robust solutions for atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances across spectra at the resolving power of 4MOST-HR. This enables large, homogeneous studies with upcoming surveys such as 4MOST 4MIDABLE-HR and provides a solid basis for tightening constraints on Galactic chemical evolution models and Cepheid distance-scale work.

authors.name: R. Albarrac\'in, M. Bergemann, N. Storm, G. Guiglion, R. I. Anderson, V. D'Orazi, A. Dimoff, G. Kordopatis, G. Bono, T. Bensby, G. Traven, R. Church

papers.title: Probing circumstellar interaction with spectroscopy of ZTF hydrogen-rich superluminous supernovae
papers.summary: Hydrogen-rich superluminous supernovae (H-rich SLSNe) are rare, exceptionally luminous transients. Most exhibit narrow Balmer emission and can be further classified as SLSNe-IIn, indicating interaction with dense circumstellar material (CSM). We present and analyse 304 optical spectra of 106 H-rich SLSNe observed by the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF). We examine their spectral evolution and Balmer-line properties, and model the H$\alpha$ profiles using Monte Carlo electron-scattering calculations. Of the 106 objects, 105 exhibit narrow Balmer emission consistent with SLSN-IIn classifications, including six with additional Ia-CSM-like characteristics and three with possible flash-ionisation features; the remaining one object exhibits only broad Balmer emission and is classified as a SLSN-II. Post-peak Balmer profiles range from approximately symmetric, exponential profiles to asymmetric profiles with prominent blue excesses or shoulders. Objects with Balmer line blue excess favour higher fitted photon-emitting shell velocities and tend to be fainter than those with persistently symmetric profiles. The H$\alpha$ pseudo-equivalent width (pEW) and FWHM of SLSNe-IIn overlap with those of lower-luminosity SNe IIn, while the pEW evolution is more diverse than in the broad-lined SLSN-II comparison sample. Our SLSNe-IIn sample's median Balmer decrement increases from 2.85 before $+100$ d to 4.40 afterwards, remaining consistently below that of the comparison Ia-CSM sample. We identify no Balmer-line morphology unique to SLSNe-IIn in the available comparison with lower-luminosity SNe IIn, although some SLSNe-IIn exhibit prolonged high-ionisation emission. Our results also support interaction with dense CSM formed through enhanced pre-explosion mass loss. We also highlight a possible hidden Ia-CSM population among luminous H-rich interacting SNe.
