papers.title: Polarization Signatures of Magnetic Reconnection Bubbles near Black Holes
papers.summary: Motivated by the observed horizon-scale polarization variability in multi-epoch Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) data, we develop a time-dependent general relativistic polarized ray-tracing framework to study how localized magnetic reconnection near a black hole imprints itself on synchrotron polarization. We model the reconnection phenomenologically as a transient magnetic bubble. While keeping the underlying spacetime, emission prescription, and polarization transport scheme unchanged, the bubble weakens the local ordered field, reorganizes its geometry, induces a conservative local kinematic response, and relaxes through a finite magnetic-memory prescription. We explore how the key bubble parameters control the recovery of the magnetic-field strength, the spatial spreading of the disturbed region, the persistence of the post-reconnection imprint, and the resulting polarization signatures. Perturbations dominated by different magnetic-field components produce distinct polarized morphologies, EVPA evolution, and Stokes-(Q, U) trajectories: azimuthal perturbations favor outward EVPA shifts, radial perturbations favor inward shifts, and vertical perturbations mainly suppress the polarized intensity. For the illustrative M87^*-like cases, the phase evolution of the \beta_2 polarization coefficient further traces how localized magnetic reconfiguration contributes to the global EVPA twist of the ring. These results show that horizon-scale polarization variability can provide a sensitive diagnostic of localized magnetic restructuring and that the present framework offers a physically transparent way to interpret time-dependent polarimetric signatures in future EHT observations.

authors.name: Yu-Xiang Huang, En-Wei Liang

papers.title: The hierarchical structure of the Milky Way I. A model-agnostic clustering of 1 billion stars in 5D
papers.summary: The Milky Way exhibits a hierarchical structure shaped by mergers, accretion, and internal dynamics. Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) enables a global view of this structure, but requires scalable, model-agnostic methods to extract multi-scale clustering patterns. We aim to characterise the hierarchical clustering structure of the Milky Way in a model-agnostic way and to assess how the resulting structures relate to existing catalogues. We apply the hierarchical density-based clustering algorithm AstroLink to a locally magnitude-complete subsample of over one billion Gaia DR3 stars with five-dimensional astrometric information. The data are corrected for selection effects and transformed using a distance contraction and feature scaling. We compare the resulting cluster hierarchy to catalogues of open clusters, globular clusters, dwarf galaxies, and stellar streams using custom availability-aware metrics and a bi-directional best-match framework. At a significance threshold of $S = 3.8\sigma$, AstroLink identifies 7410 statistically significant clusters spanning a wide range of morphologies. Compact systems are often recovered as reciprocal matches with many also exhibiting internal substructure, while extended structures are typically fragmented or partially recovered. A substantial fraction of clusters have no counterpart in the comparison catalogues, these may be new structures but additional physical checks are needed to verify this. A model-agnostic, hierarchical clustering approach can recover the multi-scale structure of the Milky Way at Gaia DR3 scale and provides a unified framework for comparing heterogeneous catalogues and identifying candidate structures.

authors.name: William H. Oliver, Tobias Buck

papers.title: SMMAN studies of AGN variability. II. Radio and optical quasi-periodic oscillations and changing variability states in the relativistic jet of the blazar PKS 0754+100
papers.summary: We report the detection of $\sim$280-day quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the SMMAN observations of PKS 0754+100 at 4.8 and 23.6 GHz, which may also be present in VLBI observations made at 15 GHz. The onset of a transition of the amplitude of variability in the radio flux density, observed more clearly in the 15 GHz and 23.6 GHz observations, coincides with the detection of a likely QPO of $\sim$1.4 days in optical observations made by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. This transition in radio variability also occurs close in time to the disappearance of the secondary knot in the VLBI radio map during the lower variability state. An X-ray flare was observed 100 days before this transition, suggesting that the mechanisms causing these quasi-periodicities are related. After the transition to a higher variability state, both the 15 and 23.6 GHz light curves exhibit indications of QPOs at $\sim$400 days. For the first time, a QPO detected in the radio band from a BL Lac has been seen to appear to shift to a QPO of lower frequency, with that transition occurring near the appearance of a QPO in optical emission at a much shorter period. This multi-waveband behavior could be related to the internal helical structure of the jet, where an instability or kink develops due to magnetic reconnection and propagates outward.

authors.name: Ashutosh Tripathi, Xin Wang, Xi Yan, Paul J. Wiita, Lang Cui

papers.title: Constraining Cosmic Deceleration using the Solar System
papers.summary: We investigate whether Solar System dynamics can provide independent constraints on the present day cosmological deceleration parameter $q_0$, offering a complementary approach to conventional cosmological probes. By relating cosmic acceleration to a weak Hooke type radial perturbation, we derive bounds using planetary perihelion precession, trans-Neptunian objects, and Oort cloud dynamics. We obtain relatively robust planetary bounds of $|q_0|\lesssim 10^9$, while the outer Solar System yields potentially stronger, albeit more model dependent, constraints approaching $10^5$. Through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analyses, we explore the statistical robustness of these estimates and their dependence on orbital measurements. Finally, we demonstrate how future precision astrometry and outer planet missions could improve these limits by several orders of magnitude, establishing Solar System dynamics as a complementary laboratory for probing cosmological acceleration.

authors.name: Paridhi Jain, Oem Trivedi, Maxim Khlopov, Jackson Levi Said, Maxim Krasnov

papers.title: Probing the origin of the LHAASO Peanut with a hidden central accelerator
papers.summary: A highly asymmetric, giant Peanut-shaped structure has been detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) in ultra-high-energy gamma rays at high Galactic latitude, $b\approx-17.5^{\circ}$, suggesting anisotropic particle transport around a Galactic accelerator. We investigate whether its spectrum and morphology can arise from a hidden central accelerator embedded in a projected anisotropic halo. The baseline model accounts for the diffuse strip and central excess, while a phenomenological prescription for a localized magnetic field reorientation toward the line of sight (LOS), together with a particle-conserved remapping of the electrons downstream of the far excess into an emitting column of prescribed transverse extent, enhances the emission at the far excess position. We explore various source ages, along with different combinations of ambient magnetic field strength and parallel diffusion coefficient, while accounting for radiative cooling when estimating the viewing geometry. The exploration reveals that relatively rapid parallel transport enhances the far component while preserving a dominant diffuse strip. Representative configurations remain compatible with the observed spectral energy distribution, although the fitted far component remains comparatively weaker than the central component above 100 TeV, even in cases where their component fluxes are comparable at 25-100 TeV. These results illustrate the plausibility of a hidden central accelerator as the origin of the LHAASO Peanut, while identifying the remaining difficulty in reproducing the relative brightness of its compact components within the adopted phenomenological framework.

authors.name: Agnibha De Sarkar

papers.title: Studying the Fullerene Nest: JWST Observations of the Planetary Nebula Tc 1. II. A Spectroscopic and Spatial Study of C$_{60}$ and C$_{70}$ Emission
papers.summary: We present a detailed analysis of the fullerene emission bands in JWST MIRI/MRS observations of the planetary nebula Tc 1. The observations reveal the emission features due to neutral C$_{60}$ and C$_{70}$ in unprecedented detail. The combined fullerene emission represents $\sim$2.6% of the total infrared output, suggesting that $\sim$0.6% of the carbon budget is locked up in fullerenes. We find no clear evidence for C$_{60}^+$, C$_{70}^+$ or C$_{60}^-$ in the spectrum. The high spectral resolution allows us to separate the fullerene bands from atomic emission lines for the first time, allowing for a much better characterization of the band profiles and yielding more accurate band ratios than previous observations. We see no spatial variation in the individual C$_{60}$ and C$_{70}$ band profile shapes across all pixels. The 17.4 and 18.9 $\mu$m C$_{60}$ bands show clear resolved ro-vibrational structure in their profiles, and similar structured emission is seen in the 12.5, 14.8, 17.7, and 21.8 $\mu$m C$_{70}$ bands, further establishing that all emitting fullerene molecules are in the gas phase. We report a higher 7.0/18.9 $\mu$m C$_{60}$ band ratio ($\sim$1.4-1.9) than previously reported ($\sim$1.3). We note that all bands, except the 8.5 $\mu$m band, contain a significant contribution from C$_{70}$, complicating the analysis. The fullerene emission is spatially concentrated in a thin, asymmetric shell at a radius of 5-6$''$ from the central star. The shell lies at the outer edge of the core of the nebula, which was ejected in a single, brief episode $\gtrsim$4,000 years ago.

authors.name: M. M. Giese, J. Cami, S. Van Schuylenbergh, E. Peeters, C. Bhatt, D. Van De Putte, C. Baerts, M. J. Barlow, J. Bernard-Salas, A. Candian, P. B. Changala, N. L. J. Cox, H. L. Dinerstein, V. J. Esposito, D. A. Garc\'ia-Hern\'andez, M. A. G\'omez-Mu\~noz, K. Justtanont, K. E. Kraemer, E. Lagadec, A. Manchado, A. Monreal Ibero, R. Sahai, A. Sidhu, G. C. Sloan, N. C. Sterling, A. G. G. M. Tielens, J. R. Walsh, R. Wesson, J. C. Whitman, A. Zijlstra, L. Finazzi, J. Martens, G. Berden, J. Oomens

papers.title: Impact of the large scale environment on the baryonic scaling relations of disc galaxies: Insights from the GASP survey
papers.summary: The Tully--Fisher relation (TFR) and the specific angular momentum--mass relation (SAMR) link the baryonic content of a disc to its kinematics and dynamics. Hence, these scaling relations should bear the imprints of any process removing baryons or altering their kinematics, such as those acting in clusters of galaxies. We test this using the MUSE survey "GAs Stripping Phenomena in galaxies" (GASP), which targets field, group, and cluster members at $z \approx 0.05$ and various stages of ram pressure stripping. For the 81 discs with favourable inclinations, we measure the distribution and kinematics of stars and ionised gas, and their specific angular momenta. Within their scatter, the stellar and baryonic relations show no significant dependence on the large scale environment: the TFRs have slopes $\alpha \approx 3.6$ and $\approx 3.5$ for any kinematic tracer, and the SAMRs have $\alpha \approx 0.65$--$0.75$, as predicted by tidal torque theory. The same holds for the ten S0-S0/as in our sample, consistent with the "faded spiral" formation scenario. Only the gas SAMR shows an environmental signature, with ram pressure stripped galaxies lying $\approx 0.16$~dex below unperturbed ones. This offset is mostly due to their enhanced star formation rate, and thus higher gas mass when inferred through the Schmidt-Kennicutt law, rather than to kinematic perturbations or disc truncation. Our results suggest that, within the area probed by MUSE ($\lesssim6$ disc scale lengths), these discs have preserved the angular momentum acquired at formation not only from cluster processes and pre-processing in filaments, but also from mergers and ejective feedback acting in any environment.

authors.name: C. Bacchini, A. Marasco, B. Vulcani, A. Moretti, J. Fritz, R. Paladino, B. M. Poggianti, M. Mingozzi, P. E. Mancera Pi\~na, F. Rizzo

papers.title: Stellar Disruption and Black Hole Retention in Massive Collisions: The Role of Thermonuclear Feedback
papers.summary: A stellar-mass black hole (BH) that collides with a massive star can be captured by drag and settle at its center as a black hole star. Hydrodynamic simulations that neglect nuclear reactions have found that the star survives and becomes a black hole star (BH*) for BH-to-star mass ratios $q\lesssim0.2$. We perform hydrodynamic simulations of head-on collisions with the \athenak\ code, including CNO burning coupled to the gas, for $q=0.1$ and $0.2$ BHs, stellar masses of $100$ and $500\,M_{\odot}$, solar, metal-deficient, and Helium-rich compositions. In all models (with $q\le0.2$), the energy dissipated by drag is comparable to or less than the binding energy that the captured BH adds to the gas so that it alone does not disrupt the star. But, under compression around the captured BH, gas is heated to $\gtrsim2\times10^8$\,K and undergoes thermonuclear burning at the $\beta$-limited hot-CNO rate. Within about one dynamical time after the BH settles at the center, the nuclear energy released during the encounter becomes a significant fraction of the star's binding energy $\tfrac32\bar{\beta}\int P\,dV$. The star loses most of its mass once the cumulative release reaches this binding energy. Below this threshold, the release rate declines. Merger between a solar-composition star and a BH with a mass ratio $q=0.2$ leads to the disruption of the star after releasing most of its total mass. But a metal-poor star, with nearly the same binding energy and total yield, survives with minor release after merger with an identical BH. After coalescence with a less massive ($q=0.1$) BH, stars with both solar and metal-poor composition survive as black hole stars, burning at a rate $\gtrsim 10^{44}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$, far from thermal equilibrium. Very massive and helium-rich stars, which are weakly bound, are the most easily disrupted.

authors.name: Hongxuan Jiang, Douglas N. C. Lin

papers.title: Radial Velocity Confirmation of Two Binary Systems Detected with the Pulsation Timing Method
papers.summary: We present follow-up radial velocity (RV) results for the subdwarf B$+$white dwarf binaries TIC 202354658 and TIC 69298924, which were originally identified using the pulsation-timing and Fourier-modulation methods applied to ultra-short-cadence photometric data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ($TESS$). Using spectra obtained with the Gemini-North telescope and the Nordic Optical Telescopes, we derived the radial velocity curves for both targets. The orbital solutions we obtained are consistent with the predictions based on pulsation timing, and they provide more precise orbital information compared with the previously obtained results. We therefore confirm that both TIC 202354658 and TIC 69298924 are binary systems with white dwarf companions. The RV solution of TIC 202354658 indicates a relatively large eccentricity ($e$ = 0.313 $\pm$ 0.013), which would be uncommon for a short orbital period sdB binary.

authors.name: Tomomi Otani, A. S. Baran, Kaydence Boyle, Julia M. Clark

papers.title: Tidally-induced vertical asymmetries in the LMC bar and disk
papers.summary: Past observations and simulations have shown that the bar in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) may be tilted with respect to the disk plane, and that the outer LMC disk could be warped. These studies propose that the tilted bar and the warp in the LMC are induced by the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) pericentric passages. We analyze and quantify the effect of the SMC passage on the vertical position and kinematic asymmetries of both the bar and disk, as a function of different impact parameters or initial conditions. We used seven representative simulations from the KRATOS suite of $N$-body simulations of the LMC, SMC and Milky Way (MW) system for this analysis. To classify bar particles and analyze the bar and disk separately, we adopted a classification method based on persistent homology. To quantify the vertical asymmetries in the bar and disk of the LMC-like galaxy, we applied Fourier decomposition. We constructed Gaia DR3 mock catalogs to study whether the observed vertical asymmetries in Gaia DR3 are caused by astrometric uncertainties. We detect strong $m = 1$ vertical asymmetries in the bar and disk of the LMC-like galaxy for all interacting simulations after the pericentric passage of the SMC-like galaxy, indicative of a warped bar and disk. We also detect $m=2$ vertical asymmetries in the bar of the LMC-like galaxy for some simulations, indicative of a buckling bar. We conclude that the SMC passages induce vertical asymmetries in both the bar and the disk of the LMC, compatible to those measured in Gaia DR3. Tidal interactions naturally give rise to a warped and buckling LMC bar, and a warped LMC disk. Comparison between our results and Gaia DR3 suggest that models with a higher mass ratio between the SMC and the LMC may be favorable for reproducing the observed tilt of the LMC bar, and that the most recent SMC pericentric passage occurred at most 210 to 300 Myr ago.

authors.name: Shuyu Wang, Marie Sch\"olch, Merc\`e Romero-G\'omez, \'Oscar Jim\'enez-Arranz, Anthony G. A. Brown

papers.title: Season by season causal analysis of the continuum and velocity-resolved H$\beta$ emission of NGC 5548
papers.summary: We investigate possible causal influences in five historical seasons (1989-1993) of NGC 5548 using a version of the Synergistic-Unique-Redundant Decomposition (SURD) method adapted for this analysis, an information-theoretic causal discovery method for time series. Two four-variable sets contain the blue wing (B), core (C) and red wing (R) of H-beta together with either total H-beta (H) or the 5100 Angstrom continuum (F). We examine 7200 decompositions with common and unequal lags, two or three seasonal flux states, and base delays of 1-30 d. We rank the individual named components within each information family, reporting their amplitudes and simultaneous leakage. In 1989, unique continuum information about the core reaches 0.799 and 0.387 of target entropy for two and three states, with leakage 0.047 and 0.276. In 1992, the red-wing history supplies unique information about the future blue wing in both variable sets and both state counts, with peak target-entropy fractions 0.106-0.166. Distinct joint influences also emerge: for the 1991 core, the two-state S(F,B) and S(F,R) components contribute 0.187 and 0.125 at 20 d with leakage 0.087, although the unique continuum term vanishes. Strong core-wing redundancy identifies candidate inputs for simpler predictive models. Large late-lag leakage, reaching approximately 0.97 in the total set, identifies targets for additional driver measurements and richer temporal histories. The resulting seasonal map of individual, shared and joint influences complements the response delays and velocity structure measured by reverberation mapping, and provides specific causal hypotheses for the evolving broad-line region.

authors.name: Ayan Mitra, Vasilios Zarikas

papers.title: Studying the Fullerene Nest: JWST Observations of the Planetary Nebula Tc 1. III. Tracing Fullerene-Linked Dust Variation
papers.summary: We have observed the fullerene-rich planetary nebula Tc 1 with the MIRI/MRS on JWST. The mid-infrared spectra of this spatially resolved source reveal that the dust emission is not co-spatial with the fullerene emission. Three broad features can be distinguished: a 6$\unicode{x2013}$9 $\mu$m plateau, a 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau and the 30 $\mu$m feature. The 6$\unicode{x2013}$9 $\mu$m plateau does not change shape spectrally across the entire field of view, indicating it is produced by stochastically heated material. Spectral variations of the 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau reveal at least three distinct components, peaking at 9.5 $\mu$m, 11 $\mu$m and 12 $\mu$m respectively. SiC produces most likely at least the 11 $\mu$m component and we find evidence that the 12 $\mu$m component might be produced by SiC grains too. The variation in relative strength of these components across the field of view hints at dust processing taking place in Tc 1. The 9.5 $\mu$m component of the 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau has a strong correlation with the SiC component(s) and is thus likely produced by similar material.

authors.name: Simon Van Schuylenbergh, Jan Cami, Els Peeters, Morgan M. Giese, Charmi Bhatt, Dries Van De Putte, Cedric Baerts, Michael J. Barlow, Jeronimo Bernard-Salas, Alessandra Candian, P. Bryan Changala, Nick L. J. Cox, Harriet L. Dinerstein, Vincent J. Esposito, D. A. Garc\'ia-Hern\'andez, Marco A. G\'omez-Mu\~noz, Kay Justtanont, Kathleen E. Kraemer, Eric Lagadec, Arturo Manchado, Ana Monreal Ibero, Raghvendra Sahai, Ameek Sidhu, G. C. Sloan, N. C. Sterling, A. G. G. M. Tielens, Jeremy R. Walsh, Roger Wesson, Joshua Cole Whitman, Albert Zijlstra

papers.title: Is Dark Energy Inhomogeneous?
papers.summary: The discovery of dark matter deficient galaxies motivates a fundamental question: Could sufficiently large regions of the Universe be deficient in dark energy as well? We investigate this possibility by developing a phenomenological framework that distinguishes genuine dark energy deficiencies from ordinary matter voids through nonlinear expansion, coherent peculiar velocities and density-momentum correlations. We show that a $10\%$ dark energy deficiency can suppress the expansion of a representative nonlinear void by approximately $2.7\%$, generating peculiar velocity residuals of order $60$-$100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ across scales of $30$-$50\, Mpc$. Intriguingly, we find that deficiencies of order $20\%$ extending over several hundred megaparsecs could also influence the locally inferred Hubble constant, potentially contributing to the $H_0$ tension, subject to stringent isotropy and dynamical consistency constraints. We identify observational strategies involving DESI, Rubin, peculiar velocity surveys, and cosmic void catalogues, opening a new avenue for testing whether the dark energy driving cosmic acceleration is truly homogeneous.

authors.name: Oem Trivedi, Abraham Loeb

papers.title: The Role of Small-Scale Flux Emergence in Pre-eruptive Magnetic Destabilization
papers.summary: Recent high-resolution observations have reported the emergence of small-scale magnetic flux shortly before the onset of solar flares; however, their role in solar eruption processes remains unclear. In this study, we perform three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations to examine the effect of small-scale emerging flux on the eruption process. We construct a bipolar active region by extrapolating a potential magnetic field from a pair of sunspots and drive the system with sustained rotational motions to build up strong shear along the polarity inversion line. A small-scale emerging flux, amounting to approximately 0.6%-3.0% of the total magnetic flux and having a polarity opposite to that of the main sunspot, is then introduced at the center of the bipole. As a result, although no significant differences are found in the pre-existing magnetic field during the early phase with or without the emerging flux, the current sheet formed in the sheared field lines collapses more rapidly, and the reconnection-driven eruption is initiated earlier in the case with small-scale emerging flux. This result suggests that small-scale emerging flux accelerates the destabilization of the pre-eruptive magnetic configuration through enhanced current-sheet thinning and magnetic reconnection, leading to an earlier eruption onset. Furthermore, we find that the involvement of highly twisted field lines during the pre-eruption phase plays a crucial role in determining the eruption onset time.

authors.name: Satoshi Inoue, Huu Minh Triet Nguyen

papers.title: Probing faint radio activity from cores to filaments in two $z=2.24$ protoclusters with uGMRT
papers.summary: We present deep 1.26 GHz radio continuum observations of the two $z=2.24$ protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) to investigate their members' radio emission and its possible environmental dependence. Among 187 and 105 H$\alpha$ emitter (HAE) members in BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, we identify ten and two robust radio counterparts, respectively, together with five potential counterparts from forced photometry. Two HAEs and the massive quiescent galaxy QG1 in BOSS1244 show strong radio excesses relative to their H$\alpha$-based star formation rates (SFRs) and are identified as strong radio-excess AGN candidates. Median stacking of the remaining 173 and 102 radio-undetected HAE members yields positive signals at $2.8\sigma$ and $3.2\sigma$ in BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, respectively. The stacked radio luminosities are consistent with those expected from the median H$\alpha$-based SFRs, indicating that star formation can account for the average faint radio emission. After excluding the robust radio counterparts, we divided the HAE members by the projected distance from QG1 in BOSS1244 and from the filament spine in BOSS1542. The largest stacked radio luminosities are found toward the denser regions in both systems, but the differences are not statistically significant, and stellar mass shows no significant dependence on environmental distance. These results identify strong radio-excess AGN candidates among the individually detected members, while the faint HAE population is on average consistent with radio emission from star formation. The similar environmental ordering is suggestive but remains tentative. Deeper radio observations at multiple frequencies and higher angular resolution are required to determine whether this apparent trend reflects weak AGN activity or variations in radio emission associated with star formation.

authors.name: Yuheng Zhang, Xianzhong Zheng, Fangxia An, Tao Wang, Qinghua Tan, Dongdong Shi, Hao Peng

papers.title: MeerKAT reveals an ultra-steep spectrum radio halo in Abell 370
papers.summary: Hubble Frontier Field cluster Abell 370 ($z=0.375$) has been the target of a suite of legacy multi-wavelength observational campaigns and is a prime candidate to host a diffuse radio halo, given its high mass ($\sim10^{15}\,\rm{M_\odot}$) and non-relaxed dynamical state. Previous detections of its radio halo were of low significance and imaging fidelity, leading to an uncertain characterisation of its nature. We use deep MeerKAT Ultra-High Frequency observations ($580-1015\,\rm{MHz}$) to robustly map the halo's spatial extent and spectral properties. We find a radio emission size of $\sim 1.1\,\rm{Mpc}$, significantly larger than previously reported. We measure a MeerKAT UHF in-band integrated spectral index of $\alpha=-1.54\pm0.05$. This result is consistent with an ultra-steep spectrum radio halo ($\alpha\lesssim-1.5$). We find a strong, sub-linear correlation ($k=0.60\pm0.08$) between the radio and X-ray surface brightness. The radio halo's position on the $P_{1.4\,\rm{GHz}}-M_{500}$ scaling relation is underluminous, consistent with the known USSRH population. The combined evidence strongly supports that the diffuse central radio emission in Abell 370 is an Ultra-Steep Spectrum Radio Halo (USSRH), refining its previous classification and providing further support for the turbulent re-acceleration model.

authors.name: Graham Lawrie, Roger Deane

papers.title: Detecting Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from Galaxy Clusters: Distance Constraints
papers.summary: We present a measurement of the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature using the largest galaxy cluster sample with spectroscopic redshift information to date, comprising 169,679 clusters selected from the WH24 catalogue based on the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. We measure the two-point correlation function in two redshift bins, $0.17\leq z<0.35$ and $0.35\leq z<0.5$, corresponding to effective redshifts of $z_{\rm eff}=0.25$ and $0.43$, with the BAO feature detected at approximately the $4\sigma$ level or above in both bins. By fitting the measured correlation functions, we obtain dilation parameters of $\alpha=0.97\pm0.07$ and $\alpha=1.01\pm0.04$, corresponding to volume-averaged distance measurements of $D_V/r_d=6.70\pm0.48$ and $D_V/r_d=11.25\pm0.47$, respectively. Using the Planck 2018 sound horizon calibration, we obtain $H_0=66.6 \pm 4.9 \,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ within the flat $\Lambda$CDM framework. We further combine our cluster BAO measurements with cosmic microwave background and Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova observations to constrain dynamical dark energy within the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder parametrization. The resulting constraints are consistent with $\Lambda$CDM, which lies within the $68\%$ joint credible region in the $w_0$--$w_a$ plane. Our results demonstrate the potential of galaxy clusters as complementary tracers for BAO measurements and cosmological constraints.

authors.name: Xiaoyun Shao, Paula S. Ferreira, Carlos A. P. Bengaly, Rodrigo S. Gon\c{c}alves, Diego Garcia Lambas, Jailson Alcaniz

papers.title: Unveiling a Concentration of Hard X-Ray Point Sources in the Nuclear Stellar Disk with XMM-Newton
papers.summary: The Galactic Center is home to the largest known concentration of X-ray sources ever detected in our Galaxy, including a sizable population of accreting compact objects. Utilizing data from the XMM-Newton Galactic Plane Heritage Survey of the central $20^{\circ}\times2^{\circ}$ of the Milky Way, we investigate the varying source populations in the inner regions of the Galaxy. We identify for the first time a concentration of extremely hard X-ray sources within $|l|<1.3^{\circ}$ and $|b|<0.3^{\circ}$, a region that overlaps the nuclear stellar disk (NSD). We determine that this hardness is intrinsic to the sources and not a manifestation of high line-of-sight column density ($N_{\rm H}$). Unlike the "soft" X-ray sources, this population does not trace the stellar mass distribution, indicating an overabundance compared to the underlying stellar population. We simulate spectra for a variety of source types to model their X-ray hardness and compare their distributions to those we observed in our survey data. We find that a significant subset of the Galactic Center X-ray population may comprise intermediate polars (IPs) with massive white dwarfs, possibly formed through dynamical processes. Our study provides novel observational insights into the distribution of stellar remnants and other X-ray sources in the vicinity of our supermassive black hole, Sgr A*.

authors.name: Shifra Mandel, Kaya Mori, Gabriele Ponti, Samaresh Mondal, Charles J. Hailey, Michael M. Shara, Tong Bao, Heshou Zhang, Mark R. Morris, JaeSub Hong, Jonathan Grindlay, Nicola Locatelli, Simone Piscitelli

papers.title: Evolving stellar wind environment around M dwarfs and its influence on magnetic star-planet interactions
papers.summary: M dwarfs are the most abundant group of stars in the Galaxy and they are expected to host a large number of exoplanets orbiting in the habitable zone. It is believed that stellar winds of M dwarfs can have a substantial effect on these exoplanets and on the observations of these systems. However, a systematic investigation of how the stellar winds of M dwarfs varies on timescales of a few months to years and how this impacts exoplanets around these stars is missing. We aim to investigate how variability of magnetic field properties of M dwarfs affects their stellar winds, which is essential for future studies of star-planet interactions (SPIs) and planetary habitability. Such variability might shed light on whether SPI signatures are going to repeat. We have compiled a total of 18 magnetic field maps for 6 M dwarfs, with masses between 0.1 and 0.6 $M_\odot$, and rotation periods between 2.7 and 175.6 days. We use these maps as input of 3D magnetohydrodynamic stellar wind simulations. We derive the mass-loss rate, the angular momentum-loss rate, and the Alfv\'en radius. For the stars with confirmed exoplanets (DS Leo, YZ Cet, and GJ 1151) we investigate the variability of stellar wind properties at the orbit. We find mass-loss rates between $1.0\times10^{-14}~M_\odot~{\rm yr^{-1}}$ and $2.3 \times 10^{-13}~M_\odot~{\rm yr^{-1}}$ and angular momentum-loss rates between $4.6 \times 10^{27}~{\rm erg}$ and $4.9 \times 10^{31}~{\rm erg}$. For individual stars the Alfv\'en radius, mass-loss rate, and angular momentum-loss rate varied with time by up to a factor of 1.5, 3.8, and 7.4 respectively. Our results follow the observational relation between mass-loss rate and X-ray flux. Due to the time-varying Alfv\'en surface, exoplanets orbiting DS Leo and YZ Cet move in and out of the sub-Alfv\'enic regime, affecting the nature of star-planet interactions and prospects for their detection.

authors.name: Szymon Petyniak, Stefano Bellotti, Aline Vidotto, Paul Cristofari, Jean-Francois Donati, Ayan Biswas, Colin Folsom

papers.title: A Census of Novae in the Small Magellanic Cloud, 1897-2026
papers.summary: A census of nova candidates in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) is presented. Twenty-six optical transients have been reported as novae or nova-like eruptions from the discovery of HV 849 in 1897 through 2026 October. Twenty-three are probable classical novae. Two, MAXI J0158$-$744 and CXOU J005245.0$-$722844, are very fast, super-Eddington eruptions that have been interpreted as novae on white dwarfs with Be-star companions, while a third, SMCN 2002-10a, is a possible Be+WD event identified only from its quiescent counterpart. Four additional Be+WD candidates that have been detected only in X-rays are briefly discussed.

authors.name: Allen W. Shafter

papers.title: Vacuum energy interacting with dark matter and dark radiation: alleviating the $H_0$-$S_8$ seesaw
papers.summary: Extensions of $\Lambda$CDM that raise $H_0$ with additional energy before recombination, such as dark radiation and early dark energy (EDE), also raise $S_8$. We study whether a late-time energy exchange between the vacuum and the dark sector can offset this increase. The coupling rate scales as $\bar m H^{\alpha}$ and is negligible before recombination for $\alpha \le -2$; the energy is transferred along the four-velocity of geodesic cold dark matter, so the dark matter produced by the vacuum carries no density perturbation and slows the growth of structure. We add the exchange to dark radiation ($\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM) and to a one-parameter EDE model ($\bar m$EDE), and constrain the models with Planck 2018, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ data (CBS), and with the SH0ES calibration added (CBSH) to test the exchange when $H_0$ is held at a high value. For CBS the posteriors favour an energy flow from the vacuum into dark matter at 1.8-2.7$\sigma$, and the exchange lowers $S_8$ by 0.02-0.08 but does not raise $H_0$: $\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM gives $H_0 = 68.83 \pm 0.91$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, 3.1$\sigma$ below SH0ES. For CBSH the exchange removes the increase of $S_8$ caused by dark radiation, giving $S_8 = 0.800 \pm 0.016$ at $H_0 = 71.34 \pm 0.70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, and about a third of that caused by EDE for $\alpha = -2$, with the coupling at 1.1-2.0$\sigma$. The reduction of $S_8$ is concentrated at $z \lesssim 0.3$: at the redshifts probed by KiDS-Legacy the lensing amplitude decreases by only 1-2%, the shear $\chi^2$ of the dark-radiation models changes by less than 3, and the exchange reduces but does not remove the excess shear $\chi^2$ of EDE. A late-time exchange can therefore offset part of the $S_8$ increase of early-time solutions, but it does not ease the Hubble tension, and current data do not require it.

authors.name: Li-Yang Gao, She-Sheng Xue, Xin Zhang

papers.title: The Dusty Circumstellar Structure of the Yellow Hypergiant IRC +10420: Constraints from the SED and Near-Infrared Imaging Polarimetry
papers.summary: The yellow hypergiant IRC +10420 is a post-red supergiant evolving toward higher temperatures. We model its circumstellar dust with the radiative transfer code RADMC-3D, including polarized scattering, constrained by the spectral energy distribution (SED) from 0.4 $\mu$m to 1.3 mm and by the K' (2.2 $\mu$m) imaging polarimetry of Shenoy et al. (2015), assuming a pole-on view. The model consists of an equatorial structure (a flared inner disk of 0.3 $\mu$m grains at 300-3000 au, a ring at 3000-16,000 au whose surface density peaks at $\approx 10^4$ au, and a thin mid-plane disk of 300 $\mu$m grains) embedded in a spherical envelope of 0.15 $\mu$m grains with $\rho \propto r^{-2.3}$. It reproduces the SED within 0.07 dex and the total- and polarized-intensity profiles; the fractional polarization peaks at 15% at 1.7 arcsec (observed: 14%). The rising surface density of the ring produces the polarized-intensity plateau, and 0.5 $\mu$m grains at its outer edge the decline beyond 2 arcsec; grains of $\gtrsim 0.7$ $\mu$m are excluded. A thin disk of large grains suggests a settled mid-plane. Stellar temperatures of 7000-8500 K fit equally well. Of the total extinction ($A_V \approx 6.9$ mag), 5 mag is interstellar. Most of the $7.4 \times 10^{-2}$ $M_\odot$ of dust is equatorial; the envelope implies a mass-loss rate of $\approx 10^{-5}$-$10^{-4}$ ($\psi$/100) $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$. Because equatorial dust redirects starlight poleward, the pole-on SED overestimates the luminosity by $\approx 1.5$; at the Gaia distance, $L_\star \approx 3.3 \times 10^5$ $L_\odot$. Subtracting a scaled stellar PSF removes most of the nebular light within $\approx 1$ arcsec.

authors.name: Kyung-Won Suh

papers.title: Ejecta fate and deposition in the Didymos-Dimorphos system after the DART impact
papers.summary: Kinetic impact is a promising technique for asteroid deflection in planetary defense. The NASA Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft collided with Dimorphos, the satellite of the binary asteroid (65803) Didymos, at 6.1449 km s^{-1} in 2022. Observations revealed changes in both the orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos and the heliocentric orbit of the Didymos-Dimorphos system. The ESA Hera spacecraft will arrive at the system at the end of 2026 to investigate the post-impact surfaces. Here, we present an analytical model, based on Maxwell's Z model, to predict ejecta behavior following the DART impact. The model provides the relationships among ejection velocity, ejection angle, and ejecta mass, allowing the momentum enhancement factor beta to be estimated for both Dimorphos and the Didymos-Dimorphos system. We show that the observed beta can be reproduced when 0.3-1% of the impact kinetic energy is converted into ejecta kinetic energy and the effective strength of the target is less than 100 Pa. The escaping mass is estimated to be 0.3-3.0% of the mass of Dimorphos. The globally averaged and minimum ejecta thicknesses on Dimorphos are estimated to be 2.0 m and 0.5 m, respectively, indicating that the entire surface was resurfaced by ejecta deposition, although boulders larger than 1 m were only partially buried. The model also predicts the momentum partition parameter kappa_p to be as low as 0.6, suggesting that the mass and the bulk density of Dimorphos may be revised upward. These predictions provide quantitative constraints for interpreting forthcoming Hera observations.

authors.name: Kosuke Kurosawa, Satoshi Takada

papers.title: The shape and velocity of black hole coronas
papers.summary: The first highly significant detection of the polarization of the X-rays from the Black Hole X-ray Binary Cygnus X-1 revealed surprisingly strong polarization parallel to its radio jet. The observation is now commonly interpreted as resulting from the Comptonization of some lower frequency seed photons in a laterally extended corona. The emitting plasma is likely moving along the jet axis with a sizable fraction beta of the speed of light, amplifying the polarization degree. In this letter we address the question of how laterally extended the corona actually needs to be to account for the observations, and we calculate the required outflow velocities of velocity-stratified coronas as a function of the stationary-frame aspect ratio h=H/2R of cylindrical coronas of height H and radius R. We find that models with h lesser equal 0.8 and beta=0.5-0.9 at the top of the corona can give both the observed photon index of Gamma=1.6 and the observed 4% polarization parallel to the symmetry axis. We do not find suitable solutions for larger h. Given the constraints on h, we discuss the likely size of the corona, emphasizing that compact coronas close to the black hole are preferred as they can tap more efficiently into the gravitational energy and the rotational energy of the black hole, and are less exposed to their own emission reprocessed in the optically thick portion of the accretion flow.

authors.name: Henric Krawczynski (Washington University in St. Louis), Kun Hu (Washington University in St. Louis), Sohee Chun (Washington University in St. Louis)

papers.title: Could globular clusters in the vicinity of the galactic centre have contributed stars to the nuclear star cluster in the past?
papers.summary: The results of direct N-body simulations of three Milky Way bulge globular clusters - Terzan 2, Terzan 4, and Terzan 5 - evolving in a time-varying galactic potential derived from the IllustrisTNG-100 cosmological database over 8 Gyr are presented. Incorporating full stellar evolution and compact remnant formation, we quantify the probability and efficiency of stellar accretion onto the Galactic nuclear star cluster (NSC) during close pericentre passages of these three clusters. To parametrize the effect of dynamical friction in the dense central environment, we introduce a velocity reduction factor (Vred) ranging from 1.00 to 0.10. It was found that all three clusters contribute stars to the NSC even in the absence of velocity reduction, with a combined bound stellar count of 730 stars and a total accreted mass of 278 Msol at Vred = 1.00, growing to 5420 stars and 1175 Msol at Vred = 0.10. Terzan 4 is the dominant contributor across all velocity reduction factors, reflecting its more frequent and closer pericentre passages near the Galactic centre. The mass distribution of accreted stars reveals a bimodal structure: a low-mass component below 1 Msol whose capture is independent of Vred, and a prominent high-mass tail extending to 20 Msol corresponding to neutron stars and black holes, which grows with decreasing Vred. Notably, Terzan 4 is the only cluster for which white dwarfs are also captured by the NSC at every Vred value. Our results suggest that the Terzan family represents a more significant source of compact remnants for the Galactic NSC than previously studied clusters, while confirming that tidal stripping of surviving globular clusters alone cannot account for the total NSC mass.

authors.name: Kalambay M., Kuvatova D., Ishchenko M., Berczik P., Omarov Ch., Kusakin A

papers.title: Dust in cold and warm dark matter in a suite of zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues
papers.summary: We use a suite of hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues to investigate how previously identified trends in dust properties of galaxies can be utilised to infer the underlying dark matter model. We use a sample of 24 comparison simulations comparing a cold dark matter (CDM) and 3.5 keV warm dark matter (WDM) particle, primarily using a dust-to-metals (DTM) ratio to post-process the dust in the simulation, with alternative methods explored. We find a preference for higher dust masses in CDM over WDM, with a median increase of 6.6 per cent in the CDM sample at redshift $z=0$, and with a peak median difference of 25 per cent at $z\approx0.25$. Both CDM and WDM samples are highly concentrated, with approximately 90 per cent of the dust located in the inner region of the halo, though slightly higher in CDM. Contrary to previous work, we find that the Gini coefficient does not consistently show a difference in comparisons of dark matter models, with differences primarily driven by high sensitivity to the unique structure of individual haloes. Finally, we conduct an analysis of some common dust scaling relations, finding that the differences between the two samples in the dust-to-stellar mass and dust-to-SFR functions do not constitute a statistically significant difference at $z=0$ with any dust production mechanism. However, at redshifts where the difference in dust mass is greatest, the alternative dust production methods show larger separations between CDM and WDM samples in total mass and scaling relations.

authors.name: Adam Ussing, Robert Mostoghiu Paun, Darren Croton, Alan Duffy, Chris Power, Celine Boehm

papers.title: Enhanced Mid-Photospheric Heating Around a Solar Pore
papers.summary: We present depth-stratified atmospheric reconstructions of a solar pore observed with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter (SCIP) aboard \textsc{Sunrise~iii}. Using spatially coupled NLTE spectropolarimetric inversions, we characterize the thermal, magnetic, and velocity structure of the pore and its surroundings from the photosphere to the chromosphere over approximately two hours. The inversions recover the canonical photospheric properties of pores: a cool umbra with strong magnetic fields dominated by the vertical component. Most photospheric velocities are subsonic, but localized downflows near the pore boundary reach transonic or potentially supersonic values around $\log\tau_{500}=0$. At higher atmospheric layers, the thermal contrast between the pore and its surroundings decreases substantially. We also detect localized mid-photospheric temperature enhancements forming a patchy, ring-like structure in the wings of the Ca\,{\sc ii} 8542\,{\AA} line, without a clear continuum counterpart. The temperature excess reaches approximately $300$\,K and corresponds to an excess thermal-energy density of up to $170$\,J\,m$^{-3}$. These regions coincide with an enhanced transverse magnetic-field component and the expanding magnetic canopy surrounding the pore. The structure is detected in all three rasters, although the cadence does not establish whether individual patches persist or repeatedly re-form. While the heating mechanism cannot be uniquely identified, the inferred magnetic topology supports an association with processes operating in the expanding canopy. These results demonstrate the value of pores for investigating the coupling between magnetic topology, convection, and atmospheric energy transport.

authors.name: Ana Bel\'en Gri\~n\'on-Mar\'in, Adur Pastor Yabar, Jaime de la Cruz Rodr\'iguez, Sami K. Solanki, Andreas Lagg, Achim Gandorfer, Jose Carlos del Toro Iniesta, Yukio Katsukawa, Pietro Bernasconi, Thomas Berkefeld, Alex Feller, Tino L. Riethm\"uller, Alberto \'Alvarez-Herrero, Masahito Kubo, H. N. Smitha, David Orozco Su\'arez, Bianca Grauf, Michael Carpenter, Alexander Bell, Valent\'in Mart\'inez Pillet, Francisco Javier Bail\'en, Julian Blanco Rodr\'iguez, Juan Sebasti\'an Castellanos Dur\'an, Edvarda Harnes, Johannes Hoelken, Francisco A. Iglesias, Ryohtaroh T. Ishikawa, Yusuke Kawabata, Takuma Matsumoto, Takayoshi Oba, Azaymi L. Siu-Tapia, Hanna Strecker, Du\v{s}an Vukadinovi\'c, Hirohisa Hara, Toshifumi Shimizu

papers.title: CMB Bounds on Primordial Black Holes via Radiation Capture: Linear Perturbations
papers.summary: We investigate the gravitational interaction between primordial radiation, consisting of photons and ultra-relativistic neutrinos, and primordial black holes (PBHs), and study its imprint on the anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Assuming that PBHs are immersed in the cosmic radiation background, we introduce a covariant energy-momentum transfer four-vector to describe the gravitational capture of radiation by PBHs. We extend the background-level framework of M. Farhang and S. M. S. Movahed [Phys. Rev. D 114, 083533 (2026)] to an inhomogeneous Universe at linear order by consistently modifying the perturbed continuity and Euler equations to account for both energy and momentum transfer. We use the imprint of this interaction on the CMB to place novel constraints on the PBH abundance, $f_{\rm pbh}$. We show that these constraints are up to two orders of magnitude tighter than those obtained from background-only analyses and exhibit a strong dependence on the PBH mass. Using Planck temperature and polarization data, we constrain the PBH fraction to $f_{\rm pbh} \lesssim 0.05-0.002$ for $M$ in the range $10^{15}-10^{17} M_\odot$. Furthermore, sensitivity forecasts for a cosmic-variance-limited survey with $\ell_{\rm max}=7000$, assuming a fiducial $f_{\rm pbh}=0$, yield projected bounds of $f_{\rm pbh} \lesssim 10^{-2}-2\times 10^{-4}$ over the mass range $10^{13}-10^{17} M_\odot$.

authors.name: M. Farhang, S. M. S. Movahed

papers.title: Particle Swarm Optimization Strategies for Lensed Gravitational Waves: Parameter Estimation, Source Classification, and Accelerated Sampling
papers.summary: The detection and parameter estimation of lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals are crucial for astrophysics and cosmology. Strong lensing introduces extra parameters, rendering the search high-dimensional, multi-modal, and strongly nonlinear. We apply Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to the search, parameter estimation, and classification of lensed compact binary coalescence GWs within a four-detector coherent network. Using the restricted 2-PN waveform as a template and a model-independent double-image lens parameterization, we assess PSO on both model-matched 2-PN signals and template-mismatched IMRPhenomD signals. Results show effective recovery of chirp mass, mass ratio, sky location, and lens parameters in the 2-PN case, with mass biases appearing under waveform mismatch. A three-class classification pipeline combining 12 PSO runs, majority voting, and a flux ratio threshold achieves 86.19% accuracy in distinguishing lensed GWs, unlensed GWs, and noise. We further propose PSO_GAUSS_MIX method, which constructs a Gaussian mixture prior from PSO estimates for nested sampling, yielding speedups of 1.38x in the restricted 2-PN cases while preserving posterior accuracy. These results establish PSO as an efficient optimizer for lensed GW searches and an effective prior constructor for Bayesian parameter estimation.

authors.name: Weiqing Yu, Meng Zhang, Xiaobo Zou, Xiao Guo

papers.title: An assessment of the Weak Field Approximation
papers.summary: The Weak Field Approximation (WFA) is widely used to infer magnetic fields from solar spectropolarimetric observations. However, its validity and sensitivity to atmospheric conditions are not fully understood. We investigate the reliability and limitations of the WFA using Generalized Response Functions (GRFs), which quantify the sensitivity of the inferred magnetic field to atmospheric perturbations. We derive analytical expressions for the WFA GRFs and compute them from synthetic Stokes profiles generated with the SIR and DeSIRe radiative transfer codes. We consider photospheric and chromospheric lines under different magnetic field strengths and inclinations. The inferred magnetic field depends on the atmospheric structure, field inclination, and wavelength range. For photospheric lines, the WFA increasingly departs from the actual field strength well before reaching the saturation value, due to the loss of linearity between Stokes V, Q, and U and the intensity profile derivatives. The transverse-field inference is particularly sensitive to the wavelength range, with line wings providing more reliable estimates. For chromospheric lines, the core and wings probe different atmospheric layers, with the wings providing reliable estimates of the photospheric field. The WFA has a more limited range of validity than commonly assumed. Its reliability depends on field strength, inclination, and wavelength selection, particularly for the transverse component. Chromospheric line wings can also provide useful information on the photospheric magnetic field. These findings support the original perturbative formulation of the WFA.

authors.name: D. Arroyo Caballero, J. C. del Toro Iniesta, D. Orozco Su\'arez, A. L. Siu-Tapia

papers.title: Intermediate-redshift ultra-luminous infrared galaxies as transitioning objects between main sequence and starburst galaxies
papers.summary: With their star formation efficiencies (SFE) and star formation rates (SFR) falling between normal star-forming galaxies and starbursts (SBs), ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs) at intermediate redshifts ($0.2<z<1$) have been postulated to be good probes of galaxies transitioning between these two regimes. Here, we present new Atacama Large Millimetre Array (ALMA) observations of a representative sample of 22 ULIRGs at redshifts $0.46<z<0.81$ evenly distributed across dust temperature ranges of $25<T_{\rm dust}<50~K$ and spanning infrared luminosities of $10^{12.0}<L_\text{IR}<10^{12.7}~L_\odot$. We detected CO(2-1) emission in 14 of these galaxies (64%). The SFE of these 14 targets are all similar, corresponding to depletion timescales on the order of hundreds of Myr. By employing two different versions of the main sequence relation of galaxies -- one based on the specific SFR (sSFR) and one based on directly observable parameters (CO and IR luminosities) -- we statistically confirm that the present sample of intermediate redshift ULIRGs indeed lies in the transitional region between MS and SB galaxies. In addition, we establish that the SFE of our sample of ULIRGs is a strong indicator of the position of a galaxy relative to the MS and the SB branches. Based on the observed morphologies and star-forming properties, we suggest that minor mergers provide a viable mechanism for temporarily enhancing the SFR and SFE of intermediate-redshift ULIRGs, although other evolutionary phases and pathways cannot be excluded.

authors.name: J. -H. Kim, D. Rigopoulou, M. Pereira-Santaella, L. Barrufet, A. Alonso-Herrero, I. Garc\'ia-Bernete, C. Pearson

papers.title: Investigating the Viability of Dedicated Microhertz Gravitational Wave Pulsar Timing
papers.summary: The microhertz gravitational wave (GW) frequency regime remains one of the least explored regions of the GW spectrum. This is due to the physical limitations of our current and upcoming GW observatories such as LIGO and LISA, which are tuned to dHz and mHz respectively. Proposed experiments targeting the $\mu$Hz regime are ambitious, expensive and unlikely to be operational within the next 20 years. Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs), with their Galaxy-sized baselines, occupy the other end of the spectrum; the frequencies they are sensitive to are a function of the observing cadence and total dataset timespan. Existing PTA campaigns have cadences and timespans corresponding to the nanohertz regime, however the possibility exists that they can be 'pushed' to detect higher frequencies. This paper investigates the viability of a custom microhertz-sensitive PTA, observing a small number of millisecond pulsars with a daily cadence, over the course of 1 and 2 years respectively. We assume the use of both 100-m and 500-m class radio telescopes for these observations, and an idealised noise model with negligible systematics to determine the most optimistic detection threshold. We compute the sensitivity of our proposed high-cadence PTA configurations to power-law signals and individual GW sources. We find that a 500-m class telescope would likely be able to set new upper limits on individual sources and GW background signals in the $0.1-1~\mu$Hz range; while a 100-m class telescope would, in the best case, only match that of the performance of the EPTA second data release in the same range. Finally we consider a possible $\mu$Hz PTA consisting of SKA-Mid and DSA observing 24 pulsars; we find this performs on par with the 500-m class while using far less telescope time, presenting a more feasible solution to microhertz-GW pulsar timing.

authors.name: C. F. Sheridan, E. F. Keane

papers.title: Upgrade of the MITHiC testbed for phase and amplitude control in the focal plane
papers.summary: High-contrast imaging for the direct detection of exoplanets is limited by stellar brightness and by wavefront errors. Coronagraphy and wavefront control reduce these effects and enable contrast levels compatible with current testbeds and future missions such as the Roman Space Telescope. Within this framework, the MITHiC testbed at the Laboratoire d'Astrophysique de Marseille is being upgraded with a new deformable mirror used to control the wavefront. It complements the existing setup, which includes a classic Lyot coronagraph and a spatial light modulator (SLM) enabling phase and amplitude control to optimize the dark-hole region. We also implement the Zernike wavefront sensor (ZELDA) to correct low-order aberrations. This contribution presents recent progress on the MITHiC upgrade and initial results, highlighting its role as a versatile platform for developing advanced high-contrast imaging techniques.

authors.name: Anton Neisius, \'Elodie Choquet, Vincent Chambouleyron, Arthur Vigan

papers.title: Measurement of the Neutrino Spectrum along the Galactic Plane with IceCube
papers.summary: We present the first measurement of the variation of the high-energy neutrino flux along the Galactic plane using 10 years of neutrino-induced particle-shower data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. In this Letter, we fit both the neutrino flux normalization and the spectral index, in multiple regions along the plane, independent of model expectations. The neutrino flux per solid angle in the inner Galactic region ($\vert l\vert60^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) at $E_\nu=5\mathrm{TeV}$. The spectral indices in the inner and outer region are $\gamma=2.76^{+0.18}_{-0.15}$ and $\gamma = 3.13^{+0.57}_{-0.37}$, respectively. Additionally, we compare the same region of Galactic emission measured in $\mathrm{TeV}$ gamma rays by LHAASO ($15^{\circ}<l<125^{\circ}$) to neutrinos, and conclude that the measurements are compatible within uncertainties, under the assumption of hadronic gamma-ray production.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the H$\alpha$ Luminosity Functions at $z\sim 1.3$ and $z\sim 2.0$ in the CANUCS Lensing Fields with JWST NIRISS
papers.summary: We present H$\alpha$ luminosity function (LF) measurements at redshifts $z\sim1.3$ and $z\sim2.0$. We adopt JWST grism data in five lensing cluster fields and their parallel fields from the CANUCS program: ABELL-370, MACS-J0416, MACS-J0417, MACS-J1149, MACS-J1423. Based on emission lines spectroscopically identified in the F115W, F150W and F200W filters, our final sample consists of 762 H$\alpha$ emitters, including 433 at $1.1<z<1.5$ and 329 at $1.8<z<2.2$. Through detailed effective volume and completeness analysis for each source, we construct the H$\alpha$ LF in two redshift bins. Thanks to the sensitivity of NIRISS WFSS and gravitational lensing magnification, our sample reaches intrinsic H$\alpha$ luminosities down to $L_{\rm H\alpha}\sim10^{40.6}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $L_{\rm H\alpha}\sim10^{41}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim2.0$ with completeness larger than 80\%. The larger survey volume and coverage of multiple independent sightlines help mitigate cosmic variance. After accounting for cosmic variance, we constrain the faint-end slopes to be $\alpha_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}=-1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $-1.42^{+0.09}_{-0.06}$ at $z\sim2.0$, indicating a mild evolution between the two redshift bins. We find a negligible contribution from bright active galactic nuclei in our sample. We estimate integrated cosmic star formation rate densities of $0.103^{+0.008}_{-0.007}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $0.149^{+0.016}_{-0.013}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim2.0$. The emission-line samples presented here will enable further detailed studies of galaxy properties including metallicities. The methodology presented here can be readily applicable to other JWST slitless spectroscopic datasets and future wide-field slitless surveys, including those from Euclid, Roman, and the Chinese Space Station Telescope.

papers.title: Depth of Maximum of EAS and Mean Mass Composition of Primary CRs from the Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Cherenkov Light According to TAIGA-HiSCORE Data
papers.summary: We present the dependence of the depth of maximum of extensive air showers (EAS), $X_{\max}$, on the energy of the primary particle, as determined from data recorded with the wide-angle Cherenkov array TAIGA-HiSCORE during the 2021--2025 observation seasons. The reconstruction of $X_{\max}$ from the experimental data uses relations obtained from EAS simulations: the dependence on the steepness of the Cherenkov light lateral distribution function ($P$-method) and on the full width at half maximum of the Cherenkov light pulse ($\tau$-method). The reconstructed $X_{\max}$ values are converted into the mean logarithmic mass $\langle\ln A\rangle$, which characterizes the primary cosmic-ray mass composition. The results are compared with measurements from Tunka-133 (2017), the Pierre Auger Observatory (2019), LHAASO (2024), TALE (2026), and other experiments.

papers.title: Ultralight scalar field domain walls and Galileo GNSS atomic clocks
papers.summary: In this article, we study the impact of an Earth-sized ultralight scalar field domain wall (DW) on the European Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System constellation and the feasibility of a related detection. In particular, a set of statistical procedures is developed and implemented to characterize the statistical properties of the background noise for a subnetwork of $N$ Galileo satellite clocks, including a false-alarm rate estimation and a detection efficiency analysis. These methods allow to implement a coincidence analysis and establish a preliminary statistical framework for a robust and controlled search for domain-wall crossings in clock data, and for deriving constraints on the associated fundamental particle physics parameters. The activity is addressed from the point of view of the scientific objectives of the Galileo for Science (G4S$\_2.0$) project.

papers.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of early-type stars. Testing Stokes parameter inversions with theoretical magnetohydrodynamic models
papers.summary: Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI) is widely used to reconstruct magnetic fields in early-type stars from time-series spectropolarimetric observations, yet its accuracy has not been systematically validated against physically self-consistent, complex magnetic field models. We aim to assess the reliability and limitations of modern ZDI techniques applied to fossil fields of early-type stars. We generated synthetic spectropolarimetric data from three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of fossil magnetic fields. The resulting Stokes profiles - individual lines and least-squares deconvolved (LSD) profiles - were inverted with contemporary ZDI codes using Stokes IQUV and IV data. We compared the reconstructed maps with the input MHD surface fields and quantified deviations in field strength, vector orientation, and harmonic energy decomposition. For Stokes IQUV inversions, ZDI recovers field vector components and strength with better than 10% accuracy, while Stokes IV inversions degrade to 15-20% for the most complex geometries. The field inclination is recovered to within 10 deg, with errors increasing to 15-20 deg in the same cases. Full Stokes inversions reproduce poloidal and toroidal energies to within a few percentage points. LSD-based inversions yield accuracy comparable to, and sometimes better than, that achieved with ZDI using individual Fe II lines. Imposing a current-free poloidal constraint, which the input field satisfies, only helps where the unconstrained Stokes IV inversion performs poorly. Cross-talk between magnetic and abundance reconstructions is weak, with spurious inhomogeneities at or below 0.1 dex on average. Modern ZDI robustly reconstructs fossil magnetic fields in early-type stars, including their smaller-scale non-dipolar features, particularly when full Stokes information is available.

authors.name: O. Kochukhov, A. Al Kanale, J. Braithwaite

papers.title: Revisiting the Einstein Cross with X-shooter spectra: New estimates of accretion disk parameters and broad emission line profiles from microlensing
papers.summary: We present a spectroscopic study of the lensed quasar Q2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, assessing the best wavelength coverage to date with the X-shooter instrument (from $3000$ to $20000$ $\mathring{A}$), and thus improving the available spectroscopic data for this system. Using as a reference the characteristic emission lines for each quasar macro-image, we estimate the chromatic microlensing effect between pairs of images and calculate the extinction curve, confirming no significant differences between spectra $C$ and $A$ caused by extinction in the lens galaxy. In addition, we model the accretion disk characterized by a temperature profile with logarithmic slope $1/p$ and size $r_{s}$, assuming a thin-disk model with a power-law function of the form $r_{s}$ $\propto$ $\lambda^{p}$. To do this, we calculated a set of three chromatic microlensing measurements compiling previous estimates from the literature to test the wavelength dependence. This temperature profile was also compared to the canonical thin-disk model with $p=4/3$. Finally, we estimated the likelihood between the disk model and the observed data collected from multiple epochs through mock microlensing magnification maps and determined the probability density functions of each parameter from a Bayesian analysis. As a result, our estimated values for the accretion disk size and its exponential index are $r_{s}=4.9^{+2.3}_{-2.6}$ $\sqrt{M/0.3M_{\odot}}$ (lt-day) and $p=0.77^{+0.47}_{-0.28}$, respectively, reinforcing a departure from the standard accretion disk model ($ T \propto r_s^{-3/4}$).

authors.name: R. Jerez-Nicurcar, A. Esteban-Guti\'errez, V. Motta, E. Mediavilla

papers.title: The Connection between Halo Assembly History and the Stellar Distribution II: A Radially Stratified Fossil Record of Past Halo Mass
papers.summary: The spatial stellar distribution in massive central galaxies preserves a stratified fossil record of their host halos' assembly history. Using a halo-mass-complete sample from the IllustrisTNG-300 hydrodynamical simulation at $z=0.4$, we quantify this connection with two diagnostics. The fossil correlation $\tilde{\rho}(z)$ measures how strongly a present-day galaxy property retains information about the progenitor halo mass at each redshift. The rank retention fraction $f_{\rm ret}(z)$ measures how many halos selected by that property today were among the most massive halos at each epoch. The central stellar mass at different galactocentric radii exhibits non-monotonic fossil correlations with past halo mass, peaking at intermediate redshifts that systematically shift from $z\sim1$ in the inner regions to $z\sim0.7$ in the outer stellar halos. These peak redshifts are robust from group to cluster scales. Partial correlations with halo accretion rate show that each peak marks the end of the epoch when that component's buildup was sensitive to halo accretion. The rank retention fraction shows that the annular stellar masses of the central galaxy beyond 10 kpc are less biased tracers of the most massive halos at intermediate redshifts than richness. This stratified fossil record originates mainly from the ex-situ phase of galaxy assembly. The outer stellar halo also traces the satellite population at intermediate redshift better than present-day richness. These results establish that the stellar profile of massive central galaxies encodes a radially stratified fossil record of halo assembly history.

authors.name: Shuo Xu, Song Huang, Conghao Zhou, Alexie Leauthaud, Benedikt Diemer

papers.title: Long before plunge: Uncovering intermediate-mass black holes through their inspiralling compact object companions with LISA
papers.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will provide novel capability to discover and study intermediate-mass (~$10^2-10^5 M_\odot$) black holes at the centres of dwarf galaxies and in dense stellar environments. We systematically map out the LISA-detectable parameter space of binaries consisting of a low-mass compact object spiralling into an intermediate-mass black hole (mass ratio ~$10^{-5} - 10^{-2}$) on equatorial orbits with generic eccentricity. The depth of the LISA survey reaches a redshift ~$5$ ($0.1$) for binaries with a primary black hole mass $m_1$ ~$10^4 M_\odot$ ($10^3 M_\odot$). If the orbital companion is a white dwarf, which could be disrupted prior to plunge, LISA's survey depth is well matched to (and, in many cases, exceeds) the one of electro-magnetic surveys. Although the maximum distance at which a source can be detected depends weakly on the orbital eccentricity, the latter strongly affects the portion of the binary inspiral over which a source is detectable. The instrument's sensitivity time-volume varies by many orders of magnitude depending on the binary's component masses: it reaches ~$1 - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$ (~$10^{-2} - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$) for the more massive systems with $m_1 = 10^5 M_\odot$ ($10^4 M_\odot$) and decreases to ~$10^{-4} - 1 Gpc^3 yr$ for lighter primary black holes with $m_1 = 10^3 M_\odot$. Importantly, from tens of percent to the overwhelming majority of the total sensitivity time-volume (and therefore number of potential detections) comes from sources that do not plunge during the yr-long mission lifetime and are observed at an earlier stage of their inspiral. Despite the poorly known merger rates of this class of sources, our results show that LISA could identify from a handful to ~$10^3$ intermediate-mass black holes providing a new observational avenue for studying these elusive objects and the environments in which they reside.

authors.name: Jean Maurice Meus, Christian Chapman-Bird, Alberto Vecchio

papers.title: ALMA detection of continuum emission from GQ Lup B
papers.summary: GQ Lup B is a massive (10-40 M$_{\text{Jup}}$) companion orbiting the young T-Tauri star GQ Lup A at a projected distance of $\sim$110 au (0.7''). It is outside the circumprimary disk in the submm continuum, but its ${\sim}\,63^\circ$ inclined orbit intersects the primary's gas disk twice per period. We report a 5.8$\sigma$ detection of continuum emission at the location of GQ Lup B, obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.89 mm (band 7). We associate this emission with a dusty disk around the companion, already detected by VLT/NACO and JWST/MIRI in the mid-Infrared. To date, this is the third disk observed at mm wavelengths around a companion spanning the brown dwarf and planetary mass regimes, following PDS 70 c, a gas giant embedded in the parent circumstellar disk, and SR 12 c, a planetary-mass companion at 1200 au from the primary. We retrieve a point source with peak intensity $54.5\pm9.4\,\mu\rm Jy\, beam^{-1}$, co-spatial with GRAVITY astrometry. The emission is spatially unresolved, placing an upper limit on the source radius of 2.3 au (from a synthesized beam of $\sim\,29\times25$ mas). For comparison, this is smaller than 1/3 of the Hill's radius (3-5 au for GQ Lup B, depending on the assumed mass), the theoretical upper limit for circum-planetary disks. Assuming optically thin thermal emission from mm-size grains in a disk-like structure, we infer a mass of 0.0032 M$_\oplus$, while the optically thick limit yields an emission radius of 0.2 au. Assuming a gas to dust ratio of 100, our results indicate a very low disk mass to accretion rate ratio, of the order of $\sim10^4$ years, analogously to the highest accretors in the stellar mass regime. In the case of GQ Lup B, this can be explained by its periodic crossings of the circumprimary disk, which could deliver a substantial amount of gas to the companion's disk over a long timescale.

authors.name: Pietro Pirola, Stefano Facchini, Gabriele Cugno, Myriam Benisty, Tomas Stolker, Jaehan Bae, Ruobing Dong, Brendan P. Bowler, Ya-Lin Wu, Richard Teague, Pietro Curone, Felipe Alarcon

papers.title: Binary pulsar studies with multi-wavelength sky surveys. II. Companion star follow ups
papers.summary: The identification of the stellar companions to binary pulsars and the extraction of the physical information encoded in their optical spectra are key to study the evolution of the binary system and how this is influenced by the interactions between the two stars. Obviously, extending the characterisation of the companion star spectra over an as large as possible wavelength range allows one to maximise the amount of information. In Paper I, we used 11 source catalogues built upon multi-wavelength (optical, infrared, ultraviolet) imaging sky surveys to search for the stellar companions of 144 field binary pulsars (i.e. not in Globular Clusters) selected from the Australia Telescope National Facility (ATNF) pulsar catalogue. For nine of these pulsars, for which the companion star had been already identified, we obtained new spectral information from imaging photometry in the surveys' bands. In particular, for some of these pulsars we provided the first possible detections of the companion star in either the ultraviolet or mid-infrared. Here, we serve this additional flux information as a base to update the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the companion stars and the multi-epoch catalogue photometry to look for flux modulation at the orbital period of the binary system.

authors.name: R. P. Mignani (INAF/IASF-Milan, University of Zielona Gora), C. Pallanca (University of Bologna), V. Testa (INAF/OAR), A. Corongiu (INAF/OAC)

papers.title: Long-term average collision frequencies between two bodies undergoing Lidov-Kozai evolution
papers.summary: The existing {\"O}pik-type collision frequency framework that accounts for the projectile's Lidov-Kozai (LK) secular evolution holds the target's semimajor axis, eccentricity, and inclination fixed and prescribes uniform precession of its longitude of the ascending node and argument of periapsis. This treatment is not readily applicable when the target's eccentricity, inclination, or orbital precession rates undergo appreciable secular variations. Here, we extend the framework of Liang and Liu (2026, arXiv:2608.30972) to address one such case, in which both the projectile and target undergo LK evolution. Using a doubly averaged quadrupole model to describe the secular dynamics of both bodies, we include the target's orbital evolution when evaluating the collision contribution of each orbital intersection configuration. In the numerical example considered, the projectile survival curve predicted using the calculated collision frequency shows an overall decay trend close to that obtained from direct N-body simulations using REBOUND. In addition, we examine whether the long-term mean collision frequency depends on initial states while holding both bodies' semimajor axes, Kozai constants and closed Hamiltonian level curves fixed. Our theoretical analysis indicates that this frequency is independent of initial states when the parameters describing their relative state are jointly equidistributed at the start of successive projectile LK cycles. Numerical cases with different initial states support this conclusion.

authors.name: Youpeng Liang, Xiaodong Liu

papers.title: Kinematic Signatures of Stellar Flybys in Protoplanetary Discs
papers.summary: Recent high-resolution molecular line observations of protoplanetary discs have revealed large-scale non-Keplerian features in the gas kinematics of several systems, which can be interpreted as signatures of warps in the disc. Warps can arise from a range of physical mechanisms, and it remains unclear whether the observed kinematic residuals can be uniquely attributed to warping, or to different competing effects. Stellar flybys are one such mechanism capable of both warping a disc and directly perturbing its kinematics. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we study the evolution of protoplanetary discs perturbed by inclined and coplanar stellar flybys, focusing on timescales of several thousand years after periastron rather than the immediate aftermath of the encounter. We find that inclined stellar flybys initially induce warping and twisting in the disc, but that this geometric perturbation is damped on a timescale set by the disc viscosity. Despite this geometric damping, synthetic ALMA observations of the CO kinematics show that complex non-Keplerian spiral features persist in the velocity residuals long after the warped morphology has relaxed, including in coplanar encounters where no warp is ever induced. Fitting these residuals with a simple warped-disc model, the degree of warping in the disc is systematically overestimated. We therefore conclude that kinematic residuals alone are insufficient to establish that a disc is warped, as flybys induce kinematic complexity independently of warps. We further show that scattered light observations provide an independent diagnostic, showing spiral arms and lateral asymmetries.

authors.name: Vasundhara Prasad, Cristiano Longarini, Carolin N. Kimmig, Cathie J. Clarke

papers.title: BAO and Type Ia Supernovae in LTB Cosmology: Constraints on Radial Inhomogeneity and Acoustic-Ruler Evolution
papers.summary: We investigate how baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia supernovae constrain radial density profiles and acoustic-ruler evolution in Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) cosmology with a cosmological constant. Extending a homogeneous Friedmann-Robertson-Walker analysis requires calculating both distances and unequal radial and transverse stretching of a single initial ruler. Combining transverse BAO with supernovae isolates relative ruler evolution without an absolute calibration, while radial BAO supplies complementary information. We connect this test to exact nonlinear models with a low-density region compensated by surrounding excess matter, varying its depth, width, distance from the observer, and background matter density. Using DESI DR2 BAO and DES-Dovekie supernovae with full covariance and identical calibration freedom, the LTB fit improves $\chi^2$ by 8.523 over flat $\Lambda$CDM for three additional parameters, mainly through the supernovae. DESI strongly rejects the particular deep profile favored by supernovae and angular BAO alone. However, a narrow depression near the observer and a broader, shallower depression farther away fit almost equally well, with $\Delta\chi^2=0.647$. The combined data therefore constrain particular geometries without uniquely reconstructing the density profile or ruler evolution.
