The inference is conditional on supernova selection and interpreting released BAO summaries through local ruler transport at effective redshifts. Homogeneous simulations show that the fit improvement does not establish a detection of inhomogeneity. Finally, in the local approximation, common LTB ruler evolution shifts angular BAO and the transverse component of three-dimensional BAO together and cannot alone explain their discrepancy.

authors.name: Myrto Magklara, Leandros Perivolaropoulos

papers.title: The Neptunian ridge depends on the choice of linear or logarithmic period
papers.summary: The Neptunian ridge has been reported as an overdensity of planets with radii of $\simeq$5-8 R$_\oplus$ and orbital periods of $\simeq$3-6 d, located between the Neptunian desert and the savanna. It was first identified in Kepler data and has recently been reanalysed using our TESS occurrence rates, where it appears as an approximately twofold excess relative to neighbouring regions. We show that the reported excess arises from expressing the occurrence density per unit period, $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}P$, rather than per unit logarithmic period, $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}\ln P$, where the logarithmic form is standard in planet demographics. Because the savanna interval used for comparison is twice as wide in period as the ridge, a population uniform in $\ln P$ naturally produces a factor-of-two contrast in $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}P$. When expressed per unit $\ln P$, the published TESS and Kepler ridge-to-savanna contrasts decrease from 1.6-2.2 to 0.8-1.2, all consistent with unity. A simulated population with a desert but no intrinsic excess reproduces the appearance of a ridge in $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}P$ precisely. Reanalysing the TESS-SPOC occurrence rates of 5.5-8.5 R$_\oplus$ planets around FGK stars, we find a ridge-to-savanna ratio of $0.91^{+0.21}_{-0.16}$ per unit $\ln P$, which does not support the claimed overdensity at the ridge. Taken together, these tests imply that the published ridge is a result of the scale choice used, rather than a definitive property of the observed planet population.

authors.name: Kaiming Cui, David J. Armstrong

papers.title: A Many-Shapes framework for Galactic Cosmic Rays
papers.summary: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. These measurements reveal that both spectra do not have a simple power--law form, and exhibit several features. The proton to helium ratio exhibits a very unexpected behavior: it decreases for rigidities $\lesssim 10^5$~GV, and increases for higher rigidities. Several authors have interpreted the observed spectral features as revealing the fact the CR spectra are formed by the contributions of a few components (in some cases as few as two) produced by sources that belong to distinct classes of astrophysical accelerators, with sources in the same class producing spectra with the same characteristic shape. Most of these authors also consider it necessary to include the contribution of one (or perhaps more than one) ``local'' sources, recently active in the vicinity of the solar system. However, this approach has several limitations, and in this work we discuss an alternative scenario in which the cosmic ray sources, even belonging to the same class, produce spectra with a broad range of shapes. The power--law form of the total source spectrum emerges as the average of these contributions. In this framework observable spectral features can be produced by statistical fluctuations, and different spectral slopes for protons and helium nuclei can be observed even if one assumes that acceleration is rigidity-dependent.

authors.name: Paolo Lipari

papers.title: The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
papers.summary: Previous work found a higher bulk iron-to-silicon (Fe/Si) ratio in rocky exoplanets relative to their host star, traditionally explained by iron enrichment. An alternative explanation is devolatilization of the planetary abundance ratios with respect to the host star, where volatile elements such as O and S are progressively depleted compared to refractory elements such as Fe and Mg, as in Earth. We explore whether these elemental molar ratios are consistent with a devolatilization trend. We revisit the core mass fraction of 14 rocky exoplanets with masses between 0.5 and 10 Earth masses whose host stars have spectroscopic abundances of Fe, Si, Mg, O, and S in the literature. We use interior structure retrievals with two independent forward models, the Marseille Super-Earth Interior model and pyExoInt, to estimate compositional parameters, including elemental molar ratios, from mass and radius measurements. We find that 8 out of 14 exoplanets in our sample present an Earth-like devolatilization trend, while only one planet shows a 1:1 relationship between planetary and stellar abundances. This suggests that devolatilization offers a plausible explanation for the observed non-1:1 relation. The two interior models agree on the devolatilization trend, demonstrating that our derived trends are robust. The main limiting factor in constraining refractory compositions of rocky planets relative to their host star is the small sample with constrained stellar abundances and the lack of variety in orbital distances. The PLATO mission will help by extending the sample of characterized rocky planets to orbital periods of up to one year. The variety in refractory elemental ratio trends may indicate a wide diversity in bulk composition, outgassing and other mantle properties relevant for habitability.

authors.name: Yared Reinarz, Lorena Acu\~na-Aguirre, Haiyang S. Wang

papers.title: Investigating the timescales traced by dynamical ages in young stellar systems
papers.summary: Stars form in clustered environments, and then the stars may congregate into star clusters. The timescale on which individual stars form is not necessarily the same as the timescale on which star clusters assemble. Therefore, developing methods to probe these different timescales is a crucial part of understanding star cluster assembly and early evolution. Dynamical ages can be constructed from the kinematics of individual stars in clusters in the solar neighborhood using Gaia data. Using a star formation simulation, we test five different dynamical age methods. We divide dynamical ages into two approaches: methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster, and methods which trace the trajectories of individual stars. We confirm that size methods cannot accurately derive ages in bound clusters whereas methods tracing individual stars can be applied to both bound and unbound systems. We find that different dynamical age methods trace different epochs of star cluster formation and assembly: The method using stars with the oldest traceback ages provides an upper limit on stellar ages and the method using the median traceback ages is the best proxy for isochronal ages. Methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster best trace the onset of cluster expansion. Our work suggests that the median traceback time of stars moving away from the cluster provides the most reliable proxy for isochronal age, and that this method can be applied to any expanding system.

authors.name: Isabella Armstrong, Alison Sills, Claude Cournoyer-Cloutier

papers.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.summary: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). The final ray-traced spectrum, computed through photoionization code with Comptonization, accounts for both: emitted and reflected components. As a result, the strength of the SXE depends on the radial extend of the warm corona, i.e., its outer edge. We show that the radial transition from warm corona to disk atmosphere is governed by line cooling. By moving away from a central black hole Compton cooling is gradually replaced by line cooling, and the temperature drops sharply in vertical direction at a narrow iron ionization front, where iron ions Fe \textsc{xxv}--Fe \textsc{xxvi} recombine to Fe \textsc{xvii}. Notably, this transition takes place at a particular value of internal heating $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-23}$ erg cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$, regardless of the Eddington ratio. We show, that at the given metal abundance, the SXE emitting area is larger for a higher accretion rate, in agreement with recent findings in changing look AGN. The overall emission spectrum from a warm corona is featureless, and the only iron K$_{\alpha}$ line comes from a reflection. The line is stronger and more gravitationally distorted for a lower accretion rate, which is a direct result of the size of the warm corona. Furthermore, by increasing the iron abundance, the iron ionization front moves closer towards black hole, and a stronger iron line complex is emitted locally.

authors.name: Parikshit Partha Biswas, Agata R\'o\.za\'nska, Debora Lan\v{c}ov\'a, Dominik Gronkiewicz, Rafa{\l} Wojaczy\'nski, Andrzej Zdziarski, Stefano Bianchi

papers.title: Three-dimensional radiative transfer modeling of the scattering polarization in the solar H$\alpha$ line
papers.summary: The H$\alpha$ line probes the solar chromosphere, but its scattering polarization is difficult to interpret because of magnetic fields, plasma motions, and atmospheric 3D inhomogeneities. We investigate its intensity and linear polarization in a 3D magnetohydrodynamic solar-atmosphere model including nonequilibrium hydrogen ionization. Using PORTA, we solve the full 3D non-LTE polarized radiative transfer problem for a multilevel hydrogen atom, accounting for atomic polarization, Hanle depolarization, horizontal radiative transfer, and macroscopic velocities. We degrade synthetic Stokes profiles to the spatial, spectral, and polarimetric resolution of ZIMPOL observations for direct comparison. The modeled center-to-limb variation follows the observed trend, with comparable polarization amplitudes. The profiles show large spatial variability from symmetry breaking by horizontal inhomogeneities and atmospheric dynamics, as well as diverse line-core asymmetries. Classifying $Q/I$ profiles by asymmetry reveals a statistical correlation between profile morphology and magnetic-field strength in the H$\alpha$ formation region, consistent with Hanle depolarization: multi-peaked profiles favor stronger fields, whereas asymmetric single-peaked profiles favor weaker fields with smaller vertical strength variations. Thus, H$\alpha$ scattering polarization reflects the interplay of magnetic fields, velocity gradients, and 3D radiative transfer. Our results highlight the need for 3D modeling to interpret H$\alpha$ spectropolarimetry and its potential to diagnose chromospheric magnetism and dynamics.

authors.name: Jaume Jaume Bestard, Jiri Stepan, Javier Trujillo Bueno

papers.title: The Swift/UVOT Observation Campaign of Comet C/2013 US10 (Catalina) and Near-nucleus UV Excess
papers.summary: We present results of a multi-wavelength extended monitoring campaign of dynamically new long-period comet C/2013 US$_{10}$ (Catalina), captured with the Ultraviolet and Optical Telescope (UVOT) on board the Swift spacecraft covering 5.8 AU inbound to 5 AU outbound. The pipeline and methodology developed for these results is introduced, along with derived water production rates, active areas, and dust content proxy $A(\theta)f\rho$. We describe a Bayesian solution to address the unknown spectral gradient $S'$ of the dust of C/2013 US$_{10}$ necessary for our continuum subtraction calculations. The comet exhibited significant hyperactivity, with the water production rate approaching $2.5 \times 10^{29}$/s and a greatly elevated active area pre-perihelion, settling to approximately 50 km$^2$ post-perihelion. We also report and quantify a near-nucleus UV excess beyond vectorial model predictions, a feature we have dubbed the Pale Blue Spot (PBS), and cover possible candidate species responsible. When interpreted as OH (A-X) band fluorescence, the PBS may point to a secondary release mechanism producing slow-moving hydroxyl radicals that is active even beyond the water snow line.

authors.name: Shawn Oset, Zexi Xing, John Wm. Noonan, Steven J. Bromley, Dennis Bodewits

papers.title: Testing Models of Disk Formation and Gravito-Viscous Evolution Against Observations of Young Protoplanetary Disks
papers.summary: Young protoplanetary disks have received increasing attention in recent years, due to observations revealing the presence of substructures in disks younger than one million years, suggesting that planet formation may begin earlier than previously thought. Other recent observations have provided new insights into the evolution of gas and dust in these early stages, enabling comparisons with evolved Class II disks. Yet the physical processes governing the earliest stages of disk evolution remain poorly understood. In this paper, we present two-dimensional thin-disk hydrodynamical simulations of the formation and early evolution of protoplanetary disks, under the influence of self-gravity and turbulent viscosity alone. We explore various properties of disks forming from the collapse of clouds with a range of initial masses and we compare our results with surveys of protoplanetary disks across multiple evolutionary stages. Our simulations broadly reproduce key observational constraints, including the mm fluxes of Class 0 disks and the dust disk radii of later stages. However, our models do not explain the observed gas and dust disk masses of Class I and II disks: while they account for the most massive observed disks, they fail to reproduce the least massive ones. We discuss that simulations incorporating the influence of the star-forming environment might be needed to resolve this discrepancy.

authors.name: Fabiola Antonietta Gerosa, Paola Pinilla, Eduard I. Vorobyov, James McKevitt

papers.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
papers.summary: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges. We model a possible underlying magnetar contribution to the unabsorbed 0.3--10~keV XRT flux over 80--430~s, evolving the spin under fallback-disk and electromagnetic torques. A descriptive estimate gives $P_0\simeq4.25$~ms, $B\simeq3.04\times10^{15}$~G and source-frame $t_{\rm fb}\simeq143$~s, with exploratory temporal-block uncertainty ranges. The effective efficiency reaches its geometry-dependent ceiling of 81.2. At observer time 200~s, this realization has $P_*\simeq4.82$~ms and magnetospheric, corotation and light-cylinder radii $r_{\rm m}\simeq235$~km, $r_{\rm co}\simeq48$~km and $r_{\rm LC}\simeq230$~km. It is on the ejector branch; light-cylinder entry near 255~s initiates negative propeller torque and steepens the decline. The smooth component declines throughout the fitted interval; additional variable emission contributes to the observed maximum near 180~s. A correlated-residual Bayesian analysis permits a fainter component and broader dynamical histories, with median $P_0=16.8$~ms and central 68 per cent interval 2.76--286~ms. However, posterior predictive checks reveal that this statistical description typically underpredicts the observed flux level and variability, limiting its physical interpretation. Fallback-modified magnetar activity remains a possible descriptive scenario, but these analyses do not establish a unique underlying component or robust constraints on the initial spin and disk-interaction history. We also discuss Lense-Thirring precession and alternative mechanisms as possible origins of the early X-ray variability.

authors.name: Nissim Fraija, Simone Dichiara, Antonio Galv\'an

papers.title: {\AA}ngstr\"om Exponent Calculation Using Wide-Field Stellar Photometry
papers.summary: The FRAM (F/Photometric Robotic Atmospheric Monitor) telescopes can measure the aerosol extinction at optical wavelengths using wide-field stellar photometry at the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) sites. The Angstrom exponent describes the wavelength dependence of aerosol extinction. In this work we extend the FRAM method from a single $B$-filter (440 nm) analysis using the Tycho-2 catalogue to a simultaneous three-filter analysis in $B$, $V$, and $R$ (440, 540, and 620 nm) using Gaia DR3 synthetic photometry, which provides photometry directly in the Johnson--Cousins system without passband transformations. The exponent is derived from the vertical aerosol optical depth (VAOD) for the B--V, V--R, and B--R filter pairs at three sites over 2021--2022. The multi-filter VAOD shows a systematic filter-dependent ordering that is inconsistent with physical expectation and produces negative exponents. It is not currently possible to determine which filter yields the correct VAOD, and none of the four processing configurations we tested resolves the ordering. We introduce an intercept correction as a practical remedy that yields physically plausible exponents. At the two southern Paranal sites (CTAO-S0 and CTAO-S1) the exponent distributions are unimodal, with mean $\alpha \approx 0.84$ (B--V) and $0.65$ (B--R) at CTAO-S0 and $0.60$ and $0.41$ at CTAO-S1. At CTAO-N (La Palma) the distributions are bimodal, with $\alpha \approx 0.2$ (B--V) during episodic Saharan dust intrusions and $\alpha \approx 1.3$ under clean background conditions. AERONET sun-photometer measurements on the dates common to both instruments show the same two populations, providing qualitative support for the FRAM method.

authors.name: Shefali Negi, Jan Ebr, Sergey Karpov, Ji\v{r}\'i Eli\'a\v{s}ek

papers.title: The Cool Circumgalactic Echo of the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relatio
papers.summary: The stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR), a key prediction of galaxy formation models, peaks at $M_* \sim 3 \times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$. This scale is often attributed to circumgalactic baryonic feedback processes, however, direct observational evidence linking the two remains scarce. Using Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) galaxy--quasar pairs, we map the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) using Mg II $\lambda\lambda2796, 2803$ absorption with stacking technique across nearly three decades in stellar mass. The radial Mg II absorption equivalent-width profile, $W_{\rm MgII} \propto D^k$, becomes progressively shallower with increasing stellar mass, following $k = 0.70\log(M_*/M_\odot)-9.12$. Crucially, we find that the $W_{\rm MgII}$ in the CGM scales tightly with the SHMR. The $W_{\rm MgII}$ peaks at the same characteristic mass as the SHMR, coinciding with a transition of the cool CGM from super-virial to sub-virial kinematics. Low-mass halos show excess non-gravitational motions consistent with recycled accretion and feedback-driven circulation, whereas massive halos show halo-centric heating that may maintain star formation quenching. This study bridges the gap between cool CGM and SHMR, showing that peak star formation efficiency coincides with the most abundant cool CGM reservoirs.

authors.name: Zeyu Chen, Enci Wang, Huiyuan Wang, Houjun Mo, Luis C. Ho, Haoran Yu, Zhijie Qu, Hu Zou, Siwei Zou, Zhicheng He, Cheqiu Lyu, Chengyu Ma, Weiwen Kong

papers.title: Coupled dark energy and apparent phantom crossing: a potential-independent lower bound
papers.summary: Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernovae, prefer a dark energy whose equation of state was below $-1$ in the past and is above $-1$ today. A canonical scalar field cannot cross this line, but it can appear to do so if it is coupled to dark matter, and we ask how strong this coupling must be, for any potential. We show that the apparent crossing requires the dark matter to lose a minimum fraction of its mass after recombination, fixed by the expansion history $H(z)$. For a constant coupling $\beta=d\ln m/d\phi$, the mass can change only as fast as the field moves, and the speed of the field is itself set by $H(z)$, so that the coupling must be larger than a minimum value $\beta_{\rm min}[H(z)]$. This bound holds for any potential, applies to the largest value of the coupling when the coupling depends on the field, and is reached exactly when the field comes to rest within the observed range. For the DESI DR2 best fits, the dark matter must lose about 5-7% of its mass by $z\simeq 0.8$, which requires $\beta_{\rm min}=0.047$-$0.058$; including the uncertainties of the data, the public DESI DR2 chains give the 95% lower limit $|\beta|>0.025$-$0.038$. We also apply the bound to published fits of coupled quintessence: all of them respect it, and those with a constant coupling reproduce only a shallow version of the crossing. Since the coupling cannot be smaller than $\beta_{\rm min}$, two known effects of the coupling have a minimum size: an extra attraction between dark matter particles of at least a few tenths of a per cent of gravity, and a lensing signal at least a few per cent weaker than the clustering of dark matter would suggest.

authors.name: Domenico Sapone, Esteban Arratia

papers.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
papers.summary: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

authors.name: Akira Dohi, Keita Izumi, Asuka Ito, Emanuele Greco, Marco Miceli, Salvatore Orlando, Shigehiro Nagataki

papers.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion
papers.summary: To understand the process of planet formation in the Solar System or any other stellar system, we need to comprehend the interaction between forming planets and the protoplanetary disk. This work presents a study of the interaction of the protoplanetary disk with the protoplanet and the following types of orbital migration that can occur, and to verify this interaction, numerical simulations were performed using the magneto-hydrodynamics code FARGO3D. The researchers made five simulations with a 2-Jupiter-mass planet in the protoplanetary disk. The only parameter varied was the initial radial position with the aim of verifying the influence of this parameter on the behavior of planetary migration. As a result of these simulations, we find that the initial radial coordinate is a very significant parameter in how the planet interacts with the gas in the disk and the formation of gas gaps.

authors.name: Fabian Menezes

papers.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
papers.summary: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. We use the "G23H" catalog to fit a model that incorporates absolute astrometry constraints from Hipparcos, Gaia DR2, and Gaia DR3, as well as Gaia DR3 photometry, excess RV variability, and includes information from the presence or absence of common-proper motion companions. The resulting posteriors can be used directly to detect new companions, to target RV and imaging follow-up observations, and for downstream demographics studies. We highlight example detections of known and new candidate companions and the companion detection rate across the HR diagram. The modelling approach we present is directly applicable to Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry and RVs. All posteriors are provided as a machine-readable catalog and user-accessible website http://exopo.st/.

authors.name: William Thompson, Dori Blakely, Alexandre Bouchard-C\^ot\'e, Trevor Campbell, Jerry Xuan, Jingwen Zhang, Kyle Franson, Jessica Speedie, Clarissa Do \'O, Doug Johnstone, Eric Nielsen, Brendan Bowler, Simon Blouin, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, Ryan Cloutier, Andre Fogal, Kaitlyn Hessel, Christian Marois, Alexandra Rochon, William Roberson

papers.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
papers.summary: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. In A1795, AGN feedback dominates the velocity dispersion in the core, similar to Perseus, and may provide turbulent heating at a rate comparable to radiative cooling. In contrast, we obtain only an upper limit on the AGN feedback contribution in A2029, where merger-driven motions dominate. Tailored simulations indicate that an off-axis minor merger $\simeq1.6$ Gyr ago displaced the central low-entropy gas in A2029, potentially suppressing AGN activity. This gas is now returning to the center, possibly facilitating the re-establishment of AGN feedback. We propose an evolutionary view of the double-cascade scenario, in which merger-driven motions dominate during and shortly after significant mergers, while feedback-driven turbulence re-emerges in cluster cores as systems relax. This framework provides a basis for interpreting XRISM kinematic measurements of (weak) cool-core clusters. Our findings highlight the importance of spatially resolved gas kinematics and detailed modeling for identifying double-cascade features and disentangling the contributions of AGN feedback and mergers.

authors.name: Congyao Zhang, Eugene Churazov, Irina Zhuravleva, Hannah McCall, Annie Heinrich, William R. Forman, Ildar Khabibullin, Michal Zaja\v{c}ek, Norbert Werner

papers.title: Forward modeling linear variable filter data: High resolution PAH and Paschen-$\alpha$ maps from SPHEREx
papers.summary: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission is a powerful tool for the study of the interstellar medium (ISM) in both Galactic and extragalactic contexts. It can reveal ionization state, radiation field, metallicity, composition, and ISM structure as sculpted by processes like turbulence and stellar feedback. Here we use NASA's SPHEREx to produce clean, high-resolution PAH maps at spectral resolution R $\sim$ 35 (compared to WISE at R $\sim$ 2). Prior treatments of the SPHEREx linear variable filter data seek to convert them to more conventional band-averaged maps that can leave striping artifacts associated with spatially variable wavelength sampling, especially at emission lines. In contrast, we deliver a scalable forward-modeling method capable of generating high-quality all-sky SPHEREx emission-line maps at 8.5 arcsec FWHM angular resolution (on 6.4 arcsec pixels), while naturally producing maps without visible striping. We reformat the data into a pixel-level database, mask stellar contamination, and infill missing pixels with a conditional, data-driven, anisotropic Gaussian process. We apply our method to produce 3.3 $\mu$m and 3.4 $\mu$m PAH and Paschen-$\alpha$ emission maps of a set of fields spanning a range of Galactic and extragalactic conditions including the Rosette nebula, the Corona Australis molecular cloud, M33, and M31. We demonstrate the quality and synergies of our SPHEREx 3.3 $\mu$m PAH maps by comparisons with other available gas and dust tracer maps and achieve sensitivities up to $\sigma(I_{3.3}) = 2.7 \times 10^{-8}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$. We estimate that a two-year extension of the SPHEREx survey, with modest modifications to the scanning strategy, would match or exceed the PAH sensitivity of WISE over the whole sky.

authors.name: Andrew K. Saydjari, Connor Hainje, Benjamin Dodge, Philipp Frank, David W. Hogg, Susan E. Clark

papers.title: The Tierras Observatory: Ultra-Precise Photometry for Characterizing Exoplanets and Their Host Stars
papers.summary: The Tierras Observatory is a fully robotic 1.3-m telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona. Tierras achieves sub-part-per-thousand (ppt) photometric precision on two timescales: intra-night, to detect and characterize transits of planets around nearby mid-to-late M dwarfs, and night-to-night across an observing season, to characterize the long-term variability of their host stars. We describe the facility and instrument design, our photometric pipeline, and our on-sky performance. We present the first ground-based light curves with sub-ppt precision over timescales of months. This precision enables a range of exoplanet-related science, including the measurement of host star rotation periods, the detection of long-period transits, and the discovery of additional terrestrial planets in known M dwarf systems.

authors.name: Juliana Garc\'ia-Mej\'ia, Patrick Tamburo, David Charbonneau, Daniel Fabricant, Jonathan M. Irwin, Robert Fata, Joseph M. Zajac, Peter E. Doherty, Brian McLeod, Pascal Fortin, Michael L. Calkins, Gilbert A. Esquerdo

papers.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
papers.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. For galaxy halos within 50 Mpc, we measure a mean DM excess of $119\pm44$ pc~cm$^{-3}$ $(p = 0.0053; \sim 2.6\sigma)$ within one virial radius. Expanding to 150 Mpc (628 intersections), we find a tentative decline in the mean DM as a function of impact parameter $(p = 0.0046; \sim 2.6\sigma)$, which is predominantly driven by typical Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies $(10 \leq \log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq 11)$. We use this DM profile to constrain parameters of the CGM electron density distribution, $n_e^\mathrm{CGM}(r) \propto r^{-3\beta}$, finding an extrapolated central electron density in the range of $(1.7-21.1) \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{\,cm}^{-3}$, with a radial power-law index of $\beta = 0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$, consistent with constraints from X-ray stacking studies of MW-like galaxies. At very low impact parameters, we detect a significant DM deficit likely due to cross-matching FRBs that originate from galaxies within our galaxy sample. By deriving the DM-galaxy cross-correlation function, we show that this deficit matches theoretical predictions if 20 FRBs originate from galaxies within 150 Mpc, indicating that CHIME/FRB detects a higher fraction of low-$z$ FRBs than previously thought. We forecast that $10^4$ FRBs with similar localization errors will provide a 5-$\sigma$ detection of the CGM, and that FRBs at intermediate redshifts ($0.4\lesssim z_\mathrm{FRB}\lesssim 0.75$) are ideal for studying intervening CGMs.

authors.name: Affan Khadir, Ayush Pandhi, Jason Hessels, Calvin Leung, B. M. Gaensler, Ludwig M. B\"oss, Amanda M. Cook, Alice P. Curtin, Klaus Dolag, Naman Jain, Victoria Kaspi, Afrokk Khan, Adam E. Lanman, Kiyoshi W. Masui, Daniele Michilli, Mason Ng, Aaron B. Pearlman, Sachin Pradeep E. T., Aniket Prasad, Mawson Sammons, Paul Scholz, Kaitlyn Shin, Kendrick M. Smith, Jenny G. Sorce, Haochen Wang, Michele Woodland

papers.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
papers.summary: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded. Furthermore, we find a positive trend in occurrence with metallicity below the mass-ratio desert, but a negative trend above. The desert therefore separates two distinct populations, plausibly two formation channels, that each scale with stellar mass: the lightest stellar-like companions of K stars ($\sim13 \, M_{jup}$) are less massive than the heaviest planet-like companions of B stars ($\sim27, M_{jup}$), which continue well beyond the deuterium-burning limit. Mass-ratio, not mass, is therefore the physically meaningful boundary between planets and their stellar-like counterparts.

authors.name: William Thompson, Alexandre Bouchard-C\^ot\'e, Dori Blakely, Trevor Campbell, Jessica Speedie, Judah Van Zandt, Kyle Franson, Jerry Xuan, Doug Johnstone, Emma Turtleboom, Jingwen Zhang, Clarissa Do \'O, Brendan Bowler, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, Eric Nielsen, Ryan Cloutier, Andre Fogal, Kaitlyn Hessel, Christian Marois, Alexandra Rochon, William Roberson, Simon Blouin

papers.title: Constraining the white-dwarf mass in the intermediate polar IGR J17014-4306 using X-ray and optical spectroscopy
papers.summary: Intermediate polars (IPs), a subclass of magnetic cataclysmic variables, often show discrepancies between white-dwarf (WD) mass measurements from X-ray spectral modeling and optical dynamical studies. We investigate the IP IGR J17014-4306. We performed a joint spectral analysis of NuSTAR observations combined with archival XMM-Newton and Swift data, modeling the broad-band X-ray spectrum with a multi-temperature cooling-flow model. Additionally, we obtained time-resolved optical spectroscopy with the SOAR telescope to measure the radial velocity of the donor star and constrain the system's orbital parameters. The X-ray spectral analysis reveals a very high post-shock plasma temperature of $kT_{\max}=50_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{keV}$, corresponding to a WD mass of $M_{\mathrm{WD}}=0.94_{-0.07}^{+0.09}\,M_\odot$. We also fitted the NuSTAR spectrum above 10 keV with the ipolar30KK model, obtaining $M_{\mathrm{WD}}=0.88_{-0.12}^{+0.14}\,M_\odot$. Our optical spectroscopy yields a radial-velocity semi-amplitude for the companion star of $K_2=165\pm4\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and an optical mass function of $f(M)=0.249\pm0.018\,M_\odot$. Combined with the eclipse geometry and the WD mass estimate from the X-ray models, these results favor a high mass ratio, $0.76\lesssim q\lesssim0.95$, and a donor-star mass of approximately $0.67\lesssim M_2/M_\odot\lesssim0.89$. In the limiting case of $q=1$, the WD mass has an upper limit of $1.14\,M_\odot$. Together with the X-ray measurements, this indicates a relatively massive WD. The lack of an independent measurement of the WD dynamical mass leaves it unclear whether the dynamical mass is consistent with the X-ray measurements or whether the X-ray mass is underestimated, as has been found for other IPs. Thus, our constraints make IGR J17014-4306 an important system for improving our understanding of IPs.

authors.name: D. C. Souza, M. P. Diaz, A. S. Oliveira, G. J. M. Luna, C. V. Rodrigues, M. Reynolds, N. Palivanas, I. J. Lima, J. Miko{\l}ajewska, M. Orio

papers.title: Scalable early warning for binary neutron-star mergers in third-generation gravitational-wave detectors
papers.summary: Third-generation gravitational-wave observatories will observe binary neutron-star coalescences for hours before merger. Over these extended time windows, Earth's motion and the long signal durations make standard search methods computationally demanding for low-latency detection. We propose an approach based on short-time Fourier transforms and convolutional neural networks that implicitly marginalizes over extrinsic parameters, effectively reducing the search to the chirp mass. The network learns the signals' nonlinear time-frequency morphology, approximating the optimal Bayesian detection statistic. Using a large-scale campaign of simulated signal injections, we compare the network's performance with a GPU-optimized matched-filtering baseline for both the ET$\Delta$ and ET2L configurations of the Einstein Telescope and signal durations from approximately 25 minutes ($f_{\rm min} = 5$ Hz) to approximately 6 hours ($f_{\rm min} = 2$ Hz). The network achieves comparable detection sensitivity while reducing computational costs by over four orders of magnitude, bringing processing times from minutes to milliseconds. This efficiency paves the way for rapid early-warning alerts for multi-messenger astronomy in the third-generation detector era.

authors.name: Martin Gerini, Rodrigo Tenorio, Davide Gerosa

papers.title: Relativistic Simulations of Self-Gravitating Radiation Fluids
papers.summary: We present an approach for numerical simulations of pure radiation fluids within the general relativistic hydrodynamics framework. The approach models radiation as a self-gravitating perfect fluid with vanishing rest mass, enabling simulations of radiation fluids in strong-gravity spacetimes. Building on the existing relativistic hydrodynamics code Whisky, within the Einstein Toolkit framework, we introduce modifications to incorporate radiation fluids, including updates to the source terms, recovery scheme, and Riemann solvers. Modifications are validated using standard shock tube tests. We present results for radiation accretion onto a single black hole, as well as a photon star solution for radiation in unstable hydrostatic equilibrium, demonstrating both collapse and dispersion under perturbations.

authors.name: Bing-Jyun Tsao, Pablo Laguna, Octavio Guerrero

papers.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
papers.summary: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

authors.name: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Difan Yuan

papers.title: Pushing the accuracy of the quasi-circular baseline for the SEOBNR family of models
papers.summary: Gravitational-wave observations have opened a new era of astronomy, with accurate modeling of binary black hole signals becoming increasingly important for source characterization and astrophysical inference as detector sensitivities improve. We present SEOBNRv5iHM, an updated quasi-circular, aligned-spin inspiral-merger-ringdown gravitational-waveform model with higher-order modes, constructed within the effective-one-body formalism and building upon SEOBNRv5HM. The improvements mainly concern the late inspiral and the merger-ringdown: we remove the non-quasi-circular corrections used in previous models and instead introduce a phenomenological intermediate region between the inspiral and the ringdown, which allows the ringdown attachment time to be chosen independently for each mode, including at the peak of the mode's amplitude. The model is calibrated and validated against 591 quasi-circular aligned-spin waveforms from the third Simulating eXtreme Spacetimes catalog. For the $(2,2)$ mode, when considering the maximum unfaithfulness against numerical relativity over a total mass range of 10-300$M_\odot$, SEOBNRv5iHM achieves a median of $4.25\times10^{-5}$, a factor of 4.5 below SEOBNRv5HM, and a factor of 3-8 below other semi-analytical models, with $84\%$ of cases below $10^{-4}$. For $M\ge150 M_\odot$, the median drops to $9.7\times10^{-6}$, comparable to the numerical-relativity surrogate NRHybSur3dq8. For polarization mismatches at inclination $\pi/3$, with modes up to $\ell_\mathrm{max} = 5$, the median maximum unfaithfulness is $4.2\times10^{-4}$, a factor of 2.6 below SEOBNRv5HM, 1.9 below IMRPhenomTHM, and 6-11 below the other semi-analytical models. Since spin-precessing and eccentric models are built on top of the quasi-circular, aligned-spin baseline, these improvements will make future SEOBNR models more accurate, reducing waveform systematics in upcoming analyses.

authors.name: Cheng Foo, Alessandra Buonanno, H\'ector Estell\'es, Lorenzo Pompili

papers.title: Horizon-penetrating rotating black-hole configurations in VCDM
papers.summary: A regular black-hole metric need not define a regular configuration of VCDM, whose preferred foliation is part of the gravitational solution. We construct stationary rotating, possibly charged configurations on the constant-auxiliary Einstein-Maxwell branch. Their Kerr-Newman and Kerr-Newman-de Sitter geometries carry nonzero constant-mean-curvature foliations that cross the future black-hole horizon and, in the de Sitter case, the future cosmological horizon. A horizon-regular flux formulation specifies the inner data and the distinct hyperboloidal and expanding asymptotic ends. Seventeen survey configurations are supplemented by a mean-flux scan at fixed four-geometry and paired flat/de Sitter comparisons down to $\kappa M = 0.01$, where $K_0 = 3\kappa$. Varying the flux changes the preferred-foliation shear without changing the background seen by standard test matter. The paired local lapse and shear differences have effective powers close to two over the computed range, with the lapse comparison requiring a fixed time normalization. Continuous residuals, geometric reconstructions, and selected grid comparisons test the numerical solutions. An exact lapse bound excludes zeros in the regular stationary exterior block with $\Delta_r > 0$. We distinguish singular finite-proper-distance endpoints from asymptotic trumpet ends and give conditional bounds on a stationary spacelike inner limit. A local cosmological interpretation requires additional matching assumptions; dynamical selection and the rotating interior endpoint are not determined by the stationary construction.

authors.name: Antonio De Felice

papers.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Bayesian Inference for Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) pose a major challenge to Bayesian parameter inference because of their complex, highly multimodal likelihood surfaces. Locating narrow high-likelihood regions is particularly difficult without knowledge of the true source parameters, which is unavailable in real observations. We develop a deep-learning-assisted Bayesian inference framework that combines neural-network-guided parameter-space localization, particle swarm optimization, and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Applied to simulated six-month EMRI signals, the framework recovers posterior distributions in close agreement with reference MCMC analyses initialized near the true parameter values, without requiring such knowledge for initialization. Once the neural network has been trained, the complete inference pipeline takes approximately 10 hours per signal.

authors.name: Jian-Jun Song, Zhong-Wu Xia, Wen-Hong Ruan, Zu-Cheng Chen, Hongwei Yu, Puxun Wu

papers.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
papers.summary: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same St\"ackel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

authors.name: Vladimir Martinusi

papers.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
papers.summary: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

authors.name: Prashant Thakur, Yeunhwan Lim

papers.title: Measuring the Hubble Constant Using Strongly Lensed Gravitational Wave Signals
papers.summary: The measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ plays an important role in the study of cosmology. In this letter, we propose a new method to constrain the Hubble constant using the strongly lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals. By reparameterizing the waveform, we find that the lensed waveform is sensitive to the $H_0$. Assuming the scenario that no electromagnetic counterpart of the GW source can be identified, our method can still give meaningful constraints on the $H_0$ with the information of the lens redshift. We then apply Fisher information matrix and Markov Chain Monte Carlo to evaluate the potential of this method. For the space-based GW detector, TianQin, the $H_0$ can be constrained within a relative error of $\sim$ 0.3-2\%, using a single strongly lensed GW event. Precision varies according to different levels of electromagnetic information.

authors.name: Shun-Jia Huang, Yi-Ming Hu, Xian Chen, Jian-dong Zhang, En-Kun Li, Zucheng Gao, Xin-Yi Lin

papers.title: Exploring tidal dissipation in rubble pile binary secondaries using a discrete element model
papers.summary: In this work, models of rubble pile binary secondaries are simulated in various spin states in a system similar in size and scale to Didymos-Dimorphos. The numerical modeling is performed in the N-body Chrono-based software GRAINS, which simulates gravity, contact, and friction forces acting on non-spherical mass elements. In a high-fidelity, high-performance computational setting, tidal dissipation successfully emerges in the simulations as a consequence of the effects of inter-element contact and friction across thousands of simulated nonspherical mass elements. We devise computational techniques and rigorous numerical procedures for studying tides in the well-established framework of GRAINS. The simulations reveal tidal deformation, phase lag, and secular spin-down, including the transition from super-synchronous rotation to synchronous libration. We also observe the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the secondary's rotation and orbit, and identify the semidiurnal tidal response through spectral and topographical analyses. Using both energy and torque-based calculations, we compute values of $Q/k_{2} \sim O(10^{2})$, whereas this value has been predicted by other studies to lie in the range $10^{2}<Q/k_{2}<10^{6}$. Further study is required to determine whether this result is representative of truly enhanced dissipativity, or a consequence of material or modeling assumptions. More broadly, this framework provides a numerical laboratory for investigating the granular mechanisms underlying tidal dissipation and their relationship to the macroscopic tidal response of rubble-pile bodies.

authors.name: Ethan R. Burnett, Iosto Fodde, John Wimarsson, Eric Frizzell, Fabio Ferrari

papers.title: EGS-z11-R0: a red, dust-rich galaxy at Cosmic Dawn
papers.summary: Context. Galaxies discovered by JWST at z > 10 are predominantly characterized by extremely blue rest-frame UV slopes. Conversely, the existence of dust-reddened systems at such early epochs has remained largely unconfirmed spectroscopically. Aims. We present the spectroscopic confirmation of EGS-z11-R0 at z = 11.45, the most distant red galaxy identified to date, discovered serendipitously through inspection of publicly available JWST/NIRSpec data. Methods. We analyze JWST/NIRSpec PRISM and G395M spectroscopy together with multiwavelength HST, NIRCam, and MIRI photometry. We identify significant detections of the C IV 1548,1551 and C III] 1908 transitions, yielding a redshift of zspec = 11.452 +/- 0.021. We measure rest-frame UV emission-line fluxes and equivalent widths and use these diagnostics to constrain the nature of the ionizing radiation field. Finally, we perform spectral energy distribution modeling with CIGALE, combining spectroscopy with photometry and including stellar, nebular, dust, and active galactic nuclei (AGN) components. Results. EGS-z11-R0 exhibits a red UV continuum slope (betaUV approximately -1.0), placing it well above the canonical MUV-betaUV relation at z~10-12 and making it the highest-z spectroscopically confirmed member of the emerging "red monster" population. Emission-line diagnostics reveal a hard ionizing spectrum consistent with extreme star formation and compatible with a composite stellar plus AGN scenario. The best-fit SED solution favors a stellar mass of log(M*/Msun) ~ 9.2-9.6, a SFR of 10-40 Msun yr^-1, and substantial dust attenuation (AV~1.2 mag). Conclusions. The confirmation of EGS-z11-R0 establishes that chemically evolved, dust-enriched galaxies were already in place at z approximately 11.5. [abridged]

authors.name: Giulia Rodighiero, Andrea Ferrara, Michele Catone, Lorenzo Napolitano, Paolo Cassata, Giovanni Gandolfi, Emiliano Merlin, Andrea Grazian, Alvio Renzini, Laura Bisigello, Marco Castellano, Pablo G. P\'erez-Gonz\'alez, Borja P\'erez-D\'iaz, Edoardo Iani, Carlotta Gruppioni, Steven L. Finkelstein, Anton M. Koekemoer, Alessandro Bianchetti, Francesco Sinigaglia, Paola Santini, Giorgia Girardi, Amelia Vietri, Roberta Tripodi, Benedetta Vulcani, Polet Roman Quesada, Gaia E. Esposito

papers.title: Model-independent Constraints on Dark Energy Density from CMB-SPA, DESI DR2 BAO, and Updated Type Ia Supernova Compilations
papers.summary: Recent combinations of DESI BAO, CMB, and Type~Ia supernova data report a preference for evolving dark energy that is obtained within the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization and depends on the choice of SN~Ia compilation. We constrain the dark energy density ratio $X(z) \equiv \rho_{\rm DE}(z)/\rho_{\rm DE}(0)$ at five redshifts over $0 < z < 2.33$, without assuming a parametric form for the equation of state, using CMB data from SPT-3G, Planck~2018, and ACT~DR6 (hereafter CMB-SPA), DESI~DR2 BAO, and the updated Pantheon+, Union3.1, and DES-Dovekie SN~Ia compilations. For all three compilations, $X(z)$ rises above unity at low redshift, crosses unity near $z \approx 1$, and falls below unity at higher redshift. Depending on the SN~Ia compilation, the preference for a departure from a cosmological constant is $2.3$--$2.8\sigma$ with the five $X(z)$ knots, compared with $3.0$--$3.2\sigma$ in the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization. Because $X(z)$ is constrained locally in redshift, we can trace how the $\Lambda$CDM tension between each pair of probes propagates into its shape. The tension between BAO and the CMB in the $h r_d$--$\Omega_m$ plane reproduces this "see-saw" shape, whereas the $\Omega_m$ tension between SNe~Ia and the CMB only raises $X(z)$ slightly and nearly uniformly. The origin of the BAO--CMB tension can be tested by Euclid and Roman BAO measurements at $z \gtrsim 1$. We derive the distance prior $(R, \ell_A, \omega_b)$ from CMB-SPA data and show that it retains essentially all the information on $X(z)$ in the CMB-SPA power spectra without the lensing reconstruction, and that adding the lensing reconstruction only marginally increases the information on dark energy. Our work demonstrates the importance of model independence in exploring the nature of dark energy.

authors.name: Zhenyuan Wang, Yun Wang

papers.title: Magnetic properties of the Abell 3391-3395 system revealed using wide-field MeerKAT polarimetry
papers.summary: Magnetic fields in cluster outskirts and the intercluster medium are poorly constrained because diffuse synchrotron emission is hard to detect at low surface brightness. Faraday rotation measures (RMs) of polarized background sources can probe foreground large-scale structure. The nearby interacting Abell 3391-3395 system hosts a well-established X-ray bridge, making it an excellent target for studying magnetization in the intercluster environment. We characterize the magnetized environment of Abell 3391/95 and its surroundings by constructing a dense RM grid from wide-field polarimetry. We observed Abell 3391/95 with MeerKAT in full polarization using a three-pointing mosaic. The data were calibrated with direction-independent and direction-dependent techniques and imaged using visibility-plane mosaicing for a large field of view at high sensitivity. Using Faraday synthesis, we formed Faraday cubes and measured RMs for polarized background sources. We defined on- and off-target regions using contours from a wavelet-filtered eROSITA image. We identified 434 polarized sources within the field, with a polarized source density ranging from about 30 sources per square degree in the outer regions to about 110 sources per square degree in the central field, and a field-averaged density of 73 sources per square degree. The clusters show a statistically significant enhancement of RM scatter relative to the off-target region. In contrast, the bridge shows comparatively low RM scatter, while an RM structure-function analysis on matched angular scales yields a tentative indication of larger RM differences in the bridge than off-target. Combined with low per-source depolarization, this suggests a bridge magnetic field relatively ordered on ~10 kpc scales, but less ordered on larger scales. The non-detection of diffuse synchrotron emission in the bridge yields improved upper limits on the emissivity.

authors.name: V. Gustafsson, M. Br\"uggen, C. Tasse, S. P. O'Sullivan

papers.title: The Hunt for Red Dual AGNs I: Spatially-Resolved Mid-IR Dual AGNs in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
papers.summary: Theoretical studies predict that dual AGNs are a critical stage of galaxy merger-driven supermassive black hole growth. Systematic searches for dual AGNs typically target late-stage mergers ($\leq10$ kpc nuclear separations) and select AGNs based on optical diagnostics. Yet, simulations predict that obscuration can occur early in the merger sequence, and that a significant fraction of dual AGNs can be found beyond $10$ kpc. Here, we report on a new sample of 155 spatially resolved mid-IR dual AGNs candidates selected based upon their mid-IR $W1-W2$ colors from the Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer and optically classified as galaxy merger candidates using imaging from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Preliminary spectroscopic results are presented for approximately 2/3 of the sample. 78 candidates have been confirmed to reside in galaxy mergers; among these, 13 have been confirmed as bona fide mid-IR dual AGNs, while 65 represent strong dual AGN candidates that require further examination. 48 candidates have been rejected as non-merger contaminants (foreground-background AGNs, separations inconsistent with interacting galaxies, etc.). 29 candidates still await spectroscopic coverage. The confirmed and high confidence dual AGN candidates exhibit separations of 14.5-129 kpc; $>50%$ reside at separations $>50$ kpc. Confirmed and high confidence candidates also exhibit a diversity of nuclear optical BPT classes. Seyfert-Seyferts and Seyfert-HIIs dominate the overall BPT pairings. 31% of confirmed mid-IR dual AGNs reside in multi-mergers involving three or more galaxies. The diversity in AGN properties and environments identified in this work highlights the importance of multiwavelength selection strategies and analyses in the quest to holistically understand dual AGNs as a population.

authors.name: Ryan W. Pfeifle, Kimberly A. Weaver, Barry Rothberg, Miranda McCarthy, Emma Schwartzman, Nathan J. Secrest, Peter G. Boorman, Daniel Stern, Joanna Piotrowska, Kevin McCarthy, Emily Moravec, Jenna M. Cann, Kimberly Engle, Kyla Mullaney, Ryan Tanner, Kelly Whalen

papers.title: Eccentric Stellar-mass Binary Black Holes: Population, Detectability, and Waveform Analysis in the LISA and LIGO Era
papers.summary: Eccentric binary black holes (BBHs) formed through dynamical interactions can significantly contribute to gravitational wave (GW) detections. In this work, we present a simulated catalog of dynamically-formed, stellar-mass BBHs in the local universe, incorporating contributions from the Galactic field (flyby interactions), Galactic nucleus (eccentric Kozai-Lidov evolution), and globular clusters (N-body interactions). Our results predict a wide, highly eccentric BBH population in the Milky Way (MW), with source counts of $\sim 25, 9, 3, 1, 1, 3, 8, 20, 50$, respectively. Extending this model to cosmological populations, we show that different dynamical channels can produce distinct eccentricity distributions in the LVK band and can contribute hundreds of additional low-SNR mHz sources. Specifically, our model yields a merger rate of $\Gamma \sim 9 \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and $\sim 150$ extragalactic mHz BBHs with $\mathrm{SNR} > 1$. However, due to the lower mass and weaker GW signals of stellar-mass BBHs, this number declines sharply at higher detection thresholds (e.g., $\sim 1$ for $\mathrm{SNR} > 8$). We further highlight the impact of eccentric BBH signals on the LISA global fit, showing that their individual harmonics can be independently detected in the Milky Way, and may mimic circular binaries with systematically biased chirp masses. Lastly, we show that post-Newtonian waveforms converge reliably for eccentric BBHs with masses of $\lesssim 10^3 M_\odot$ in the mHz band. Overall, eccentric BBHs represent a prevalent and promising target for future space-based GW observatories. The simulated catalog and the LISA Eccentricity Astrophysics Package (LEAP) developed in this work are publicly available at https://github.com/zeyuanxuan/lisa-leap/.

authors.name: Zeyuan Xuan, Smadar Naoz, Kyle Kremer, Michael L. Katz, Bence Kocsis, Erez Michaely

papers.title: Spectro Capture: A Software System for Automated Small-Observatory Spectroscopy
papers.summary: Spectro Capture is a Python-based software system developed to automate small- observatory fibre-fed spectroscopy. The system integrates target selection, telescope slewing, guide star acquisition, fibre position restoration, calibration and science exposure sequencing within a single observing workflow. The paper describes the design and operational behaviour of the system at Shenton Park Observatory, where it has been used for unattended multi-target spectroscopic observing. Log analysis from January to May 2026 shows that the system completed 339 of 345 attempted science target blocks in primary unattended batch runs, corresponding to a completion rate of 98.3%. The results demonstrate that reliable unattended spectroscopy is practical at a small observatory when target acquisition, guiding, scheduling and calibration control are treated as an integrated software problem.

authors.name: Paul Luckas

papers.title: Loss-Cone-Limited Dark Matter Capture by Early Black Hole Seeds
papers.summary: The rapid appearance of supermassive black holes at high redshift motivates a reassessment of non-baryonic growth channels. We develop a new loss-cone framework for collisionless dark-matter (DM) capture by early black-hole seeds, with particular attention to phase-space depletion and refilling. The calculation combines Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, a relativistic direct-capture boundary, and an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of angular-momentum transport. Primordial black holes (PBHs) are treated as massive perturbers whose refilling strength depends on both their abundance and individual mass. Collisionless refilling by triaxial or chaotic centrophilic orbits is included as a phenomenological upper-envelope channel. We show that ordinary stellar relaxation gives negligible DM-driven growth for the fiducial high-redshift seeds. PBH-driven granularity can yield order-of-magnitude growth in sufficiently compact halos, while triaxial or full-loss-cone supply can produce a rapid early burst. In the self-consistent calculations, however, the evolution generally becomes supply-limited. Once the accessible low-angular-momentum phase-space reservoir is depleted, the capture rate collapses and the black-hole mass saturates. Fixed-background NFW calculations therefore overestimate sustained growth, especially in the full-loss-cone limit. A TNG50-calibrated NFW benchmark gives negligible growth even under optimistic refilling assumptions. Collisionless DM capture is therefore unlikely to solve early SMBH growth in generic NFW-like halos, but it can provide a radiatively dark upper envelope in rare compact environments with efficient angular-momentum refilling.

authors.name: Brian Zhang, Grant J. Mathews

papers.title: Neutron Star Mass-Radius Constraints for EXO 0748$-$676 from 2008-2025 Quiescent X-ray Spectra
papers.summary: We present new constraints on the mass and radius of the neutron star in the neutron star low-mass X-ray binary EXO 0748$-$676 obtained from a joint analysis of 20 quiescent X-ray observations obtained between 2008 and 2025, including 14 Chandra and 6 XMM-Newton exposures. These data sample two quiescent episodes separated by the 2024$-$2025 outburst. We model the 0.5$-$10 keV spectra with a hydrogen-atmosphere model, assuming a source distance of 7.1 kpc. In a global Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis in which the hydrogen column density, neutron star mass, and radius are tied across all observations, we obtain a neutron-star mass of $1.77^{+0.17}_{-0.22}\,M_\odot$ and a radius of $12.62^{+0.56}_{-0.74}$ km ($1\sigma$ credible intervals). We further perform independent fits to the first and second quiescent epochs and find that the combined data set significantly reduces the low-mass tail in the posterior distribution, leading to tighter lower bounds on the neutron-star mass. Incorporating the distance uncertainty of $7.1\pm1.2$ kpc, we conservatively constrain the neutron-star mass and radius to $M\simeq 1.41-2.11~M_{\odot}$ and $R\simeq 10.15-15.13$ km, favoring relatively stiff dense-matter equations of state. We also trace the thermal evolution across two quiescent epochs and find evidence for renewed crust cooling following the 2024$-$2025 outburst, providing a unique opportunity to compare the thermal relaxation behavior after two distinct accretion episodes.

authors.name: Mingyang Wang, Guobao Zhang, Ang Li

papers.title: The kinetic-energy bottleneck in Fast Radio Burst models
papers.summary: Most Fast Radio Burst (FRB) models invoke a two-step process in which energy released by the central engine is converted into particle kinetic energy and subsequently radiated as coherent GHz emission. We derive model-independent constraints on this picture and apply them to the three main classes of FRB models. (i) Inner-magnetospheric models violate brightness-temperature and kinetic-luminosity limits unless particles are continuously re-accelerated in situ. Magnetar-strength fields can provide the required parallel electric field out to $R\lesssim10^{10}\mathrm{cm}$. Monster shocks provide continuous acceleration but, under a single-pass kinetic-energy interpretation, require extreme particle densities and predict emission well above GHz frequencies. Even mechanisms that bypass the kinetic bottleneck through conservative wave conversion remain subject to charge availability, which independently limits magnetospheric GHz production to $\lesssim 10^{10}$ cm for fiducial parameters. (ii) Light-cylinder forced-reconnection naturally provides continuous acceleration, but typically converts only $\lesssim10^{-6}$ of the injected energy into radio emission. (iii) External-shock maser models satisfy the kinetic-luminosity and brightness-temperature constraints, but the upstream wind is unavoidably optically thick to induced Compton scattering, independent of the model's principal parameters. Proposed escape routes - emission above the maser peak or upstream magnetization $\sigma_{\rm w}\gtrsim30$ imply very low efficiencies, while the former also conflicts with narrow FRB spectra. We conclude that near-surface magnetospheric models with continuous particle acceleration remain the most promising scenario, provided the radiation can escape the magnetosphere.

authors.name: Paz Beniamini, Pawan Kumar

papers.title: Too shy to spin? Cosmic wallflowers as proto-globular clusters
papers.summary: We investigate the rotational properties of star-forming clusters at $z \sim 7.6$ in the high-resolution simulation MassiveBlackPS, focusing on two formation channels: clusters forming in galactic discs via gravitational instability and isolated circumgalactic systems, referred to as cosmic wallflowers, born out of cosmic filaments. Using stellar kinematics, we compare their rotational velocities, $v_{\rm rot}$, and rotational support, $v/\sigma$, to study whether formation environment leaves a clear dynamical imprint. We find a clear separation, wherein cosmic wallflowers systematically have lower rotational velocities and span a wide range in $v/\sigma$, whereas the identified disc clusters are strongly rotation-dominated and extend to higher $v_{\rm rot}$. When combined with stellar surface densities, a subset of the low-$v_{\rm rot}$ cosmic wallflowers lie surprisingly close to the observed globular cluster population in the Milky Way, whereas disc clusters remain offset. Within the cosmic wallflower population, we identify two regimes: lower-density, weakly rotating systems that overlap with these globular cluster properties, and denser, more rotationally supported systems that likely follow a different evolutionary pathway, possibly linking them to the origin of massive black hole seeds at high redshift. We further find that the gas content correlates with this behaviour, with gas-rich cosmic wallflowers preferentially occupying this low-rotation regime. This all suggests that environment and baryonic content together play a key role in setting the initial dynamical state and possible fate of clusters. In particular, weakly rotating, gas-rich cosmic wallflowers emerge as natural proto-globular cluster candidates, potentially evolving towards present-day systems through angular momentum loss and dynamical heating.

authors.name: Floor van Donkelaar, Lucio Mayer, Pedro R. Capelo

papers.title: The Maximum Initial Mass in low-thrust spacecraft trajectory design
papers.summary: We introduce the maximum-initial-mass problem as a standalone optimal-control formulation for low-thrust trajectory design and analyze its structure within Pontryagin's framework. For prescribed transfer time and endpoint states, the formulation maximizes the initial spacecraft mass, with necessary conditions yielding full-throttle control in the nondegenerate case and standard primer-vector steering. We establish that extremals of this single formulation correspond to extremals of two distinct problems: minimum-time and maximum-time transfer. The sign of the terminal dynamics-only Hamiltonian distinguishes the two normal representations, while the zero-Hamiltonian case admits an abnormal representation. We also clarify the relationship between free-time transversality and costate normalization in indirect formulations. This unified perspective offers two practical advantages. For reachability analysis, it replaces separate minimum- and maximum-time conditions with a single initial-mass threshold, simplifying both feasibility checks and the learning of reachability maps. For homotopy methods, it opens extended continuation paths that connect branches beyond those accessed by tracking individual time-optimal solutions. Applied to a benchmark multiple-revolution GTO-to-GEO transfer, the approach recovers the best known minimum-time solution, identifies previously unreported extremals, and reveals a funnel-like arrangement of transfer-time minima and maxima along a constant-initial-mass contour, including a previously reported trajectory that is a local maximum rather than a minimum.

authors.name: Dario Izzo, Giacomo Acciarini

papers.title: Star Planet Interactions
papers.summary: Star-planet interactions (SPIs) describe the continuous exchange of energy, momentum, and mass between exoplanets and their host stars through radiative, tidal, magnetic, and particle-driven processes. Together, these interactions shape the structure, evolution, and observable properties of exoplanetary systems. In this review, we bring together current theoretical and observational understanding of SPIs, highlighting how stellar radiation, winds, and magnetic activity influence planetary atmospheres, interiors, and orbital evolution, while using the Solar System as a valuable reference for interpreting these processes. High-energy stellar radiation, particularly in the far- and extreme-ultraviolet and X-ray bands, drives atmospheric heating, photochemistry, ionisation, and escape. These effects are further influenced by stellar winds and magnetic interactions, which can either protect planetary atmospheres or accelerate their loss over time. Tidal interactions redistribute energy and angular momentum, producing internal heating and driving orbital migration and circularisation. Magnetic star-planet coupling provides additional pathways for energy transfer through reconnection and current systems, potentially enhancing atmospheric escape, heating planetary ionospheres and interiors, and generating observable signatures such as radio emission and enhanced stellar activity. We discuss how these processes work together, emphasising that their long-term impact depends on stellar evolution, planetary properties, atmospheric structure, and magnetic field strength. By presenting radiative, tidal, and magnetic interactions within a unified framework, this review highlights the physical mechanisms that shape planetary environments and identifies the key observational signatures that will complement future studies of exoplanet evolution and habitability.

papers.title: Fast and accurate bandpass integration of complex SEDs with neural networks
papers.summary: The paper presents a novel ML-based approach for fast and accurate bandpass integration of spectral energy distributions (SEDs). The non-locality of the integral operator involved guarantees the smoothness of the target function to be approximated, making it an excellent use-case for neural networks. The computational method developed for this work has been wrapped within pyfine (FINE: Fast Function Interpolation via NEural NEtworks). This new Python package makes the relevant code available and easy to use by everyone within the scientific community. The method is demonstrated with two different bandpass integration test cases with 3 and 9 free parameters, respectively, where both accuracy and computational performance are analyzed. The results show that the method is capable of predicting values of the bandpass integral with maximum relative residuals as low as 0.002% and 0.08% respectively, within the sampled region of the parameter space, fast run times, and very little memory overhead. The usage of pyfine is especially effective when the computation of an SED functional form, given a set of values for its free parameters, is expensive. However, already in the first of the two test cases, where a simple modified black body SED was employed, the neural network's measured run times resulted faster by two orders of magnitudes than an optimized multithreaded version of the ``brute force'' exact calculation of the integral.

authors.name: L. A. Bianchi

papers.title: On Bimodality in the Eccentricity Distribution of Galactic Double Neutron Stars
papers.summary: The detection of Galactic double neutron stars (DNSs) through pulsar timing offers a unique opportunity to probe massive stellar and binary evolution. The current observed DNS population shows a scarcity of systems at intermediate eccentricities, although the present sample does not provide statistically significant evidence for an underlying bimodal distribution. We explore whether such a feature can arise naturally from DNS formation physics and serve as a prediction for future observations. We propose that this possible bimodality can result from a non-monotonic relationship between progenitor mass and neutron star (NS) mass, provided that the second-born NS receives a sufficiently small natal kick. We illustrate this scenario using the population synthesis code COMPAS, and find that our DNS population model produces an intermediate-eccentricity deficit broadly similar to that suggested by current observations and can reproduce the observed orbital period--eccentricity distribution relatively well. We also show that most measured second-born NS masses fall within the ranges predicted by our model at the corresponding DNS orbital eccentricities, providing a complementary observational diagnostic that is less sensitive to uncertainties in the preceding binary evolution. Our results therefore predict that an eccentricity bimodality should become more apparent as the Galactic DNS sample grows.

authors.name: Aldana Grichener, Paul Disberg, Ryosuke Hirai, Ilya Mandel

papers.title: Evidence for the Moon and Sun shadows with cosmic rays at an average energy of $\text{7}{\times}\text{10}^\text{17}\,$eV
papers.summary: Interactions of cosmic rays with the Moon and the Sun produce deficits in their arrival-direction distributions relative to an isotropic flux. Such shadows have been observed previously at energies between $10^{12}\,$eV and $10^{16}\,$eV. We report the first evidence for the Moon and Sun shadows at cosmic-ray energies larger than about $10^{16}\,$eV (average energy of $7\times10^{17}\,$eV), using data collected by the Pierre Auger Observatory. We employ data from three detector arrays covering $3000\,\text{km}^2$, $27\,\text{km}^2$, and $2\,\text{km}^2$, with spacings of $1500\,\text{m}$, $750\,\text{m}$, and $433\,\text{m}$, respectively. The data amount to over 10.6 million events. The Moon and Sun shadows are detected with a combined significance of approximately $3\sigma$. These observations confirm the pointing accuracy of the Surface Detector of the Pierre Auger Observatory using celestial bodies. From the combined Sun and Moon shadows, we infer an overall angular resolution of $(0.59^{+0.15}_{-0.11})^\circ$.
