Out-of-time-ordered correlators can likewise become exponentially small, showing that their late-time saturation value alone does not witness computational hardness and constituting a classically tractable example of emergent free independence. Finally, we relate these separations to operator resource theories, showing how operator entanglement beyond the Gaussian baseline lower-bounds the number of non-Gaussian gates in doped matchgate circuits. Our results present a practical toolbox for computing exact averages over random matchgates, while clarifying the distinction between quantum resources versus simulation complexity, and their dependence on the representation being exploited.

authors.name: Gregory A. L. White, Jens Eisert, Neil Dowling

papers.title: Breaking the Bounded Entanglement Barrier for Quantum Position Verification
papers.summary: Position verification, introduced by Chandran et al. (SIAM J. Computing 2014), allows verifiers to test a prover's claimed position by an interactive protocol. Classical position verification is impossible. Even for Quantum Position Verification (QPV), there always exists an LOCC (Local Operations and Classical Communication) attack if the adversary can hold an exponentially large amount of preshared entanglement. Somewhat surprisingly, we show that we can circumvent this barrier in the idealized continuous-time model, where time is represented by a real-valued parameter and challenge messages can be sent at a time sampled uniformly from a real interval. In this model, we give a BB84-based protocol that remains secure against any finite coalition of LOCC adversaries with arbitrary finite (possibly exponential) quantum storage and entanglement. Our construction can also be instantiated in the discrete-time model. Although prior impossibility results apply, our information-theoretic QPV protocol achieves any desired polynomial gap between the honest parties' total resources (communication and storage) and the adversarial resource bound. To our knowledge, all prior constructions that do not rely on idealized oracles required resources of the honest parties to be at least as large as the proven adversarial entanglement bound. Interestingly, the resource gap depends on the precision in measuring time. As clock precision improves, the adversarial resource bound increases while honest resources remain largely unchanged. We call this the "I sleep, you work" paradigm. Finally, we show that our techniques extend to an information-theoretic, position-based message authentication protocol, which in turn extends to an information-theoretic, position-based quantum key exchange protocol with the same guarantees as our position-verification protocol in the continuous-time and discrete-time models.

authors.name: Amit Behera, Vipul Goyal

papers.title: Optimal Scaling of Unitary Design Formation in $U(1)$-Symmetric Random Circuits: A Bottleneck Slower than Charge Transport
papers.summary: Understanding randomness formation under conservation laws is important both for characterizing chaotic phenomena in isolated quantum systems and for symmetry-constrained quantum information processing. $U(1)$-symmetric random circuits on an $N$-qubit system provide a minimal tractable setting for this problem, in which the formation rate of unitary designs was conjectured to be governed by charge transport in the underlying circuit geometry. However, whether charge transport indeed sets the slowest relaxation mode has remained an open problem, due to the difficulty in deriving a tight lower bound on the symmetric design formation rate. In this work, we resolve this problem by determining the optimal scaling of the unitary $k$-design formation rate for $k\leq O(\sqrt{\log N})$ across a wide range of circuit geometries, including lattices, expander graphs, and all-to-all interactions. In particular, for $k\geq 2$, we find that the formation rate is governed by a two-particle encounter rate---the rate at which two random walkers encounter each other in a given circuit geometry. This encounter rate is parametrically smaller than the single-particle transport rate in many geometries, thereby disproving the previous conjecture. We further establish that this encounter mechanism indeed sets the design formation rate by deriving its matching lower bound with a novel proof technique based on an auxiliary subgroup ensemble. Although this encounter mode imposes a robust bottleneck on design formation in $U(1)$-symmetric random circuits, we also show that this bottleneck can be circumvented by using symmetry-breaking local gates and provide an explicit protocol that achieves faster design formation. These results establish a new picture of randomness formation under conservation laws and provide guiding principles for characterizing and efficiently generating symmetry-constrained randomness.

authors.name: Toshihiro Yada

papers.title: From Static Lindblad Stabilizability to Robust Physical Control Sequences
papers.summary: We derive checkable convergence, error, and execution-cost bounds for repeating a supplied finite control sequence from a static Lindblad stabilization certificate and complete implementation data, including concurrent background dynamics. The static decay bound and error bounds from static to planned evolution and from the plan to execution together bound the actual cycle's contraction factor in one fixed Lyapunov metric. For target-preserving planned and actual paths and a controller returning to its initial state each cycle, a uniform contraction bound below one gives cycle-end convergence from every initial state under cycle-varying uncertainty. Uniformly bounded within-cycle amplification in that metric extends this convergence throughout physical time when cycle durations are bounded above and away from zero. With leakage, uniform error bounds relative to certified target-preserving paths give explicit long-time distance bounds. Cycle and within-cycle bounds also screen a specified finite hardware library for sequences certified to meet and maintain a prescribed tolerance. In a four-level cascade with finite pulses, calibration and timing errors, always-on dephasing, and bounded pumping, the selected sequence brings every initial state within trace distance $0.1$ of the target in one complete cycle of explicitly bounded duration and maintains that tolerance under repetition.

authors.name: Yibin Wang, Ruifeng Liu

papers.title: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a coupled three-dimensional double well, at an excited eigenstate
papers.summary: For the coupled three-dimensional double well $H=\tfrac12|p|^2+2\sum_i(q_i^2-1)^2-\sum_{i<j}q_i^2q_j^2$ we exhibit, at the first excited energy level (and also at the ground state), a linear functional on polynomials of degree $\le 6$ that satisfies every constraint of the standard level-3 eigenstate bootstrap, has a strictly positive definite moment matrix, and nevertheless assigns a negative value to a nonnegative polynomial. It is therefore an interior point of the level-3 relaxation that is realized by no quantum state. The construction reflects a fact that holds at every level: the eigenstate rows never reach the top-degree momentum moments. At level 3, where strictly feasible points exist, this means that the corresponding block of the moment matrix carries no information about which energies admit one. Every algebraic ingredient is an exact rational certificate, and the only numerical ingredients (spectral enclosures of an eigenfunction) are carried out in rigorous ball arithmetic.

authors.name: Daniel Keren, Ye Zhou

papers.title: Testing bosonic and fermionic Gaussian states with a constant number of copies
papers.summary: Bosonic and fermionic Gaussian quantum states play a central role in quantum physics and quantum information processing. We study the problem of testing whether a given pure state is Gaussian or is bounded away from the set of pure Gaussian states. Earlier work left open whether a fixed number of copies could suffice even as the number of modes (system size) grows. We show that it does: the number of copies needed depends only on the desired accuracy and confidence. Our tests exploit the symmetries of identical copies of Gaussian states; their analysis combines a gradient flow argument with a spectral gap studied previously for the Kac random walk on the sphere.

authors.name: Jop Bri\"et, Davi Castro-Silva, Michael Walter, Freek Witteveen

papers.title: Pauli Decomposition by Character Theory: A Memory-Bounded Algorithm for Qubits and Qudits
papers.summary: Pauli decomposition of an $n$-qubit operator is expensive if each of the $4^n$ Pauli strings is treated as an unstructured object. Labeling those strings by the configuration space $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ makes them displacement operators $X^{\otimes x}Z^{\otimes z}$ on the computational space: shifts by~$x$ and multiplications by characters $Z^{\otimes z}$ in the computational basis. That labeling organizes the operator into $2^n$ fibers of length $2^n$, one per shift~$x$, each collecting the computational-basis amplitudes that hop by~$x$. Expanding each fiber function in the character basis of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ --- a length-$2^n$ Walsh--Hadamard transform --- recovers the Pauli coefficients at total cost $O(n\cdot4^n)$. The same fiber / shift--character picture extends to $(\mathbb{Z}_p)^n$ (Heisenberg--Weyl qudits). \texttt{paulikit} is a memory-bounded realization for qubits: for matrix-sparse inputs, peak memory need not densify to a full $2^n\times2^n$ operator. Performance is checked on a stated low-end GNU/Linux platform for a coupled-oscillator sweep beyond a billion Pauli terms.

authors.name: Mohammadreza Khellat, Mohammad Masoumi, Saman Nasoori, Soroush Nasoori

papers.title: Perfect discrimination of an orthogonal $2\otimes2$ basis may require collective separable measurements on two copies
papers.summary: We consider an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ with three entangled states and one product state. This basis is not perfectly distinguishable by LOCC or even by separable measurements when a single copy of the unknown state is available. We show that with two copies no adaptive separable protocol, which measures the copies one at a time, distinguishes the basis perfectly. We then show that a collective separable measurement on the two copies does. Whether two copies suffice for LOCC remains open.

authors.name: Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay

papers.title: General Master Equation for Two Accelerated Detectors: Stationary States and Entanglement
papers.summary: We derive a general master equation for two uniformly accelerated two-level detectors with different internal orientations, following the same worldline and weakly coupled to independent bosonic fields in the Minkowski vacuum. We consider coherent and dissipative contributions and allow arbitrary field masses, spacetime dimensions, and coupling tensors. For equal orientations, we prove that singlet-triplet coherences decay exponentially when the Kossakowski matrix has rank at least two. For fixed couplings and a common field spectrum, we classify the acceleration dependence of stationary concurrence in terms of the transverse coupling ratio, including acceleration-independent behavior and entanglement loss and recovery. We illustrate the framework with massless scalar fields in four spacetime dimensions, considering isotropic and mixed coupling for equal orientations. For isotropic coupling, any nonzero misalignment of the detectors yields a unique separable stationary state, while near alignment entanglement generated from a separable initial state can persist over timescales proportional to the inverse square of the misalignment angle.

authors.name: Riccardo Acquaviva, Paolo Facchi

papers.title: Noise redistribution by stabilizer codes: an organizing view of concatenated three-qubit codes
papers.summary: We formulate stabilizer-code error correction as a code- and recovery-dependent transformation of the noise channel. For a fixed recovery map, syndrome projection produces a block-diagonal logical channel whose diagonal Pauli weights follow from code-induced error classes, with no physical Pauli twirl; concatenation is then iterated redistribution, with the dominant logical error guiding the next code. The bit-flip and phase-flip three-qubit codes with standard recoveries supply a closed-form benchmark, and logically inequivalent recoveries appear as a design degree of freedom for shaping the channel presented to the next decoder. For amplitude damping, the three-qubit rules select C2(sigma_y)C1(sigma_x): one level converts the damping into a nearly pure logical-X channel at the price f1 = 1 - 3gamma/4, the second level suppresses that channel to f2 = 1 - (9/4)gamma^2, and the concatenated protocol overtakes the unencoded channel below gamma_c = 0.292 (f_c = 0.848); across the n-qubit repetition family the suppression order rises as gamma^(w+1), with w = (n-1)/2, while the gate budget grows as n^L. Correlated noise requires joint class statistics, whereas coherent noise retains intra-class coherences that make the same transformation usable in reverse as a tomographic fingerprint; there the companion work proves local identifiability from a rank certificate evaluated inside the parameter domain, classifies the sole permutation-symmetry ambiguity as structural at any chain length, and closes it with one two-qubit marginal channel. The construction remains an analytic benchmark, not a universal prescription for an inner code beneath a surface code.

authors.name: Long Huang

papers.title: Electron-photon entanglement in real space from quantum electrodynamics
papers.summary: We study the entanglement between an electron and the photon it scatters, resolved in real space and time. Starting from nonrelativistic QED in Fermi's oscillator representation, we write Fock's coupled equations for components with fixed photon number in the photon configuration space, in the length gauge, where the photon is created around the atom through a nonlocal kernel. Truncated at one photon, the equations are solved numerically without the rotating-wave approximation for a one-dimensional model atom in a waveguide with a single transverse mode and enhanced coupling. The atom is driven by a short, off-resonant laser pulse, with the electron and photon represented on real-space grids. The global electron-photon entanglement is largely transient. It peaks during the pulse and decreases as the polarized electron cloud returns to the core, leaving a state close to a product of the electron state and a superposition of the field vacuum with a single scattered photon. Local entanglement, obtained from walkers sampled across both photon-number components, exhibits opposite spatial patterns for the two particles. The electron entropy is smallest at the nucleus and maps the local strength of the dipole coupling, whereas the photon entropy is largest near the atom, where photons are created and absorbed, and smaller in the outgoing wave packets.

authors.name: Ivan P. Christov

papers.title: Floquet engineering of quantum relaxation
papers.summary: Dynamical decoupling suppresses decoherence by averaging selected interactions between a quantum system and its environment. Here, we extend this notion through a general Floquet formalism that maps periodic control onto relaxation and dephasing channels. Environmental fluctuations are decomposed into Floquet components that sample the noise spectrum at distinct frequencies, with coupling strengths determined by control-induced Floquet coefficients. We experimentally investigate this approach using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond under multi-pulse control. By tuning the drive and detuning, we reshape the coupling to environmental fluctuations and create isolated operating points where the dominant decoherence channel vanishes, strongly suppressing Floquet dephasing. The resulting coherence enhancement follows the predicted Floquet coupling coefficients and can be shifted by modifying the control sequence. These results establish Floquet driving as a general framework for engineering transverse and longitudinal relaxation through the design of quantum control protocols.

authors.name: Kang Xu, Dionisio Cendoya, Nazar Delegan, F. Joseph Heremans, Olga Shenderova, Daniela Pagliero, Lisandro Buljubasich, Carlos A. Meriles

papers.title: Quantum Temporal Marginal Problem
papers.summary: Experiments on a multi-time quantum process may reveal its responses only on selected, possibly overlapping, sets of times. We ask whether these partial descriptions admit a common underlying process, and formulate this process tensor marginal problem as a semidefinite feasibility test. Agreement on overlaps is necessary but insufficient: three locally consistent qubit marginals can have no common extension. Another family is incompatible as a time-ordered process even though a single quantum channel satisfies both its channel and temporal marginal constraints. This isolates temporal causality as the obstruction. We quantify incompatibility by the mixing needed to restore compatibility and derive finite tests using separate interventions at each time and final measurements. We further show that incompatibility is equivalent to an advantage over every compatible family in a multi-time process-discrimination task. Together, these results test whether process descriptions obtained in different experiments can arise from one causally ordered quantum process.

authors.name: Dingqian Wang, Jiayi Zhao, Ge Bai

papers.title: Single-port homodyne detection achieves optimal multiphase sensing in an $n$-port ring cavity
papers.summary: Estimating several phases simultaneously is more than estimating them one at a time: the optimal measurements for different parameters may not commute, and in a multiparameter problem the quantum Cram\'er-Rao bound is not automatically achievable. Ring cavities are a natural setting for this question, since a single coherent input can be made to interact repeatedly with every internal phase before it is read out. We study the simultaneous local estimation of the $n$ internal phases of a lossless $n$-port ring cavity probed by a fixed-energy multimode coherent state, optimizing over the full coherent-input space and over the operating point of the cavity. We identify a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimum: the input energy should be distributed equally among the ports, and the internal phases and input phases satisfy a simple phase-matching condition for every port. The optimum is unique up to a common optical phase and minimizes both the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) cost and the sloppiness of the model. At this point the quantum Fisher information matrix is full rank and its spectrum is obtained in closed form, the Uhlmann curvature vanishes, and no incompatibility penalty has to be paid. The precision retains the coherent-state scaling and the dependence on the number of phases, but the cavity feedback reduces the prefactor relative to $n$ independent single-pass experiments. Finally, we show that this bound may be achieved in practice: the Fisher information of a balanced homodyne measurement at each output port, with local-oscillator phases locked to the prepared input phases is equal to the optimal quantum Fisher information. Our results establish the ring cavity as a platform for optimal multiphase sensing and provide the ultimate benchmark against which nonclassical probes may be evaluated for further precision enhancement.

authors.name: Jiayu He, Aviral Kumar Pandey, Krishna Mohan Mishra, Devendra Kumar Mishra, Matteo G. A. Paris

papers.title: Simple proof of conditions requiring maximal entanglement for local state verification and discrimination
papers.summary: For deterministic state verification by separable measurements, the Schmidt rank of an entangled resource must be at least that of the state being verified [N. Yu, R. Duan, and M. Ying, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 60, 2069 (2014)], and if the two are equal, the resource must be maximally entangled [S. Akibue, J. Miyazaki, and H. Osaka, Lett. Math. Phys. 116, 110 (2026)]. The latter was derived from a general theorem proved using algebraic geometry. In this paper, we give a simple, self-contained proof of both statements using only linear algebra. We then use these results to show that among pure entangled resources of local dimension at most $d$, a maximally entangled state of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$ is necessary and sufficient for perfect local discrimination of a generic orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$, however weakly entangled. The same holds for local implementation of a generic orthogonal measurement.

authors.name: Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay

papers.title: The most entangled states of four and seven qubits
papers.summary: Pure states of four and seven qubits cannot be maximally entangled across every balanced bipartition; we determine how entangled they can be on average. For four qubits we prove the conjecture of Higuchi and Sudbery: the mean von Neumann entropy of the three $2|2$ cuts is at most $1+\tfrac12\log_2 3$ bits, with equality exactly on the local-unitary orbits of their state $M_4$ and its complex conjugate. For seven qubits the mean purity of the 35 balanced $3|4$ cuts is at least $121/917$ and their mean entropy is at most $2.965356029\ldots$ bits, each with a unique optimiser up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. The two optimisers are distinct members of one icosahedral family, so minimum purity and maximum entropy select different states. The proofs bound moments of the marginal spectra by positive identities on several copies of the state, some of them spin flipped, and bound the entropy by a polynomial in those moments. The four-qubit maximum has an analytic proof; the seven-qubit proofs, and some of the four-qubit refinements below, are computer-assisted, with exact arithmetic and rigorous error bounds. We also prove the Gour--Wallach conjecture for R\'enyi entropies of all orders, with the maximiser changing from $M_4$ to cluster states at $q_*\approx1.588$, and obtain sharp Tsallis bounds, mixed-state bounds and quantitative stability.

authors.name: Antony Lewis

papers.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
papers.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.

authors.name: Wan-Peng Gao, Xiao-Liang He, Zheng-Qi Niu, Si-Qi Li, Da-Qiang Bao, Kuang Liu, Jian-Qiang You, Jaw-Shen Tsai, Zhen Wang, Zhi-Rong Lin

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.summary: Process tomography built on stabilizer codes compares the logical channel of a repetition code with a reference channel, and the decoder that produces it is almost always fixed to the standard minimum-weight one. Under a fixed measurement basis, where the gate count is a resource rather than a bookkeeping artefact, we enumerate every recovery design for three, five and seven qubits and decide the rank of each exactly. The minimal counts are $0$, $1$ and $5$ single-qubit Pauli gates, against $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding, and the count depends on how many sites are corrected, never on which. Correcting more sites is not monotonically better: at seven qubits full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, proved in rational arithmetic. At the median of $40$ working points the three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the six-gate decoder, and the ordering holds at every one.

authors.name: Long Huang

papers.title: Sharp error tolerance of the monogamy-of-entanglement game
papers.summary: The BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement (MoE) game has numerous applications in quantum cryptography, including quantum key distribution, position verification, and unclonable encryption. In this short note, we improve the error threshold for parallel repetition with identical answer strings from the approximately $3.7\%$ certified by the original bound to the sharp threshold $(1-1/\sqrt2)/2\approx14.64\%$. When the players need not give identical answers, we also obtain exponential decay whenever the sum of their error tolerances is below this threshold. These bounds strengthen existing security reductions to the BB84 MoE game, improving security bounds and certified noise tolerances for cryptographic protocols.

authors.name: Lloren\c{c} Escol\`a-Farr\`as, Florian Speelman

papers.title: Scaling at quantum phase transitions above the upper critical dimension
papers.summary: The hyperscaling relation and standard finite-size scaling (FSS) are known to break down above the upper critical dimension due to dangerous irrelevant variables. We establish a coherent formalism for FSS at quantum phase transitions above the upper critical dimension following the recently introduced Q-FSS formalism for thermal phase transitions. Contrary to long-standing belief, the correlation sector is affected by dangerous irrelevant variables. The presented formalism recovers a generalized hyperscaling relation and FSS form. Using this new FSS formalism, we determine the full set of critical exponents for the long-range transverse-field Ising chain in all criticality regimes ranging from the nearest-neighbor to the long-range mean field regime. For the same model, we also explicitly confirm the effect of dangerous irrelevant variables on the characteristic length scale.

authors.name: A. Langheld, J. A. Koziol, P. Adelhardt, S. C. Kapfer, K. P. Schmidt

papers.title: Gapped and gapless quantum spin liquids on the ruby lattice
papers.summary: The ruby lattice has been the subject of much interest recently due to its realization in Rydberg atom arrays, where its rich variety of frustrated interactions gives rise to topologically ordered quantum spin liquids. Similarly, numerical studies of ruby-lattice spin models, with both isotropic and anisotropic interactions, have provided evidence of gapped and gapless spin-liquid ground states with different low-energy gauge structures. Motivated by these findings, we perform a projective symmetry group (PSG) classification of U(1) and $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ fermionic spinon mean-field theories$\unicode{x2014}$respecting space-group and time-reversal symmetries$\unicode{x2014}$for $S=1/2$ spins. We obtain a total of 50 U(1) and 64 $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ PSGs, and upon restricting their realization via mean-field $\textit{Ans\"atze}$ with up to second-nearest-neighbor singlet amplitudes (relevant to the models studied here), only 8 U(1) and 18 $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ distinct states are obtained. We present the singlet fields for all $\textit{Ans\"atze}$ up to third-nearest-neighboring bonds and discuss their spinon dispersions as well as their dynamical spin structure factors. Building on this information, we also obtain the phase diagram of the Heisenberg model in the presence of first- ($J_{1}$), second- ($J_{1}'$), and third- ($J_{2}$) neighbor antiferromagnetic couplings within a self-consistent mean-field approximation.

authors.name: Atanu Maity, Rhine Samajdar, Yasir Iqbal

papers.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
papers.summary: We seek an extension to Schrodinger's equation that incorporates the macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse phenomenon. We find that a suitable hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in a way that is consistent with Born's rule. Our theory posits that the Bohmian particle is guided by the wavefunction and, conversely, the wavefunction gradually localizes towards the particle's position. As long as the particle can visit any state, as in a typical microscopic system, the localization effect does not favor any particular quantum state and, on average, the usual Schrodinger-like time evolution results. However, when the wavefunction develops spatially well-separated lobes, as would happen during a macroscopic measurement, the Bohmian particle can remain trapped in one lobe, which causes the wavefunction to eventually localizes. This proposed loss of ergodicity mechanism recasts one of the foundational postulate of quantum mechanics as a emergent feature and has important implications regarding the feasibility of large-scale quantum computing.

authors.name: Axel van de Walle

papers.title: Topology of the Fermi surface and universality of the metal-metal and metal-insulator transitions: $d$-dimensional Hatsugai-Kohmoto model as an example
papers.summary: The earlier theory \cite{Chitov:2025} of the quantum phase transitions related to the change of the Fermi Surface Topology (FST) is advanced. For such transitions the Fermi surface as a quantum critical manifold determined by the Lee-Yang zeros, the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ as the $d$-volume of the Fermi sea, and the special FST universality class were introduced in \cite{Chitov:2025}. The exactly solvable Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) $d$-dimensional ($d=1,2,3$) model of interacting fermions is analyzed. We explore the relation between the Lee-Yang zeros, the Luttinger and the plateau (Oshikawa) theorems. The validity of the Luttinger theorem in the HK model is confirmed. It is shown that the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ and the FST universality class describe the transitions between metal and band/Mott insulators, as well as the Lifshitz and van Hove gapless-to-gapless transitions. The gapless phases are established to be the ferromagnetic Fermi liquids (metals), where the quantum critical manifold is also a locus of ferromagnetic order with spontaneous breaking of the rotational symmetry occurring at $T=0$. In addition to the conventional paradigm with a continuous order parameter, we apply the homology theory to analyze the FST transitions. They are critical points of the Morse function. To quantify FST we use the Euler characteristic, which is calculated for each phase of the HK model. We claim that the FST universality class is robust with respect to interactions and other model details, under the condition that the conduction band function is smooth and the critical points are non-degenerate.

authors.name: Gennady Y. Chitov

papers.title: Genuine quantum scars in Floquet chaotic many-body systems
papers.summary: Unstable periodic orbits act as organizing structures for classical chaotic systems and underpin quantum scarring. Long known in single-particle systems, genuine quantum scars based on unstable periodic orbits have been recently extended to isolated many-body systems for time-independent Hamiltonians. Their fate under periodic driving, however, remains largely uncharted, challenged by the expectation that these systems should in general heat to infinite temperature. Here, we investigate how genuine scarring competes with the drive in a Floquet many-body system. Using chaotic spin chains, we demonstrate that Floquet states remain scarred in the high-frequency limit. Beyond this static correspondence, we uncover additional, driving-induced Floquet scars with no static analog. We construct a rich dynamical stability diagram with intermediate-frequency regimes of enhanced and quenched scarring, which we understand with a classical analysis of the Lyapunov exponent. Our results position Floquet systems as a natural platform for tuning the scarring behavior of quantum many-body systems.

authors.name: Harald Schmid, Andrea Pizzi, Johannes Knolle

papers.title: Design and Analysis of Quantum Dual-Containing CSS LDPC Codes based on Quasi-Dyadic Matrices
papers.summary: Quantum error correcting codes are essential to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computation. This work introduces two constructions of high-rate, dual-containing (DC) Calderbank--Shor--Steane low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes based on quasi-dyadic matrices. We characterize the automorphism group of such codes, investigate their minimum distance behavior, and provide several theoretical results on their cycle properties. Monte Carlo simulations under depolarizing and phenomenological noise show better finite-length logical error rates than the considered DC benchmark codes and competitive performance against several state-of-the-art quantum LDPC code families. Finally, we employ an automorphism-ensemble belief propagation decoder to improve their decoding performance.

authors.name: Alessio Baldelli, Marco Baldi, Massimo Battaglioni, Franco Chiaraluce, Paolo Santini

papers.title: Quantum statistics in an extended collider coupled to a qubit
papers.summary: Mesoscopic colliders provide an effective platform for probing the mutual statistics of quantum particles. Recent experiments have successfully extracted the mutual statistics of fermions, and more exotic anyons using quantum point contacts (QPCs). Coupling a point-like collider, such as a quantum point contact, to a two-level impurity or qubit can induce statistical transmutation of fermions, causing them to display boson-like bunching tendencies. Here, we extend the analysis to an extended collider. We investigate the scattering of two incoming fermionic and bosonic wave packets in the presence of postselection on the impurity state, and systematically analyze the possible benchmarks used to characterize bunching and infer the underlying mutual statistics. We show that only a specific benchmark faithfully captures the mutual statistics of the colliding particles, while alternative choices can produce spurious statistical signatures. Hence, the correct benchmark for probing the quantum statistics depends on the intricate details of the mesoscopic collider.

authors.name: Rishav Chaudhuri, Sai Satyam Samal

papers.title: Breathing mode of quantum droplets in dipolar quantum gases: A sum-rule analysis
papers.summary: We investigate theoretically the ground-state properties and breathing-mode collective excitations of three-dimensional dipolar Bose gases in anisotropic harmonic traps incorporating quantum fluctuations. Combining a Gaussian variational ansatz with a sum-rule analysis, we derive explicit analytical expressions for both axial and radial breathing-mode frequencies, which are validated by numerical solutions of the time-dependent extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Our theoretical predictions show great agreement with existing experimental data for $^{166}$Er and $^{162}$Dy gases. By constructing comprehensive phase diagrams across the parameter space of the $s$-wave scattering length, atom number, and trap aspect ratio, we reveal both discontinuous first-order phase transitions and smooth crossovers between the dilute Bose-Einstein condensate and dense quantum droplet phases. We confirm that the enhanced incompressibility induced by quantum fluctuations significantly elevates the breathing-mode frequencies in the droplet phase compared with conventional weakly interacting Bose gases. Furthermore, the system undergoes a phase transition and a crossover over the scattering length under the elongated and flattened confinements, characterized by discontinuous jumps and continuous crossovers in peak density and atomic cloud sizes, respectively. Our work offers a useful analytical framework to characterize collective excitations in dipolar quantum gases, providing quantitative insights for forthcoming ultracold atom experiments in lanthanide atoms and polar molecules.

authors.name: Xinran Zhang, Junli Liu, Huiyun Xiao, Xiao-Long Chen, Yunbo Zhang

papers.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
papers.summary: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\to\tau$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(\tau/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.

authors.name: Joon Hyung Lee

papers.title: Such stuff as magic is made on: compact operator algebra, stabilizer polytope and the structure of reduced density matrices in a Kitaev spin liquid
papers.summary: Quantum many-body systems exhibit rich and complex behaviour. Magic has recently emerged as a powerful new diagnostic for probing such systems, complementing other key features such as many-body entanglement. Here, starting from an investigation of the onset of magic within subsystems of a larger many-body quantum system, we show that intricate structures emerge which shed important light on the underlying many-body physics. Focusing on the Kitaev honeycomb model, we first identify the temperature below which local subsystems acquire magic. Remarkably, we find that the optimal magic witnesses active at the onset of magic reveal compact operator spaces that continue to capture the local thermal states throughout their subsequent evolution. For the six-site hexagonal marginal, this connection can be made stronger: the same operator space emerges independently from the symmetries of the local marginal and forms the symmetry-resolved plaquette algebra. When these symmetries are realized exactly, the local state lies entirely within this algebra and the reduced robustness of magic is equal to the full robustness of magic. The same reduced description can also be applied to other local quantum resources, which we illustrate using genuine multipartite entanglement. Furthermore, the operator spaces possess a rich algebraic structure in the form of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, with a natural interpretation in terms of bond and bond-cycle operators. Our general methodology therefore show how the onset of local magic can reveal a compact, physically meaningful operator structure underlying the finite-temperature Kitaev spin liquid, and opens up a new avenue towards reduced descriptions of quantum resources in many-body systems.

authors.name: Snigdh Sabharwal, Nic Shannon, Paul Skrzypczyk

papers.title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
papers.summary: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $q(\beta)$ depending on a parameter $\beta$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $\beta\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $q(\beta)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at inverse temperature $\beta$. In that case, the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (also known as unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of R{\'e}nyi $\alpha$-entropies as $\beta\to\infty$.

authors.name: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Jakub Czartowski, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligab\`o

papers.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
papers.summary: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

authors.name: Franz Luef, Eduard Ortega

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning of formation energies and band gaps in hybrid perovskites through SHAP analysis and SISSO modelling
papers.summary: Accurate and interpretable property prediction is essential for exploring hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. Here, we combine machine-learning screening with SHAP analysis and SISSO descriptor discovery. Using 4,456 compounds, optimized XGBoost models achieved test-set $R^2$ values of 0.99 for formation energy and 0.93 for band gap and were applied to over 180,000 candidates. Comparison across approximately 17,000 common compounds revealed broadly overlapping distributions from XGBoost and CGCNN but substantially lower predictions from UPET, suggesting potential limitations in its transferability to hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. SHAP analysis and correlation-based pruning retained eight primary features for each property, from which SISSO derived expressions comprising four nonlinear descriptors. These expressions couple molecular and inorganic properties for formation energy and emphasize relative atomic sizes and B-site characteristics for band gap. This framework supports efficient candidate prioritization and interpretable analysis of learned structures-property relationships in hybrid perovskites.

authors.name: Christopher Xia, Hao Zhang, Qingyuan Jin

papers.title: Hierarchical Design of Ambidirectional LCE Sheets for Three-State Gaussian Shape Morphs
papers.summary: Modulation of surface curvature is a commonly exploited strategy to achieve adaptability within natural and synthetic systems where structure governs function. While Gaussian curvature of inextensible surfaces is fixed, surfaces made of extensible materials can adapts their Gaussian curvature under strain, unlocking capabilities such as locomotion, dynamic coloration, and tunable stiffness. This feature is commonly exploited to develop soft actuators capable of complex functionalities; however, traversing the entire spectrum of Gaussian curvature was previously difficult to achieve without the use of multi-material constructs or spatially varied stimulus fields. In this work, we present a strategy for generating a diverse range of dynamic Gaussian shape morphs using multiphase liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) as ambidirectionally deforming building blocks. Taking advantage of the materials sequential contraction and elongation during phase transitions, we design and investigate the deformation response of radially aligned flat LCE sheets which consecutively morph into negatively and positively curved flat surfaces in response to monotonically increasing temperature. We then investigate the influence of mesoscale asymmetry and macroscale geometry on curvature magnitude and bending symmetry, thereby demonstrating that a single form factor can be programmed to undergo a rich library of deformation behaviors. Finally, inspired by the strategy of cephalopods to couple mechanical deformability to dynamic optical properties, we fabricate a structurally colored LCE sheet which couples its dynamic Gaussian curvature to a dynamic color-changing response. This approach offers a route toward adaptive structures capable of multistate shape reconfiguration for applications in soft robotics, deployable systems, and responsive surfaces.

authors.name: Atalaya Milan Wilborn, Gurminder K. Paink, Raphael Kay, Patryk Wasik, Friedrich Stricker, Jacopo Movilli, Shucong Li, Joanna Aizenberg

papers.title: Topology and Information in Regularized Transport on Graphs
papers.summary: We study how two geometries of mass on a finite graph interact: the information geometry of the generalized entropy $F_q$ used for regularized transport, and the arithmetic of divisors governed by the Riemann--Roch theorem of Baker and Norine and by the Jacobian. Because the correction term of $F_q$ is affine, $F_q$-regularization at strength $\gamma$ is Tsallis regularization at temperature $\gamma/q$. Over the reals, chip-firing connects all configurations of equal degree, so the Jacobian enters transport only through integrality. We introduce the transport defect, the worst-case cost of steering $d$ chips towards a target by chip-firing, and prove $1/d\le\delta_{\TV}(D)\le(d-r(D))/d=(g-1-r(K-D))/d\le\min(1,g/d)$ whenever $g\ge1$; vertex multiplicities give a lower bound and an equality criterion. A regularized topological gap $\Gamma_{q,\gamma}(D,E)$ tends to the chip-move defect as $\gamma\to0$, lies in an explicit window, has a high-temperature slope given by Tsallis coupling entropies, and admits a positive regime if and only if $g\ge1$. Dual potentials certify exactly the convex relaxation of a linear system; the remainder is an integrality gap. Zeros in optimal plans occur only for $q>1$, by a mechanism different from the sign change of $\Gamma$. Exact computations on $1784$ divisor classes find the rank bound $(d-r(D))/d$ attained in $1769$ of them, an observed frequency. Experiments on honeycomb and Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi networks with $10^2$ to $10^5$ nodes test the statements on regularized plans, not $\Gamma$; over $10^3\le n\le10^5$ their transport costs are consistent with growth like $n^{1/2}$ and $\log n$, respectively.

authors.name: Shintaro Yoshizawa

papers.title: Enhancement of the magnetorheological effect using discontinuous shear thickening with a mixture of magnetic and non magnetic particles
papers.summary: The phenomenon of discontinuous shear thickening (DST) is observed in suspensions of solid particles with a very high-volume fraction. Using a suspension of magnetic particles at high-volume fraction we have, for the first time, demonstrated experimentally the presence of a frictional network of particles by a simultaneous measurement of the electrical resistance of the suspension and of the rheological curve. An obstacle for the applications of MRS remains the sedimentation and aggregation linked to the high density of the iron microparticles. We have recently found that a small fraction of ferromagnetic particles within a concentrated suspension of calcium carbonate particles is not only sufficient to trigger the transition by application of a magnetic field but also optimum for the amplitude of the jump in viscosity observed in DST. We shall explain this result from stress transmission between the magnetic particles and nonmagnetic ones, both inserted in the percolated network of particles. We will also highlight the role of the polyelectrolyte adsorbed on the surface of the particles in the DST transition through the balance between the repulsive entropic force between two layers of polymer adsorbed on different particles and the magnetic attraction force.

authors.name: Georges Bossis (INPHYNI), Yan Grasselli (INPHYNI), Olga Volkova (INPHYNI)

papers.title: A transversely isotropic constitutive model for semisoft elasticity in main-chain liquid crystal elastomers
papers.summary: Monodomain main-chain liquid crystal elastomers exhibit pronounced stiffness anisotropy and broad semisoft plateaus following finite onset strains. At fixed chain anisotropy, the neo-classical model predicts equal principal Young's moduli, while its transversely isotropic extension with a constant semisoft modulus constrains the relation between reorientation onset and subsequent stress growth. We develop a finite-strain, isothermal elastic model combining transversely isotropic network elasticity with a deformation-dependent quadratic semisoft penalty. Within a weak-fluctuation approximation, a reduced statistical closure based on assumed linear contraction of effective local anisotropy fluctuations at fixed mean anisotropy yields an exponential transition from an initial to a residual semisoft modulus. The network energy preserves ideal soft modes, and the formulation recovers the de Gennes strain-director coupling in the infinitesimal limit. Analytical relations for perpendicular tension show that the rotating-stage stress depends on both the current semisoft modulus and its derivative with respect to the first deformation invariant. This permits a finite onset followed by a substantially flatter rotating response than in the constant-modulus limit. Oblique tension couples director rotation, shear and lateral contraction. Comparisons with orientation-dependent measurements using a common parameter set capture the principal stiffness contrast and broad perpendicular plateau, with discrepancies remaining in oblique stresses and intermediate-angle initial moduli.

authors.name: Donghao Li, Xin Yi, Fan Feng

papers.title: Superconductivity in the Metallic Wigner Crystals of Rhombohedral Graphene: Possible Realization of an Electronic Supersolid
papers.summary: Recent experiments on rhombohedral multilayer graphene have reported metallic Wigner crystals (MWCs), in which spontaneously broken translational symmetry coexists with mobile charge carriers. Their proximity to time-reversal-symmetry-breaking superconductivity raises the intriguing possibility that collective excitations of the electron crystal mediate pairing among the residual itinerant carriers, giving rise to a superconducting Wigner crystal---an electronic analog of a supersolid. Here we investigate this possibility using a realistic model of electron-doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene with spin and valley polarization, whose low symmetry removes the usual Cooper instability. We use self-consistent and time-dependent Hartree-Fock theory to map the evolution of the self-doping fraction and characterize the collective-mode spectrum of the MWCs, followed by a multiband linearized Eliashberg analysis of pairing. Upon increasing density, we find an instability of the MWC, triggered by a weakly dispersing unoccupied band approaching the chemical potential. Pairing remains weak deep in the stable MWC. However, on approaching the instability, we identify a collective mode composed of interband electron-hole excitations that softens. We show that this mode drives pairing at experimentally relevant temperatures. The leading pairing instability is at finite momentum and combines Fermi surface states with states in the incipient band, making a Fermi surface or single-band pairing analysis inadequate. Our results establish collective-mode-mediated superconductivity in MWCs as a viable scenario for rhombohedral graphene and motivate experimental searches for coexisting electronic charge order in its superconducting phases.

authors.name: F\'elix Desrochers, Mark R. Hirsbrunner, Yong Baek Kim, Ashvin Vishwanath

papers.title: Energy-resolved current response and the crossover between two approximately linear-in-$T$ resistivity regimes in the infinite-$U$ Hubbard model
papers.summary: We study charge transport in the two-dimensional infinite-$U$ Hubbard model with hopping amplitude $t$ using full exact diagonalization (ED) on $N=16$- and $18$-site square clusters with a single doped hole. We first provide a proof, treating degeneracies explicitly, that a constant dc $f_x$ function, defined as the sum of the squared current matrix elements connecting eigenstates at a given energy to eigenstates of nearly the same energy, averaged over degenerate initial states, is necessary and sufficient for strictly linear-in-$T$ resistivity: $\rho_x(T)=\alpha T$ for all $T>0$ with a constant $\alpha$. The numerically extrapolated dc $f_x$ is not exactly constant, but it is approximately flat over a broad region in the interior of the many-body spectrum and varies strongly within a scale $\varepsilon_{f_x}$ of the spectral edges. This scale $\varepsilon_{f_x}$ is related to a characteristic temperature $T_{\mathrm{cr}}$, which quantifies the leading departure of the resistivity from high-temperature linearity upon cooling. Within the studied temperature range $T/t \geq 0.05$, our ED resistivity results reveal a gradual crossover between high- and low-temperature approximately linear-in-$T$ regimes, with characteristic crossover temperatures $T_{\mathrm{cr}}/t\approx0.414$ and $0.467$ for $N=16$ and $18$, respectively. We also find a broad specific-heat peak associated with this gradual crossover, at $T/t \approx 0.70$ and $0.68$ for $N=16$ and $18$, respectively.

authors.name: Shuo Liu, Aman Kumar, Yuhao Ma, Philip W. Phillips, Hitesh J. Changlani, B. Andrei Bernevig

papers.title: Mimicry of $\textit{d}$-wave Andreev Signatures by Interlayer Pairing
papers.summary: The recent discovery of high-$T_{\rm c}$ superconductivity in bilayer nickelates has attracted enormous attention. Despite dominant theoretical studies pointing to interlayer pairing, the pairing symmetry is strongly debated due to conflicting evidence on nodeless bulk gaps and $d$-wave-like transport signatures. Here, we demonstrate that a nodeless interlayer pairing can naturally mimic $d$-wave Andreev signatures when the point contact is not evenly coupled to the two layers. The phenomenon can be understood by recognizing how a contact potential, which is odd under the layer-exchanging mirror symmetry, acts like an effective Zeeman field on the layer pseudospin. This pseudo field then binds in-gap Andreev states that sweep through the gap with the width and strength of the barrier. We further demonstrate in a realistic model for La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ that the simulated subgap conductance for a top-layer barrier can reproduce the orientation dependent ZBCP usually interpreted as a fingerprint of $\textit{d}$-wave pairing. By revealing this mirror-selective Andreev response from an interlayer pairing state, our work offers a natural scenario to reconcile the conflicting experimental evidence in bilayer nickelates and advances our understanding of unconventional superconductivity.

authors.name: Zhongyi Zhang, Shengshan Qin, Chui-Zhen Chen, Hoi Chun Po, Jiangping Hu, Xianxin Wu

papers.title: Controlled Oxidation of Tellurium Nanoparticles for Telecom Detection
papers.summary: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. At 1550 nm, the device exhibits rise and fall times of 17.7 and 40.2 s, respectively, and an estimated shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 1.3 * 10^6 Jones. These findings highlight the importance of controlling surface oxidation to balance interparticle charge transport and dark-current suppression, offering insights for the development of solution-processed Te-based photodetectors for short-wave infrared applications.

authors.name: Biman Jana

papers.title: Hidden memory above the Neel temperature programs antiferromagnetic order in Cr2O3
papers.summary: Control of antiferromagnetic order is central to magnetoelectric and antiferromagnetic spintronic devices. In the prototypical magnetoelectric antiferromagnet Cr2O3, domains are conventionally selected by simultaneous application of electric and magnetic fields during cooling through the Neel temperature (T_N) or at a fixed temperature below T_N. Here, we show that antiferromagnetic order can instead be programmed by electric-field conditioning entirely in the paramagnetic state above T_N. By measuring the magnetoelectric coefficient (alpha_zz) of bulk Cr2O3 crystals under different thermal and field histories, we find that a sufficiently large electric field above T_N establishes a reversible state that persists after the field is removed. Subsequent magnetic-field cooling with no applied electric field produces a single-domain state with the opposite Neel-vector orientation from conventional magnetoelectric field cooling. The electrically induced state can be reversibly written, erased, and allowed to relax at high temperatures, demonstrating a long-lived internal electric bias that governs domain selection. The observed behavior is consistent with a metastable surface-associated polar state that may generate this internal bias. These results reveal an unexpected coupling between electrically programmed memory and antiferromagnetic domain formation in Cr2O3.

authors.name: Josiah Keagy, Sumukh Mahesh, Wei-Cheng Liao, Jing Shi

papers.title: Optimizing one-dimensional lithographically defined nanowires in semiconducting heterostructures
papers.summary: One-dimensional nanowires can host remarkable electronic properties and are central to studying quantum transport. Although heterostructure-defined confinement combined with gate-defined potentials can greatly reduce the effects of impurities as measured via electron mobilities, the realization and interpretation of novel effects at this scale are complicated by disorder. Experiments on lithographically defined one-dimensional nanowires therefore do not exhibit ideal behavior. Using theoretical and computational models, we predict that optimizing the geometry of split gates in semiconducting heterostructures will lead to higher-quality channels for transport measurements. Further, we show that this optimization is essential for resolving features of interest such as the Rashba-induced spin gap. This new approach to lithographically defined conduction channels provides better energy resolution and is less susceptible to disorder.

authors.name: Leah Tom, Yik Kheng Lee, Karina L. Hudson, Krittika Kumar, Jackson S. Smith, Alex R. Hamilton, S. N. Coppersmith, Jared H. Cole, Mark Friesen

papers.title: Current-voltage characteristics of layered cuprate superconductors with intrinsic Josephson junctions
papers.summary: A brief review of the results for the current-voltage characteristics study in highly anisotropic cuprate superconductors is presented, considering the existence of the intrinsic Josephson effect in multilayer HTSC compounds. We analyzed the observations of multi-branch current-voltage characteristics for current in the c-direction both for the hole-doped and electron-doped cuprate SCs wich conveniently viewed as a strack of intrinsic Josephson junctions, where the CuO2 layers serve as superconducting plates and the buffer layers as dielectric interlayers. It was shown that the tunneling characteristics of intrinsic Josephson junctions in optimally doped p- and n-type cuprates indicate a predominantly d-wave symmetry of the order parameter, demonstrating high conductivity in the subgap regime: U < 2delta/e. The analysis carried out confirms the theoretically predicted power-law dependences U ~ I^gamma with gamma = (0.33 - 0.50) in the hole-doped Bi- and Tl-compounds, which is typical for SCs with monotonic dx^2-y^2 - wave symmetry of the order parameter and with gamma = (0.70 - 0.76) for electron-doped SCs with a non-monotonic d-wave symmetry within the framework of the two-band/two-gap model.

authors.name: T. B. Charikova, V. N. Neverov, M. R. Popov, S. D. Popov, N. G. Shelushinina

papers.title: Temperature-Driven Evolution of Magnetization Dynamics in Cobalt-Doped Fe$_5$GeTe$_2$
papers.summary: Understanding magnetization dynamics in metallic van der Waals ferromagnets is essential to uncover their magnetic interactions and evaluate their potential for high-frequency spintronics applications. In this study, we investigate the temperature-dependent magnetization dynamics of a single crystal of cobalt-doped $Fe_{5}GeTe_{2}$ (CFGT) using broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy. At high temperatures, the FMR response is dominated by a single broad resonance that shifts toward lower magnetic fields upon cooling. Fits to the frequency dependence of the resonance field and linewidth yield an effective $g$ factor of approximately 2.45 and an effective Gilbert damping parameter of approximately 0.15 near room temperature. The effective magnetic anisotropy evolves strongly with temperature, with an increasingly pronounced easy-plane contribution upon cooling toward 200 K. Below approximately 200 K, an additional resonance emerges and evolves into a distinct two-mode response that persists to the lowest measured temperature of 25 K. The two branches exhibit different temperature dependences of their resonance fields and linewidths, and the emergence of the additional mode is not accompanied by a comparably pronounced anomaly in the static magnetization. These results reveal a dynamical crossover in CFGT that is not readily apparent from bulk magnetometry and highlight the sensitivity of FMR to the magnetic behavior of chemically substituted van der Waals ferromagnets.

authors.name: Sourabh Singh, Soumik Aon, Andrew F. May, Joost Ridderbos, Ramanathan Mahendiran, Wilfred G. van der Wiel

papers.title: A Transport-Constrained Gradient-Flow Description of Continuum Dislocation Dynamics
papers.summary: Gradient flow frameworks are fundamental to numerous models of defect and microstructure evolution. This work develops a gradient flow formulation for continuum dislocation dynamics, with the key distinction that the admissible rates are transport-constrained. Using the dislocation density and compatible slip fields as the primary state variables, their admissible rates are restricted by geometric conservation laws. The corresponding transport velocities are then selected variationally through a constrained Onsager principle. The resulting model has both a variational gradient flow structure and consistency with the geometric dislocation conservation statement; existing models of dislocation evolution typically have either one or the other feature. This thermodynamic structure provides a dislocation driving force that includes elastic stress contributions -- corresponding to the classical Peach--Koehler force -- as well as contributions from the core and nonconvex lattice energies. A simplified version of the model is used to study the energetics and dynamics of an opposite-sign dislocation pair. The lattice energy keeps the cores compact, and an external applied shear either assists annihilation or, above a threshold, separates the pair.

authors.name: Paria Behnoud, Anthony Rollett, Carlos Mora-Corral, Kaushik Dayal

papers.title: On the nature of low-energy electronic states in twisted bilayer graphene: a first-principles study
papers.summary: The nature of low-energy electronic states in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the magic angle has been extensively discussed in the literature on qualitative grounds, since these states play a key role in the construction of effective few-band models toward a many-body theory. Here, we report extensive and systematic first-principles calculations of TBG electronic states in the magic-angle range, using density functional theory with no further approximations. We construct moir\'e-scale localized Wannier states for the low-energy bands and develop an effective ten-band model for each $K$ valley. The Wannier orbitals contain both atomic and moir\'e-scale details and are centered near the high-symmetry stackings in the moir\'e cell. We calculate Coulomb and exchange integrals of these localized states, quantities that are the basic ingredients in many-body models. We also compare the values of these integrals to those obtained or assumed in previous works. By symmetrizing the ten-band Hamiltonians and basis orbitals, we provide insight into how the dominant hoppings between the flat-band orbitals evolve as a function of twist angle.

authors.name: Albert Zhu, Daniel Bennett, Daniel T. Larson, Mohammed M. Al Ezzi, Efstratios Manousakis, Efthimios Kaxiras

papers.title: Atomically abrupt sp-sp$^2$ all-carbon heterojunction preserving the electronic identity of constituent allotropes
papers.summary: Covalently integrating distinct carbon allotropes with atomic precision remains, to date, elusive, despite the clear advantage of combining complementary functionalities while preserving their electronic identities. Here, we realize an all-carbon lateral heterojunction combining ($sp^2$) armchair graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) and $sp$-$sp^2$ hydrogenated graphdiyne (hGDY) on Au(111) through Fe-mediated hierarchical on-surface synthesis. Low-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy combined with density-functional theory reveal an atomically abrupt (<0.5 nm), asymmetric type-I interface. Redistribution of an edge-localized GNR state onto the first hGDY unit demonstrates local electronic continuity, whereas their characteristic electronic structures re-emerge immediately beyond the interface. Calculations further indicate that heterojunction formation weakens the interaction of both constituents with the underlying Au(111) substrate, widening their gaps and reducing adsorption-induced interfacial polarization. These results establish lateral covalent integration as a route to engineer atomically defined electronic interfaces and substrate coupling in all-carbon nanostructures.

authors.name: Alice Cartoceti, Masoumeh Alihosseini, Gianni Conti, Eliecer Pelaez-Sifonte, Alessio Orbelli Biroli, Francesco Sedona, Paolo D'Agosta, Francesco Tumino, Andrea Li Bassi, Jorge Lobo-Checa, Carlo S. Casari, Simona Achilli

papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
papers.summary: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidity for one day. These results demonstrate that mica substrates enable high-mobility, flex-out-compatible In2O3-based TFTs.

authors.name: Hyeonjun Kong, Ping-Hsein Wu, Xian-Ye Jiang, Yasutaka Matsuo, Ying-Hao Chu, Hiromichi Ohta

papers.title: Discovery of Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line Topological State in strongly correlated material CeAuAl$_3$
papers.summary: Kramers nodal lines (KNLs) are predicted in all achiral, non-centrosymmetric crystal structures, and yet there are very few experimental realizations of KNLs, only in weakly correlated systems. Especially, their realization in strongly correlated systems remains unexplored. Here we investigate KNL topology in the non-centrosymmetric, achiral Kondo lattice CeAuAl$_3$, using magnetotransport, thermodynamic measurements, density functional theory (DFT), and tight-binding toy model calculations. We find that CeAuAl$_3$ hosts KNLs in the $\mathit{\Gamma}\text{-}Z$ and $X\text{-}P$ directions, protected by time-reversal and mirror symmetries. Breaking of these crystalline symmetries, along with time-reversal symmetry via spin polarization, lifts the KNL degeneracy, which, in turn, generates Berry curvature resulting in an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE). More importantly, CeAuAl$_3$ shows large AHE not only below the magnetic ordering temperature $T_N$ but rather below the Kondo temperature. This underscores the role of the Kondo correlations in bringing the KNLs at the Fermi surface rather than at accidental energies, as would be expected without correlations. Our work identifies a new topological state, Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line, with CeAuAl$_3$ being the first compound explicitly identified to host this new correlated topological state, and demonstrating the expected AHE associated with it. More generally, our work outlines the pathway for finding Kondo-KNL systems in all compounds that combine achiral, non-centrosymmetric structure with Kondo correlations.

authors.name: Hari Bhandari, Kevin Allen, Kuan-Sen Li, Yuan Fang, Arushi, Karthik Rao, Mounica Mahankali, Sanu Mishra, Jian-Xin Zhu, Christopher Lane, Qimiao Si, Emilia Morosan

papers.title: Momentum-Resolved Kondo Hybridization of Nonsymmorphic Dirac-Derived Bands in CeAgBi$_2$
papers.summary: How symmetry-constrained conduction states acquire heavy-quasiparticle character is a central question in correlated quantum materials. Combining angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, Ce $4d \rightarrow 4f$ resonant photoemission, and first-principles calculations, we investigate the nonsymmorphic Kondo lattice CeAgBi$_2$. We identify quasi-two-dimensional Bi-square-net-derived bands consistent with calculated Dirac crossings and nodal lines. Resonant photoemission resolves a nearly dispersionless Ce 4$f$ band near the Fermi level, establishing Kondo heavy-quasiparticle states. Its pronounced momentum-dependent spectral weight at intersections with the identified Dirac-derived branches provides direct spectroscopic evidence for their participation in $c$-$f$ hybridization. Complementary measurements on independently cleaved samples and an effective hybridization model connect these branches to the Kondo heavy-quasiparticle spectrum. The combined results support preservation of nonsymmorphic Dirac-band connectivity under Kondo renormalization, showing how symmetry-constrained conduction states become constituents of correlated heavy quasiparticles.

authors.name: Yang Luo, Hao Liu, Zhong-Tuo Fu, Qi-Yi Wu, Bo Chen, Zheng-Tai Liu, Mao Ye, Da-Wei Shen, Chen Zhang, Ying Zhou, Cun-Hui Lyu, Jin-Dong Bai, Zi-Jie Xu, Hai-Long Deng, Zhen-Xing Wu, Jun-Jie Wu, Sai-Chao Deng, Yu-Xia Duan, Jian-Qiao Meng

papers.title: Multifractality in sputtered crystalline and amorphous transition metal nitride thin films
papers.summary: In this work, we present evidence for multifractal growth in Titanium and Niobium nitride thin films on different substrates. Self-similar multifractal structures such as dendrites and multi-branched snowflake-like structures are reported. The fractal dimensions are controlled by a combination of processing parameters and conditions at the film-substrate interface. Significantly, fractal growth is observed not only in crystalline films on crystalline and amorphous substrates but also on amorphous films on crystalline substrates. The 2D Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (2D MFDFA) carried out on the scanning electron micrographs, clearly reveals the multifractal nature of the nitride thin films. The statistical moments were varied between -5 to +5. The Hausdorff dimensions for the TiN films are in the range of 1.65 to 1.79 while it is 1.64 to 1.74 for the NbN thin films. It is proposed that the observed multifractality is due to a competition between morphological instabilities and Diffusion-Limited Aggregation

authors.name: K. Anantha Padmanabhan, Kuraganti Vasu, P. Manimaran, M. Ghanashyam Krishna

papers.title: Transverse quasiparticle heat transport in p-wave magnetic Josephson junctions
papers.summary: We study transverse heat currents carried by Bogoliubov quasiparticles in $p$-wave magnetic Josephson junctions under a longitudinal temperature bias. We find that such a junction supports a transverse spin heat current while the net transverse heat current vanishes. This effect stems from the $p$-wave magnetism, which shifts the two spin sectors oppositely in transverse momentum space and thereby causes them to carry opposite heat currents. A weak Zeeman field lifts the compensation between the two spin-sector contributions, thereby generating a finite net transverse heat current. The directions of both currents can be switched by reversing the sign of the $p$-wave magnetic splitting or tuning the superconducting phase difference, while both currents vanish in the absence of $p$-wave magnetism. These findings highlight $p$-wave magnetic Josephson junctions as a versatile platform for switchable transverse heat transport and controllable spin caloritronics.

authors.name: Jin-Xing Hou, Pritam Chatterjee, Song-Bo Zhang

papers.title: Extended No-Go Theorem and Its Verification in Spin-Selective Transport through Chiral Cyclodextrin Assemblies
papers.summary: The classical two-terminal single-channel no-go theorem relies on time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and scattering-matrix unitarity. In open systems, omitted channels or environment leakage break unitarity, so TRS and the symplectic reciprocity symmetry TRS\(^{\dagger}\) are no longer equivalent, invalidating the classical premises. We prove that if the two-terminal single-channel scattering matrix satisfies TRS\(^{\dagger}\) plus central inversion symmetry, transmission remains no spin selectivity; this result provides an important complement to the classical no-go theorem in nonunitary regime. When these conditions are violated or the single-channel constraint is lifted, spin-selective transport occurs. In charge transport through devices based on chiral \(\gamma\)-cyclodextrin molecular assemblies, we verify separately the classical no-go theorem in unitary case and its supplementary version together with its multichannel corollary in nonunitary case: when the conditions for the corresponding no-go theorem hold, the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) of the assembly disappears, whereas when they are violated, CISS emerges. These results extend the no-go theorem to nonunitary scattering systems and establish an effective theoretical framework for studying CISS in real molecular assemblies.

authors.name: Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, Hua-Hua Fu

papers.title: Pseudogap in hole doped cuprates: a status report
papers.summary: The pseudogap state, an anomalous momentum dependent partial suppression of low energy electronic excitations persisting well above the superconducting critical temperature in underdoped cuprates, remains one of the most profound enigmas in condensed physics today. This review summarizes over three decades of experimental and theoretical progress. It appears that pseudogap is not a mere precursor to superconductivity, but a distinct, intertwined state of matter characterized by a complex interplay of competing and cooperating electronic orders. We critically examine the bulk probes like resistivity and magnetic susceptibility and the surface hallmark spectroscopic signatures observed via angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) in this review. ARPES reveals a Fermi surface truncated into disconnected segments and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) visualizes a spatially heterogeneous energy gap around the Fermi level. These observations are contextualized alongside transport anomalies, including resistivity and bulk magnetic susceptibility, to construct a phenomenological portrait of a phase that violates conventional Fermi liquid theory. By mapping the electronic phase diagram, we highlight the abrupt transition at above optimal doping. We conclude with open questions still to be answered. This review underscores the role of the pseudogap as a key to unlocking the unconventional pairing mechanism of hole doped cuprates and the broader physics of strongly correlated electron systems.

authors.name: Saleh Hasan Naqib, Raihana Shams Islam

papers.title: Dopant Cluster Engineering for Tunable Room-Temperature Ferromagnetism in 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
papers.summary: Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (2D-TMDs) offer a promising platform for realizing dilute magnetic semiconductors. However, simultaneously achieving large magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) and high Curie temperature (T$_\text{c}$) remains a major challenge. In this work, we employ DFT+U to systematically investigate the thermodynamic stability and magnetic properties of 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ doped with transition metal atoms. We found that the paired dopant configurations are more stable than previously attributed isolated dopants. Despite their nearly identical crystal structures, 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ show contrasting properties upon doping. All paired dopants in 2D-MoSe$_2$ exhibit long-range ferromagnetic coupling (FMC) primarily due to carrier-mediated exchange interactions, whereas those in 2D-WSe$_2$ show weak exchange coupling. Interestingly, 2Mn$_\text{2W}$ shows a transition from less stable antiferromagnetic coupling (AFMC) in the short range to highly stable FMC in the long-range. The combined effect of spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, and orbital hybridization gives rise to a large MAE with maximum in-plane values of $-$3.5 meV for 2V$_\text{2Mo}$ and $-$3.2 meV for 2Mn$_\text{2W}$. Monte Carlo simulations estimate T$_\text{c}$ $\simeq$ 440 K for 2Fe$_\text{2Mo}$ and ensure its high-temperature stability in 2D-MoSe$_2$. Our results establish dopant clustering as an effective route to engineer high-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D-TMDs and highlight their potential for nano-spintronic applications.

authors.name: Shivangee, Sachin Grewal, Akash Singh

papers.title: Quartet ferromagnetism in the small-exchange limit
papers.summary: Rare-earth magnets are often regarded as classical owing to their large angular momentum J, but this picture breaks down when exchange is smaller than the crystalline electric-field (CEF) energy scale, allowing the degeneracy of low-lying CEF manifolds to dictate the emergent quantum phases. Here, we uncover such a regime in the RV6Sn6 (R = rare-earth) kagome metals with strong magnetic anisotropy. Thermodynamic and neutron-diffraction measurements reveal successive axial and tilted ferromagnetic (FM) phases in DyV6Sn6, arising from independent ordering of the axial Mz and transverse Mx dipolar components enabled by a rare quasi-quartet ground state. On the other hand, HoV6Sn6 has a similar tilted magnetic anisotropy, but remains axial down to 0.03 K.
