papers.title: Lightweight Neural Prediction for MDCT-Based Perceptual Audio Coding
papers.summary: Perceptual audio codecs often use predictive coding to further reduce signal redundancy. Rather than learning the entire codec pipeline end-to-end, we insert a small neural network as a drop-in, deterministic predictor in an otherwise conventional codec: the network estimates the next Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) coefficient block from a short context of reconstructed blocks, and the encoder transmits the quantized residual. We compare Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictors against a non-predictive baseline and a per-line Normalized Least Mean Squares (NLMS) linear predictor (similar to the MPEG-2 AAC Main Profile predictor). The CNN consistently outperforms the MLP, the linear predictor, and the baseline in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), noise-to-mask ratio (NMR), and MUSHRA evaluation scores. Using a 512-sample analysis window (w = 512), our neural predictors recover, and the CNN exceeds, the coded quality obtained by the non-predictive baseline after quadrupling the analysis-window length to w = 2048, at substantially lower algorithmic delay. The CNN uses only 0.13M parameters (roughly 20x fewer than the MLP) and has a decoder real-time factor (RTF) of ~0.10 on a consumer CPU.

authors.name: Niccolo Abate, Gabriel Soule, Marina Bosi

papers.title: Two-Timescale Receive Combining for Fronthaul-Constrained Uplink XL-MIMO with Visibility Regions
papers.summary: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) arrays are hard to deploy in virtualized radio access networks, because the fronthaul data rate grows with the number of antennas when the radio unit forwards every antenna sample. We propose a two-timescale receiver that allocates the per-user combining ranks under the fronthaul stream budget from the channel statistics. The radio unit applies the long-timescale transform, after which the distributed unit applies a minimum mean-squared-error receiver in the reduced dimension. For disjoint visibility regions, we prove that the reduced-dimension receiver decouples across users. We characterize the sum-rate loss to second order and show that the greedy allocation, which we call saturating capture, minimizes its leading term. In simulations, the allocation gains over a uniform-rank baseline, matches a budget-trimmed threshold rule at a small number of users and exceeds it as the array and the user count grow. The gain grows with the heterogeneity of the per-user eigenvalue profiles and vanishes for identical profiles. Under out-of-cell interference offset by at least half a window width, the gain survives with clean covariances, which window-restricted estimation keeps for disjoint windows.

authors.name: Jaebum Park, Robert W. Heath Jr

papers.title: Control of Linear Dynamical Systems with Operational Constraints
papers.summary: This paper presents a method for designing servo-controllers that enforce operational constraints on multi-input multi-output linear time-invariant dynamical systems. The proposed method introduces a control augmentation that complements a baseline controller to ensure forward invariance of state/output trajectories within prescribed box constraints. The derivations of the control design are based on the Nagumo Theorem, the Comparison Lemma, and principles from min-norm optimal control akin to the theory of Control Barrier Functions. Importantly, an explicit piecewise-linear feedback control law is derived, which provides continuous enforcement of constraints without online optimization, enabling rigorous stability and robustness analysis via classical linear systems theory. Extensions to handle estimation errors in output feedback and integral action in proportional-integral control are provided. Theoretical results are validated through flight control simulation studies that demonstrate input/output constraint satisfaction, robustness to disturbances, and closed-loop stability. The proposed method offers a mathematically rigorous, practical, and analyzable alternative to common heuristic or optimization-intensive constrained control strategies.

authors.name: Marcel Menner, Eugene Lavretsky

papers.title: Sample-Covariance Regularization for Data-Driven Predictive Control from Frequency Response Functions under Colored Noise
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate how sample covariance obtained from frequency-response functions (FRFs) can be exploited to improve performance of data-driven frequency-domain predictive control (FreePC) in the presence of colored measurement noise. In case of periodic multisine excitation, this covariance is obtained directly from repeated periods and provides a frequency-dependent measure of uncertainty without requiring an additional parametric noise model. To incorporate this information into both indirect and direct predictive control, we develop a frequency-domain subspace predictive controller (FD-SPC) and establish its equivalence to the direct FreePC formulation in the noiseless setting. Regularization terms for both formulations are then motivated by expected prediction-error criteria and constructed from the sample covariance of the FRF estimates. Across all tested noise models and data sizes, regularization consistently reduces the median realized control cost relative to the corresponding controller without covariance regularization, with reductions of up to 35%.

authors.name: M. Wind, T. J. Meijer, V. S. Dolk, W. P. M. H. Heemels

papers.title: Dynamic Traffic Modeling using Equivalent Circuit Models
papers.summary: This paper presents an equivalent circuit model (ECM) for dynamic traffic modeling by exploiting analogies between electrical and transportation variables. Vehicle concentration is represented by capacitor voltage, while traffic flow is modeled using controllable current sources. The proposed formulation is shown to preserve the conservation and sending/receiving relationships of the spatially discretized Lighthill Whitham Richards traffic model. The framework is extended to restricted inflow, traffic signals, and two road merging and diverging scenarios. Validation against microscopic Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulations, involving traffic signals, two-road merging, and single-road diverging scenarios, demonstrates that the proposed ECM successfully reproduces the principal macroscopic traffic dynamics, including queue formation, backward congestion propagation, vehicle accumulation, saturation, and subsequent traffic recovery.

authors.name: Joseph Moyalan, Ricardo de Castro, Iman Ebrahimi, Xuchang Tang, Xinfan Lin

papers.title: Simulating Nonlinear Resistive Networks using a Behavioral Splitting
papers.summary: An operator splitting method is developed for computing operating points of nonlinear resistive networks. Our behavioral formulation separates the device laws from Kirchhoff's laws and casts simulation as a zero-finding problem. Branch port resistances then provide a diagonal preconditioner for the relaxed Peaceman-Rachford iteration in scattering variables. Each iteration requires solving independent scalar equations and a linear system with a fixed weighted Laplacian matrix. Convergence is established for maximal monotone device laws when an operating point exists. Contractive branch reflections also yield a linear convergence bound independent of network topology. Numerical experiments on crossbar arrays illustrate the computational advantages.

authors.name: Ryan Alizadeh, Thomas Chaffey, Dominic Liao-McPherson, Alberto Padoan

papers.title: Coexistence of LEO Satellite Communication Systems under Regulatory Protection Constraints
papers.summary: This paper investigates the coexistence of two low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems sharing the same frequency band: a primary system with regulatory precedence over the spectrum and a secondary system that must not cause excessive interference to the primary system's ground users. This spectrum sharing paradigm was recently formalized by the United States Federal Communications Commission (FCC) through short-term and long-term protection criteria that limit primary-link unavailability and throughput degradation due to interference inflicted by the secondary system. To facilitate coexistence, we propose a satellite selection mechanism that associates the secondary system's satellites with clusters of ground cells at each handover to maximize secondary-user throughput while abiding by these regulatory constraints. Our mechanism enforces both constraints through a cumulative assessment that combines past primary-link performance with predicted performance over the upcoming handover interval. Simulation results show that our proposed method achieves up to 31% higher secondary-user throughput than prior work that imposes interference-to-noise ratio (INR) constraints, even when its constraints are tuned to satisfy the FCC's throughput-based protection criteria.

authors.name: Sunwoo Min, Daesik Hong, Jemin Lee, Ian P. Roberts

papers.title: Soft-then-Hard: Joint Link Association and Precoding Optimization for LEO Satellite Networks
papers.summary: Spatial multiplexing in dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks is hindered by two bottlenecks. First, line-of-sight (LoS)-dominant propagation from a high orbital altitude places the users in a narrow angular region, which limits the spatial resolution achievable by a single satellite. Second, the visible satellites cause severe inter-satellite interference. Both effects call for joint link association and precoding, because the association decides which users are served together and which streams interfere. However, conventional block coordinate descent with hard association updates suffers from premature turning-off, where an inactive link loses precoder power and cannot be reactivated in subsequent iterations. To overcome this limitation, we propose a soft-then-hard update scheme that relaxes the association into continuous weights via iterative scaling, keeping candidate links active. Annealing progressively concentrates the association weights as the precoders are updated, after which a single hard matching determines the serving links. We further extend this framework to the LEO space-time channel, where distinct Doppler shifts provide user separability beyond angular geometry. Numerical results show that, over the space-time channel, the proposed design outperforms the baselines while effectively exploiting this separability.

authors.name: Hyeongtak Yun, Wonjae Shin, Jeonghun Park

papers.title: On Real Eventual Exponential Positive property of complex-valued Laplacians and their pseudoinverses
papers.summary: The property of real eventual exponential positivity guarantees the state trajectories of a linear time-invariant system to evolve asymptotically to right half of the complex-plane [1]. It has applications in the characterization of herdability and reachability of states in networked systems. Networks with complex-valued edge-weights arise in AC power systems and opinion dynamics. Recent work has introduced real eventual exponential positive (rEEP) Laplacians, for which the trajectories of the associated network flow eventually converge to consensus. We establish further properties of rEEP Laplacians and their pseudoinverses. Firstly, we show that the rEEP property for complex-valued matrices exhibits invariance under specific rotational transformations. Secondly, we establish that the property of rEEP is preserved under the MoorePenrose pseudoinverse operation, highlighting its robustness under algebraic manipulations. These results apply to effective impedance computation in AC networks and to consensus in multi-agent systems. Finally, we provide numerical examples to validate our theoretical results.

authors.name: Aditi Saxena, Twinkle Tripathy, Rajasekhar Anguluri

papers.title: An Overview on Multimodal Wireless and Visual Sensing for Environment Reconstruction: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.summary: Physical-scene reconstruction through visual sensing and channel knowledge map (CKM) reconstruction through wireless sensing have attracted growing research interest but have largely evolved independently within the computer vision and wireless communications communities, respectively. When applied to the same physical environment, the two sensing modalities provide complementary observations. Visual sensing captures detailed scene geometry and appearance but is constrained by occlusion and poor lighting. Wireless sensing can provide information beyond visual line of sight regardless of lighting conditions, but its measurements are often sparse and difficult to associate with scene structures. These complementary strengths motivate a unified multimodal approach to physical-scene and CKM reconstruction. This paper provides an overview of such unified environment reconstruction through wireless and visual sensing. We first compare the capabilities and limitations of the two modalities and discuss potential applications that benefit from jointly reconstructing both targets. We then review two complementary research directions, namely wireless-assisted physical-scene reconstruction and vision-assisted CKM reconstruction, highlighting how each modality supports the reconstruction task associated with the other. Building on these perspectives, we discuss design principles for a joint representation that supports both targets and identify mutual refinement, in which each modality helps improve the reconstruction associated with the other. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions, offering insights into developing site-specific environment models for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond networks.

authors.name: Guanlin Wu, Chao Hu, Yilong Chen, Yudong Guo, Rongfei Fan, Juyong Zhang, Han Hu, Jie Xu

papers.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
papers.summary: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback--Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy--security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy--security trade-off in practical scenarios.

authors.name: Mahyar Mohammadi, Subhrakanti Dey, Arunava Naha

papers.title: BAmbiDrop: Array-Agnostic Speech Enhancement with Zero-Shot binaural Reproduction using Multi-center Ambisonics Encoding
papers.summary: Array-agnostic enhancement networks generalize across microphone geometries but produce a single channel, while binaural enhancement methods preserve interaural cues only for one fixed device geometry. We propose BAmbiDrop, a framework that extends array-agnostic enhancement to binaural reproduction without retraining. Exploiting the fact that the Ambisonics origin is an arbitrary point in space, a frozen single-channel AmbiDrop network estimates a complex mask at multiple centers across the array; these masks are fused by a complex mean into a single shared mask, applied to the microphone signals and rendered by fixed BSM filters. Across 21 free-field and rigid-sphere arrays, the fused mask improves enhancement and interaural cue reproduction simultaneously, whereas masking each microphone independently degrades the latter without a consistent gain in the former.

authors.name: Michael Tatarjitzky, Vladimir Tourbabin, Boaz Rafaely

papers.title: Wireless Interference Recognition with Limited Data via Utilizing Diffusion Model
papers.summary: Accurate recognition of interference signals is essential for maintaining the reliability and security of modern wireless communication systems. However, existing approaches face several significant challenges: the high cost and the scarcity of accurately labeled datasets adaptable to diverse environments, coupled with the limited ability to evaluate uncertainty factors arising from propagation in complex electromagnetic environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a diffusion-driven model for wireless interference recognition. Specifically, we develop a composite data augmentation strategy that integrates geometric transformation and modal augmentation to enrich the limited data distribution. Geometric transformation expands scarce signal data, and modal augmentation generates semantically consistent multimodal data by modeling the correlations among cross-domain features. Following that, we propose a novel diffusion-based generative model with an interference classifier to accurately capture the distribution of interference signals within given signal data. It hence significantly improves the understanding of environmental uncertainty factors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art methods by over 5.84\% in wireless interference recognition.

authors.name: Rui Wang, Tong Li, Chanchan Zhu, Shaolong Gu, Zhu Xiao

papers.title: Bridging Semantics and Signals: An LLM-Driven MoE Framework for Radio Map Prediction
papers.summary: High-fidelity radio map prediction is essential for wireless network optimization, yet existing single-network models frequently fail to generalize across diverse multi-band and multi-terrain scenarios due to rigid parameter constraints. We introduce LLM-MoE, a framework that employs a divide-and-conquer Mixture-of-Experts strategy to dynamically allocate modeling tasks to matched expert sub-networks. Our approach features a heterogeneous expert pool for characterizing varied physical propagation behaviors, combined with an LLM-driven semantic extractor that provides global physical awareness. A cross-modal fusion module integrates these macroscopic semantics with local spatial features for adaptive routing. Experimental results on the SpectrumNet dataset show that LLM-MoE outperforms top-tier baselines, achieving a 10.0\% reduction in Mean Squared Error (MSE) and 9.7\% in Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE), while ensuring robust generalization across heterogeneous environments.

authors.name: Qi Yang, Xinyue Jiang, Tong Li, Chanchan Zhu, Shaolong Gu, Zhu Xiao

papers.title: Shifted Interaction Functions: A Unified Framework for Imperfect Actuation and Sensing in Consensus Networks
papers.summary: Practical networked robotic systems rarely implement ideal consensus interactions exactly, since local actuation constraints, sensing biases, and heterogeneous interaction maps may shift the input-output relations used by distributed controllers. Rather than focusing solely on whether consensus occurs, such imperfections can fundamentally alter the structure of the asymptotic collective behavior, typically yielding global or clustered velocity alignment, while exact static agreement arises only in special cases. This paper develops a shifted-interaction framework for analyzing collective alignment under imperfect actuation and sensing. Shifted functions provide a compact representation of local actuator and sensor maps, allowing actuation constraints and sensing biases to be represented by horizontally and vertically shifted monotone interactions. The framework distinguishes nodal shifted actuation from edge-wise shifted sensing. For shifted actuation, a Lyapunov analysis establishes global velocity alignment under compatible actuation ranges, including bounded, non-invertible, and deadzone-type maps. For shifted sensing, a maximum-principle argument and a paired-sensitivity condition establish convergence to velocity clusters over edges with infinite accumulated sensitivity; uniform sensing sensitivity yields exponential global velocity alignment. In the linear case, closed-form expressions characterize asymptotic behavior and identify actuation as a special case of sensing. Simulations illustrate static, globally aligned, and clustered velocity-aligned behaviors.

authors.name: Yang Xu, Enric Morella Violeta, Hector Garcia de Marina

papers.title: From Discrete Snapshots to Geometric Entity: Motion-Native Channel Tracking for THz Near-Field XL-MIMO
papers.summary: Channel tracking in mobile terahertz (THz) near-field extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems is challenging because spherical-wave propagation couples angle and range, leading to rapid and nonlinear channel evolution under sparse pilot observations. Existing approaches typically estimate pilot-local channel or position snapshots before applying temporal tracking or smoothing, making them vulnerable to information loss during snapshot formation. To break this bottleneck, we propose a paradigm shift from tracking discrete snapshots to estimating a holistic geometric entity, namely, one shared continuous UE trajectory over the tracking window. Specifically, we parameterize the trajectory using a low-dimensional cubic B-spline representation and directly couple the per-pilot profile likelihoods through this shared trajectory before any pilot-local position estimate is finalized, thereby inducing continuous near-field channel evolution. We further characterize the efficient geometric information supplied by each pilot observation and its aggregation in the shared spline-coefficient space. Based on this formulation, we develop a regularized maximum a posteriori estimator and a quadratic-penalty lifted solver that separates parallel pilot-local geometric updates from a structured global spline update. The resulting global system is banded and, for a fixed spline degree, admits linear-complexity factorization, enabling an efficient structured implementation. Simulations demonstrate consistently improved tracking accuracy over representative temporally refined baselines in the tested medium-to-high-SNR regime, together with a favorable accuracy--runtime trade-off. These results highlight the benefit of coupling sparse pilot observations through a shared continuous trajectory rather than temporally processing independently estimated snapshots.

authors.name: Yuheng Fan, Chuang Yang, Mugen Peng

papers.title: Intelligent Reflecting Surface for ISAC: From Beamforming to Joint Design With Surface Orientation
papers.summary: Rotatable semi-passive intelligent reflecting surfaces (SIRSs) provide an additional spatial degree of freedom (DoF) by proactively adjusting the orientation, while dedicated sensors directly receive target echoes. To exploit this DoF for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), we investigate the joint optimization of SIRS rotation, base station (BS) transmit beamforming, and SIRS phase-shifts to minimize the Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) for target's spatial-frequency estimation subject to per-user communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints. We first establish an orientation-dependent system model that characterizes the effective aperture gains, based on which the CRB is derived. To gain useful insights, closed-form expressions of the beamforming and rotation designs are derived in the sensing-only and communication-only cases. For the co-located user and target case, we further characterize the condition under which the sensing-oriented rotation design also satisfies the communication requirement. In the single-user single-target case with ideal unit aperture gains, we analyze the channel correlation and its impact on ISAC performance. For the general multi-user case, an effective method based on the genetic algorithm is developed. Numerical results demonstrate the superiorities of the rotatable SIRS over the fixed-orientation SIRS and show that jointly optimizing the SIRS orientation and beamforming can improve the effective aperture gains and the correlation between communication and sensing channels.

authors.name: Qiaoyan Peng, Qingqing Wu, Guangji Chen, Yong Zeng, Sai Huang, Zhiyong Feng, Shanpu Shen, Wen Chen

papers.title: Two-Timescale Trajectory Control, Task Reassignment and Resource Scheduling for Multi-UAV Cooperative Mobile Edge Computing
papers.summary: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) is a promising technology, leveraging the advantages of UAVs including flexible deployment, wide coverage, and reliable wireless communication. In this paper, we study the task reassignment and offloading problem in a multi-UAV cooperative operating environment, and consider the real occurrence that the computing tasks arrive more frequently than UAVs make flight decisions. In addition, we also take into account the position offset of the UAV during flight and the unavailability of the UAV due to external interference. We propose a two-timescale optimization framework, where the trajectory of the UAV is carried out on a large timescale, while the task reassignment and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized on a small timescale. The core objective is to maximize the long-term average system gain, which takes both energy consumption and task delay into account. To address the UAV trajectory optimization problem under large timescale constraints, we propose a constrained multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm. For decision-making within small timescale, to jointly optimize task offloading decisions and computing resource allocation, we integrate convex optimization with a heuristic algorithm. Finally, we conduct extensive simulations to evaluate the proposed algorithms against the baseline, achieving a 24% reduction in latency and a 28% reduction in total system cost.

authors.name: Bin Li, Shiyu Sun, Lei Liu, Zesong Fei

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Massively Parallel Simulation for Low-Thrust Multi-Revolution Rendezvous
papers.summary: The growing demand for on-orbit servicing and constellation management in low Earth orbit requires autonomous and reliable low-thrust rendezvous. Traditional numerical methods struggle with the long-horizon nature of multi-revolution maneuvers under perturbations, while standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods are limited by low simulation throughput and poor sample efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a massively parallel DRL guidance framework. A fully tensorized, GPU-resident orbital propagator is developed to integrate $J_2$-perturbed orbital dynamics and policy optimization within a zero-copy pipeline, achieving up to a 67-fold increase in simulation throughput over conventional CPU baselines. In addition, the rendezvous problem is formulated in modified equinoctial elements and trained with a progressive curriculum learning strategy to improve convergence and generalization across increasingly challenging rendezvous scenarios. Simulations show that the proposed framework can learn robust rendezvous trajectories for complex multi-revolution rendezvous over a broad range of orbital configurations. Additional evaluations under a high-fidelity model and eclipse-induced thrust interruptions further demonstrate the robustness of the learned policy under practical mission constraints. Moreover, the trajectories generated by the proposed framework can be used as effective initial guesses for optimization-based trajectory solvers, improving the convergence of high-precision trajectory optimization. The method offers a scalable approach for real-time low-thrust guidance and trajectory optimization.

authors.name: Chenglong Wu, Yi Zhou, Bin Cheng, Nan Zhang, Hexi Baoyin

papers.title: Real-Time Threat Classification in Multi-Agent Systems via Topology-Coupled Hidden Markov Models
papers.summary: Networked multi-agent systems coordinating in adversarial environments face compound cyber threats that alternate between false-data injection (FDI), denial-of-service (DoS), and stealthy decoy perturbations designed to mimic benign operational anomalies. Because the switching policy is latent and the plant dynamics evolve continuously, deterministic threshold detectors struggle to isolate deception without causing excessive false alarms. This paper presents an online, data-driven framework that couples distributed continuous time unknown input observers (UIOs) with a topology-aware Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for real-time attack detection and classification under unknown adversarial strategies. By decoupling FDI signals from augmented node states, distributed observers deployed across the network generate local augmented residuals that are discretized into emission sequences. The HMM embeds the underlying directed communication graph into the off-diagonal blocks of its transition probability matrix, explicitly capturing inter-agent attack propagation. Both transition and observation probabilities are updated recursively online via an Expectation-Maximization (EM) scheme, adapting the classifier to evolving threat behaviours without prior offline calibration. Numerical simulations on a directed network demonstrate that incorporating graph topology into the latent transition dynamics resolves the severe classification ambiguity between nominal and decoy modes, outperforming decoupled agent-independent decoders while restricting observer deployment to a sparse subset of nodes.

authors.name: Ailin Barzegar, Davide Spinello, Mohammad Pirani

papers.title: A Bussgang-based Latent Lifting Method: Discrete RIS Channel Estimation and Beamforming
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of discrete phase-shift optimization in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multiuser communication systems. Practical RIS hardware often utilizes low-resolution phase shifters, leading to challenging combinatorial optimization problems. To address this challenge, we propose a Bussgang-based latent lifting (BuLL) method that represents discrete phase shifts as quantized outputs of continuous latent variables. Our BuLL method calibrates the Bussgang gain and distortion covariance under a reference distribution and keeps these moments fixed during deterministic latent optimization. These fixed moments are then used to construct a distortion-aware continuous surrogate that incorporates reference-averaged discretization effects without penalty terms. For uplink channel estimation, we develop a matrix quadratic transform-based algorithm to optimize a mean-square-error surrogate. For downlink beamforming, we develop a generalized power iteration-based RIS phase-shift optimization algorithm for a spectral efficiency (SE) surrogate. Numerical results demonstrate improvements in channel estimation accuracy and sum SE over conventional benchmarks in the evaluated low-resolution RIS settings.

authors.name: Mintaek Oh, Namyoon Lee, Jinseok Choi

papers.title: Sparse Graph Neural Networks With Spectral Virtual Nodes for MIMO Detection
papers.summary: Graph neural network (GNN) detectors achieve high accuracy in large multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, but exchange messages between all pairs of transmitted symbols, so their complexity grows quadratically with the number of streams. We first propose a sparse GNN (SGNN) detector that restricts each symbol's messages to its most strongly coupled neighbors, so the message count grows linearly with the system size. However, pruning discards small couplings that jointly shape the weak channel directions, which limit detection accuracy. Even on the dense graph, learned messages capture these directions only partially. We therefore propose a sparse GNN with spectral virtual nodes (SVGNN), which filters the node states through a scaled regularized inverse of the channel Gram matrix to emphasize the weak directions. With two neighbors per symbol, SVGNN reduces the number of multiplications by a factor of 18 relative to the approximate message passing GNN (AMP-GNN) in a 64 x 64 MIMO system. Simulations with QPSK, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM over i.i.d. and correlated channels show that SVGNN matches or outperforms both AMP-GNN and expectation propagation, with gains of up to 3.2 dB, and lowers the error floors of AMP-GNN in several configurations. The virtual nodes improve AMP-GNN even without pruning, indicating that message passing alone, whether sparse or dense, cannot fully capture the weak directions.

authors.name: Fatemeh Jalili, Ghaya Rekaya-Ben Othman

papers.title: Modified CNN-Learned Surrogate Covariance With Krylov/Lanczos Subspace for DoA Estimation
papers.summary: Recently, learning-based approaches have been employed to improve the robustness of subspace methods in DoA estimation. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was used as a data-driven framework employing an autoencoder to generate a well-conditioned surrogate covariance optimized end-to-end through a differentiable classical estimator, such as the Root-MUSIC. The complete system is designed to estimate the directions of arrival based on a spectral decomposition using the EVD of this covariance matrix. In this work, a new approach is proposed by formulating the spectral stage of the Root-MUSIC algorithm in terms of the orthogonal complement of the signal subspace, thereby eliminating the need for the noise subspace and noise eigenvalues. Furthermore, the full EVD is replaced by a Lanczos tridiagonalization with reorthogonalization, reducing the overall computational cost.

authors.name: R. Brandt, F. Rangel de Sousa, V. J. Brusamarello

papers.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
papers.summary: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy. Theoretical analysis proves the stability of long steps during quasi-steady-state evolution and quantifies the attainable speedup. On a modified IEEE 39-bus system with frequency regulation and load restoration, the framework accurately reproduces the dynamics of all timescales and runs 15 to 18 times faster than conventional simulation of the detailed model. The accuracy and speedup of the proposed method are further verified on a 390-bus system, demonstrating its scalability to large power systems.

authors.name: Kaiyang Huang, Min Xiong, Yang Liu, Kai Sun

papers.title: Missed Interferers in Ray-Traced Radio Maps: A Digital-Twin and Stochastic Geometry Study of Aerial Coverage
papers.summary: Ray-traced digital twins are increasingly used to plan where cellular-connected uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) can fly. In this paper, we build a Sionna RT digital twin around Raleigh, NC, with 18,591 buildings and two overlapping sub-1 GHz operator networks, and study the downlink signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of UAVs at 40-300 m. We show that the Monte Carlo radio-map solver of Sionna RT misses distant line-of-sight (LOS) interferers on aerial planes. With $10^7$ rays per sector and 5 m cells, it therefore underestimates the coverage at low SINR thresholds and overestimates it at high thresholds, by up to 26 percentage points at $\pm$2 dB and 50-100 m. Using a LOS-aware deterministic engine validated with Sionna's path solver, we then develop a stochastic geometry model with strongest-sector association and own-site leakage that matches the engine without fitting. The analysis shows that the interference grows logarithmically with the modeled network radius, so a twin that omits distant LOS sites overestimates the coverage, and that altitude mainly reduces the coverage at high SINR thresholds. Finally, selecting the better of two operators raises the minimum SINR along the best corridor by 1.0-3.9 dB up to 100 m.

authors.name: Saad Masrur, Ismail Guvenc

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Data Generation for Learning Nonlinear MPC Policies
papers.summary: Learning MPC requires large datasets generated by repeatedly solving MPC problems. For Nonlinear MPC (NMPC), dataset generation is computationally expensive because feasible initial states are difficult to sample efficiently. The feasible set is often non-convex or even disconnected, and many randomly sampled states are infeasible, leading to wasted optimization solves and unnecessary computational effort. In this work, we propose a data-generation framework for learning NMPC policies that combines active-set exploration with projection-based sampling. First, a bilevel formulation samples activity weights to promote solutions associated with different active sets while preserving optimality for the original NMPC problem; second, a simpler slack-based formulation uses weighted slack variables to target different active sets at the single level. These reference solutions are then used to construct local linearized feasible sets, from which candidate initial states are sampled and projected through the nonlinear NMPC problem to recover feasible and locally optimal training samples. Our approach is up to $37\times$ faster than baseline uniform sampling with $99\%$ acceptance rate, while maintaining a representative coverage of the feasible set.

authors.name: Pietro Gori, Anton Pozharskiy, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini, Moritz Diehl, Armin Nurkanovi\'c

papers.title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
papers.summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit a current that is either zero or at least a minimum rate, typically 6 A, which makes this allocation problem non-convex. Existing methods either solve a mixed-integer program with a commercial solver, which can be computationally expensive, adds software dependencies, and incurs licensing costs, or apply heuristics without optimality guarantees. This paper proposes Bisect-Index-Choose (BIC), a fast and solver-free scheduling algorithm that computes a globally optimal allocation among EVs under mild assumptions on their utilities. For $n$ EVs, BIC runs in $O(n \log n)$ time when all EVs share one maximum rate and in $O(n^2)$ time for two, times a logarithmic factor in the numerical precision. In tests with up to 1000 EVs, BIC attains global optimality and is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the solver. On real-world charging data, it needs less capacity and delivers more energy than existing heuristics. We implement BIC on a low-cost microcontroller and show that it solves instances with 1000 EVs in less than 90 ms.

authors.name: Can Berk Saner

papers.title: MPSi: Neural Extraction of Site-Specific Multipath Propagation Properties for Massive MIMO
papers.summary: Accurate extraction of site-specific multipath propagation properties enables a wide range of wireless applications, including initial access, wideband channel reconstruction, and the generation of channel datasets for learning-based and continual-learning systems. Classical parametric channel-sounding algorithms such as RIMAX provide physically interpretable estimates, but their data-dependent model-order selection and iterative nonlinear refinement introduce substantial delay and computational cost. This paper proposes MPSi, a physics-guided neural framework that replaces these costly stages with a compact path-count network and a fixed-depth, deep-unfolded Levenberg-Marquardt refinement. MPSi estimates the complex gain, angle of arrival, and propagation delay of each multipath component while preserving the underlying physical channel model. We evaluate MPSi in two site-specific ray-traced environments, a small cell and a dense urban area, and show that it achieves initial-access and full-channel-estimation performance comparable to an enhanced RIMAX baseline while requiring significantly fewer optimization iterations. The reconstructed channels also yield bit-error-rate performance close to the perfect-channel knowledge reference. These results position MPSi as a promising low-overhead framework for extracting multipath propagation properties in massive-MIMO systems and for generating cell-specific channel pseudo-labels for training when direct ground-truth measurements are unavailable.

authors.name: Maryam Rezvani, Raviraj Adve, Amr El-Keyi, Akram bin Sediq

papers.title: An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
papers.summary: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined by terminal DC voltages and line resistances, which inherently limits the capability of changing individual line currents for essential grid services such as power flow management and overloading prevention. To address these two limitations, DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC power flow controllers (DCPFCs) have been developed. The conventional DCCBs are two-port devices installed in series with DC lines at their terminals in an MTDC converter substation, so that any fault current flowing through the line can be rapidly cleared. Additionally, a DCPFC can be installed at line terminals to adjust terminal voltages and power exchanges among adjacent lines. As a result, for a substation that connects to multiple lines, it needs to host multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, which significantly increases the cost and footprint of both the substation and the MTDC grid. To this end, this work proposes an integrated equipment combining multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, called the interline multiport DCCB with DCPFC, which can reduce the number of components and enhance the economic feasibility of MTDC networks. This paper presents the topology, operation principles, and component selection procedures of the proposed equipment, and compares it with the state-of-the-art technologies. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results validate the fault interruption and power flow control performance of the interline multiport DCCB with PFC.

authors.name: Maliha Ferdous, Zhi Jin Zhang, Qichen Yang, Maryam Saeedifard

papers.title: Kinematic Total-Body PET Video Reconstruction via Hierarchical List-Mode EM and Validation-Adaptive Space-Time Regularisation
papers.summary: Kinematic PET is introduced as an imaging task focused on visualisation of early radiotracer delivery and rapid multi-organ motion without gating. The proposed kinematic video reconstruction method uses 33-ms frames (~30 frames per second), initialised with 3D expectation maximisation (EM) time of flight (TOF) list-mode reconstruction, followed by cycles of a 2-stage update. These 2 stages are i) a hierarchical EM (HEM) update using multiple temporal pooling levels, and ii) a validation-adaptive space-time (VAST) regularisation update. HEM combines frame-specific EM corrections with corrections estimated from higher-count temporal blocks, slowing noise amplification for the ultrashort frames. VAST mixes each 3D target patch in a frame with source patches sampled nearby in space and time. It selects the candidate that best matches the mean of the corresponding patches in the two adjacent frames, with the unchanged patch also eligible. Optional temporal block sum correction uses the initial EM temporal sum as a reference to reduce loss of spatial detail. HEM+VAST was evaluated with a dynamic digital phantom, and demonstrated on human FDG data acquired on a Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra (28 - 58 s post-injection). At a background spatial coefficient of variation of 10%, the temporal full width at half maximum of the fastest phantom bolus was 151 ms with HEM+VAST, compared with 86 ms for the ground truth. The video frame rate FDG images reveal vascular and organ detail, radiotracer bolus passage and respiration-related multi-organ motion. Kinematic PET could complement conventional dynamic PET by supporting the development of image-derived physiological biomarkers and motion estimation for quantitative reconstruction. Future work should compare HEM+VAST with prior 4D PET reconstruction methods at the same 33-ms frame duration and matched noise levels.

authors.name: Andrew J. Reader, Gary J. R. Cook, Paul K. Marsden, Sarah-May Gould, Alexander Hammers, Simon R. Cherry

papers.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
papers.summary: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.

authors.name: Yuxi Chen, Muhammad Iqbal Rochman, Kyler McCormack, Jakob Kotz, Monisha Ghosh

papers.title: Feasibility-Aware Learning for Network-Constrained Unit Commitment
papers.summary: Learning-based approaches to network-constrained unit commitment (NCUC) usually still rely on an optimization solver to repair or complete their predictions, which limits the speedup they can deliver. This paper proposes FALCON-UC, a feasibility-aware graph learning framework that predicts commitment and dispatch jointly and produces final schedules without solving a mixed-integer program at inference time. It combines an LSTM--GraphSAGE predictor over a fully connected generator graph, a differentiable correction that embeds commitment-dependent dispatch bounds, power balance, and PTDF-based branch flows in training, and deterministic commitment, dispatch, and ramp-coupled reserve repairs at inference. On the 2383-bus system, FALCON-UC achieves $99.09\%$ commitment accuracy and a $0.4350\%$ mean absolute cost gap with all evaluated constraints within tolerance at $0.0562$ s per instance, a $2.27\times10^{3}$ speedup over the solver. MTLR R-SCUC-FL is slightly more accurate but still needs an optimization solver to complete each schedule, which takes $262.2$ s per instance, $4.67\times10^{3}$ times the FALCON-UC runtime. A label-only baseline without repair violates the balance and branch limits on every 2383-bus test instance, and FALCON-UC also meets all evaluated constraint tolerances on a 1354-bus system.

authors.name: Hien Thanh Doan, Yeji Lim, Hongseok Kim

papers.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization
papers.summary: This work presents a 65 nm SoC for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation. The SoC performs low-noise in-ear EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A dedicated accelerator is developed, featuring a memory reuse technique to efficiently process long kernels required for low-frequency EEG feature extraction. A runtime dynamic quantization is incorporated, reducing model size by 3.88 times with only a 0.28% loss in accuracy. A sensitivity of 98.3% is achieved for deep sleep detection, enabling effective sleep modulation.

authors.name: Yaqian Xu, Xinyu Chen, Yuhan Hou, Jianxiong Xu, Hao You, Yu Huang, Bowen Liu, Ashley Hung, Andrew G. Richardson, Roman Genov, Xilin Liu

papers.title: Virtual-Flow: Virtual Microphone-based Speech Enhancement via Semi-supervised Flow Matching
papers.summary: Neural network-based virtual microphone estimation (neural-VME) synthesizes microphone signals at unobserved spatial locations from a limited set of real microphone (RM) physical recordings. This enables high-resolution arrays that improve spatial processing for downstream tasks such as speech enhancement. However, existing methods rely on supervised training with ground-truth signals captured at virtual locations, requiring datasets that scale with the number of virtual microphones (VM) and leaving open the question of how to design optimal large-array configurations. We propose Virtual-Flow, a flow-matching framework that implicitly generates VM signals conditioned on real recordings, without requiring ground-truth VM signals. We introduce a semi-supervised training strategy based on pseudo-VM targets constructed from time-delayed superpositions of real recordings. Virtual-Flow shows improved magnitude estimation in high-frequency bands, yielding richer spatial cues for beamforming. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed Virtual-Flow, combined with reflow distillation, outperforms existing neural-VME baselines in VM-based beamforming and achieves competitive end-to-end speech enhancement performance with low computational cost.

authors.name: Dongheon Lee, Ashutosh Pandey, Sanjeel Parekh, Zhaoheng Ni, Daniel Wong, Jacob Donley, Buye Xu, Juan Azcarreta

papers.title: Learning the NMPC with Stability Guarantees
papers.summary: Although nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) is widely used, its online optimization is computationally expensive. Neural network approximations of NMPC can effectively reduce the online computational burden but generally lack stability guarantees. This paper proposes an approximate NMPC framework with guarantees of constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability. The approximation error is addressed through constraint tightening, and the resulting tightened NMPC is used to generate the training dataset of the approximate NMPC. The maximum allowable approximation error is prescribed a priori for the design of tightened NMPC and satisfied in a probabilistic sense through an iterative trial-and-error procedure alternating between network training and a posteriori verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a numerical example of a constrained nonlinear system.

authors.name: Shuyou Yu, Yan Sun, Jun Ai, Qifang Liu, Hong Chen

papers.title: Numerical Stability Issues and a Mitigation Method in Switching Events Calculation Considering State Variable Discontinuities for EMT Simulation
papers.summary: Some existing methods for switching events calculation considering state variable discontinuities for EMT simulation can encounter numerical stability issues, either over-stabilizing or destabilizing the studied power systems. This paper documents these issues in detail with a concrete example. The underlying mechanism of the issues are revealed via systematic analysis. A mitigation method for the issues is proposed. The convergence behavior of the method is analyzed. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. It is observed that the method also helps to improve the accuracy of the simulation results.

authors.name: Sheng Lei

papers.title: Synergizing CKM and ISAC for Environment-Aware Wireless Networks
papers.summary: Channel knowledge map (CKM) and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) have emerged as two key technologies for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks, enabling a new paradigm toward environment-aware system design. CKMs provide static or stochastic wireless environment information a priori by learning location-dependent mappings from transceiver positions to channel knowledge of various types, whereas ISAC exploits wireless signals to sense environmental objects in real time. CKM and ISAC have primarily been studied separately in prior works, while their integration offers a promising approach for enhancing the environment awareness of 6G networks and further improving both sensing and communication capabilities. On the one hand, sensing can support CKM construction by providing location-tagged measurements and richer environmental observations, while also enabling real-time CKM refinement in dynamic environments. On the other hand, CKM can enhance sensing by offering prior environmental information for clutter mitigation, and CKM and sensing information can be jointly leveraged to improve communications. This article provides an overview of the complementary interactions between CKMs and ISAC, with particular emphasis on three design approaches: sensing-assisted CKM construction and refinement, CKM-assisted sensing, and joint CKM- and sensing-enhanced communications. We also discuss future research directions for achieving environment-aware wireless networks.

authors.name: Juncong Zhou, Yilong Chen, Yuan Guo, Zixiang Ren, Han Hu, Jie Xu, Rui Zhang

papers.title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
papers.summary: Inference providers size their accelerator fleets for the interactive peak and sell spare capacity through fixed discounts, such as batch tiers at half price. However, inference differs from conventional cloud capacity in four respects: capacity depends on the latency tier through batching, moving weights between models is slow and costly, spot demand can wait until its deadline, and power can bind. In this paper, we develop a framework for dynamic capacity allocation and pricing of AI inference on a shared accelerator fleet. We consider a provider that serves several models under a power cap and sells each model in an interactive tier with a speed promise and in a spot tier for preemptible work with a deadline. In each period, the provider chooses how many replicas of each model to keep loaded and what spot price to quote. We show that one interactive token displaces a fixed number $\rho_m>1$ of spot tokens, and that the optimal spot price lies midway between the interactive price and the effective cost of capacity in the deadline window, which is close to the prevailing half price only when the fleet is slack. We further show that a spot tier raises the optimal reliability of the interactive tier, and that placement should follow persistent demand shifts while prices absorb transients. Building on these results, we design a model predictive controller based on a linear program with explicit approximation bounds, which solves each period in milliseconds. Numerical experiments on a simulated week with a measured daily demand profile, a flash crowd, and a grid curtailment show that the controller raises profit by 7.4% over fixed half-price practice, captures 93% of the gain available with perfect forecasts, keeps the interactive promise through both events, and leaves spot buyers better off.

authors.name: Quanyan Zhu

papers.title: Grid-forming Control of Offshore Wind through a Diode-Rectifier HVDC System: a 2 GW Case Study
papers.summary: Diode-rectifier-unit (DRU)-based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission considerably reduces the volume and weight of the offshore converter platform for remote wind farms and, hence, its cost, but shifts the task of forming and regulating the offshore AC network to the wind-turbine converters. This paper examines which grid-forming control strategy is the most suitable for DRU power transfer. The DRU commutation relationship shows that the delivered active power depends on the offshore voltage magnitude (but not on the converter voltage angle), so the angle-based active-power loop of virtual synchronous machine control is not closed through the rectifier. A $P-V/Q-{\omega}$ grid-forming architecture, which regulates active power via the voltage magnitude and derives frequency from the reactive power error, is therefore adopted. Electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1GWaggregated grid-forming turbine on a 66 kV collector network with a $\pm$525 kV bipolar DRU link show that the commanded power is delivered over 800 to 1000MW with the offshore voltage held near nominal. The paper also examines how grid-forming operation changes the allocation of control duties within the Type-4 turbine: once the grid-side converter forms the network, DC link regulation must move to the machine-side converter, which limits the achievable bandwidth of the DC-link control. Extending the system to 2 GW with two 500 MW grid-following units achieves full power transfer in simulation, but with the grid-forming converter loaded beyond its continuous rating and a steady-state offshore frequency deviation of approximately 1.8 Hz.

authors.name: Ishi Nigam, Saif Alsarayreh, Tuanku Badzlin Hashfi, Milo\v{s} Cvetkovi\'c, Joris van Doorn, Aleksandra Leki\'c

papers.title: GFM Control Automatic Compliance Toolbox
papers.summary: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation reduces system inertia, short-circuit strength, and voltage support. European grid codes, including the ENTSO-E Network Code on Requirements for Generators and the ACER Demand Connection Code, now define disturbance-based validation procedures for grid-forming (GFM) generation and converter-based demand. Commercial RMS tools, however, lack an integrated workflow aligned with these recent requirements. This paper presents an automated Python-PowerFactory compliance toolbox and an RMS test bench for a co-located system comprising a 1 MW GFM photovoltaic (PV) plant, a 0.3 MW GFM battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 1 MW converter-interfaced dynamic load at a 20 kV point of common coupling fed from a 110 kV grid. Extended virtual synchronous machine models and a DCC-oriented load model are tested in batch, with results automatically extracted and plotted for assessment. Results show compliant RMS performance for the slower, electromechanical tests, while the paper identifies which tests require complementary electromagnetic transient (EMT) verification.

authors.name: Tejas Kunbi, Rahul Rane, Dan Wu, Aleksandra Leki\'c

papers.title: Nonlinear Interference Estimation in Coherent Optical Systems: Principles and Applications
papers.summary: Accurate estimation of nonlinear interference (NLI) is important for monitoring and optimizing coherent optical networks. This invited paper reviews the main techniques proposed for receiver-side NLI estimation, with particular focus on longitudinal power monitoring (LPM). We discuss the principles, advantages and limitations of LPM-based NLI estimation, including recent experimental demonstrations. We then experimentally investigate the impact of the spatial step size and the number of averaged constellation blocks on estimation accuracy. The results show that accurate NLI estimation does not necessarily require a highly accurate power profile, with limited improvements obtained by increasing the number of averaged blocks. Finally, we discuss the main practical limitations and applications of NLI estimation, with particular attention to end-to-end and span-wise optical power optimization.

authors.name: Dario Pilori

papers.title: WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation
papers.summary: Wireless foundation models learn transferable channel state information (CSI) representations across heterogeneous wireless systems. However, conventional grid-aligned representations couple feature sequence length to CSI dimensions, restricting the allocation of representation capacity to different propagation conditions and task requirements while increasing inference overhead. This paper proposes WiFo-R, a wireless foundation model that learns progressive channel representations with selectable capacity. A channel-query cross-attention encoder aggregates spatial, temporal, and spectral CSI information, while parameter-shared recurrent updates refine existing channel features and introduce additional latent tokens. Multi-mask, multi-depth self-supervised pretraining equips intermediate states with strong reconstruction capabilities, followed by task-aligned post-training for channel estimation and CSI feedback. WiFo-R supports temporal and frequency-domain channel prediction, channel estimation, and variable-rate CSI feedback, and transfers to localization and LoS/NLoS classification. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution channel configurations demonstrate accurate reconstruction, progressive performance improvements, and strong transferability. A single feedback encoder--decoder supports six payload lengths at fixed quantization precision, while cross-attention and selectable recurrent depth improve the accuracy--complexity trade-off for large-scale CSI observations.

authors.name: Liu Xuanyu, Cao Keyi, Cheng Xiang

papers.title: Energy-Harvesting-Aware Cell-Free LEO Satellite Networks: A Lyapunov Framework for Sustainable User-Centric Beamforming and Clustering
papers.summary: We study battery-aware downlink control in user-centric cell-free low Earth orbit satellite networks with intermittent solar harvesting and finite onboard batteries. A perturbed Lyapunov controller coordinates clustering and hybrid beamforming using measured battery states and causal harvest forecasts. The per-slot solver combines group-sparse association, rate bounds, a quadratic transform, and successive convex approximation. We establish robust battery invariance for feasible implemented actions and give a utility bound conditional on a comparison policy and the per-slot implementation gap. Multi-orbit control-layer simulations show that queue-aware scheduling preserves a larger battery reserve in the stressed scenario at the expense of effective energy efficiency. A separate fixed-cluster matrix snapshot illustrates recovered hybrid beam patterns and the per-slot objective trace.

authors.name: Wali Ullah Khan

papers.title: Capability-Guided Iterative Online Optimization of Cascaded Spoken-Dialogue Modules
papers.summary: Cascaded spoken dialogue systems comprise perception-and-comprehension, decision-making, and response-generation modules. We study iterative optimization of the first and last modules. Their reciprocal speech-content interfaces enable one-sided data to provide cross-module supervision: acoustic observations, such as waveforms or feature sequences, can be pseudo-labeled to train generation, whereas content-only samples can be rendered into speech to train comprehension. Because the reliable teacher-student direction varies across domains, we propose a two-stage, capability-guided pipeline for iterative online optimization. Stage 1 compares both modules through a shared intelligibility probe and obtains a domain-wise capability prior. Stage 2 activates the compatible one-sided-data route, constructs and filters supervision with the current teacher, updates the selected student, and refreshes the relevant checkpoints across cycles. We instantiate comprehension with Whisper large-v3 and generation with CosyVoice2. After only 200 steps for Whisper and 600 for CosyVoice2 of our iterative online optimization, we observe that, on the Chinese MAGICDATA-RAMC dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 14.18% to 10.77%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 4.78% to 4.04%. On the Japanese Common Voice dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 15.23% to 15.10%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 14.85% to 11.18%. These results demonstrate the feasibility of capability-guided iterative optimization of complementary spoken-dialogue modules.

authors.name: Yuhang Qiu, Bohan Li, Wenbin Huang, Zhihan Li, Yiwei Guo, Hankun Wang, Xie Chen, Kai Yu

papers.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Transport Electrification for Low-Carbon Urban Planning: A Case Study of Phu Quoc, Vietnam
papers.summary: Urban net-zero strategies require a defensible emissions boundary and quantitative estimates of the contribution achievable through individual mitigation measures. This study assesses road-transport electrification within a planned residential development in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, using the assumptions and scenario data of an urban-planning study originally prepared in 2022. A vehicle-class inventory combines population-dependent fleet projections, assumed travel activity, gasoline and diesel consumption, fuel-specific carbon dioxide (CO_2) factors, and electricity-related emissions from battery-electric vehicles. The reference case projects annual road-transport emissions of 59.41, 73.86, and 87.23 tCO_2 for 2022, 2025, and 2030, respectively. Three year-specific substitution scenarios, corresponding to nominal electric-vehicle shares of 25%, 50%, and 100%, yield source-reported avoided emissions of 9.43, 13.64, and 55.41 tCO_2/year, or 15.9%, 18.5%, and 63.5% of their respective baselines. However, a cross-scenario audit identifies an inconsistency in the 2025 mixed-fleet results under time-invariant vehicle-class emission-intensity ratios: under that additional assumption, 2025 avoided emissions would be 23.45 rather than 13.64 tCO_2/year. The original detailed vehicle-energy input tables are not included in the available source document, preventing definitive reconciliation. The study therefore provides a transparent, preliminary planning assessment rather than evidence of citywide net-zero attainment. Its principal value is a reproducible accounting structure and an explicit identification of the data, electricity-system, and infrastructure constraints that must be resolved before policy or investment decisions.

authors.name: Tien-Khai Nguyen

papers.title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
papers.summary: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an $A$-invariant complement.

authors.name: Yong Joo Do, Jin Gyu Lee

papers.title: Local Certificate Repair for Asynchronous Controller Updates in Recommender Systems
papers.summary: We study how to adapt an existing distributed recommendation controller when local dynamics or objective weights change. Starting from a quadratic stability and cost certificate, we construct positive semidefinite corrections with finite spatial support and an explicit residual. A joint admission test allocates the available dissipation margin to these residuals and to interactions among changes and corrections, including pending updates. The test covers complete declared parameter ranges, allowing different operators to progress independently. For a fixed compatible batch, the corrections define a common storage that guarantees exponential stability and bounds the cost accumulated throughout deployment. When the admitted collection evolves, a reservation protocol preserves the certificate and a rate bound on storage increases ensures exponential convergence. Regional linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) design proposes new gain rows for the operators' own users, and a separate residual-based calculation can certify that the final gain lowers the expected cost. A recommendation-network example illustrates the tradeoff between repair depth, data access, and the benefits of deploying an update.

authors.name: Simone Mariano, Paolo Frasca

papers.title: Radiation-Pattern-Based Channel Estimation for Reconfigurable Pixel Antennas
papers.summary: Reconfigurable pixel antennas provide spatial diversity through multiple radiation patterns generated by a single antenna aperture, but exploiting this diversity can require substantial pilot overhead for exhaustive channel estimation. This paper jointly considers beam-steerable pixel-antenna design and its communication-side channel estimation. A pixel antenna is designed to generate diverse radiation patterns, whose electromagnetic correlation is then exploited to interpolate unobserved channel responses from a limited number of measurements. The proposed approach is evaluated in terms of SNR gain and NMSE, demonstrating that effective pattern selection can be achieved with significantly reduced channel-observation overhead and can even outperform exhaustive scanning at low SNR.

authors.name: Daniel Dinis, Leo M. Lahti, Pasi Yl\"a-Oijala, Risto Wichman

papers.title: Ultrawideband Polarization-Rotating Antenna for Enhanced Ground Penetrating Radar Detection
papers.summary: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) represents a powerful and widely adopted tool for nondestructive subsurface detection and imaging. To overcome the impaired detection performance caused by polarization mismatch in conventional single-channel GPR systems, this paper presents an innovative ultrawideband polarization-rotating (UPR) antenna that achieves rotating linear polarizations (LPs) by varying the source frequency for enhanced detection. The developed UPR antenna achieves a continuous polarization rotation from $0^\circ$ to $170^\circ$ across 1.2 to 3.2 GHz, as verified by both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements. The antenna is subsequently integrated into a single-channel stepped-frequency GPR system and evaluated against targets of varying geometries in a sandy environment. Compared with a conventional fixed-LP GPR system, the UPR antenna-enabled GPR system delivers markedly more consistent detection performance across all target types, with particularly pronounced enhancements for polarization-sensitive targets. By enabling ultrawideband frequency-dependent polarization agility, the proposed GPR system enhances subsurface target detection while maintaining the simplicity and low cost of a single-channel measurement architecture.

authors.name: Ming Li, Yuki Gao, Shu-Lin Chen, Hai-Han Sun, Y. Jay Guo

papers.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
papers.summary: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.

authors.name: Sandesh Thapa, He Bai

papers.title: Descriptor: UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC)
papers.summary: Anchor self-calibration estimates the positions of fixed nodes of an indoor radio positioning or localization system from observations among the nodes and to mobile devices. It replaces the survey of every anchor, which is costly and goes stale when anchors move. The UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC) is a testing ground for such methods, recorded in one industrial hall with ultra-wideband (UWB) two-way ranging. It has three parts. The first is two measured deployments. In the line-of-sight (LOS) deployment, 10 anchors range with a walking tag tracked by motion capture. In the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) deployment, 12 nodes range among obstructions, and one of them roves over surveyed markers in 20 quasi-static sessions. Both deployments also hold static sessions, and a total station surveyed every fixed node. The second part is a seeded range simulator that draws synthetic ranges on the surveyed geometry with adjustable error components, from noise-free ranges to NLOS errors, for benchmarks at controlled error levels. Its 81 frozen draws in 5 conditions serve as the reference. The third part is a set of readers that convert the ranges among the static nodes of two public UWB datasets, TWR-CLOUD-Bern and selfloc, into the same format without redistribution. All parts share open Parquet and YAML files, in which topology views select the ranges for each class of calibration method. Raw recordings with rebuild scripts, quality reports, and field labels of the line of sight complete the dataset.

authors.name: Paul Schwarzbach

papers.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.summary: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.

authors.name: Mitchell A. Thornton

papers.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
papers.summary: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.

authors.name: Changrui Liu, Robin Wroblowski, Anil Alan, Shengling Shi, Rodolphe Sepulchre, Bart De Schutter

papers.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
papers.summary: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. The topology exploits this: a thermoelectric thin film lies flat on a diamond substrate beside the device drain (the electron exit), so bulk Joule heat leaves vertically into the substrate. A lateral fin model gives a closed form for the recirculation factor gamma: the vertical pillar yields gamma = 1, while the horizontal film yields gamma_max = sqrt(2) L_z/L_x, about 0.03 for L_z = 10 um, L_x = 500 um.
