Our work uncovers new frontiers in speech emotion classification, highlighting the increasing significance of LLMs in this field moving forward.

authors.name: Siddique Latif, Muhammad Usama, Mohammad Ibrahim Malik, Bj\"orn W. Schuller

papers.title: RJD-BASE: Multi-Modal Spectral Clustering via Randomized Joint Diagonalization
papers.summary: We revisit the problem of spectral clustering in multimodal settings, where each data modality is encoded as a graph Laplacian. While classical approaches--including joint diagonalization, spectral co-regularization, and multiview clustering--attempt to align embeddings across modalities, they often rely on costly iterative refinement and may fail to directly target the spectral subspace relevant for clustering. In this work, we introduce two key innovations. First, we bring the power of randomization to this setting by sampling random convex combinations of Laplacians as a simple and scalable alternative to explicit eigenspace alignment. Second, we propose a principled selection rule based on Bottom-$k$ Aggregated Spectral Energy (BASE)--a $k$-dimensional extension of the directional smoothness objective from recent minimax formulations--which we uniquely apply as a selection mechanism rather than an optimization target. The result is Randomized Joint Diagonalization with BASE Selection (RJD-BASE), a method that is easily implementable, computationally efficient, aligned with the clustering objective, and grounded in decades of progress in standard eigensolvers. Through experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we show that RJD-BASE reliably selects high-quality embeddings, outperforming classical multimodal clustering methods at low computational cost.

authors.name: Haoze He, Artemis Pados, Daniel Kressner

papers.title: TsetlinKWS: A 65nm 16.58uW, 0.63mm2 State-Driven Convolutional Tsetlin Machine-Based Accelerator For Keyword Spotting
papers.summary: The Tsetlin Machine (TM) has recently attracted attention as a low-power alternative to neural networks due to its simple and interpretable inference mechanisms. However, its performance on speech-related tasks remains limited. This paper proposes TsetlinKWS, the first algorithm-hardware co-design framework for the Convolutional Tsetlin Machine (CTM) on the 12-keyword spotting task. Firstly, we introduce a novel Mel-Frequency Spectral Coefficient and Spectral Flux (MFSC-SF) feature extraction scheme together with spectral convolution, achieving a record-high accuracy of 87.35% for TM-based models on the 12-keyword spotting task. Secondly, we develop an Optimized Grouped Block-Compressed Sparse Row (OG-BCSR) algorithm that delivers a remarkable 9.84$\times$ reduction in model size, significantly improving the storage efficiency of CTMs. Finally, we propose a state-driven architecture tailored for CTMs, which simultaneously exploits data reuse and sparsity to attain high energy efficiency. The full system is evaluated in 65 nm process technology, consuming 16.58 $\mu$W at 0.7 V with a compact 0.63 mm$^2$ core area. TsetlinKWS demonstrates a Power-Performance-Area (PPA) product of 60.2 and requires only 907k logic operations per inference, corresponding to 1.4$\times$ and 10$\times$ reductions, respectively, compared with state-of-the-art KWS accelerators. These results position the CTM as a highly efficient candidate for ultra-low-power speech applications.

authors.name: Baizhou Lin, Yuetong Fang, Renjing Xu, Rishad Shafik, Jagmohan Chauhan

papers.title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
papers.summary: We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available. The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.

authors.name: Shuwen Lu, Mark E. Lewis, Jamol Pender

papers.title: CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction Empowered by Language Models
papers.summary: Achieving reliable communication has long been a fundamental challenge in networked systems. Semantic Error Correction (SEC) leverages the semantic understanding capabilities of language models (LMs) to perform application-layer error correction, complementing conventional channel decoding. While promising, existing SEC approaches rely solely on context captured by LMs at the application layer, ignoring the rich information available at the physical layer. To address this limitation, this paper introduces Cross-Layer SEC (CL-SEC), an LM-empowered error correction framework that integrates cross-layer information from both the physical and application layers to jointly correct corrupted words in text communication. Using a Bayesian combination in product form tailored to this framework, CL-SEC achieves significantly improved performance over methods that process information in isolated layers. CL-SEC shows substantial gains across multiple error-correction metrics, including bit-error rate, word-error rate, and semantic fidelity scores. Importantly, unlike most semantic communication systems that focus solely on recovering the semantic meaning of transmitted messages, CL-SEC aims to reconstruct the original transmitted message verbatim, leveraging the semantic understanding capabilities of LMs for precise reconstruction.

authors.name: Yirun Wang, Yuyang Du, Soung Chang Liew, Yuchen Pan, Feifan Zhang, Lihao Zhang

papers.title: Towards Optimal Passive Feedback Control of LTI Systems under LQR Performance
papers.summary: We study state-feedback design for continuous-time LTI systems with a control input and an external input-output pair. Our objective is to determine feedback gains that render the closed-loop system (strictly) passive with respect to the external port while minimizing the standard LQR cost in the disturbance-free case. The resulting constrained optimization problem is intractable due to bilinear matrix inequalities. We analyze the set of passivating gains, showing it is unbounded, possibly nonconvex, path-connected, and contractible. We propose an indirect approach, in which the set of passivating feedback gains is inner-approximated by a compact, convex polytope. A projected gradient flow is employed to compute a gain within this polytope that minimizes the LQR cost. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

authors.name: Armin Gie{\ss}ler, Pol Jan\'e-Soneira, S\"oren Hohmann

papers.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
papers.summary: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.

authors.name: Corentin Briat, Francesco Ferrante, Christophe Prieur

papers.title: State space modeling of RLC ladder circuits
papers.summary: Large-scale electrical circuits span a wide range of research topics from highly integrated circuits in microelectronics up to power grids for cities and countries. As the complexity increases significantly by each additional component, we find a need to describe large-scale circuits in a manner easy to understand. In this article, we study cascades of simple circuits consisting of resistors, capacitors and inductors, which we call ladder circuits. Such electrical ladders are common in electronics to design filters and they are also used in other disciplines, for example to describe diffusion or wave phenomena. In particular, we derive linear time-invariant state space models for three simple ladder types and we discuss the specific matrix structures of the large-scale second-order differential equations. Furthermore, we exemplify our findings with simulations to unveil the intrinsic dynamical behavior of each ladder type.

authors.name: Stephan Scholz

papers.title: VocalCoachBench: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models on Expert Feedback for Singing
papers.summary: Recent audio-language models are increasingly evaluated on recognizing, describing, and reasoning about audio, but expert-facing applications require a different capability: producing feedback that identifies problems and suggests corrective actions grounded in the input. We introduce VocalCoachBench, a benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on expert vocal coaching feedback for singing. VocalCoachBench contains 515 recordings annotated by 18 professional vocal trainers, yielding 1,064 expert audio-level reviews and 12,216 atomic coaching claims. It comprises a same-song subset for controlled comparison and a diverse-song subset for segment-grounded feedback across varied songs and recording conditions. To accommodate the open-ended nature of expert feedback, VocalCoachBench separates deterministic structured targets from claim-based assessment of free-form diagnosis and corrective guidance. Human annotation analysis shows that expert agreement varies strongly with label granularity, motivating hierarchical structured metrics and claim-based evaluation of open-ended feedback. Experiments with 12 recent audio-language models reveal a persistent gap: while the strongest models can compare performances and identify broad issue domains in free-form feedback, the best Top-3 macro-F1 only slightly exceeds a label-prior baseline, and strict diagnosis hit rates remain below 8%. To our knowledge, VocalCoachBench provides the first public testbed for evaluating audio-grounded expert feedback for singing, moving audio-language evaluation beyond description toward analytic feedback. Data, code, and audio examples are available at https://hayeonbang.github.io/VocalCoachBench.

authors.name: Hayeon Bang, Hounsu Kim, Wonil Kim, Juhan Nam

papers.title: Autonomous Precision Milling of Biological Structures via Generic Anatomical Priors and Active Boundary Perception
papers.summary: Autonomous precision milling of biological structures is challenged by incomplete knowledge of target geometry, local material thickness, and critical internal boundaries. Subject-specific preoperative models can address geometric and thickness variations, but static models cannot determine boundary status encountered during execution, while repeated target-specific imaging limits scalability. This article presents a state-adaptive autonomous milling framework that assigns complementary roles to generic anatomical priors and active boundary perception. A generic anatomical prior provides conservative global guidance and is transformed through semantic-guided registration and hybrid vision-force calibration into robot-executable guidance for individual targets. As milling approaches uncertain boundaries, the robot actively probes the remaining structure and uses relative stiffness changes to estimate boundary status and structural detachability. A state-adaptive controller governs transitions between active perception and spatially selective incremental refinement, repeating this cycle until the termination criterion is satisfied. Hierarchical experiments on biological surrogates and in vivo mouse cranial window creation demonstrate accurate anatomical prior transfer, reliable boundary adaptation, and autonomous precision milling of biological structures.

authors.name: Enduo Zhao, Xiaofeng Lin, Yifan Wang, Yuhan Song, Weihan Li, Saul Alexis Heredia Perez, Kanako Harada

papers.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
papers.summary: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.

authors.name: Cynthia Cheng, Xudong Chen

papers.title: Distributed Learning of $\alpha$-Potential Functions in Strategic Multi-agent Systems
papers.summary: We study the problem of computing the tightest \(\alpha\)-potential approximation of a general-sum game over continuous action spaces, within a prescribed class of potential functions and when each player has access only to its own utility function. The difficulty is twofold: the approximation error involves a worst-case search over an infinite set of unilateral deviations, and the required utility information is distributed across players. For a linear-in-parameters potential class, we use an exact finite-tuple reformulation that separates the problem into a global outer search over deviation tuples and distributed convex inner problems. We develop a primal--dual inner oracle tailored to this structure and establish a uniform one-sided accuracy guarantee. This oracle can be combined with global outer search to obtain an end-to-end guarantee on the outer optimization error. We also develop a projected zeroth-order outer method as a computationally lighter alternative for higher-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy--computation tradeoff between the two outer-search methods and show that the proposed optimization framework can improve upon analytical \(\alpha\)-potential constructions.

authors.name: Yifei Chen, Chinmay Maheshwari

papers.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
papers.summary: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

authors.name: Namhyun Kim, Sadjad Alikhani, Ahmed Alkhateeb

papers.title: FastSAR: Open-Source SAR Image Formation on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs, and a Matched Comparison of Algorithms, Precisions, and Processors
papers.summary: The number of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) collectors is growing exponentially, each returning raw collections that must be formed into images. Exact backprojection needs 1.6 trillion interpolated reads and 90 trillion floating-point operations for a 108-megapixel Umbra image. How long it takes to form an image, and at what price, depends on the algorithm, the arithmetic, and the hardware. Open-source implementations have never been compared on matched hardware against a common reference, and none run on Google tensor processing units (TPUs). This paper presents FastSAR, an open-source SAR image formation library for central processing units (CPUs), NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs), and TPUs. With it, we compare three SAR image formation algorithms, four floating-point formats, and six cloud devices in every supported combination, with cost per image at on-demand cloud prices as the fair common measure. FastSAR is 1.06 to 22,000 times faster than the tested open-source implementations at equal or better accuracy, and the full suite of hardware, algorithm, and floating-point combinations lets a user choose the Pareto-optimal configuration for their balance of accuracy, speed, and cost. The L4 GPU forms images the cheapest overall. Larger GPUs are faster but cost more per image because their price rises faster than their speed. The TPUs come close to the GPUs in cost, but only for the factorized algorithm, and the CPU is far less efficient in both speed and cost. Lower precision formats buy less of a speedup than expected, and each step down in precision costs accuracy.

authors.name: Paul Singerman, Tom Braun

papers.title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
papers.summary: Collision-free motion planning for multi-agent robotic systems remains an active research area because of the complexity of coordinating robot trajectories, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. Importantly, the analytical difficulty of nonconvex collision-avoidance constraints has so far driven the development of exclusively numerical methods. We derive a complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots with zero initial and final velocities, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective. We prove that these trajectories belong to eight distinct contact families and determine which family applies for each configuration of initial and final positions. We analyze the geometrical properties of the optimal trajectories and provide a numerical algorithm for computing them. These insights have already been adopted to improve the performance of numerical methods for multi-agent motion planning by several orders of magnitude.

authors.name: Jan Kamm, Antonio Terpin, Raffaello D'Andrea

papers.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
papers.summary: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

authors.name: Andr\'e Tits, Pierre-Antoine Absil, No\'e Tits

papers.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Tactile Sensing System for Intelligent Object Recognition
papers.summary: Tactile sensing provides information about object properties that can improve robotic grasping and manipulation. However, accurate object recognition during the early stages of grasping remains challenging, particularly under strict real-time constraints. This study presents a flexible, distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing system for early-stage object recognition. The system was experimentally evaluated using six everyday objects and three recognition approaches: feature-based classification using support vector machines (SVMs), raw-signal classification using 1D convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs) and convolutional recurrent neural networks (C-RNNs), and spatiotemporal heatmap classification using a 2D-CNN. The effects of sensor count and temporal window size on recognition accuracy and real-time feasibility were systematically investigated. Increasing the number of sensing elements improved recognition performance across all approaches. The best-performing method, based on spatiotemporal heatmaps and a 2D-CNN, achieved F1-scores of 0.9796, 0.9846, and 0.9903 using 16, 24, and 32 sensors, respectively. The optimal configuration, comprising 32 sensors and a 100-ms temporal window (50 samples), was deployed on an embedded edge platform, achieving an end-to-end recognition latency of approximately 101 ms from contact onset and an energy consumption of 63.8 microjoules per inference. These results demonstrate the potential of distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing for accurate, energy-efficient, and real-time object recognition during robotic grasping.
